qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Paint Stewardship Program, requiring producers of architectural paint or a representative organization to submit a plan to the Maryland Department of the Environment by July 1, 2025, to establish a statewide collection, reuse, and recycling system for postconsumer paint. The program is financed by a uniform paint stewardship assessment added to the purchase price of architectural paint sold in the State.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment (Office of Recycling)
qa_results.stakeholders: Architectural paint manufacturers/producers, paint retailers and distributors, consumers purchasing paint in Maryland, and local governments managing solid waste and household hazardous waste.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Recycling Trust Fund special fund expenditures and revenues increase correspondingly by $70,200 in FY 2026 and $64,300 in FY 2027 to cover MDE's contractual staffing for plan and annual report reviews, fully offset by review fees paid by producers or their representative organization. Beginning in FY 2026, State and local expenditures increase minimally to cover the paint stewardship assessment on government paint purchases. Local governments may experience cost savings in local waste management and household hazardous waste operations due to producer-funded paint collection and recycling.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency responsible for administering the Paint Stewardship Program, reviewing and approving program plans and annual reports, collecting review fees deposited into the State Recycling Trust Fund, maintaining public lists of compliant producers, and enforcing compliance.

MES provides solid waste and recycling services across the state, coordinates with MDE's Office of Recycling on biennial recycling and solid waste studies, and served as an information source for the legislation.

The OAG enforces state antitrust and consumer protection laws; the bill explicitly grants participating producers and representative organizations immunity from state antitrust, restraint of trade, and unfair trade practice claims for actions taken under an approved program.
DGS oversees state facilities maintenance and central procurement of commodities, including architectural paint, which will incur the newly established paint stewardship assessment fees on purchases.

The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the State Recycling Trust Fund, which receives new revenues from the paint stewardship plan and annual report review fees as well as enforcement penalties.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the State Recycling Trust Fund, which receives fee revenues and penalties authorized under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and the governing bodies of Maryland counties to establish a subclass of real property for vacant lots or properties cited as vacant and unfit for habitation, and to set a special property tax rate for that subclass. It also establishes an annual reporting requirement regarding the special tax rate, revenues generated, and adaptive reuse plans.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City, county governing bodies, and the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners of vacant and abandoned properties (including small businesses), county governments, Baltimore City, and local communities affected by blighted properties.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: County and Baltimore City property tax revenues may change depending on whether jurisdictions establish the subclass and what special tax rate is set. Administrative and reporting requirements can be handled within existing local resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires Baltimore City or any county that establishes a special tax rate for vacant and abandoned property to submit an annual report to the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) regarding the rate, affected properties, revenues generated and their uses, and the viability of properties for adaptive reuse.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits institutions of higher education in Maryland that receive State funds from considering legacy preferences or donor preferences as criteria for admissions standards, while permitting institutions to collect data on applicants' familial relationships to alumni.
qa_results.responsible_party: Institutions of higher education in Maryland that receive State funds
qa_results.stakeholders: Higher education applicants, college alumni, institutional donors, and public and private institutions of higher education in Maryland that receive State funding.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material fiscal impact on the State or local governments. Public four-year colleges and universities can update admissions policies using existing resources. Local community colleges and Baltimore City Community College do not use legacy or donor preferences, resulting in no local impact. Any potential impact on private institutions' tuition revenue or donations cannot be reliably estimated, but is assumed to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: USM is directly subject to the bill's mandate, which prohibits its 12 constituent public universities from using legacy or donor preferences as criteria for admissions.
As an independent public university receiving State funds, Morgan State University is directly bound by the bill's prohibition on considering legacy or donor preferences in admissions.
As a public institution of higher education receiving State funds, St. Mary's College of Maryland must comply with the prohibition on considering legacy and donor preferences in admissions decisions.
MHEC is the state's coordinating and regulatory agency for postsecondary education policy and oversees standards and state-funded programs across Maryland's public and private institutions.

As the state's coordinating agency responsible for establishing statewide higher education policies and standards, the commission is relevant to overarching policy changes affecting institution admissions standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill codifies the common law crime of indecent exposure and creates a new misdemeanor offense for committing indecent exposure with prurient intent when the offender knows or reasonably should know that a minor is present (if the minor is at least two years old and more than four years younger than the offender). The new offense carries penalties of up to five years imprisonment and/or a maximum fine of $10,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals charged with or convicted of indecent exposure, minor victims, law enforcement, state courts, and state and local correctional facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues and expenditures will experience minimal increases due to the bill's incarceration and monetary penalty provisions. State general fund revenues will increase minimally from fines collected in District Court, while local revenues increase from circuit court fines. Expenditures for state and local correctional facilities will increase minimally due to longer terms of incarceration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an enhanced penalty of up to five years imprisonment for indecent exposure in the presence of a minor, which will impact DPSCS operations and expenditures for state incarceration and post-release supervision through the Division of Parole and Probation.

The bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense and statutory penalties, impacting District Court and Circuit Court case filings, judicial proceedings, and fine collections administered by the Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new criminal penalties carrying up to five years of incarceration, directly impacting OPD caseloads and representation for indigent defendants charged with the offense.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is responsible for investigating violations and enforcing criminal statutory provisions related to indecent exposure across the state.
The OAG represents the State of Maryland in criminal appeals arising from convictions under the newly codified and expanded criminal provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Housing Innovation Pilot Program and the Housing Innovation Fund within the Department of Housing and Community Development to provide low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities and county governments for developing mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing projects.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Local public housing authorities, county governments, housing developers, low- and moderate-income renters, and residential construction businesses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general obligation bond expenditures increase by $10.0 million in FY 2025 due to a contingent capital budget restriction, with equivalent special fund revenues and expenditures for the Housing Innovation Fund. From FY 2026 to FY 2029, $5.0 million annually in GO bonds or PAYGO general funds is anticipated to be reallocated to the fund. State general fund administrative costs increase by $170,535 in FY 2025, rising to $175,200 by FY 2029 for 1.5 personnel. Local revenues and expenditures increase substantially as local housing authorities and counties receive loan funding, match program funds dollar-for-dollar, and operate housing projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Housing Innovation Pilot Program and the Housing Innovation Fund within the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), tasking the agency with administering the program, developing application criteria, selecting projects, and issuing low- or no-interest loans.
The bill statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly created Housing Innovation Fund separately and to invest the fund's moneys in the same manner as other State moneys.
The bill statutorily designates the Comptroller to account for the newly established Housing Innovation Fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include a $5,000,000 appropriation to the Housing Innovation Fund in the annual operating or capital budget for fiscal years 2026 through 2029.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a residential leasehold estate to be subjected to a condominium regime if an affordable housing land trust owns the reversionary fee simple estate.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Clerks of the Circuit Court)
qa_results.stakeholders: Affordable housing land trusts, low- to moderate-income homebuyers and families, and condominium developers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands housing options and homeownership models for low- and moderate-income families by allowing affordable housing land trusts to establish condominium regimes, directly aligning with the agency's mission to support and finance affordable housing.
The Secretary of State oversees the registration and governance disclosures of residential condominiums in Maryland under the Maryland Condominium Act.
Condominium regimes are established by recording declarations, bylaws, and plats with the circuit court land records, which are supported and administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local property tax collectors to include an insert in each property tax bill, designed by the State Tax Sale Ombudsman, that describes the Homeowner Protection Program and encourages taxpayers to make voluntary donations to the program. It also directs the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to maintain a website to process electronic donations and credit them to the Homeowner Protection Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (State Tax Sale Ombudsman)
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income, elderly, and disabled homeowners at risk of tax sale foreclosure, property taxpayers making voluntary donations, and local tax collection agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase beginning in fiscal year 2025 due to voluntary donations made to the Homeowner Protection Fund, though the total amount cannot be reliably estimated. State administrative expenses can be absorbed with existing resources and minimal transaction offsets. Local government expenditures increase beginning in fiscal year 2025 to produce and include the required inserts in tax bills, with sample reported costs ranging from $3,200 annually in Havre de Grace to $70,000 annually in Montgomery County. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill promotes funding and awareness for the Homeowner Protection Program, which assists low-income, elderly, and disabled homeowners facing tax sale foreclosure. This aligns directly with DHCD's mission to preserve homeownership and promote housing stability across Maryland communities.

AOC was consulted regarding the bill's intersection with tax sale foreclosure proceedings in the court system, although provisions directly amending tax sale certificate fees were struck prior to final passage.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires charter counties (including Baltimore City) and certain code counties to affirmatively further fair housing through their housing and urban development programs. Comprehensive plans enacted or amended on or after January 1, 2025, must include a fair housing assessment within the housing element, and relevant state departments must provide technical assistance upon request.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning, in consultation with the Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Charter counties, Baltimore City, code counties exercising land use powers, local planning commissions, and residents seeking fair and affordable housing.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be implemented with existing resources, with no effect on state revenues. The bill is not expected to have a direct, material fiscal impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 17 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP). The bill specifically mandates that MDP, in consultation with the Department of Housing and Community Development, provide technical assistance to charter counties upon request to help them develop the fair housing assessment in their comprehensive plans.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to consult with the Maryland Department of Planning in providing technical assistance to counties developing the housing element of their comprehensive plans. Furthermore, the bill references DHCD statutory definitions and builds upon state fair housing policies administered by DHCD.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes the common name of the northern snakehead as 'Chesapeake Channa' in Maryland law, renames the commercial fishing license to include Chesapeake Channa, and directs the Department of Natural Resources to adopt regulations and update all applicable published materials to reflect the new common name by January 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial fishers, seafood businesses, anglers, and consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not expected to change, as the Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill's provisions using existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal impact. Small businesses in the commercial fishing and seafood industry may experience a meaningful economic benefit if the rebranding improves marketing and increases harvesting and sales of northern snakeheads.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to adopt regulations establishing 'Chesapeake Channa' as the common name for the northern snakehead, update its commercial licensing references, and use the new name in all applicable materials published by the department.

The Department of Agriculture oversees the marketing of Maryland agricultural and seafood products. Renaming the invasive northern snakehead to 'Chesapeake Channa' is intended to promote consumer marketing and commercial harvesting within the state's seafood industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Highway Administration (SHA) to expand its pollinator habitat plan by including policies and procedures to encourage native plants, maintain roadside pollinator habitats while adhering to safety standards, and conduct public education. The bill also directs SHA to track, evaluate, and apply for relevant federal funding programs and update its published pollinator habitat plan annually starting October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists, bicyclists, pedestrians, community associations, the general public, and local pollinator populations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase minimally, estimated at $35,000 in fiscal 2025 for informational signs and public events, and are anticipated to remain under $50,000 annually. Federal fund revenues may potentially increase if SHA applies for and is awarded federal pollinator habitat grants. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the State Highway Administration to update its pollinator habitat plan to include specific policies, public outreach, and procedures for native plants and pollinator habitats along State highways, track and apply for federal funding, and annually update the plan and published habitat locations.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund is directly impacted to cover the costs of public communication, signage, and events associated with the pollinator habitat plan.

The bill amends the Agriculture Article concerning pollinator habitat plans, which are established in consultation with the Maryland Department of Agriculture and must be as protective as MDA's managed pollinator protection plan, while preserving MDA's weed control authorities.
DNR is one of the partner agencies codified under Section 2-1801 alongside SHA and MES that is required to establish and maintain a state pollinator habitat plan.
MES is codified alongside SHA and DNR under Section 2-1801 as one of the state entities subject to the pollinator habitat plan statute amended by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires all qualified health plans (QHPs) sold through the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to include essential pediatric dental benefits by repealing an exception that allowed health plans to exclude them when stand-alone dental plans were available on the exchange. It also repeals the Exchange's separate authority to require children enrolling in a QHP to obtain pediatric dental benefits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals, families, and children purchasing health coverage through the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, health insurance carriers offering plans on the Exchange, and small businesses purchasing plans via the SHOP Exchange.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not substantively change State activities or operations, and has no local fiscal impact. Carriers currently operating on the Exchange already voluntarily include pediatric dental benefits in their plans, resulting in minimal or no economic impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory requirements governing Qualified Health Plans (QHPs) certified and offered through the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, mandating the inclusion of pediatric dental benefits and repealing related Exchange authorities.

The bill is a departmental initiative requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration, which regulates health insurance carriers, approves plan forms and premium rates, and enforces compliance with State insurance standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the authorized uses of the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account (SMWOBA) within the Department of Commerce by allowing eligible fund managers to provide financial assistance in the form of grants up to $10,000 when issued in conjunction with a loan of any amount.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses, as well as eligible fund managers such as local economic development corporations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected; the Department of Commerce can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, and revenues into and expenditures from SMWOBA do not change. Local economic development entities serving as eligible fund managers may see altered expenditures and revenues beginning in FY 2025 due to grant issuance and foregone loan repayments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 26 is a departmental bill for the Department of Commerce, which administers the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account (SMWOBA). The bill alters program rules to allow eligible fund managers to award grants of up to $10,000 in conjunction with a loan.

The statute governs the SMWOBA fund, for which the Comptroller is statutorily tasked with maintaining accounting and issuing warrants to pay out funds upon approved transmittals from the Department of Commerce.
Statute designates the State Treasurer to invest and reinvest money held in the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account.

The statutory provisions amended and reenacted by the bill specify that eligible fund managers receiving SMWOBA funds and the utilization of funds allocated are subject to audit by the Legislative Auditor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Conforms Maryland health insurance laws and regulations with existing federal requirements, including consumer protections under the federal No Surprises Act regarding emergency services. The bill also revises the material errors that trigger special enrollment periods in the SHOP Exchange, authorizes the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to adopt expanded open enrollment periods, and updates regulatory reference dates for grandfathered plans, essential health benefits, and medical loss ratio standards.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, health care providers of emergency and behavioral health services, and insured individuals and small business employees purchasing qualified health plans.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Any changes in State activities resulting from the bill will not materially affect State finances. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 30 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration to align state insurance law with federal statutes, including the No Surprises Act. It requires the Insurance Commissioner to update and adopt regulations concerning grandfathered plans, essential health benefits, and medical loss ratios, while enforcing carrier compliance for emergency services.

The bill explicitly impacts MHBE operations by altering the material errors that trigger special enrollment periods within the SHOP Exchange and authorizing MHBE to adopt expanded open enrollment periods and alternate effective coverage dates.

The bill amends § 19-701 of the Health - General Article regarding definitions of emergency medical conditions and emergency services applicable to health maintenance organizations, and the department served as an information source for the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local building permit offices to include an estimated cost of construction when submitting copies of issued building permits to the county supervisor of assessments.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local building permit offices and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
qa_results.stakeholders: Local government permitting offices, county supervisors of assessments, property assessors, and property owners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not significantly affected. Local fiscal impact is minimal because many jurisdictions already collect or provide construction cost estimates as part of their standard permitting procedures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires local permit offices to provide estimated construction costs along with building permits to county supervisors of assessments to assist in real property valuation. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board directly hears appeals arising from the property assessments and valuations determined by these county supervisors of assessments.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest administrative review body adjudicating real property assessment appeals that originate from valuations made by county supervisors of assessments, though the bill does not impose direct administrative duties on the court.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the rescission period for public adjuster contracts from 3 to 10 business days and prohibits public adjusters from soliciting clients between 8:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. It requires public adjusters who enter into contracts within 72 hours of a property loss to notify the Maryland Insurance Commissioner within one business day, updates mandatory contract disclosures, and expands the prohibition against contractors fraudulently offering to pay an insured's deductible from only weather-related damages to damages caused by any loss-producing event.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners/insureds, public adjusters, home repair and remodeling contractors, and property and casualty insurance companies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on local government revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 36 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration. The bill establishes new regulatory requirements for public adjusters, alters contract terms and rescission windows, mandates that adjusters report certain contracts directly to the Insurance Commissioner, and expands definitions of fraudulent insurance acts under the Insurance Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City from adopting or enforcing local laws that require new motor vehicle off-street parking for developments that include residential use located within a 0.25-mile radius of an existing or planned MARC, MTA Light Rail, Metro, or Red Line transit station.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential property developers, small business builders, Baltimore City residents, and public transit users near transit stations in Baltimore City.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances. It may have a potentially meaningful impact on small businesses by reducing construction and development costs for residential projects located within 0.25 miles of specified transit stations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly references MTA mass transit assets—prohibiting Baltimore City from requiring off-street parking for residential developments within 0.25 miles of MARC, MTA Light Rail, Metro, and planned Red Line stations, which influences transit-oriented development and ridership surrounding MTA facilities.

MDOT oversees the state's multi-modal transportation network and transit-oriented development policies, and served as an official information source evaluating the impact of removing parking mandates around state mass transit stations.

The bill amends the state's Land Use Article to limit Baltimore City's municipal zoning authority regarding off-street parking near transit stations. MDP advises on land use planning, smart growth, and transit-oriented development, and served as an information source for the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to reimburse a residential service agency (RSA) for personal assistance services only if the services are provided by an individual classified as an employee rather than an independent contractor.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential service agencies (RSAs), personal care aides and homecare workers, and Medicaid participants receiving personal assistance services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct impact on Medicaid revenues or expenditures assuming RSAs transition fully to an employee staffing model by January 1, 2026. If RSAs fail to comply, MDH may experience an indeterminate operational cost beginning in fiscal 2026 to verify, disenroll, and revalidate providers. No local government fiscal impact. Participating small business RSAs may incur meaningful costs to convert independent contractors to employees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Maryland Department of Health by restricting Medicaid reimbursements to residential service agencies for personal assistance services only to those provided by individuals classified as employees.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the enforcement of state labor laws, workplace protections, and worker misclassification standards, which are directly related to requiring residential service agencies to classify personal care aides as employees.

qa_results.bill_summary: This departmental legislation aligns Maryland law with federal law by repealing the exemption allowing active-duty military personnel under age 21 to purchase tobacco products and electronic smoking devices. It also authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to reallocate projected unspent local public health cancer grant funds between counties during the fiscal year, transfers the payment responsibility for abused or neglected children's emergency medical care to the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, repeals the requirement for an annual expert panel on child abuse and neglect, and eliminates duplicative tobacco reporting mandates.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
qa_results.stakeholders: Active-duty military personnel aged 18 to 20, tobacco and electronic smoking device retailers, county health departments, and abused or neglected children receiving emergency medical services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected, as transferring emergency medical payments aligns statute with current practice and grant funds are already budgeted. Local government revenues and expenditures may be impacted to the extent that the Maryland Department of Health reallocates projected unspent cancer grant funds from one county to another mid-year instead of allowing them to revert to the Cigarette Restitution Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This was a departmental bill requested by MDH. It authorizes MDH to reallocate projected unspent Local Public Health Cancer Grant funding between counties, repeals the requirement for the Secretary of Health to convene an expert panel on child abuse and neglect, removes MDH's role as payor of last resort for child abuse emergency medical treatment, and repeals duplicative tobacco counter-marketing reporting requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally transfers statutory responsibility and regulatory authority to GOCPP as the payor of last resort for emergency medical treatment charges incurred on behalf of abused or neglected children.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory responsibilities and reporting mandates of the State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect (SCCAN), requiring it to coordinate with the Maryland CHAMP Initiative and report on child abuse diagnosis and treatment data.

The bill amends provisions in the Family Law Article concerning child abuse and neglect medical examinations, which involve local departments of social services under DHS determining medical assistance eligibility.
The bill touches statutory provisions where MDH consults and collaborates with the Office of the Comptroller regarding enforcement strategies for laws prohibiting tobacco distribution to minors.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes county and municipal governments to designate local highways with maximum speed limits of up to 30 miles per hour (or up to 35 miles per hour in Golden Beach Patuxent Knolls) where individuals with a valid driver's license may operate an unregistered golf cart equipped with required lighting devices, replacing several localized statutory authorizations with a uniform statewide framework.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA)
qa_results.stakeholders: Golf cart owners and drivers, motorists, and county and municipal governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations, according to the Department of Legislative Services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) administers vehicle registration exemptions under the Maryland Vehicle Law and is responsible for establishing requirements and approvals for lighting devices on golf carts operating on public highways.

As the parent department overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration and statewide transportation policy and statutes, MDOT is directly impacted by amendments to the Maryland Vehicle Law concerning highway vehicle operations and registration exemptions.

The Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing motor vehicle laws and traffic safety regulations across the state, including equipment, licensing, and operational requirements for vehicles on roadways.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the sale, barter, or exchange of legally acquired mounted specimens of game birds (excluding migratory game birds) and game mammals if the original owner is deceased and the specimen is personal property being liquidated or distributed as part of the decedent's estate.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Personal representatives, heirs, and legatees administering decedents' estates; estate auctioneers; and buyers or collectors of taxidermy mounted specimens.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 45 was introduced as departmental legislation by the Department of Natural Resources. It amends the Natural Resources Article to create an exception allowing the sale, barter, or exchange of legally acquired mounted specimens of game birds or mammals from a deceased individual's estate under DNR's wildlife regulatory framework.

The Register of Wills oversees the administration and probate of decedents' estates and personal property. The bill directly affects estate liquidation and distribution powers regarding mounted specimens held as personal property of a decedent.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission to oversee competitive grant awards from the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund and alters the fund's authorized uses to focus solely on pediatric cancer research, removing prevention and treatment. It also permits up to 5% of the fund to be used for administrative expenses and a promotional account allocated to a State-based childhood cancer organization to promote donations and educate the scientific community.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Pediatric cancer researchers, healthcare providers, academic institutions, hospitals, pediatric cancer patients and their families, and childhood cancer advocacy organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $52,900 in FY 2025 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire a part-time (0.25) physician program manager to support the commission, increasing to $69,000 by FY 2029. Up to 5% of the fund may be used for administration and promotional activities. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Health administers the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund, provides staff and administrative support for the fund and the commission, adopts implementing regulations, submits annual reports to the General Assembly, and serves (or designates an individual to serve) on the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission to oversee competitive research grants from the fund, establish evaluation guidelines, and conduct progress reviews.

The bill specifically mandates that each member of the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission disclose to the State Ethics Commission whether they are employed by or hold a financial interest in an entity that may apply for grant funds.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the non-designee members of the newly established Pediatric Cancer Research Commission and holds statutory authority to remove members for specified causes.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees to the newly established commission.

The bill specifies membership seats on the Commission for scientists and physicians with expertise in pediatric cancer from the University of Maryland, and university researchers are eligible grant applicants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Provides paid parental bereavement leave to all State employees across the Executive, Judicial, and Legislative branches, including temporary employees, independent personnel systems, and public institutions of higher education. Qualified employees may take up to 10 days of paid leave within 60 days following the death of a child aged 6 months to under 27 years, or up to 60 days of paid leave within 60 days following a stillbirth or the death of an infant under 6 months old, without being required to use other available paid leave.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: State government employees (including temporary staff and employees of public institutions of higher education) who experience a stillbirth or the death of an infant or child under the age of 27.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially impact State operations or finances because employee salaries are already budgeted and temporary replacements are not typically hired. State agency expenditures may increase minimally in limited situations where overtime coverage is necessary. An estimated fewer than 90 employees will qualify annually. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the principal personnel agency for the State of Maryland overseeing the State Personnel Management System, DBM's Secretary is directly mandated by the bill to adopt regulations governing the implementation of parental bereavement leave.

The bill explicitly applies to all employees of public institutions of higher education, requiring USM to incorporate paid parental bereavement leave policies and adjust independent human resources and payroll systems.

The bill applies to all employees in the Judicial Branch of state government, requiring the Administrative Office of the Courts to update its independent personnel system policies to provide paid parental bereavement leave.

MDOT operates an independent personnel system covering its modal administrations and must update its internal leave rules and human resources systems to comply with the mandated parental bereavement leave.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts residential property transfers from an estate to an heir or legatee, or land transfers where the grantee assumes the grantor's property tax obligations, from the requirement that all property taxes be paid prior to transfer if a payment plan is entered into. The bill also requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to contract with a vendor to run an installment payment program for homeowners to pay taxes in advance, currently due, or in arrears, and authorizes local governments to establish their own installment payment programs for residential taxes in arrears.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman (within the State Department of Assessments and Taxation)
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners, heirs and legatees inheriting residential property, grantees assuming property tax obligations, and local tax collection authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $67,271 in FY 2025 (increasing to at least $89,900 by FY 2029) to hire a program manager within the State Tax Sale Ombudsman's Office, with additional general fund support potentially required for vendor contract costs. State revenues are not materially affected beyond potential shifts in collection timing. Local government revenues are not materially affected overall, but local expenditures and penalty/interest revenues may change if jurisdictions adopt their own installment payment programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly affects land recordation procedures carried out by the Clerks of the Circuit Court, which are supported administratively, technologically, and operationally by the Administrative Office of the Courts. Circuit Court clerks must accept an affidavit of a property tax payment plan to record property transfer instruments to heirs, legatees, or assuming grantees without requiring full prepayment of property taxes.

The bill facilitates the transfer of residential real property from a decedent's estate to an heir or legatee by permitting the transfer even if property taxes are in arrears, as long as a payment plan is established. This directly impacts estate administration and probate proceedings overseen by the Register of Wills.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Commission on Veterans and Military Families to study and develop recommendations for a statewide strategic plan and key performance indicators to improve the quality of life for veterans and military families in Maryland, requiring a final report by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland veterans, military families, military spouses, and service members
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $74,237 ($74,200 rounded) in FY 2025 only for the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs to hire one temporary contractual administrative officer to staff the commission and complete the report. Expense reimbursements for members are minimal and absorbable within existing resources. There is no effect on State revenues and no material impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Veterans Affairs (or designee) serves as the chair of the newly created Commission on Veterans and Military Families, and the department is responsible for staffing the Commission, resulting in a direct general fund expenditure impact of $74,237 in FY 2025.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the temporary Maryland Commission on Veterans and Military Families to study and recommend a statewide strategic plan and performance indicators for veterans and military families.
The Adjutant General, or their designee, is designated by statute as a mandatory member of the newly formed Commission on Veterans and Military Families.
The bill explicitly requires the Commission to consult with the Office of Military and Federal Affairs and the Maryland Military Installation Council, both situated within the Department of Commerce.
The Governor is responsible for appointing five members of the Commission and will receive the Commission's final study, findings, and recommendations report by December 1, 2024.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees, which includes the five members appointed by the Governor to this Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the statutory definition of "disability" relating to eligibility for rehabilitation services in Maryland to mean any physical or mental impairment that constitutes or results in a substantial impediment to employment or independent living, aligning the term with federal rehabilitation law.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (Division of Rehabilitation Services)
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with physical or mental impairments seeking vocational rehabilitation, employment placement, or independent living services in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. Updating the definition to align with federal standards is not anticipated to affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 60 directly amends the Education Article regarding the definition of 'disability' for rehabilitation services administered by the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), an operating unit within the Maryland State Department of Education.

As the principal agency coordinating disability policy and services across state government, the Department of Disabilities is impacted by statutory modernization of definitions affecting employment and independent living services for individuals with disabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the time limit for an equal employment officer to investigate and the head of a principal unit to issue a written decision on discrimination or harassment complaints filed by State employees or job applicants from 30 days to 60 days, and allows an additional 30-day extension if the complainant provides written authorization.
qa_results.responsible_party: Heads of principal State units, Fair Practices Officers, and Equal Employment Officers (with oversight by the Department of Budget and Management)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland State Executive Branch employees and job applicants filing harassment or discrimination complaints, as well as State equal employment and fair practices personnel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The changes are procedural in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM serves as the State's central personnel agency overseeing State personnel policies, employee rights, and equal employment opportunity regulations. Appeals of decisions regarding these discrimination and harassment complaints are made directly to the Secretary of Budget and Management.

The Commission on Civil Rights enforces Maryland's employment anti-discrimination and anti-harassment laws, including the underlying standards in Title 20 of the State Government Article referenced by the complaint procedures in this bill.

MDOT operates a large personnel system within the Executive Branch whose equal employment and fair practices officers investigate employee discrimination and harassment complaints subject to the extended procedural timelines.

USM is a major public employer in the state whose employee relations and equal employment practices are directly informed by state statutory timelines for workplace harassment and discrimination complaints.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the eligibility for an optional local property tax credit on the dwelling house of disabled veterans to include individuals with a nonpermanent, service-connected disability rating of 100% from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, provided they do not qualify for an existing complete property tax exemption. It also permits counties and municipalities to enact local laws restricting eligibility to veterans with permanent disabilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: The governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations (including Baltimore City)
qa_results.stakeholders: Honorably discharged veterans with a 100% nonpermanent service-connected disability rating, surviving spouses of eligible disabled veterans, and local county and municipal governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues for counties and municipalities may decrease beginning in FY 2025 to the extent jurisdictions offer the credit and expand eligibility to veterans with 100% nonpermanent service-connected disabilities. However, because local governments may choose to limit eligibility to existing permanent disability criteria, any revenue reduction depends on local adoption; specific dollar estimates are unavailable. Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands eligibility for property tax credits for disabled veterans with nonpermanent service-connected disabilities. As the state agency tasked with advocating for Maryland veterans and helping them access benefits and housing resources, this change directly aligns with their mission and outreach efforts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to enact local property tax credits for residential property owned as the primary dwelling by a public school employee, apartment or condominium buildings where the owner made health or safety improvements on or after July 1, 2024, and apartment or condominium buildings used on or after July 1, 2024, for local housing programs for homeless individuals or families.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school employees who own residential property, owners of apartment and condominium buildings, homeless individuals and families participating in local housing programs, and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None. Local Effect: Potential significant decrease in local property tax revenues beginning in FY 2025 to the extent local jurisdictions authorize and grant the credits; local expenditures are not directly affected. As an illustrative example, granting a $2,500 credit to 10% of public school employees statewide would decrease local property tax revenues by $31.25 million annually.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes local jurisdictions to establish a property tax credit for employees of local public school systems, an incentive that directly impacts public school personnel overseen and tracked by the Maryland State Department of Education.

The bill authorizes local property tax credits for buildings where health and safety improvements are made and for properties used for local housing programs for homeless individuals and families, which intersects with DHCD's mission regarding housing standards and homeless solutions.
The PTAAB has jurisdiction to hear appeals and resolve disputes regarding property tax credits and exemptions, which may arise if local jurisdictions adopt the authorized property tax credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum civil penalties that the Maryland Insurance Commissioner may impose on unauthorized insurers from $50,000 to $125,000 per violation, and increases the maximum civil penalty on licensed insurance producers and public adjusters from $500 to $5,000 per violation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration (Insurance Commissioner)
qa_results.stakeholders: Unauthorized insurers, licensed insurance producers, public adjusters, and Maryland insurance consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase, likely minimally, starting in FY 2025 to the extent that the Maryland Insurance Administration assesses higher penalties under the bill. State expenditures are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration, this legislation directly empowers the Insurance Commissioner to assess increased maximum civil penalties on unauthorized insurers, insurance producers, and public adjusters who violate state insurance law.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases transparency and reporting requirements for continuing care retirement communities (CCRCs). It requires providers to publish disclosure statements on their websites, hold quarterly meetings with subscribers, present annual summaries of internal grievances, and allow subscriber governing body members to report nonconfidential information. It also mandates that providers issue status reports to former subscribers or beneficiaries when entrance fee refunds depend on reoccupying units that remain vacant after nine months, and requires the Maryland Department of Aging to collect grievance data and report annually to the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: Continuing care retirement community (CCRC) providers, CCRC subscribers and residents, and subscribers' beneficiaries and estates.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Aging (MDoA) is the primary regulatory agency overseeing continuing care retirement communities (CCRCs) under Title 10 of the Human Services Article. The bill directly requires MDoA to annually collect data on internal grievances from CCRC providers and report these findings to the Senate Finance Committee and House Health and Government Operations Committee by December 1 each year.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the Teacher Development and Retention Program by expanding eligibility to include students initially enrolled at any Maryland community college, delaying the stipend award periods and program termination date by one year (to June 30, 2030), authorizing the Teacher Development and Retention Fund to cover administrative expenses, and requiring the Maryland Higher Education Commission to conduct the program evaluation internally rather than contracting an independent consultant.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Community college students, teacher preparation candidates, Maryland public school systems, and high-needs schools facing teacher shortages.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures decrease by an estimated total of $1.0 million through FY 2029 by removing the requirement to hire an independent consultant for the program evaluation. Program stipend disbursements are delayed by one year, supported by $10.0 million in general funds previously appropriated in FY 2024 to capitalize the special fund. The bill has no effect on State revenues and no direct fiscal impact on local community colleges or local school systems.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC (through its Office of Student Financial Assistance) is the primary administering agency for the Teacher Development and Retention Program and the associated special fund. The bill expands program eligibility to community college students, delays stipend award cycles and program termination, authorizes the fund to be used for administrative expenses, and requires MHEC to directly conduct the program evaluation rather than hiring an external consultant.

Duplicate listing for the Maryland Higher Education Commission, which is the primary agency responsible for administering the Teacher Development and Retention Program, managing the fund, establishing eligibility, and conducting the required program evaluation.

MSDE partners with MHEC by identifying the high-needs schools, grade levels, and content areas with teacher shortages that define participant service obligations, and previously coordinated funding transfers for the program.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Teacher Development and Retention Fund.
The State Treasurer is responsible for holding and investing the moneys in the Teacher Development and Retention Fund.
The Governor's Office receives the final evaluation report on the effectiveness of the program by January 1, 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Permanently authorizes licensed pharmacists who meet specific training and certification requirements to order and administer influenza, COVID-19, and public health emergency vaccines to individuals as young as 3 years old, administer FDA-approved or ACIP-recommended vaccines to individuals at least 7 years old, and administer travel vaccines to adults.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, pharmacies, children age 3 and older, adult vaccine recipients, pediatric healthcare providers, and parents or caregivers of minors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It is anticipated to have a meaningful economic impact on small business pharmacies due to the permanent expansion of vaccine administration capabilities, alongside a potential offsetting decrease in vaccinations administered by other health care providers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) regulates health occupations and professionals, including the State Board of Pharmacy, the Board of Physicians, and the Board of Nursing. The bill requires MDH, in consultation with these boards, to establish vaccine administration protocol criteria in regulations, oversees pharmacy vaccination reporting to MDH's ImmuNet Program, and sets standards for pharmacist-administered vaccinations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates the governance and administrative operations of the Maryland Environmental Service (MES). It broadens the definition of "municipality" to include federal entities and the District of Columbia, allows the Board Secretary to delegate duties to an employee serving as Deputy Secretary, authorizes MES to issue initial project proposals instead of immediate proposed contracts, establishes that MES is not obligated to perform services prior to contract execution, aligns annual audit and reporting deadlines to November 15, and repeals the requirement for an additional audit on unauthorized spending and accounting errors.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Environmental Service (MES)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Environmental Service, Board of Directors and employees, as well as municipal, State, federal, and D.C. public entities that contract with MES for environmental and infrastructure services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. MES will experience modest administrative efficiencies through streamlined contracting processes, reporting deadlines, and secretarial delegation. Repealing the requirement for a separate audit on unauthorized spending could yield minimal cost savings if that audit was previously intended to be recurring (a prior audit cost $10,000 in 2022).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 78 directly governs the Maryland Environmental Service (MES), altering its internal board delegation powers, contract and proposal procedures, and statutory audit and annual reporting deadlines and requirements.
MES is statutorily required to provide a copy of its annual independent financial audit and any board recommendations to the Department of Budget and Management under the updated deadlines.
The bill updates the statutory deadline and content requirements for the annual report that MES must submit to the Governor regarding its activities and financial audit.

qa_results.bill_summary: Known as Lochlin's Law, this bill requires hospitals and urgent care centers in Maryland to implement evidence-based protocols consistent with CDC guidelines for the early identification and treatment of sepsis, severe sepsis, and septic shock by January 1, 2025. It also requires periodic staff training on the protocols and requires specialty psychiatric hospitals to establish screening, recognition, and transfer procedures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients seeking treatment at hospitals and urgent care centers in Maryland (especially adults and children at risk of sepsis), as well as clinical, laboratory, and pharmacy staff at these facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can oversee protocol implementation using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds provisions to the Health - General Article requiring hospitals and urgent care centers to implement sepsis protocols and provide them to the Department upon request. The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) regulates these healthcare facilities and also directly operates state specialty psychiatric hospitals that must comply with screening and transfer procedures under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 86 requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), in consultation with county boards of education, to establish a policy authorizing school nurses and designated school personnel to administer bronchodilators to students perceived to be experiencing asthma-related symptoms or respiratory distress. The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is required to identify or develop training on recognizing and distinguishing symptoms of asthma, respiratory distress, and anaphylaxis. The bill mandates public schools to store bronchodilators and delivery devices (such as inhalers with spacers) for emergency use, permits nonpublic schools to adopt similar policies, and grants civil immunity for good-faith emergency administration.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public and nonpublic school students (particularly those with asthma or respiratory conditions), parents and guardians, school nurses, designated school staff and teachers, local boards of education, and local health departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $32,200 in FY 2025 for MDH to hire a contractual nurse consultant to assist in developing the bronchodilator policy; MSDE can implement its training and reporting duties with existing resources. Local expenditures increase for local school systems and local health departments to provide paid staff training (estimated at $22 to $55 per hour) and to purchase and maintain emergency stock bronchodilators and spacers (county school system estimates range from $8,500 to $40,000 annually), which may be mitigated by donations or grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 86 requires the Maryland Department of Health, in consultation with county boards of education, to establish a policy for public schools authorizing the emergency administration of bronchodilators to students. The bill results in a direct fiscal impact on MDH ($32,208 in FY 2025) to hire contractual staff to develop the policy.

The bill mandates that the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), in consultation with MDH and specific organizations, identify or develop paid professional development training for school personnel, create and disseminate standard reporting forms, and collect data on school bronchodilator administrations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Provides immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for an individual serving as the State Superintendent of Schools upon taking office.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: The State Superintendent of Schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Because the bill applies to only one State Retirement and Pension System member at a time, it has no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates, and no effect on revenues. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill was submitted on behalf of the Department of Education to grant immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System to the State Superintendent of Schools, who leads the department.

The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System and is responsible for implementing vesting schedules and tracking retirement benefits for members, including the State Superintendent of Schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to allow business entities that qualify as small employers to be represented by authorized individuals, such as officers, partners, members, or designated employees, instead of an attorney during certain hearings held by or on behalf of the Maryland Insurance Administration.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner and the Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Small employers (corporations, partnerships, LLCs, and sole proprietorships with an average of 50 or fewer employees) involved in Maryland Insurance Administration hearings, their authorized representatives, and insurers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances and has no local fiscal impact. It is expected to have a meaningful economic benefit for small businesses by reducing the legal costs of hiring counsel to pursue claims before the Maryland Insurance Administration.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 90 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) amending the Insurance Article. It directly impacts MIA administrative hearing procedures by requiring the Insurance Commissioner to allow qualifying small employer business entities to be represented by designated non-attorney representatives rather than legal counsel.

The Office of Administrative Hearings conducts contested case hearings on behalf of state agencies, including the Maryland Insurance Administration. The bill's provisions allowing designated non-attorneys to represent small employer business entities apply to administrative hearings held on behalf of MIA.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Resources and Education for All Prisons (REAP) Act requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to help incarcerated individuals access federal Pell Grants for higher education by consulting with specified colleges and universities. Additionally, the department must set participation goals, establish tracking systems to monitor postsecondary enrollment and credits earned by incarcerated individuals, forward progress data to the Maryland Higher Education Commission, and adopt related regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals in Maryland correctional facilities, public and private higher education institutions, the Maryland Higher Education Commission, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies—including the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, the Maryland Higher Education Commission, and public universities—along with local community colleges, can implement the bill using existing resources. The bill directs the Governor to include sufficient funds in the annual budget for marketing and tracking systems; however, because it lacks a specific dollar amount or formula, it does not create a mandated appropriation, making any future funding discretionary. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including assisting incarcerated individuals with accessing federal Pell Grants, setting postsecondary education goals, creating tracking systems, forwarding data, and adopting regulations.
MHEC is statutorily mandated to assist DPSCS in establishing tracking systems for incarcerated individuals in postsecondary programs and to receive tracking data on college credits earned.
MHEC is statutorily mandated to assist DPSCS in establishing tracking systems for incarcerated individuals in postsecondary programs and to receive tracking data on college credits earned.
All USM institutions are specifically designated by the bill for consultation by DPSCS to assist incarcerated individuals in accessing federal Pell Grants for postsecondary education.
Morgan State University is explicitly enumerated in the bill as an institution of higher education that DPSCS must consult with to help incarcerated individuals access federal Pell Grants.
The bill directs the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual state budget bill to fund DPSCS marketing for postsecondary education programs and tracking systems.

DBM oversees the state budget development process and would be involved in administering any discretionary or mandated funding included in the annual budget bill for the program's marketing and tracking systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 93 expands the statutory circumstances under which a residential tenant's liability for rent is limited to no more than two months after vacating the premises. It allows early lease termination if a tenant or authorized occupant has a mental disorder that makes continued habitation unfeasible or unsustainable or requires relocation to obtain a higher level of care, and authorizes licensed psychologists, in addition to licensed physicians, to provide the required written medical certification.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants with qualifying mental health conditions, residential landlords, licensed physicians, and licensed psychologists.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances, and any effect on small business landlords is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory conditions under Maryland's landlord-tenant law regarding early lease termination and rent liability for medical reasons, which affects civil actions and breach of lease claims adjudicated within the Maryland District Court system.

The bill references statutory definitions of mental disorders under the Health - General Article and expands the authority to issue medical certifications for lease termination to licensed psychologists and healthcare providers regulated by boards housed within MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the statutory authority of the Division of Correction to arrange for the employment of inmates in agricultural work at specified correctional camps.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Correction, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Inmates in correctional camps in Queen Anne’s County and other applicable counties, as well as agricultural employers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to have a material impact on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 94 directly repeals the authority and requirement of the Division of Correction, a unit within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, to arrange for the employment of inmates in agricultural work at designated camps.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to implement newborn screening for any core condition added to the federal Recommended Uniform Screening Panel within 18 months of its addition, repealing the previous approval process by the Secretary of Health and the State Advisory Council on Hereditary and Congenital Disorders. It also requires the Department to implement newborn testing for infantile Krabbe disease within one year after the federal government issues a final recommendation to add it to the panel, subject to reporting requirements in case of procurement delays.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Newborn infants, parents and caregivers, healthcare providers, and the Maryland Medicaid program.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill potentially significantly increases special fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health's Laboratories Administration to screen for additional conditions starting as early as FY 2026. For infantile Krabbe disease, costs are estimated at $850,000 for one-time equipment and $750,000 annually for maintenance, supplies, and staffing. Special fund revenues from newborn screening fees (currently $106 per infant) will increase correspondingly to cover these costs. Medicaid expenditures (50% general funds, 50% federal funds) and federal fund revenues will also increase to cover fee increases for the approximately 50% of Maryland births covered by Medicaid. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency responsible for the Newborn Screening Program, operating the state public health laboratory that conducts the screenings, implementing tests for new RUSP conditions and infantile Krabbe disease, and administering Medicaid, which covers newborn screening fees for about half of all Maryland births.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the role of the State Advisory Council on Hereditary and Congenital Disorders by repealing its requirement to approve core conditions added to the federal Recommended Uniform Screening Panel, while authorizing MDH to screen for conditions recommended by the Advisory Council.
The statute specifies that all fees collected under the newborn screening subtitle are paid to the Comptroller, who must distribute them to the Newborn Screening Program Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Known as Rudy's Law, this bill prohibits selling baby food containing toxic heavy metals that exceed FDA limits starting January 1, 2025. It requires baby food manufacturers to test representative samples of products at least monthly through an accredited laboratory and provide results to the Maryland Department of Health upon request. Beginning January 1, 2026, manufacturers must publish test results and FDA information on their websites and include a QR code on product labels directing consumers to these results.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Infants and children under age two, parents and consumers, and baby food manufacturers, processors, and retailers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $27,700 in FY 2025 and between $25,500 and $28,600 annually thereafter for the Maryland Department of Health to hire a part-time contractual administrative specialist to review heavy metal test results, ensure compliance, and handle consumer reports. State revenues are unaffected. Local expenditures may minimally increase if local health departments conduct additional inspections.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) with requesting and receiving laboratory test results for toxic heavy metals from baby food manufacturers and handling consumer reports regarding non-compliant products. MDH incurs general fund expenditures for personnel to oversee compliance and investigate complaints.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the existing felony crime of sexual solicitation of a minor to prohibit soliciting a minor, a law enforcement officer posing as a minor, or the consent of a parent or guardian of a minor, with the intent to produce or distribute child pornography.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, the Judiciary, and State law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Minors, parents and guardians, law enforcement officers posing as minors, and individuals charged with child pornography or sexual solicitation offenses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations. State incarceration expenditures and workloads for the Judiciary and the Office of the Public Defender are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for the incarceration and supervision of individuals convicted of state felony offenses. The bill expands the felony offense of sexual solicitation of a minor to include intent to produce or distribute child pornography, directly impacting potential correctional facility admissions and terms of confinement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent individuals facing criminal charges where incarceration is a possibility. The expansion of felony criminal offenses under § 3-324 may result in an increase in caseloads and legal defense operations for public defenders.

The Judiciary manages the adjudication of criminal felony charges in state courts. Expanding the statutory definition of sexual solicitation of a minor impacts trial court proceedings, filings, and judicial caseloads.
