MSP is the primary state law enforcement agency responsible for investigating criminal violations and child sexual exploitation, including operations where undercover law enforcement officers pose as minors or guardians.
The OAG represents the State of Maryland in criminal appeals resulting from felony convictions under state criminal statutes and provides legal counsel on criminal law matters.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a rear passenger on a motorcycle to be able to firmly position their feet on the footrests while seated, except for passengers unable to do so due to a permanent physical disability.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police and the Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorcycle drivers and motorcycle passengers, particularly young children or individuals of shorter stature who may be unable to reach footrests
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from fines imposed in the District Court for violations (misdemeanor subject to a fine up to $500). State enforcement and court caseloads can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. No material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is responsible for driver licensing and vehicle regulation, and it must assess points against the driver's license of any motorcycle operator or passenger who violates state motorcycle passenger restrictions.

The bill amends the Maryland Transportation Article regarding motorcycle passenger safety regulations, directly falling under MDOT's overarching jurisdiction over state transportation rules and safety administration.
The Maryland State Police is the primary statewide traffic law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing motor vehicle laws, including citing violations of motorcycle passenger restrictions.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the District Court, which will process citations, manage any contested cases, and collect fine revenues resulting from violations of the new passenger restriction.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct a feasibility study on including coverage for removable full and partial dentures and per-patient provider reimbursements for house calls and extended care facility visits under the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program, as well as setting reimbursement rates at specified benchmark levels.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Dental care providers, low-income Marylanders enrolled in the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program/Medicaid, and residents of extended care facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can complete the required study and submit the report by December 1, 2024, using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct a feasibility study on expanding dental services and setting reimbursement rates under the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program, consult with relevant stakeholders, and submit a report to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes individuals who received a probation before judgment (PBJ) for driving while impaired or under the influence to petition for record expungement after a 15-year waiting period, expands mandatory participation in the Ignition Interlock System Program (IISP) to drivers granted PBJ for driving under the influence or convicted of/granted PBJ for driving while impaired, defines the start of program participation as the date of device installation, and establishes annual reporting requirements for the Motor Vehicle Administration.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration and the Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Drivers charged with, convicted of, or granted probation before judgment for alcohol-related driving offenses; ignition interlock system service providers; state and local courts; and law enforcement agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues increase by $279,900 in FY 2025 and approximately $373,200 annually thereafter from ignition interlock participation and licensing fees. State general fund expenditures increase by up to $997,600 in FY 2025 and reach $1,315,000 by FY 2029 for the Judiciary to hire up to 17 clerks to process expungement petitions, with potential additional indeterminate administrative costs for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services. Local expenditures may increase minimally for local law enforcement and record custodians to process expungement orders.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that MVA expand the Ignition Interlock System Program (IISP) to individuals granted probation before judgment for certain impaired driving offenses, adjust program start rules, collect program data, and report annually to the Governor and the General Assembly.

The bill allows expungement of certain probation before judgment records for drunk driving offenses after 15 years, requiring District and circuit courts to process petitions and causing significant fiscal expenditure for additional court personnel.
As the parent department of the MVA, MDOT experiences an increase in Transportation Trust Fund revenues from additional IISP participation and interlock-restricted driver's license fees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) within DPSCS is responsible for processing court-ordered expungements of criminal history records, which will see increased volume under the bill.
OAH adjudicates administrative appeals regarding driver's license suspensions, revocations, and ignition interlock referrals resulting from MVA actions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent clients who may seek expungements of qualifying driving offenses or require counsel in proceedings involving probation before judgment and interlock requirements.
MSP is a primary law enforcement repository that must comply with court-ordered expungements of police arrest and investigation records.
The bill requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to submit an annual report regarding IISP participation and recidivism statistics to the Governor beginning December 1, 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases annual compensation for nonstudent members of the Baltimore County Board of Education from $7,500 to $16,500, sets the board chair's compensation at $17,500, and increases the higher education scholarship awarded to a student member completing a full term from $7,500 to $10,000, effective with future terms of office.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and student members of the Baltimore County Board of Education, Baltimore County Public Schools, and Baltimore County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Baltimore County expenditures increase by $39,250 in FY 2027, $65,500 in FY 2028, $87,100 in FY 2029, and $102,500 annually by FY 2030 as higher compensation and scholarship rates take effect across successive terms. County revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education provides oversight and leadership for Maryland's 24 public school systems, including the Baltimore County public school system. While the bill only adjusts local board compensation and student scholarships funded by the county with no state fiscal impact, it directly concerns the governance structure of a local school system under MSDE's policy purview.

qa_results.bill_summary: This departmental bill modifies the regulations regarding the alteration or removal of submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) in Maryland tidal waters. It reduces the allowable width of cleared access corridors for property owners, marinas, and utilities from 60 feet to 20 feet, limits allowable actions for piers and marinas to trimming or cutting rather than full eradication, expands regulations across all tidal waters in the State, and mandates that individuals notify the Department of Natural Resources and use best harvesting methods prior to cutting or trimming SAV.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and renters of docks, piers, ramps, and marinas on tidal waters, public utility and telecommunications companies, and recreational boaters.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations. The Department of Natural Resources can administer the bill's notification and plan requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 109 is a departmental bill sponsored at the request of the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). DNR is the primary agency responsible for administering submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) regulations, receiving required notifications and alteration plans, providing best harvesting methods, and adopting implementing regulations.

The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) regulates tidal wetlands, dredging, filling, and shoreline alterations through its Wetlands and Waterways Program. The bill clarifies the statutory distinction between SAV trimming/removal overseen by DNR and activities under MDE's regulatory jurisdiction.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers and consolidates beneficial ownership disclosure requirements for businesses contracting with state and local governments by repealing filings with the Secretary of State and requiring registration statements disclosing beneficial ownership to be submitted to the State Board of Elections within 15 business days of contract award, alongside corresponding campaign contribution disclosures and certifications.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Businesses entering contracts of $200,000 or more with Maryland state or local government entities, the Maryland State Board of Elections, the Secretary of State, and the Board of Public Works.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Affected state agencies can implement the administrative changes within existing budgeted resources. Special fund revenues to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund may increase minimally beginning in FY 2025 from late filing fees ($20 to $50 per day, up to $1,000) or civil penalties (up to $1,000). The bill has no material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections (SBE) is the primary regulatory and enforcement body under the bill. SBE is required to receive registration statements and beneficial ownership disclosures from persons doing public business, adopt regulations regarding updates to beneficial ownership, administer filing timelines, and assess late filing fees and civil penalties.

This was a departmental bill requested by the Secretary of State to streamline public business reporting. The bill repeals Section 13-221 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, removing the requirement that businesses holding State contracts submit beneficial ownership disclosures to the Secretary of State.

The bill explicitly requires that if a contract awarded to a person doing public business is subject to Board of Public Works approval, the awarding governmental entity must require the contractor to certify to the Board of Public Works that they have filed the required statement of political contributions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits an adult supervising a minor from allowing the minor to ride a horse, donkey, mule, or pony on a highway, public riding path, or equestrian facility grounds unless the minor wears an ASTM-compliant protective helmet, subject to specific exceptions for agriculture, highway crossings between private land, Amish and Mennonite communities, and certain medical therapy services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Minors who ride horses, supervising adults and parents, equestrian facilities and riding schools, and law enforcement agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from fines up to $500 per violation. State expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health may decrease if traumatic head injuries are prevented, reducing Medicaid and Developmental Disabilities Administration costs. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 21 of the Transportation Article (Maryland Vehicle Law) regarding rules of the road and equestrian safety on highways and public thoroughfares under the jurisdiction of the Maryland Department of Transportation.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing the Maryland Vehicle Law on highways, the Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing this new violation and issuing citations when adults fail to ensure minors wear required protective headgear.

The bill applies to public horse-riding paths and trails, many of which are situated on public lands, forests, and state parks managed by the Department of Natural Resources and patrolled by the Natural Resources Police.

The fiscal note identifies potential expenditure savings for the Maryland Department of Health through reduced Medicaid and Developmental Disabilities Administration costs resulting from a decrease in traumatic brain injuries from equestrian accidents.

Violations of the helmet requirement are subject to a civil or traffic fine of up to $500 under the Maryland Vehicle Law, which is processed and adjudicated through the state court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees the statewide emergency medical system and maintains the Maryland State Trauma Registry, which tracks equestrian-related head injuries and fall data analyzed in the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a commitment unit to include the telephone number of the Maryland Crime Victims Resource Center in required notifications provided to a victim, victim's representative, or witness when a sentenced defendant or child respondent is released from confinement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commitment units (including the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of Juvenile Services, and local detention centers)
qa_results.stakeholders: Crime victims, victims' representatives, and witnesses to crimes of violence
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS operates state correctional and confinement facilities that serve as commitment units for sentenced defendants. Under the bill, DPSCS must include the telephone number of the Maryland Crime Victims Resource Center when providing required release notifications to victims, their representatives, or witnesses.

DJS operates facilities and holds custody of child respondents as a commitment unit. The bill mandates that DJS include the telephone number of the Maryland Crime Victims Resource Center in release notifications sent to victims, representatives, or witnesses when a child respondent is released from confinement.
AOC manages the state judicial system and court case management processes, including the transmission and tracking of victim notification request forms and court commitment orders.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Geological Survey Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund within the Department of Natural Resources to finance operating and administrative costs of the Maryland Geological Survey, including long-term project budgeting, equipment purchases, and procurements, and allows the fund to retain its interest earnings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: The Maryland Geological Survey, Department of Natural Resources staff, and clients of the Survey such as local governments, nonprofits, and private entities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Overall special fund revenues for the Department of Natural Resources are not materially affected, though the fund will earn and retain minor interest earnings and reallocate certain service payments (estimated at approximately $156,000 had it been in place in FY 2023). Special fund expenditures may be delayed into future fiscal years to accumulate resources for large projects and equipment purchases. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 117 establishes the Maryland Geological Survey Fund within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and assigns DNR the responsibility to administer the fund to cover operations, projects, equipment, and administrative costs of the Maryland Geological Survey.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Maryland Geological Survey Fund separately and to invest the money in the fund in the same manner as other state funds.
The bill explicitly designates the Comptroller to account for the newly established Maryland Geological Survey Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Giving Infants a Future Without Transmission (GIFT) Act expands requirements for HIV and syphilis testing and reporting to reduce perinatal transmission. It requires universal syphilis and HIV testing for pregnant women at delivery, HIV testing for newborns when maternal status is unknown, and the inclusion of pregnancy status when reporting HIV diagnoses. Additionally, it establishes confidentiality protections for reporting records in legal proceedings and increases fines for unlawful disclosures of personal identifying health information.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant women, newborn infants, healthcare providers, hospitals, medical laboratories, and Medicaid recipients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by an estimated $783,600 in FY 2025 ($115,900 general funds, $667,700 federal funds) to cover additional syphilis and HIV testing at delivery, with federal fund revenues increasing by $667,700 accordingly. Annual expenditures increase to approximately $1.18 million by FY 2029, though costs are expected to be offset by substantial long-term healthcare savings from early detection and treatment. Local health departments experience a minimal workload increase handled with existing resources, and any impact on fine revenues is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 119 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). It alters HIV and syphilis testing and reporting requirements, authorizes MDH to adopt rules and regulations, manages the HIV registry, and impacts MDH's Medicaid budget by increasing expenditures for prenatal and delivery testing.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands loan eligibility under two programs administered by the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO). For the Maryland Oyster Shucking House Loan Fund, MARBIDCO is authorized to provide up to $10,000 per seasonal full-time job created or retained, and loan recipients must annually certify job metrics for three years. For the Maryland Watermen's Microloan Program, eligibility is expanded to include Maryland residents holding commercial fishing licenses issued by the Potomac River Fisheries Commission, and statutory minimum and maximum loan limits are repealed.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland commercial watermen, licensed seafood dealers and processors, seasonal seafood processing workers, and Potomac River Fisheries Commission commercial licensees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are not directly affected because the bill does not alter existing mandated appropriations. Nonbudgeted expenditures and loan repayment revenues for MARBIDCO increase beginning in FY 2025 to the extent that expanded eligibility increases participation in the Maryland Oyster Shucking House Loan Fund. Maryland Watermen's Microloan Program funds are expected to be reallocated among eligible borrowers at varying loan amounts without changing total program funding. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is the primary implementing entity responsible for administering the Maryland Oyster Shucking House Loan Fund and the Maryland Watermen’s Microloan Program, both of which have their eligibility criteria and loan parameters altered by this legislation.

The bill references DNR-issued commercial tidal fish licenses and involves statutory provisions under the Natural Resources Article regarding loan forgiveness tied to returning oyster shells to DNR and planting spat-on-shell verified by DNR.

The bill expands loan eligibility to Maryland residents holding commercial fishing licenses issued by the Potomac River Fisheries Commission (PRFC), a bi-state interstate compact entity in which Maryland participates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts monthly supervision fees from the court-ordered payments an individual must be current on to accrue earned compliance credits, allowing eligible individuals on probation, parole, or mandatory supervision to reduce their term of active supervision even if they owe supervision fees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Parole and Probation within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals under the supervision of the Division of Parole and Probation (on probation, parole, or mandatory release)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No local effect. At the State level, shortening the active supervision period for eligible individuals is expected to decrease caseloads for the Division of Parole and Probation and reduce the volume of uncollected supervision fees transferred to the Central Collection Unit. While general fund revenue from supervision fees could theoretically decrease, any impact is considered speculative because affected individuals often fail to pay the fees in full under current law.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS and its Division of Parole and Probation (DPP) are the primary implementing entities of the bill. The legislation excludes monthly supervision fees from the payment conditions required to earn compliance credits, which directly reduces active supervision caseloads managed by DPP.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU) is housed within DBM. Because the bill shortens active supervision periods and impacts how outstanding supervision fees accumulate and transfer upon case closure, it is expected to decrease CCU's collection workload.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes circuit court clerks to keep electronic records rather than physical books for recording and indexing military discharge papers for members of the uniformed services. It also permits the inspection of military discharge records 70 years after they were recorded without requiring proof of relation or good cause, provided Social Security numbers are redacted, and allows relatives to obtain certified copies after 70 years without demonstrating good cause.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Court
qa_results.stakeholders: Uniformed service members, military veterans, their families, and researchers or individuals seeking historical military records
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected; the Judiciary can implement the bill's provisions using existing resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the responsibilities of the clerks of the circuit courts regarding the recordation, indexing, electronic recordkeeping, and inspection of military discharge records, including mandatory redaction of Social Security numbers. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative, legal, and operational support to the circuit court clerks.

The bill affects the public availability, privacy protections, and access rules for military discharge documents of veterans who served in the uniformed services, an area directly concerning the constituency served and supported by the Department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Nonoccupational Postexposure Prophylaxis (nPEP) Standing Order Program, authorizing licensed pharmacists registered with the program to dispense nPEP medication under a standing order without an individual prescription, subject to screening and clinical criteria consistent with CDC guidelines.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals exposed or potentially exposed to HIV, victims of sexual assault, licensed pharmacists, and Medicaid enrollees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can implement the program using existing budgeted resources. General fund revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount to the extent MDH collects program administration fees. Near-term Medicaid expenditures and federal matching funds may increase due to higher nPEP utilization, but these costs are likely offset over time by indeterminate healthcare savings from prevented HIV infections. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 127 is a departmental bill requested by MDH. The department is directly responsible for establishing, administering, and adopting regulations for the Nonoccupational Postexposure Prophylaxis (nPEP) Standing Order Program, setting training guidelines, collecting fees, and receiving patient referrals through its disease intervention specialists.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP administers the Program for Preventing HIV Infection for Rape Victims, which is explicitly referenced in the bill to exempt qualifying sexual assault victims from fees under the nPEP Standing Order Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Maryland local jurisdictions with at least 150,000 residents to annually report data regarding residential building and development permit applications—including application counts, processing times, and use of expedited processes—to the Department of Housing and Community Development and the Maryland Department of Planning, and publish the report on their website.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development, Maryland Department of Planning, and qualifying local jurisdictions
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments with at least 150,000 residents, residential housing developers, building permit applicants, and the public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations can implement the reporting requirements with existing resources, resulting in no change to state revenues or expenditures. Local government expenditures may increase for certain covered jurisdictions that require software programming changes to track and report the required metrics (for example, Charles County estimated a one-time programming cost of $10,000).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires local jurisdictions with at least 150,000 residents to submit annual reports containing detailed data on residential building and development permit applications to the Department of Housing and Community Development.

The bill explicitly requires local jurisdictions with at least 150,000 residents to submit annual reports on residential building and development permit applications to the Department of Planning, aligning with its role in tracking land use and development trends.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes a unified anti-retaliation framework prohibiting employers from taking or threatening adverse action against employees who inquire about their rights, file complaints, or participate in proceedings under various Maryland labor and employment laws, including Wage and Hour, Equal Pay, Wage Payment and Collection, Workplace Fraud, Employment of Minors, and Living Wage laws. It authorizes the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to investigate violations, attempt informal mediation, issue orders for lost wages and civil penalties up to $1,000, and enables legal enforcement actions, while also penalizing bad-faith or groundless complaints.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Commissioner of Labor and Industry)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers, employees (including minors and service contract workers), and labor investigators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $225,049 in FY 2025 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire 2.5 personnel (a civil rights officer, a wage and hour investigator, and a part-time Assistant Attorney General) and make necessary database upgrades. Out-year expenditures range between $209,300 and $237,000 annually. State general fund revenues are expected to increase minimally through civil penalties and administrative fines imposed on noncompliant employers and bad-faith complainants. Local government operations and circuit courts are not anticipated to experience material fiscal impacts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the Maryland Department of Labor with investigating alleged adverse action violations, conducting mediation, issuing compliance orders, and assessing civil penalties, requiring additional personnel and funding for enforcement.

The Commissioner of Labor and Industry may request the Office of the Attorney General to initiate civil enforcement actions on behalf of employees against noncompliant employers, and the fiscal note accounts for funding an assistant Attorney General position.

Orders and administrative penalties issued by the Commissioner are subject to the Administrative Procedure Act, resulting in potential contested case hearings before administrative law judges at the Office of Administrative Hearings.
The bill creates civil causes of action allowing employees or the Commissioner to file enforcement actions in the District Court or circuit courts for damages, back pay, and penalties.

qa_results.bill_summary: Provides civil immunity to administrative, educational, or support staff of public, private, or parochial schools for personal injury or property damage resulting from intervening in student altercations or disturbances, provided they acted in an official capacity, in a reasonably prudent manner, and without gross negligence or willful, wanton, or intentionally tortious conduct.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Administrative, educational, and support staff at public, private, and parochial schools, as well as students and their families.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides civil immunity for administrative, educational, and support staff in public, private, and parochial schools when intervening in student altercations. As the oversight agency for public education policy and educator standards across Maryland, MSDE is directly relevant to policies impacting school personnel conduct and protections.

The bill creates an explicit statutory defense of civil immunity against personal injury and property damage tort claims arising from educator interventions, directly affecting civil actions adjudicated within the Maryland court system.

As the independent unit within MSDE tasked with coordinating school safety and providing guidance and training for public and private school environments, the bill's provisions regarding intervention in student disturbances and altercations intersect with the center's school safety resources and guidance.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 139 expands existing residential lease notice requirements for utility payments to include gas and electric services alongside water and sewer. For residential buildings with six or more units where tenants pay utility costs to the landlord, the landlord must provide lease notice and either provide a copy of the bill or provide an annual written summary of the prior year's utility costs by utility type. For buildings with five or fewer units, the landlord must include notice in the written lease and provide copies of the utility bills. These requirements do not apply when tenants pay utility providers directly or where utilities are allocated via a ratio utility billing system.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants and residential landlords in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. The impact on small business landlords is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General enforces state consumer protection laws, including statutory disclosure requirements and unfair trade practices within residential landlord-tenant leases, and served as an information source for the legislation.

The bill as originally introduced placed direct requirements and penalty enforcement authority under the Office of Home Energy Programs within the Department of Human Services, although these provisions were amended out of the final enacted legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that contracts for the initial sale or resale of condominium units are unenforceable unless they include specified disclosures regarding actual knowledge of the presence of asbestos, its location, and any abatement history.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: Condominium buyers, sellers (developers and individual unit owners), and condominium councils of unit owners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Small business effects are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is statutorily responsible for the registration and oversight of condominiums and time-shares in Maryland, including the public offering statements referenced in the bill's disclosure requirements for initial sales of condominium units.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees and enforces consumer protection standards relating to required statutory disclosures in consumer transactions and real property sales.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters several provisions of the Public Employee Relations Act by defining 'interested employee organization,' adjusting the timeline for employers to notify exclusive representatives regarding new employee check-in events, clarifying that deputy directors are primarily responsible for their specific areas of labor relations, and refining the investigative procedures for unfair labor practice charges.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public employers (State agencies, community colleges, and local school boards), public employees, and labor organizations or exclusive representatives representing public employees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct state or local fiscal impact, as the alterations are procedural in nature. Any operational adjustments for state agencies or training for administrative law judges can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 144 is a departmental bill requested by PERB to modify and clarify provisions of the Public Employee Relations Act, including deputy director responsibilities, definition of interested employee organizations, and unfair labor practice investigation procedures.

DBM serves as the central personnel agency for State government. The bill alters notice and onboarding check-in timeline requirements for new bargaining unit employees, which DBM noted may create operational adjustments and human resources responsibilities across State agencies.

The bill directly modifies statutory references regarding hearings and evidence transmission involving OAH in unfair labor practice complaints, requiring OAH to train administrative law judges on substantive changes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Maryland health occupations boards that lack existing statutory authority to adopt regulations establishing reciprocal licensure and certification for health professionals licensed or certified in another state that provides similar reciprocity, provided applicants meet specified equivalence, good standing, application, and fee requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Health occupations boards within the Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Out-of-state licensed and certified health professionals, Maryland health occupations boards, and patients accessing health care services in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures may experience a potential minimal increase for boards needing resources to process reciprocity applications. Special fund revenue impact is indeterminate, as fees for reciprocity may be lower than regular out-of-state licensing fees, though overall revenue could increase if applicant volume is sufficiently high. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 146 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). It directly authorizes health occupations boards housed within MDH that lack reciprocity authority to adopt regulations establishing reciprocity for licensed or certified individuals from other states.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a claimant who purchases tobacco tax stamps to receive a refund for stamps lost due to theft, provided they submit a police report with a detailed inventory and a signed, notarized affidavit. The bill requires claimants to return refunds if stolen property is recovered and establishes a fine of double the refund amount for fraudulent claims.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed tobacco wholesalers, cigarette distributors, and other claimants purchasing tobacco tax stamps who experience theft.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an indeterminate amount, potentially beginning in FY 2024, due to refunds issued for stolen tobacco tax stamps (partially offset by any fines assessed for false claims). The Comptroller's Office can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering tobacco tax stamps and processing claims for refunds. Under this bill, the Comptroller receives required documentation (police reports and affidavits), processes refunds for stamps lost due to theft, collects returned refunds or fines for false claims, and is authorized to adopt implementing regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the required retention period for medical records, laboratory reports, and X-ray reports from 5 years to 7 years (and for minor patients, until 7 years after reaching the age of majority). It requires that notices regarding the proposed destruction of records be sent by both first-class mail and email, and extends the period a patient or guardian has to retrieve such records before destruction from 30 days to 60 days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients, parents and guardians of minor patients, health care providers and facilities, and local health departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can handle updates to records retention schedules using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues. Local health departments may experience a minimal expenditure increase if additional storage is required to retain records longer; local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 149 directly amends the Health - General Article regarding medical record retention and destruction standards for health care providers and facilities. The Secretary of Health is tasked with adopting regulations governing the destruction of medical records, and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) must update record retention schedules and procedures across all MDH-operated facilities and state hospitals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Charles County Board of Education to fill a board vacancy within 90 days after it occurs, with an option not to fill a vacancy that occurs during an election year for that seat. It also requires the board to livestream and publicly archive video recordings on its website of open meetings where applicants for a board vacancy are interviewed.
qa_results.responsible_party: Charles County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and voters of Charles County, candidates applying for school board vacancies, and members of the Charles County Board of Education.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. The Charles County Board of Education can handle the required livestreaming and archiving of public interview meetings using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE provides general oversight and leadership for Maryland's 24 public school systems, including the Charles County public school system. Although the bill specifically governs local board procedures for filling vacancies and requires no state fiscal expenditure or direct implementation from MSDE, it modifies the Education Article governing local school board administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits health care providers from charging fees for providing copies of medical records requested by an attorney representing a patient, if the records are to be used for filing a claim or appealing a denial of Social Security Disability Income (SSDI) or Social Security benefits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients seeking or appealing Social Security disability and benefit claims, attorneys representing these patients, health care providers (including small business providers), and local health departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially impact State operations or finances. Local government revenues may decrease to the extent that local health departments charge fees for medical record copies, while local expenditures remain unaffected. Small business health care providers will experience a loss of fee revenue when providing records requested by attorneys for SSDI or Social Security claims.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Health - General Article regarding medical record fees charged by healthcare providers and directly affects local health departments, which MDH oversees and which may experience decreased fee revenues when fulfilling medical record requests for Social Security disability claims.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender was consulted for the bill's fiscal analysis regarding legal representation and obtaining client medical records, although the measure primarily applies to attorneys handling federal Social Security disability claims and appeals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) to accept homeowners' property tax credit applications up to three years late from individuals enrolled in the Homeowner Protection Program. Additionally, it requires SDAT to calculate current-year homestead property tax credit assessments for eligible homeowners aged 70 and older as if they had received the credit in prior years for which they failed to apply.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners enrolled in the Homeowner Protection Program, senior homeowners aged 70 and older, the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase beginning in FY 2025 depending on the number of eligible Homeowner Protection Program participants granted retroactive credits (estimated illustratively at $36,500 for 25 homeowners for a 1-year retroactive credit or $109,500 for a 3-year credit). Annuity Bond Fund revenues decrease beginning in FY 2025 due to granted homestead credits, which could necessitate general fund spending or tax rate adjustments to cover debt service. Local government property tax revenues and supplemental credit revenues also decrease starting in FY 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under § 9-104(u)(5) of the Tax - Property Article as referenced in the bill, upon certification by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, the Comptroller is responsible for paying the property tax credit due to eligible homeowners. Additionally, the Comptroller's Office was consulted as an information source for the fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Act of 2024 establishes standards and application procedures for installing and using electric vehicle recharging equipment (including for electric bicycles) in cooperative housing corporations, rendering conflicting restrictions void. It also amends existing laws for condominiums and homeowners associations regarding insurance requirements prior to installation, and requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to provide information, contractor lists, dispute resolution resources, and a point of contact on its common ownership community website.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Members, unit owners, lot owners, and governing bodies of common ownership communities (cooperative housing corporations, condominiums, and homeowners associations), as well as electric vehicle and electric bicycle owners, electrical contractors, and insurers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $41,686 in FY 2025, accounting for the October 1, 2024 effective date, to hire one part-time development officer within the Department of Housing and Community Development to manage web resources, serve as a point of contact, and assist with dispute resolution. Annual costs rise to $46,000 in FY 2026 and reach $52,500 by FY 2029 due to annualization and inflation. State revenues are not affected, and the bill has no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) expand its common ownership community website to include information regarding electric vehicle recharging equipment requirements, certified contractors, insurers, dispute resolution resources, and a designated department point of contact, resulting in a direct general fund expenditure impact to hire staff.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts specified individuals—including people recently released from correctional facilities, homeless individuals, certain youth in state programs, and individuals under the care of the Maryland Department of Health—from MVA identification card fees. The bill also extends the expiration term of certain learner's instructional permits from 180 days to one year and preserves the validity of driver's licenses for federal contract employees serving outside the state and their dependents.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeless individuals, recently incarcerated individuals, youth under the care of DJS or DHS, Maryland Department of Health patients, drivers seeking instructional permits for different vehicle classes, and federal contract employees stationed outside Maryland and their dependents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected. Although fee exemptions are expanded, MVA notes that the cost to collect and account for the existing $1 fee exceeded revenue generated. Computer reprogramming changes can be managed within existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary implementing agency responsible for issuing driver's licenses, learner's instructional permits, and identification cards, and must administer the expanded fee exemptions, permit validity extensions, and out-of-state license provisions.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and sponsored this departmental legislation affecting Transportation Trust Fund revenues and operations.
Youth under the care of DJS are explicitly made eligible for identification card fee waivers upon presenting documentation.
Youth aged 15 through 20 participating in approved DHS programs are explicitly eligible for fee exemptions for identification cards.
Individuals currently under the care of MDH are explicitly made exempt from identification card issuance fees upon presenting documentation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands fee exemptions for identification cards to individuals recently released from correctional facilities, requiring coordination regarding documentation upon release.
DHCD oversees homeless services and solutions and was consulted as an information source regarding the documentation process for homeless individuals seeking identification card fee waivers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller to discontinue 20% of State aid for local highway user revenues and disparity grants for any county, municipality, or special taxing district that fails to submit its required annual financial audit report within two calendar years after the statutory deadline. Discontinued funds may be reinstated if the report is submitted within the same fiscal year; otherwise, the withheld funds revert to the State's General Fund (disparity grants) or Transportation Trust Fund (highway user revenues).
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland and the Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland local governments, including counties, municipalities, and special taxing districts that fail to timely submit required annual audit reports, as well as the residents receiving local public services funded by highway user revenues and disparity grants.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2027, local jurisdictions that fail to file required audit reports within two calendar years will face a 20% reduction in State aid for highway user revenues and disparity grants. If the audit is not submitted in the same fiscal year, the withheld funds revert to the State, resulting in decreased Transportation Trust Fund and General Fund expenditures for State aid to local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary implementing agency tasked with ordering the discontinuance of 20% of State aid (highway user revenues and disparity grants) to non-compliant local jurisdictions upon notice from the Department of Legislative Services, as well as ordering reinstatement once reports are filed.
Local governments must submit their annual audit reports directly to the Legislative Auditor (head of the Office of Legislative Audits), whose office tracks filing deadlines and compliance.

The bill impacts local highway user revenues funded through the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which is administered by MDOT. Withheld and unsubmitted highway user funds revert back to the TTF, decreasing TTF expenditures.
DBM oversees the State budget and General Fund execution. Under the bill, discontinued disparity grant funds that are not cured within the fiscal year revert to the State General Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of the Maryland Department of State Police to determine the manner, format, and payment methods for applications, renewals, and fingerprint submissions for private detectives, security guards, security systems technicians, special police officers, and railroad police officers, enabling the transition to an automated, electronic licensing process.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants, licensees, and employers in regulated occupations, including private detectives and detective agencies, security guards and guard agencies, security systems technicians and agencies, special police officers, and railroad police officers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are projected to decrease minimally, likely by less than $10,000 annually (estimated at approximately $9,500 starting in FY 2025), due to a 3% vendor fee for electronic payment processing that the Department of State Police does not plan to pass along to applicants. Administrative requirements will be absorbed using existing departmental resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental initiative for the Department of State Police, authorizing the Secretary of State Police to determine the manner, format, and payment methods for licenses and certifications for private detectives, security guards, security systems technicians, railroad police, and special police.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates fingerprint submission format requirements processed through the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR), which is housed within and operated by DPSCS.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a person or towing company that removes a vehicle from a parking lot to provide notice to the vehicle's insurer of record electronically, rather than by certified and first-class mail, if agreed to in writing or by electronic communication by both the tower and the insurer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation (Motor Vehicle Administration)
qa_results.stakeholders: Towing businesses, vehicle insurers of record, and vehicle owners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Small business towing companies and insurers may experience minimal administrative efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) oversees vehicle administration and maintains a database of addresses for providing notice to insurers of record, which towers access to fulfill statutory notification requirements.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the administration of the Maryland Transportation Article, which is directly amended by this bill.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates motor vehicle insurers operating in the state, who are permitted under the bill to receive electronic notifications from towing companies upon mutual agreement.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Safe Sleep Act of 2024 requires hospitals, prior to discharging a newborn infant, to provide oral and written educational resources to parents or legal guardians on how to maintain a safe sleep environment, avoid shaken baby syndrome, and manage caregiver stress. Hospitals must also assess the infant's planned home sleep setting, document that educational materials were provided, and offer a list of resources to acquire safe sleep equipment if needed. Additionally, the Maryland Department of Health, in consultation with local health officers, must develop and annually update a county-by-county list of safe sleep resources.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Newborn infants, new parents and legal guardians, hospitals, and local health departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $19,400 ($19,444 detailed) in FY 2025 only for the Maryland Department of Health to hire a part-time contractual health educator to develop the county-level resource directory. State revenues are unaffected, and local health departments can update annual resource lists using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is specifically tasked under the bill with developing and maintaining a county-by-county list of resources for parents and legal guardians to obtain items needed for a safe sleep environment, in consultation with local health officers. The fiscal note also identifies a direct fiscal impact on MDH of approximately $19,444 in FY 2025 for contractual staffing to compile the initial list.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue special disabled veteran registration plates without the international symbol of access to U.S. Armed Forces veterans who are between 50% and 99% service-connected disabled, subject to standard vehicle registration fees and surcharges, and exempts surviving joint owners or spouses from replacement plate fees upon transfer of the vehicle.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: U.S. Armed Forces veterans with a 50% to 99% service-connected disability rating and their spouses or joint vehicle owners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures are not materially affected because newly qualifying veterans must still pay standard registration fees and surcharges, the Motor Vehicle Administration already has a supply of plates available, and replacement fee exemptions are negligible. System reprogramming can be handled using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) with establishing, issuing, and regulating the special disabled veteran registration plates for eligible veterans, as well as managing replacement fee exemptions and plate returns.

The Motor Vehicle Administration is a modal unit within the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT), and vehicle registration revenues and plate administration impact the Transportation Trust Fund.

The bill creates a specific benefit and vehicle recognition for armed forces veterans who are between 50% and 99% service-connected disabled, which falls under DVMF's mission of advocacy and resource navigation for Maryland veterans.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill makes administrative, technical, and clarifying changes to the Summer Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) for Children and alters requirements for the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers Scholarship. It removes specific statutory application and notification deadlines for counties applying for food supplement matching funds, allowing the Department of Human Services (DHS) to establish these dates, and permits DHS to use program funds to offset administrative costs of the federal Summer Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) program. For the scholarship program, the bill modifies the service obligation to 15 months per academic year awarded (within eight years of receiving the scholarship), replaces the letter of intent with a written agreement, and allows the Maryland Higher Education Commission to determine repayment amounts for noncompliance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services and the Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income children and families receiving food supplement benefits, participating county governments, and higher education students pursuing careers in targeted Department of Human Services positions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill primarily alters the allowable uses of existing funds by enabling DHS to use State Summer SNAP funds to cover the State's share of administrative costs for the federal Summer EBT program. Administrative changes for DHS and MHEC can be managed within existing budgeted resources. There is no material impact on local revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 183 was requested by the Department of Human Services as a departmental bill. DHS is the primary agency responsible for administering the Food Supplement Program (Summer SNAP for Children) and collaborates on the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers, which prepares individuals for targeted careers within DHS.

The bill directly alters the terms and administration of the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers Scholarship, which is administered through MHEC and its Office of Student Financial Assistance. The bill requires scholarship recipients to enter into written agreements with MHEC and grants MHEC authority over service obligations and repayment terms.

The bill directly amends provisions governing the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers Scholarship overseen by the Commission, altering service obligation requirements, written agreement execution, and repayment determinations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Eastern Shore code home rule counties to increase their maximum hotel rental tax rate from 5% up to 6% with the unanimous consent of the county commissioners.
qa_results.responsible_party: Boards of County Commissioners of Eastern Shore code counties (Caroline, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Worcester counties)
qa_results.stakeholders: Tourists and hotel guests, hotel and lodging businesses, and county and municipal governments in Eastern Shore code counties (specifically Caroline, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Worcester counties, as well as municipalities such as Ocean City).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. If all four eligible Eastern Shore code counties raise their hotel rental tax rate to the maximum 6%, county revenues are estimated to increase by approximately $501,000 annually, and municipal revenues (particularly Ocean City) are estimated to increase by approximately $5.4 million annually. Local expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's chief financial officer and tax administrator. While the bill authorizes local Eastern Shore code counties to alter their local hotel rental tax rates with no direct impact on state revenues, the Comptroller's Office monitors state and local tax structures and served as an information source for the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires residential service agencies (RSAs) providing certain Medicaid home- and community-based personal assistance services to submit an annual report to the Maryland Department of Labor documenting average, highest, and lowest wage rates for personal care aides starting September 1, 2025. Additionally, it requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit a report to the General Assembly within 180 days following the release of the final federal Ensuring Access to Medicaid Services rule detailing an overview of the rule and implementation plans.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor and Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential service agencies (RSAs), personal care aides (PCAs), and Medicaid home- and community-based services recipients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected; the Maryland Department of Labor can handle report collection and the Maryland Department of Health can complete the required report using existing budgeted resources. Local governments are not affected. Small business residential service agencies may face potential administrative impacts to track and submit required annual wage reporting.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires residential service agencies employing personal care aides to submit annual wage reports to the Maryland Department of Labor in a form and manner determined by the department.

The bill governs services reimbursed under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program administered by the Department of Health and requires MDH to submit a report to the General Assembly regarding the federal Ensuring Access to Medicaid Services rule and the process for reviewing personal care aide wage reports and reimbursement rates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Anne Arundel County and municipalities within the county to decrease the maximum speed limit on highways to not less than 15 miles per hour following an engineering and traffic investigation, and prohibits the installation of new speed monitoring systems to enforce speed limits on highways where the limit has been reduced under this authority.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County and municipal governments within Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists, pedestrians, and residents in Anne Arundel County and its municipalities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally from additional speeding citations. In Anne Arundel County, county and municipal expenditures increase to the extent engineering and traffic investigations are conducted; local revenues may increase if speed limits are lowered on roads where speed cameras are already operating.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under Maryland transportation law, any alteration of speed limits on state highways or extensions thereof initiated by local authorities requires review and approval by the State Highway Administration (SHA).

As the parent department overseeing state highway policies, vehicle safety regulations, and the State Highway Administration, MDOT is impacted by statutory modifications to local highway speed limit authorizations.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the District Court, which adjudicates citations and contested traffic violations that may arise from lowered speed limits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Purple Alert Program within the Department of State Police to facilitate the rapid dissemination of information to assist in locating certain missing individuals who have a cognitive impairment, mental disorder, intellectual or developmental disability, brain injury, or are deaf, deafblind, or hard of hearing, whose disappearance poses a credible threat to their safety and who do not qualify for a Silver Alert.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Missing persons with qualifying cognitive impairments, disabilities, mental disorders, or hearing impairments, along with their caregivers, law enforcement agencies, broadcasters, and high school student volunteers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 195 directly mandates the Department of State Police to establish, administer, and operate the Purple Alert Program, including developing guidelines, training local law enforcement, coordinating alerts, and handling notifications.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to consult with the State Highway Administration to establish a plan to broadcast Purple Alert information via statewide dynamic message signs.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to consult with the State Department of Education to develop a program allowing high school students to earn student service-learning hours by assisting in missing person searches.
MDOT is the parent department of the State Highway Administration, which must coordinate on the dynamic message sign activation plans for the Purple Alert Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to exempt furloughed federal civilian employees from the requirement to actively seek work in order to qualify for unemployment insurance benefits during a full or partial federal government shutdown, provided they remain able to work, available for work, and work-attached.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Furloughed federal civilian employees in Maryland affected by a federal government shutdown.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. The bill does not materially affect the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund because federal employees must reimburse the trust fund for any benefits received once back pay is awarded after a shutdown ends, leading to no net effect on the fund balance. Local government finances and operations are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was sponsored as a departmental request by the Maryland Department of Labor and directly authorizes the Secretary of Labor to exempt furloughed federal civilian employees from the work search requirement for unemployment insurance benefits eligibility.

qa_results.bill_summary: Temporarily pauses for three fiscal years (FY 2025 through FY 2027) the statutory mandate requiring the Secretary of Transportation to withhold 35% of Maryland's annual operating grant to the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) when WMATA's budget grows by more than 3%. The bill also establishes new conditions requiring the Secretary to withhold 35% of operating grants if WMATA's board chairman serves more than two prior years or is from the same jurisdiction as the chair for the prior two years, or if the Purple Line light rail is operational but not included on transit maps in WMATA stations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation (Secretary of Transportation)
qa_results.stakeholders: WMATA transit riders, commuters, and residents in the Washington Suburban Transit District (primarily Montgomery and Prince George's counties), as well as WMATA management and personnel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by an estimated $223.7 million in FY 2025 ($150.0 million in general funds and $73.7 million in Transportation Trust Fund special funds) because MDOT will not withhold 35% of its operating assistance to WMATA despite a budget increase exceeding 3%. State expenditures may also experience indeterminate increases in FY 2026 and FY 2027. State revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) and the Secretary of Transportation are directly responsible for administering operating grants to the Washington Suburban Transit District for WMATA and enforcing the withholding conditions. The bill directly impacts Transportation Trust Fund expenditures.

WMATA is an interstate compact agency governed by an agreement among Maryland, Virginia, and the District of Columbia. The bill alters Maryland's funding contributions to WMATA and places requirements on WMATA Board of Directors governance and map signage.

As the principal agency for state budget development and fiscal planning, DBM is impacted by the significant fiscal adjustment, including the release of $150 million in General Funds through the Dedicated Purpose Account.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters requirements for community schools and community school coordinators in Maryland. It directs the State Director of Community Schools within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to create a common needs assessment tool and an evaluation form for coordinators. It expands the definitions of 'community school' and 'wraparound services' to include hearing services, therapists, and transportation to off-site learning opportunities, requires regular reviews of implementation plans, and mandates annual evaluations and reporting to MSDE and the Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB).
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (Director of Community Schools) and the Accountability and Implementation Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Community school students, families, educators, community school coordinators, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None; MSDE and AIB can implement the provisions using existing resources, and State Concentration of Poverty Grant expenditures are not affected. Local Effect: No net change in community school expenditures, though local school systems with large numbers of community schools may experience increased administrative costs associated with annual coordinator evaluations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 200 directly impacts the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). The bill tasks the Director of Community Schools within MSDE with developing a common needs assessment tool and an evaluation form, authorizes MSDE to review and provide comments on community school implementation plans, requires MSDE to make submitted community school evaluations publicly available, and mandates that MSDE jointly submit a report to the General Assembly with the Accountability and Implementation Board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill places direct statutory responsibilities on the Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB), requiring it to receive annual evaluations from community school coordinators, make these evaluations publicly available, and jointly submit a report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024, regarding methods to ensure appropriate and effective use of Concentration of Poverty Grant funds.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Higher Education Commission, in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Health and other educational entities, to develop guidelines for public primary, secondary, and higher education schools to train athletic coaches to recognize indicators of mental illness and behavioral distress in students, including depression, trauma, violence, youth suicide, and substance abuse. It also mandates that public schools and public institutions of higher education offering athletic programs provide this training to all participating coaches.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and Maryland Higher Education Commission, in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Public elementary, secondary, and higher education athletic coaches and student-athletes.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies (MSDE, MHEC, MPSSAA, and MDH) can develop the required guidelines using existing resources. State expenditures may increase minimally for public higher education institutions and the Maryland School for the Deaf to provide training to coaches, though costs are generally absorbable. Local school system and community college expenditures may increase minimally to cover training materials or coach stipends. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Department of Education, in collaboration with the Department of Health and other entities, to develop guidelines for public schools to train coaches to recognize indicators of mental illness and behavioral distress in students.
The bill directly mandates that the Commission, in collaboration with the Department of Health, develop mental health training guidelines for coaches at public institutions of higher education.

The Commission is directly mandated by the bill to collaborate with the Department of Health to develop guidelines for public institutions of higher education to train coaches to recognize indicators of mental illness and behavioral distress.

The bill statutorily requires the Maryland Department of Health to collaborate with both the State Department of Education and the Maryland Higher Education Commission to develop mental health and behavioral distress training guidelines.

As public institutions of higher education with intercollegiate athletic programs, USM constituent universities are required by the bill to provide the specified mental health training to all participating coaches.
As a public institution of higher education with an athletic program, Morgan State University is required to provide the mandated mental health training to each participating coach.
As an independent public institution of higher education offering athletic programs, the college is required to implement and provide the mandated mental health training to coaches.

As a state-funded public educational facility offering school athletic programs, the school is impacted and may incur minimal expenditures to provide the required mental health training to its coaches.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission to examine correctional and juvenile justice education, evaluate prison workforce programs, and develop a statewide policy framework and recommendations aimed at increasing public safety and reducing recidivism.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, individuals under supervision of the Division of Correction, justice-involved youth, correctional education providers, and criminal justice agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $144,000 in FY 2025 and $73,800 in FY 2026 for contractual staff to assist the commission with research and reporting. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (formerly GOCPYVS) to provide staff support for the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission, incurring fiscal expenditures for two contractual positions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
