agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO administers the Equitech Growth Fund and is directly authorized by this bill to utilize fund monies to cover administrative operating expenses.
DBM prepares and oversees the state budget, which includes the statutory annual mandated appropriation of $5,000,000 to the Equitech Growth Fund through FY 2033.
The Governor is statutorily mandated to include a $5,000,000 appropriation to the Fund in the annual budget bill and receives an annual report from TEDCO on awards made.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the Equitech Growth Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund.
The Comptroller of Maryland is statutorily tasked with accounting for the Equitech Growth Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit annual reports to specified committees of the General Assembly by December 1 in 2024, 2025, and 2026 regarding FDA-approved opioid overdose reversal drugs and whether the department has incorporated each approved drug into a standing order, including explanations for any exclusions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals at risk of experiencing an opioid overdose, individuals assisting those at risk, healthcare providers, pharmacists, and state health policymakers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the Maryland Department of Health can handle the reporting requirements with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations/finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 411 specifically mandates that the Maryland Department of Health submit annual reports to the General Assembly by December 1 of 2024, 2025, and 2026 regarding FDA-approved opioid overdose reversal drugs and their inclusion in standing orders.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies that the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System may pay remaining earned financial incentive compensation to the Chief Investment Officer if they retire directly from the Investment Division, and makes a technical correction specifying that the requirement to terminate Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) participation prior to age 60 applies only to members of the State Police Retirement System and not members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: The Chief Investment Officer of the State Retirement and Pension System, members of the State Police Retirement System (SPRS), and members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. It is technical and clarifying in nature and has no effect on State or local pension liabilities, contribution rates, or revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the administration of the State Retirement and Pension System, clarifying rules for incentive compensation payouts to the Chief Investment Officer upon retirement from the Investment Division and correcting DROP participation rules for system members.

The bill clarifies DROP provisions specifically affecting members of the State Police Retirement System (limiting extension to age 60) and references human resources acknowledgments from the Department of State Police.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 416 prohibits public school active shooter safety drills or trainings from including traumatic elements, such as simulated gunfire or live role-playing shooters and victims. It requires local school systems to notify parents in advance of drills, provide post-drill mental health follow-ups, and collect data on the drills' effectiveness and psychological impact. In addition, it directs the Maryland Center for School Safety to collaborate with a research institution to analyze drill data, identify best practices, and create model content on firearm safe storage laws to distribute annually to parents.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents and guardians, public school personnel, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $200,000 in FY 2025 and by $100,000 annually thereafter for the Maryland Center for School Safety to contract with a higher education institution or research entity to analyze local school data. Local school system expenditures may increase to provide required mental health follow-up services to students and school personnel, though a specific estimate is not feasible. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill places primary implementation responsibilities on the Center, including collaborating on research regarding the psychological impact of active shooter drills, establishing best practices, determining compliance with trauma-sensitive drill restrictions, and developing model content on Maryland's firearm storage laws.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), within which the Center is housed, is authorized to adopt regulations regarding drills, must consult with the Center regarding drill components, and is required to annually review best practices and update the annual drill schedule for local school systems.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to consult with the Department of State Police in developing the model content informing parents of Maryland's safe firearm storage laws.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 418 alters the composition of the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council by adding the Comptroller and designating the Secretary of Budget and Management as chair, while removing references to the Governor's Grants Office. It tasks the Council with studying the feasibility, costs, and impacts of establishing a State Grants Ombudsperson, extends the deadline for its final recommendations report to July 1, 2027, and extends the Council's termination date by four years to June 30, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management and the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council
qa_results.stakeholders: State grant-making agencies, grant applicants, and grant recipients (including nonprofit organizations and local governments)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local fiscal effect is none. Extending the council's term and altering reporting deadlines has no material effect on governmental finances or revenues, and member agencies can handle staffing duties and the ombudsperson study with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Budget and Management as the Chair of the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council, transfers responsibilities previously held by the Governor's Grants Office to the Department, and requires the Department to provide technical assistance, receive recommendations, and submit reports to the General Assembly.

The bill removes the Governor's Grants Office from the Council's membership and statute, transferring its prior leadership, technical assistance, and reporting functions over the Council to the Department of Budget and Management.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership, duties, reporting timelines, and termination date of the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council, extending its existence through June 30, 2029.
The bill adds the Comptroller, or the Comptroller's designee, as a designated member of the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council.
The Chief Procurement Officer (housed within DGS) serves as a member of the Council and shares staffing responsibilities.
The State Treasurer or designee serves as a member of the Council and shares in council staffing responsibilities.
The Attorney General or designee serves as a member of the Council and shares in council staffing responsibilities.
The Secretary of Health or designee serves as a member of the Council, shares staffing responsibilities, and designates a Chief Accountability Officer.
The Secretary of Human Services or designee serves as a member of the Council, shares staffing responsibilities, and designates a Chief Accountability Officer.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development or designee serves as a member of the Council, shares staffing responsibilities, and designates a Chief Accountability Officer.
The Secretary of Agriculture or designee serves as a member of the Council, shares staffing responsibilities, and designates a Chief Accountability Officer.
The Secretary of the Environment or designee serves as a member of the Council, shares staffing responsibilities, and designates a Chief Accountability Officer.
The State Superintendent of Schools or designee serves as a member of the Council, shares staffing responsibilities, and designates a Chief Accountability Officer.
The Secretary of Natural Resources or designee serves as a member of the Council, shares staffing responsibilities, and designates a Chief Accountability Officer.
The Director of MEA or designee serves as a member of the Council and shares staffing responsibilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director or designee serves as a member of the Council and shares staffing responsibilities.
The Chair of the Commission or designee serves as a member of the Council and shares staffing responsibilities.
The Governor appoints five representatives of private nonprofit organizations to the Council and holds the authority to remove members for neglect of duty, incompetence, or misconduct.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Recreation Communication Boards Pilot Program within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to fund the purchase and installation of communication boards—devices featuring symbols, pictures, words, and braille—in newly constructed and altered play areas in State and local parks.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with communication, speech, or language disabilities, children and families visiting public park play areas, local governing bodies (county governments, Baltimore City, and M-NCPPC), and businesses that produce or install communication boards.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances experience no net effect, as DNR is authorized to reallocate up to $100,000 from the Park System Capital Improvements and Acquisition Fund to support the pilot program between FY 2025 and FY 2028. Local revenues and expenditures may increase as local governments receive and spend grant funds (capped at $3,000 per board), and local expenditures may rise further if total board purchase and installation costs exceed grant limits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) with administering the Maryland Recreation Communication Boards Pilot Program, constructing communication boards in newly constructed play areas under its jurisdiction, awarding grants to local governing bodies, utilizing funds from the Park System Capital Improvements and Acquisition Fund, and submitting annual evaluation reports to the General Assembly.

As the principal state agency coordinating accessibility and inclusive services for Maryland residents with disabilities, the Department of Disabilities has an advisory and policy interest in expanding play area accessibility via communication boards and was consulted during the legislative analysis of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals requirements that the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County hold public hearings on proposed assisted family housing, issue written reports of hearing findings, and publish hearing notices and annual financial report summaries in local newspapers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County residents, individuals and families seeking or residing in assisted housing, the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County, and local newspapers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect. It is not anticipated to materially affect Montgomery County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 424 amends the Housing and Community Development Article governing local housing authorities (specifically the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County). While the bill's changes pertain directly to local commission administrative procedures with no state fiscal impact, the Department of Housing and Community Development oversees state-level affordable housing policy and was consulted during the legislative review.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires motion picture theaters to provide fully operational closed captioning technology for screenings when available, and requires movie theaters with eight or more screens to offer at least two open-captioned screenings per week for each motion picture during its first three weeks of premiere, subject to certain screening frequency conditions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights
qa_results.stakeholders: Motion picture house owners and operators (specifically those with eight or more screens), moviegoers, and individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights can handle any additional complaints resulting from the bill with existing resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MCCR is the state agency responsible for enforcing Maryland's laws against discrimination in places of public accommodation under Title 20 of the State Government Article, which this bill amends. Any administrative complaints regarding captioning non-compliance at movie theaters fall under MCCR's enforcement jurisdiction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: ODHH promotes the welfare of Deaf and hard-of-hearing residents and advocates for equal access to public resources and community life. Closed and open captioning requirements in movie theaters directly address communication access for the population ODHH serves.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates statewide policies and programs ensuring accessibility and inclusion for individuals with disabilities, aligning closely with the bill's public accommodation accessibility mandates.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for fiscal analysis, as civil actions or enforcement appeals arising from public accommodation violations could potentially be brought before the state court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Rental Assistance for Community School Families Program and Fund to provide rental assistance, utility assistance, and relocation payments to eligible student households at community schools who are at risk of homelessness or experiencing housing instability. The program is administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development in consultation with the Maryland State Department of Education.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development (in consultation with the Maryland State Department of Education)
qa_results.stakeholders: Community school students and their families who are facing housing instability or homelessness, community school coordinators, landlords, and utility providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million in FY 2025, which was budgeted contingent on the bill's enactment, with special fund revenues and expenditures increasing commensurately. Additionally, special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $1.3 million in FY 2025 and $1.7 million annually thereafter via a contingent statutory distribution of District Court summary ejectment surcharges under Chapter 124 of 2024. If discretionary annual general fund appropriations of $10.0 million are provided starting in FY 2026, total special fund revenues and expenditures will be $11.7 million annually. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary agency responsible for administering the newly established Rental Assistance for Community School Families Program and managing the associated special fund.

MSDE is required to consult on the administration of the program, and its Director of Community Schools and community school coordinators play direct roles in identifying eligible households and facilitating support.

The bill statutorily tasks the Director of Community Schools to coordinate with the Governor's Office for Children to support the outreach and implementation of State programs for children in community schools.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly created Rental Assistance for Community School Families Fund separately and exempts the fund from standard interest accrual rules.
The bill specifically directs the Comptroller to account for the newly established Rental Assistance for Community School Families Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 431 renames the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs to the Department of Veterans and Military Families and renames the Secretary of Veterans Affairs accordingly. It also requires the Secretary to appoint a Deputy Secretary of Military Family Policy and Programs to direct policies and programs supporting military families.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families (formerly Department of Veterans Affairs)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland veterans, military families, and Department personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $178,600 in FY 2025 to hire a Deputy Secretary of Military Family Policy and Programs ($145,646 salary and fringe benefits, $7,926 operating expenses) and for one-time renaming/supply expenses ($25,000). Out-year general fund expenditures range between $170,300 and $193,600 annually through FY 2029. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 431 directly renames the Department of Veterans Affairs to the Department of Veterans and Military Families and its Secretary accordingly. It also creates and establishes the duties and funding for a new Deputy Secretary of Military Family Policy and Programs within the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill makes technical corrections across the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article and the Criminal Procedure Article by replacing outdated terms such as "mental retardation" and "insanity" with modern terminology, specifically "intellectual disability" and "mental disorder."
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals involved in the criminal justice and juvenile court systems who have an intellectual disability or mental disorder, legal professionals, and state healthcare and disability service providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is technical in nature and has no effect on State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates statutory terminology from 'mental retardation' to 'intellectual disability' across multiple sections of the Courts and Judicial Proceedings and Criminal Procedure articles that govern commitments to the Department of Health and services provided by the Developmental Disabilities Administration.

The bill updates legal definitions and statutory standards utilized by judges and courts during juvenile proceedings, criminal competency determinations, and not criminally responsible (NCR) adjudications.

The legislation modifies statutory definitions and competency evaluation standards applicable to children in juvenile court proceedings under Title 3, Subtitle 8A of the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates terminology directly relevant to criminal and juvenile defense practice, specifically regarding competency to stand trial, written pleas of not criminally responsible, and commitment proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that spend $500 or more to compensate regulated lobbyists from the requirement to file a statement of political contributions with the State Board of Elections.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations employing or compensating lobbyists in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections administers and receives statements of political contributions filed by persons providing lobbyist compensation under § 5-716 of the General Provisions Article; this bill directly exempts 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations from that filing requirement.
The bill amends the Maryland Public Ethics Law governing lobbying and regulated lobbyists, an area regulated and enforced by the State Ethics Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters provisions governing the calculation and modification of child support for incarcerated obligors by establishing that incarceration can constitute a material change of circumstances warranting modification, prohibiting incarcerated parents from being treated as voluntarily impoverished or having potential income imputed to them, and repealing restrictions regarding sentence length and intent that previously limited when child support arrearages could be suspended during incarceration.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated parents with child support obligations (obligors), custodial parents receiving child support (obligees), and their children.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $124,800 in FY 2025 only for one-time computer programming costs incurred by the Department of Human Services. The bill ensures compliance with federal rules, thereby helping protect federal funding for child support services and the TANF block grant. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 435 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Human Services (DHS) to align Maryland's child support enforcement program with federal Title IV-D regulations. DHS directly administers child support services, adjusts payment accounts for incarcerated obligors, and incurs a fiscal impact of $124,800 in FY 2025 for necessary system programming changes.

The bill directly impacts state court proceedings and judicial determinations by altering statutory standards under the Family Law Article for modifying child support awards, prohibiting courts from considering incarcerated parents voluntarily impoverished, and barring courts from imputing potential income to incarcerated obligors.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill codifies the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council into the Annotated Code of Maryland, alters and clarifies its membership to include additional public officials and industry representatives, and establishes interim and final reporting requirements on zero-emission vehicle infrastructure through June 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Zero-emission and electric vehicle manufacturers, charging equipment manufacturers, electric companies, automotive recyclers, local governments, environmental advocates, and electric vehicle owners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as altering representation and codifying the council does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill codifies the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council within the Transportation Article. The Secretary of Transportation serves on the Council, and the Department is designated to provide primary staff support.

The Director of the Maryland Energy Administration serves as a statutory member of the Council, and the agency is specifically charged with assisting the Department of Transportation in providing staff support.
The Executive Director of the Technical Staff of the Maryland Public Service Commission is a designated member of the Council, and the Commission is required to assist in providing staff support.
The bill explicitly adds the Secretary of General Services (or designee) as a member of the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council.
The Secretary of the Environment (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of Planning (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The People's Counsel (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Council.
The Governor appoints numerous public and industry members, designates the chair or cochairs of the Council, and receives mandatory interim and final reports on its work and recommendations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill codifies, alters the composition of, and updates statutory reporting requirements for an executive advisory board (the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council).
The bill establishes and adjusts various gubernatorial appointment categories to the Council that will be vetted and administered by the Office of Appointments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reestablishes a nonrefundable State income tax credit of up to $75 per antlerless deer for expenses incurred to butcher and process deer meat donated to a qualified 501(c)(3) venison donation program, capped at $300 per individual per tax year unless harvested under a deer management permit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Hunters donating venison, charitable venison donation programs, and recipients of donated venison food assistance
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues are estimated to decrease by $175,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2029 due to credits claimed. The Comptroller's Office can administer the credit with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for administering state income tax credits, processing returns claiming the credit, and receiving annual reporting from venison donation programs regarding donors and donated deer.

Eligibility for the tax credit is contingent on compliance with State hunting laws and regulations and references deer harvested in accordance with deer management permits, which are regulated and issued by the Department of Natural Resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 449 authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of up to $20.0 million in the annual State budget for the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program starting in fiscal year 2026. It also mandates that, beginning in fiscal year 2026, at least 40% of the program's grant funding be allocated to projects located in or directly benefiting underserved or overburdened communities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments, residents of flood-prone areas, and residents of underserved and overburdened communities in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances because the funding authorization of up to $20.0 million per year is discretionary rather than mandated, and planned capital spending already aligns with this authorization ($10.0 million annually in GO bonds in the Capital Improvement Program). The Maryland Department of the Environment can administer the 40% allocation target with existing resources. Local government finances are not affected in total, but the distribution of grant funds among jurisdictions may shift to favor projects in or benefiting underserved or overburdened communities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE houses and administers the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program, which is directly modified by this bill to require at least 40% of funding to be dedicated to projects in or benefiting underserved or overburdened communities starting in FY 2026.

MDP participates directly in the administration of the program through its State Clearinghouse review of grant applications, reviews applicant compliance in cooperation with MDE prior to awards, and consults on required regulations.
Grants and expenditures under the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program are subject to the review and approval of the Board of Public Works.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of up to $20,000,000 in the annual State budget for the program beginning in fiscal year 2026.
MDEM is statutorily tasked with reviewing and approving local emergency response plans that are required as conditions for automated flood warning project grants under the program.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires an annual distribution of $500,000 from the State's Unclaimed Property Fund to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund starting in fiscal year 2025. It also increases the annual mandated State budget appropriation for the CASH Campaign of Maryland from $500,000 to $800,000 starting in fiscal year 2026, requiring at least $150,000 of that appropriation to be used for grants to external entities operating on-demand or mobile tax clinics for seniors, rural communities, and other under-resourced populations. Additionally, recipient law school and volunteer clinics must coordinate annually with the CASH Campaign.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland residents, senior populations, rural communities, new American populations, the CASH Campaign of Maryland, University of Maryland School of Law, University of Baltimore School of Law, and the Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues decrease by $500,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to the diversion of unclaimed property funds, while Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $500,000 annually (with higher education revenues and expenditures increasing by $333,300). General Fund expenditures increase by $300,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 to fund the increased mandate for the CASH Campaign. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was introduced by request of the Office of the Comptroller. It requires the Comptroller, as administrator of abandoned property, to distribute $500,000 annually to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund, which the Comptroller administers and accounts for.

Two of the three designated recipients of the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund are the University of Maryland School of Law and the University of Baltimore School of Law, resulting in an annual higher education revenue and expenditure increase of $333,300. The law clinics are also mandated to interact with the CASH Campaign annually.

The bill establishes an increased statutory mandated general fund appropriation of $800,000 annually starting in FY 2026 for the CASH Campaign of Maryland, impacting executive budget development and overall state general fund expenditures.
The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include a mandated appropriation of $800,000 in the annual state budget bill beginning in FY 2026 for the CASH Campaign of Maryland.

Under the amended section of the Tax - General Article governing the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund, the State Treasurer is responsible for holding the fund separately and investing its monies.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Stop Scam Tax Preparers Act strengthens regulation and enforcement against unauthorized and fraudulent individual tax preparers in Maryland. It requires the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers to publish a code of ethics and rules of professional conduct by January 1, 2026, establishes mandatory reporting of disciplinary actions and violations between the Board and the Comptroller's Office, empowers the Field Enforcement Bureau as peace officers to enforce tax preparation laws, and establishes criminal misdemeanor penalties and fines up to $5,000 for preparing tax returns without being registered or licensed, directing fine revenue to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Individual Tax Preparers (Maryland Department of Labor) and the Office of the Comptroller (Field Enforcement Bureau)
qa_results.stakeholders: Individual income tax return preparers, Maryland taxpayers, low-income Marylanders utilizing legal tax clinics, and legal clinics operating under the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $32,300 in FY 2025 only for Judiciary computer programming updates. State special fund revenues to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund will see a minimal increase beginning in FY 2025 from misdemeanor penalties of up to $5,000 per violation. All other enforcement and administrative duties can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 452 was requested by the Office of the Comptroller. It grants peace officer powers to authorized employees of the Comptroller's Field Enforcement Bureau to enforce laws related to income tax preparation, mandates notification procedures between the Comptroller and the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers, and directs new misdemeanor fine revenues into the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund administered by the Comptroller.

The Department of Labor houses the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers, which is directly tasked under the bill with publishing a code of ethics and rules of professional conduct on its website, reporting disciplinary actions and injunctions to the Comptroller within five business days, and referring unregistered tax preparer violations to the Comptroller's Field Enforcement Bureau.

The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense for unauthorized income tax preparation and allows the Board to seek injunctions in circuit courts. The Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) incurs a direct fiscal impact of $32,300 in FY 2025 for computer programming and case management updates to track the new misdemeanor charges.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals obsolete statutory provisions governing income tax revenue distributions to municipalities dating back to fiscal year 1990 and corrects an erroneous cross-reference concerning the catalytic revitalization projects tax credit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers, businesses claiming the catalytic revitalization project tax credit, and the Office of the Comptroller.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as the revisions are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 453 is a departmental bill requested by the Office of the Comptroller. It amends the Tax - General Article to repeal obsolete provisions regarding the distribution of income tax revenue administered by the Comptroller and corrects a statutory cross-reference.

The bill corrects an erroneous statutory cross-reference concerning the catalytic revitalization project tax credit, which references Title 6, Subtitle 9 of the Housing and Community Development Article administered under DHCD programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 454 clarifies and expands the definition of tax information, specifically adding digital advertising gross revenues tax returns and general tax returns and filings. It authorizes the Comptroller to disclose confidential tax information to persons, governmental entities, and tax compliance organizations for tax compliance activities under binding written data use agreements and supervisory protocols, while establishing criminal misdemeanor penalties for unauthorized disclosures by recipients.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers, the Comptroller's Office, external tax compliance organizations (such as the Multistate Tax Commission and Northeastern States Tax Officials Association), and partner governmental entities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general and special fund revenues, special fund expenditures for local highway user revenue grants, and local revenues may potentially increase beginning as early as FY 2025 due to enhanced tax compliance and audit activities; however, specific dollar estimates are indeterminate. Implementation of data use agreements and compliance monitoring will be handled within existing budgeted resources, and criminal penalty provisions will not have a material fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 454 is a departmental bill requested by the Comptroller. It expands the Comptroller's authority to disclose tax information to third parties and compliance organizations to assist in tax compliance activities, and requires the Comptroller to establish, execute, and supervise binding data use agreements.

As an entity authorized to receive tax information under § 13-203(c)(14), the commission is newly mandated under § 13-203(g) to enter into a binding data use agreement with the Comptroller and be subject to ongoing supervision regarding data security.

As a recipient of tax information under § 13-203(c)(14), MDH is directly subject to the bill's new requirement under § 13-203(g) to execute a binding written data use agreement with the Comptroller and be supervised in its handling of confidential tax records.

As an authorized recipient of tax information under § 13-203(c)(14), DHS is specifically required under § 13-203(g) to enter into a binding data use agreement governing confidentiality and security and submit to Comptroller supervision.

As an entity receiving tax information under § 13-203(c)(14), MSDE is specifically subjected by § 13-203(g) to new requirements to execute a binding data use agreement and be supervised by the Comptroller regarding data protection.

Under § 13-203(g), the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board (administering MarylandSaves) is explicitly required to execute a binding written data use agreement with the Comptroller and adhere to supervisory requirements prior to receiving tax information under § 13-203(c)(15).

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 455 phases in mandatory electronic filing requirements for various Maryland taxes and fees administered by the Comptroller, including specified business and environmental fees starting after 2026, corporate and pass-through entity income taxes starting after tax year 2026, and individual income taxes starting after tax year 2029, with exemptions for certain individuals and small corporations. It also prohibits tax return preparers and software developers from charging separate fees for electronic filing beginning January 1, 2030, subject to civil penalties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers (individuals, corporations, and pass-through entities), businesses subject to state excise and environmental fees, professional tax return preparers, and tax software developers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may see a minimal increase beginning in FY 2030 from civil penalties ($500 for a first violation and $1,000 for subsequent violations) assessed on tax preparers or software companies that charge separate electronic filing fees. State expenditures are not materially affected, as the Comptroller's Office can implement the requirements with existing resources and anticipates operational efficiencies through reduced paper processing. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 455 is a departmental bill requested by the Office of the Comptroller that requires electronic filing for numerous state taxes and fees, establishes exemptions, and authorizes the Comptroller to enforce compliance and levy civil penalties against tax preparers and software vendors that charge separate fees for electronic filing.

The bill amends provisions in the Environment Article governing the submission of returns for the tire recycling fee and the bay restoration fee, which fund environmental restoration programs overseen by MDE.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires producers or sellers of synthetic turf to disclose to customers typical maintenance requirements and the industry standard costs for removing, replacing, and disposing of synthetic turf. Additionally, requires the Maryland Department of the Environment, in consultation with industry and community stakeholders, to conduct a study on synthetic turf and submit a report of its findings to the General Assembly by July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Synthetic turf producers, sellers, and buyers (including local governments, public and private school systems, higher education facilities, and sports organizations), as well as environmental and community stakeholders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $59,400 in FY 2025 and $63,900 in FY 2026 for the Maryland Department of the Environment to hire one contractual environmental compliance specialist to conduct the required study and submit the report. State and local revenues are unaffected. Local governments and public higher education institutions can consult on the study within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of the Environment is the primary state agency tasked with implementing this legislation. MDE must conduct a comprehensive study on synthetic turf, existing synthetic turf fields, and the synthetic turf industry in the State, and submit a final report to the General Assembly by July 1, 2026.
The legislation specifies that MDE must consult with synthetic turf users, specifically including higher education facilities, in conducting its study regarding turf maintenance, disposal, and use.

As a public higher education institution that operates athletic fields and facilities, Morgan State University is among the higher education facilities that may be consulted by MDE during the synthetic turf study.

As an independent public higher education institution with athletic facilities, Saint Mary's College of Maryland is encompassed within the higher education facilities identified for consultation in MDE's study.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits a court or a party in a criminal or juvenile delinquency case from disclosing or allowing the inspection of an electronic or paper court filing to a nonparty if it includes identifying information of a minor victim, unless all identifying information is redacted or the court finds by clear and convincing evidence that there is good cause to order otherwise.
qa_results.responsible_party: The Maryland Judiciary (District and Circuit Courts) and the Supreme Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Minor victims of crimes or delinquent acts, parties to criminal and juvenile delinquency cases, court clerks and staff, and nonparties or members of the public seeking inspection of court filings.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures and operational impacts for the Judiciary will increase minimally to accommodate the additional clerical time and procedures needed to redact minor victim identifying information from filings. State and local revenues are unaffected, while local circuit courts may experience operational impacts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judiciary and court administration by prohibiting courts from disclosing or allowing inspection of court filings containing minor victim identifying information without redacting such details, creating an operational and clerical workload impact on court staff across District and circuit courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As primary counsel representing defendants in criminal and juvenile delinquency cases, public defenders are parties subject to the bill's restriction prohibiting parties from disclosing or permitting nonparty inspection of filings without redacting minor victim identifying information.
The bill directly applies to filings and proceedings within juvenile delinquency cases, which involve youth and matters overseen by the Department of Juvenile Services.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals and certain prosecutions, making it subject to the bill's requirements when handling case records and court filings involving minor victims.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the State Advisory Council on Quality Care at the End of Life to the State Advisory Council on Serious Illness Care.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging and the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Marylanders facing serious or life-limiting illnesses, healthcare providers, hospice and palliative care organizations, and members of the State Advisory Council on Serious Illness Care.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as renaming the advisory council does not affect state finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 461 directly renames the State Advisory Council on Quality Care at the End of Life to the State Advisory Council on Serious Illness Care.
The Department of Aging is statutory co-staff providing operational support and technical assistance for the Advisory Council, and the Secretary of Aging serves as an ex officio member.

The Office of the Attorney General jointly provides staff support and technical assistance for the Advisory Council, the Attorney General serves as a member, and the agency is statutorily required to consult with the council.
The Advisory Council is established under the Health - General Article, the Secretary of Health is a member, and the council consults on health forms and provides recommendations to the department.
The Secretary of Disabilities or the Secretary's designee is designated by statute as a member of the Advisory Council.
The Governor appoints the council chair and 17 public members, and the council carries out duties requested by the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 464 updates and expands the statutory definition of the practice of audiology in Maryland. It authorizes audiologists to evaluate, diagnose, manage, and treat auditory or vestibular conditions; prescribe, order, sell, dispense, or fit hearing aids and external sound processors for cochlear implants and osseo-integrated devices; conduct health screenings; remove non-impacted cerumen and foreign bodies not requiring anesthesia; order cultures, bloodwork, and radiographic imaging; and perform in-office nonradiographic imaging. The bill explicitly excludes surgical procedures and the performance, operation, or preparation of radiographic imaging from the scope of practice.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed audiologists, patients receiving treatment for auditory or vestibular conditions, and individuals using hearing aids, cochlear implants, or osseo-integrated devices
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected, and the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists can implement the bill and update regulations using existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees health occupations licensing boards, including the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists, which is responsible for implementing the expanded scope of practice and adopting updated regulations.

The Maryland School for the Deaf employs audiologists and provides comprehensive audiological and support services to deaf and hard-of-hearing students, making updates to the statutory scope of practice for audiology relevant to their clinical operations.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees school-based health screenings and special education services, which frequently involve licensed educational audiologists affected by scope-of-practice definitions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum civil penalty from $5,000 to $10,000 for each employee an employer knowingly misclassifies under the Workplace Fraud Act. It also requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to refer complaints alleging specific tax withholding and tax fraud violations to the Comptroller, local State's Attorneys, the U.S. Department of Justice, the U.S. Department of Labor, and the U.S. Department of the Treasury upon a showing of clear and convincing evidence of a workplace fraud or prevailing wage violation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Commissioner of Labor and Industry) and the Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Employers, contractors, and subcontractors (especially in construction, landscaping, and public works), misclassified workers and employees, and tax enforcement authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally starting in FY 2025 due to higher civil penalties and potential tax collections resulting from increased compliance and referrals. General fund expenditures could increase by approximately $88,000 to $100,000 per employee annually if additional tax compliance referrals necessitate hiring new staff within the Comptroller's Office. There is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary implementing and enforcement agency for the bill. Its Commissioner of Labor and Industry is responsible for enforcing the Workplace Fraud Act and Prevailing Wage Law, assessing the increased civil penalties, and making mandatory referrals of alleged tax violations.

The bill requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to refer complaints alleging certain tax violations under the Tax-General Article to the Comptroller for investigation and potential tax compliance enforcement, which may result in additional workload, staffing needs, and tax collections.

Administrative law judges from the Office of Administrative Hearings hear contested misclassification cases under the Workplace Fraud Act and are statutorily charged with applying the specified statutory factors to assess the increased civil penalties of up to $10,000.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland to study and develop recommendations regarding best practices, standards, fire prevention and suppression, extended producer responsibility, and public and first responder education concerning lithium-ion batteries. The commission must provide an interim report by December 1, 2024, and a final report with recommendations by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the State Fire Marshal
qa_results.stakeholders: Lithium-ion and vehicle propulsion battery manufacturers, grid-scale energy storage industry, battery recycling and solid waste operators, public utilities, first responders and firefighters, emergency response personnel, and Maryland consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $64,700 in FY 2025 and $27,600 in FY 2026 for the Office of the State Fire Marshal to hire one contractual management associate to provide staff support and complete the required reports until the bill sunsets. Local government finances and State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM), a division of the Maryland State Police, is tasked with serving on and providing primary staff support for the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety, incurring operating expenditures to hire contractual staff.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly creates a temporary advisory body, the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland, tasked with studying safety standards and making legislative and regulatory recommendations.

The Director of the Maryland Energy Administration appoints three members to the Commission, including an MEA representative and battery manufacturing industry representatives, to examine grid-scale energy storage and battery safety standards.

The Secretary of the Environment is required to appoint a representative to the Commission, which is tasked with studying environmental issues such as lithium-ion battery recycling, decommissioning, and fire suppression at recycling facilities.
The Chairman of the Public Service Commission appoints a representative to the Commission, which will assess battery safety standards for utility applications and grid-scale storage systems.
The Secretary of Natural Resources is required to appoint a representative from the department's Power Plant Research Project to serve on the Commission.
The Commission is mandated to submit its final report containing findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 471 alters postelection procedures in Maryland, including broadening the scope of election documents a local board of canvassers must investigate for errors in consultation with the State Administrator. It modifies procedures for handling member dissents, authorizes the Board of State Canvassers and State Board of Elections to reject inaccurate local statements under clear and convincing evidence, permits members of the Board of State Canvassers to designate specific deputies to serve in their place, and aligns gubernatorial election certification and proclamation procedures with federal law by requiring online publication rather than newspaper notices.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections, the State Administrator of Elections, the Board of State Canvassers, and local boards of canvassers
qa_results.stakeholders: Election officials, members of local and state boards of canvassers, political candidates, and Maryland voters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the responsibilities and timelines for the State Board of Elections and the State Administrator regarding election canvassing, investigating errors, handling dissents, adopting certification regulations, and publishing the Governor's proclamation on its website.

The bill alters postelection responsibilities of the Governor regarding the ascertainment of election results, compliance with received election returns, and the issuance and transmission of certificates of electors under federal law (3 U.S.C. § 5).
The Attorney General is a statutory member of the Board of State Canvassers, and the bill authorizes the Attorney General to appoint the Deputy Attorney General as a designee to serve on the board.
The Comptroller is a member of the Board of State Canvassers, and the bill authorizes the Comptroller to designate the Chief Deputy Comptroller to serve on the board.
The State Treasurer serves on the Board of State Canvassers, and the bill amends the statutory provisions regarding the designation of the deputy treasurer to serve on the board.
The Secretary of State serves on the Board of State Canvassers, and the bill authorizes the appointment of a Deputy Secretary of State as a designee to the board.
The bill affects the Maryland Judicial Branch by authorizing the Clerk of the Supreme Court of Maryland to appoint the Chief Deputy to serve on the Board of State Canvassers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the convening timeline, powers, duties, and membership designee rules of the Board of State Canvassers, an ex-officio state board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the School Mapping Data Program within the Maryland Center for School Safety to provide grant funding to local school systems to produce standardized electronic mapping data of public school facilities and grounds for emergency first responders. It directs the Interagency Commission on School Construction to establish uniform facility mapping standards and exempts school mapping data from public inspection under the Maryland Public Information Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety and the Interagency Commission on School Construction
qa_results.stakeholders: Local school systems, public and charter school students and staff, first responders, and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected; the Maryland Center for School Safety and the Interagency Commission on School Construction can implement the program with existing budgeted resources. Grants will be funded through the existing Safe Schools Fund, which may decrease funds available for other safety programs. Local school system revenues and expenditures will increase to the extent grants are awarded, but there is no net direct effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the School Mapping Data Program within the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS), which administers the program and works with the Interagency Commission on School Construction to ensure data meets facility mapping standards.

The bill explicitly mandates the Interagency Commission on School Construction to adopt facility mapping standards for the uniform mapping of the physical attributes of public schools and consult with MCSS.

MCSS is an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education, and the State Superintendent of Schools chairs the School Safety Subcabinet that directs MCSS and administers the Safe Schools Fund.
The bill specifies the Maryland Department of Emergency Management as one of the authorized public safety entities permitted to inspect confidential school safety and emergency mapping records.
The Department of State Police is statutorily authorized to inspect school emergency plans and mapping records, and the Secretary serves on the School Safety Subcabinet.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is explicitly named as an entity authorized to inspect protected school safety, emergency response, and mapping records under the Public Information Act provisions.
The Comptroller is referenced in existing statutory provisions re-enacted by the bill to account for the Safe Schools Fund in conjunction with the Executive Director of MCSS.
The Treasurer is referenced in existing statutory provisions re-enacted by the bill to hold and invest moneys in the Safe Schools Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Open-Source Phonics Matching Grant Program within the Maryland State Department of Education to award grants to qualifying nonprofit organizations, higher education institutions, and public libraries that provide free, open-source phonics learning materials aligned with the science of reading for adults tutoring students in Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations, higher education institutions, public libraries producing or distributing phonics materials, adult tutors, and Maryland students receiving tutoring in reading and phonics.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $150,000 annually starting in FY 2025 for the grant program. Funding is discretionary in FY 2025 and becomes a mandated annual appropriation of $150,000 beginning in FY 2026. MSDE can administer the program with existing resources. State revenues and local school system finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Open-Source Phonics Matching Grant Program within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). MSDE is responsible for administering the program, disbursing grants, reviewing phonics materials for alignment with the science of reading, and reporting biennially to the General Assembly.
The bill establishes a statutory mandated general fund appropriation of $150,000 annually beginning in FY 2026, which impacts DBM's annual budget preparation and supervision duties.
The bill requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $150,000 for the program in the state budget bill.

The bill defines eligible 'open-source phonics organizations' to include public libraries that produce or distribute free open-source phonics materials, directly touching the network coordinated and supported by the Maryland State Library Agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts forensic genetic genealogical DNA analysis and searches (FGGS) from statutory restrictions and judicial authorization requirements when the analysis is conducted solely to identify a deceased individual or an individual who is the subject of a missing person report whose whereabouts are unknown.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Law enforcement investigators, missing persons, unidentified deceased individuals, and their families.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary statewide law enforcement agency handling criminal investigations, missing persons cases, and unidentified remains, the Maryland State Police utilizes forensic DNA analysis. The bill exempts law enforcement from burdensome judicial authorization and procedural requirements when conducting FGGS solely to identify missing or deceased individuals under the age of 18.

Under existing law, initiating an FGGS requires extensive judicial authorization, sworn affidavits, and regular progress reports submitted to the courts. By exempting FGGS conducted solely to identify missing or deceased minors from these statutory requirements, the bill directly affects court filings and judicial oversight workloads.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender monitors criminal procedure and evidentiary standards regarding genetic privacy, DNA collection, and forensic evidence. Modifications to statutory exemptions governing forensic genetic genealogical searches have relevance to criminal discovery and individual privacy rights.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes individuals to receive a raffle ticket for each antlerless deer hunted during a qualifying January raffle program aimed at hunting antlerless deer, provided the program was held at least once between January 1, 2020, and January 30, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Deer hunters, organizers of qualifying deer hunting raffles, farmers, and small businesses related to hunting and automotive repair.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It may have a potential meaningful impact on small businesses by stimulating hunting-related expenditures and reducing deer-related crop and property damage.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article regarding hunting and the prohibition on bartering or exchanging game mammals, specifically creating an exemption to allow hunters to receive raffle tickets for harvesting antlerless deer. The Department of Natural Resources regulates deer hunting seasons and manages wildlife resources in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a seller of residential real property located within one mile of a National Priorities List (NPL) Superfund site to include a specific addendum in the contract of sale identifying the site, providing links to EPA Superfund websites, and granting the buyer a five-day right of rescission with a full refund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Buyers and sellers of residential real property located within 1.0 mile of an NPL Superfund site, as well as real estate agents and brokers handling those sales.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Small business effect is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE administers the State's Superfund program and oversees hazardous waste site remediation in Maryland, which directly relates to the Superfund sites requiring disclosure under this bill.

MD Labor oversees the Maryland Real Estate Commission, which regulates and licenses real estate agents and brokers responsible for executing standard residential contract forms and disclosure addenda.
The OAG's Consumer Protection Division oversees enforcement against deceptive trade practices in residential real estate disclosures and served as an informational source for the legislation.
The Judiciary and state courts may adjudicate breach of contract or rescission disputes arising from the mandatory disclosure addendum requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends through tax year 2026 the Maryland income tax subtraction modification of up to $1,000 for donations of disposable diapers, infant hygiene products, feminine personal hygiene products, or designated cash to diaper banks and other qualified charitable entities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Individual and corporate taxpayers donating to diaper banks and hygiene distributors, registered diaper banks and shelters, and low-income families and individuals receiving donated diapers and hygiene products.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are estimated to decrease by $250,000 annually in FY 2025 through FY 2027. Special fund revenues and expenditures (HEIF and TTF) may also experience minor decreases to the extent corporations claim the subtraction. Local government revenues are projected to decrease by approximately $165,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027 due to the reduction in local income taxes, with minor potential decreases in local highway user revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the state income tax subtraction modification, registering qualified charitable entities, verifying donation values on tax returns, and adopting regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission to publish the names of candidates for appointment to the Baltimore County Board of Education on its website prior to interviewing them. It also mandates that meetings involving formal action on candidates be open to the public, while meetings involving interviews or deliberations must be held without the public present, recorded, and made available for public inspection within 48 hours of a request.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Candidates applying for appointment to the Baltimore County Board of Education, members of the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, and Baltimore County residents and school community members.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and no effect on local revenues. Baltimore County can handle recording and publishing requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission's sole purpose is to select and recommend qualified candidates to the Governor for appointment to the Baltimore County Board of Education.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in managing appointments to public boards and commissions, which includes processing nominees submitted for gubernatorial appointment to the Baltimore County Board of Education.
The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and the governance statutory frameworks of local school boards under the Education Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill defines 'consent' for sexual crimes as clear and voluntary agreement and establishes that consent, or lack thereof, must be determined based on the totality of circumstances, including words and conduct. It repeals the requirement of force or threat of force from the crime of second-degree rape, thereby establishing that engaging in vaginal intercourse or a sexual act without consent constitutes second-degree rape. The bill also requires the Maryland Judiciary to collect and annually report data on charges and convictions for specified sexual crimes to the General Assembly through April 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals involved in sexual offense cases (victims and defendants), the Maryland Judiciary, State's Attorneys' offices, the Office of the Public Defender, and State correctional facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $7,000 in FY 2025 only for Judiciary information technology costs to meet reporting requirements, with potential additional expenditures if new CJIS codes are needed. General fund expenditures may also increase significantly due to potential increases in second-degree rape prosecutions, incarcerations, and Office of the Public Defender caseloads (OPD projected $476,347 in FY 2025 rising to $654,224 by FY 2029). Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Maryland Judiciary annually track and submit a detailed report to the General Assembly regarding charges and convictions for specified sexual offenses disaggregated by modality, county, offender age, race, and sex. The Administrative Office of the Courts incurs direct information technology costs to implement these reporting requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: By repealing the requirement of force or threat of force from second-degree rape and redefining consent, the bill is anticipated to increase caseloads for public defenders, leading to higher workloads and potential staffing needs to represent indigent defendants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the elements of felony second-degree rape, punishable by up to 20 years of imprisonment. An increase in prosecutions and convictions would directly impact the department through increased state prison populations and incarceration costs for individuals serving sentences over 18 months.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the fee for a nonresident sika deer hunting stamp in Maryland from $25 to $200.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonresident hunters seeking to hunt sika deer in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Net special fund revenues to the Wildlife Management and Protection Fund increase by an estimated $332,200 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 due to the stamp fee increase. Additionally, federal fund revenues are estimated to increase by $996,500 annually beginning in fiscal 2026 through federal matching grants under the Federal Aid in Wildlife Restoration Act. Expenditures are not directly affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for managing Maryland's wildlife resources and issuing hunting licenses and stamps. The bill alters the fee for the nonresident sika deer stamp, directly increasing special fund revenues to DNR's Wildlife Management and Protection Fund and generating additional federal matching grant funds for DNR's Wildlife and Heritage Service.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the annual reporting requirements for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program administered by the Maryland Legal Services Corporation, requiring specific data points such as case counts disaggregated by eviction type, attorney compensation per case, geographic distribution, case dispositions, allocations of state and federal funds to designated organizations, and representation across multiple cases.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Legal Services Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income tenants facing eviction proceedings, designated legal services organizations and attorneys participating in the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program, and the Maryland Legal Services Corporation.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances. The Maryland Legal Services Corporation can implement the modified reporting requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Legal Services Corporation is required to submit the annual Access to Counsel in Evictions Program report directly to the Governor, detailing caseloads, attorney payments, fund allocations, and case disposition metrics.

The bill alters reporting requirements on legal representation and case dispositions in eviction proceedings, which take place throughout the Maryland District Court system overseen by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires owners of private dental offices to designate a licensed dentist as the supervising dentist responsible for all office-wide infection control activities, including water quality testing, spore testing, and adherence to federal CDC guidelines. Supervising dentists must register with the State Board of Dental Examiners, and an interim supervising dentist must be appointed if the position is vacated.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Private dental office owners, licensed dentists designated as supervising dentists, and dental patients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the State Board of Dental Examiners are estimated to increase minimally by approximately $1,500 in FY 2025 and $2,000 annually thereafter from an anticipated $10 registration fee charged when a private dental office changes its designated supervising dentist. The board can implement registration and regulations using existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires private dental offices to designate a supervising dentist responsible for infection control and requires registration with the State Board of Dental Examiners, which is a regulatory health occupation board housed within the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum civil and criminal fines that a charter county may impose to enforce its ordinances, resolutions, bylaws, or regulations from $1,000 to $5,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Charter county governments
qa_results.stakeholders: Charter counties and individuals or businesses subject to local charter county ordinances, regulations, and penalties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, though the Judiciary notes a potential negligible increase in jury trials. Local revenues for charter counties may increase to the extent that individual counties elect to raise civil and criminal fines up to the new $5,000 limit; local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the state judicial system. The bill increases maximum criminal fines for charter county violations, which the Judiciary noted may result in an increase in jury trial prayers, though no significant fiscal or operational impact is expected.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $1.0 million in the State budget for the Maryland Department of Planning to grant to the Maryland Humanities Council for the Marilyn Hatza Memorial Strengthening the Humanities Investment in Nonprofits for Equity (SHINE) Grantmaking Initiative. The council must use the funds to provide general operating grants to small and mid-size humanities, arts, cultural, and educational nonprofit organizations, considering racial and geographic diversity, and submit an annual reporting summary to the Department.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
qa_results.stakeholders: Small and mid-size humanities, arts, cultural, and educational nonprofit organizations in Maryland, as well as the Maryland Humanities Council
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Planning increase by $1.0 million annually beginning in FY 2025 to fund the grant initiative, assuming discretionary funds are provided. The Department can administer the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected.
