agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Planning to receive the annual $1.0 million appropriation and pass it as a grant to the Maryland Humanities Council, as well as receive annual reporting from the Council detailing grant awards and expenditures.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of $1,000,000 in the annual state budget bill for the grantmaking initiative.
As the agency responsible for preparing the Governor's budget and overseeing state appropriations, DBM is affected by potential discretionary funding provisions in the annual budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Morgan State University and St. Mary's College of Maryland to provide mandatory employee sexual harassment prevention training through webinar, computer-based, or online formats, provided the training includes an evaluative component that ensures engagement and assesses comprehension.
qa_results.responsible_party: Morgan State University and St. Mary's College of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Employees, supervisors, and administrators at Morgan State University and St. Mary's College of Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes Morgan State University to provide required employee sexual harassment prevention training via webinar, computer-based, or online training formats with an evaluative component.

The bill explicitly authorizes St. Mary's College of Maryland to offer mandatory employee sexual harassment prevention training through webinar, computer-based, or online training formats with an evaluative component.

The bill amends the statute governing USM's training delivery authority to extend the same online and computer-based sexual harassment training flexibilities already afforded to USM to Morgan State University and St. Mary's College of Maryland.
The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights coordinates with state entities regarding the implementation and content of state-mandated sexual harassment prevention training.

As the central personnel agency managing state employee training requirements and enforcing statewide Equal Employment Opportunity standards, DBM oversees compliance with state employee training statutes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing bodies of Allegany County, Garrett County, and municipalities located within those counties to grant a local property tax credit of up to $10,000 over five taxable years for newly constructed residential dwellings that meet specified criteria.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing bodies of Allegany County and Garrett County, and municipal corporations located within Allegany and Garrett counties
qa_results.stakeholders: Homebuyers purchasing newly constructed homes in Allegany and Garrett counties, residential builders/developers, and local governments within Allegany and Garrett counties.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Local property tax revenues for Allegany County, Garrett County, and eligible municipalities will decrease beginning as early as FY 2025 to the extent local credits are granted. The exact decrease depends on local enactment; for illustrative purposes, if all newly constructed single-family homes received the maximum credit, revenues could decrease in FY 2025 by $95,000 in Allegany County and $715,000 in Garrett County, growing to $690,000 and $3,600,000 respectively by FY 2029.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of child abuse in laws governing Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) cases and mandatory child abuse and neglect reporting to include labor trafficking by any individual. It requires local departments of social services to refer suspected child labor trafficking victims to regional navigators and expands the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program and its services, including housing, to cover child victims of labor trafficking.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services and local departments of social services
qa_results.stakeholders: Child victims of labor trafficking, children involved in CINA proceedings, local departments of social services, mandatory reporters of child abuse, and victim service provider grantees under the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances. Although it expands the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program to serve labor trafficking victims, it does not mandate additional State grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS oversees local departments of social services, which investigate reports of suspected child abuse and neglect, make referrals to regional navigators for labor trafficking victims, and are required under the bill to submit annual data reports on child labor trafficking cases to the Governor and General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP administers the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program, which is expanded by the bill to cover child victims of labor trafficking, and requires the Executive Director to submit biennial evaluation reports on grantee services.
The bill amends the definition of abuse in Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) proceedings heard in the state's juvenile courts to include child labor trafficking.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent parents and children involved in CINA cases in juvenile court and is statutorily designated to coordinate with regional navigators under the Safe Harbor program.
DJS is explicitly enumerated in the statute as an agency required to coordinate with regional navigators to respond to and facilitate services for youth victims of trafficking.

The Governor receives mandated annual reporting from DHS regarding child sex and labor trafficking cases and dispositions, as well as biennial evaluation reports on the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the eligible recipients of funding under the Department of Housing and Community Development's Business Facade Improvement Program to include qualifying community development organizations that serve at least one sustainable community.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Community development organizations, local governments (political subdivisions), and businesses located in designated sustainable communities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Overall State finances for the Business Facade Improvement Program are not affected, and the Department of Housing and Community Development can administer the program expansion using existing budgeted resources. For local governments, funding availability may decrease to the extent that eligible community development organizations apply for and are awarded program funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Business Facade Improvement Program administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), expanding eligible funding recipients to include community development organizations and requiring the department to establish corresponding application and rating criteria.
The statute mandates the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $5,000,000 for the Business Facade Improvement Program in the annual state budget bill.
As the principal agency responsible for state budget preparation and execution, DBM oversees the inclusion and allocation of the mandated $5,000,000 annual appropriation for the program.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies reporting requirements for individuals and businesses licensed or regulated by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to pack, deal in, or catch fish resources, as well as those holding recreational angler or coastal sport fishing licenses, requiring them to submit reports in accordance with DNR regulations rather than specifically on department-prescribed paper forms.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial fish packers and dealers, licensed commercial fishers, licensed recreational anglers, and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct effect on State or local finances. Any potential future costs associated with expanding electronic reporting systems would depend on how the regulations are implemented and will be evaluated when regulations are proposed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article to alter fish and fisheries reporting requirements, authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to adopt regulations governing reporting by licensed fishers, packers, dealers, and recreational anglers.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Road Worker Protection Act of 2024 updates the State's work zone speed control system program. It increases civil penalty fines from a maximum of $40 to $80 effective June 1, 2024, and implements a tiered penalty structure from $60 to $500 (doubled when workers are present) effective January 1, 2025. The bill expands the types of highways where work zone speed cameras may be placed, authorizes local governments to deploy them, clarifies that operators need not be present, permits multiple camera systems within a single work zone, mandates specific work zone signage and flashing blue lights, and alters the distribution of fine revenues among the State Highway Administration, the Department of State Police, and the Transportation Trust Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Highway Administration and the Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists traveling through highway work zones, roadway and utility construction and maintenance workers, law enforcement personnel, and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by an estimated $15.8 million in FY 2025 and $16.9 million in FY 2026 due to higher and tiered penalties and expanded system deployment, tapering down to $13.1 million by FY 2029 as compliance improves. Special fund expenditures for administration and implementation increase by $4.2 million in FY 2025 and $4.4 million annually thereafter; remaining revenues are allocated 25% to the Department of State Police for vehicles/equipment and 75% to the Transportation Trust Fund for work zone safety and State Highway Administration system preservation. General fund revenues increase indeterminately from contested District Court citations. Local revenues and expenditures may increase significantly beginning in FY 2025 if local jurisdictions implement work zone speed cameras under the expanded authority.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Highway Administration is directly responsible for implementing and administering work zone speed control systems, receives revenue distributions for system preservation and administrative costs, is required to submit annual reports on pilot programs and technology, and jointly adopts regulations with the Department of State Police.

The Department of State Police jointly administers the work zone speed control program with the State Highway Administration, adopts program regulations, and receives dedicated revenue distributions for administrative costs and replacement police vehicles and equipment.

The Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the Transportation Trust Fund (which receives 75% of residual fine revenue for highway and work zone safety) and is required to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly on the expenditure of these funds.
The District Court must prescribe the uniform citation form, establish prepayment amounts, and adjudicate an anticipated increase in contested citations, collecting penalties in contested cases.
The Comptroller receives civil fines collected under the Maryland Vehicle Law and is specifically directed by statute to distribute work zone speed camera revenues to the dedicated special fund.
The Motor Vehicle Administration receives additional Transportation Trust Fund revenues via flag fees placed on vehicle registrations for unpaid work zone citations.
The bill is an Administration initiative resulting from the Governor's Work Zone Safety Work Group, and mandates annual reports from SHA and MDOT to the Governor.

The Lieutenant Governor coordinates work zone safety initiatives (including the Governor's Work Zone Safety Work Group that originated this legislation) and prepared the small business economic impact evaluation for the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup to Study the Fiscal and Operational Viability of Public–Private Partnerships for Calvert County Public Schools to study and make recommendations on using public-private partnerships for financing, constructing, maintaining, and operating public schools in Calvert County.
qa_results.responsible_party: Calvert County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Calvert County Public Schools students, staff, school administrators, and Calvert County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances. Local expenditures for Calvert County Public Schools may increase for temporary staffing or consultant support to assist the workgroup, though a reliable dollar estimate is not feasible; there is no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Chair of the Interagency Commission on School Construction (or designee) as a member of the Workgroup and requires the Workgroup to submit its final report to the Commission.
The bill designates the Executive Director of the Maryland Stadium Authority (or designee) as a member of the Workgroup to provide expertise on alternative financing and construction delivery models.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary advisory body, the Workgroup to Study the Fiscal and Operational Viability of Public–Private Partnerships for Calvert County Public Schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: Allows complaints alleging real estate advertising violations submitted to the State Real Estate Commission to be made anonymously and without being under oath, provided the complaint is accompanied by documentary or other evidence.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons, members of the public filing advertising complaints, and the State Real Estate Commission.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or operations, though additional staff may be required if a significant number of additional complaints are submitted. It has no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Real Estate Commission is housed and administered under the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill directly alters complaint filing requirements for advertising violations handled and investigated by the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health to jointly develop State guidelines by December 31, 2024, regarding public middle and high school student participation in telehealth appointments during the school day. It also requires each county board of education to adopt and implement a student telehealth policy based on these guidelines prior to the 2025-2026 school year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Public middle and high school students, parents and guardians, school nurses, school-based health and behavioral health providers, school administrators, and health care providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2025 only for the Maryland State Department of Education to obtain contractual support to consult stakeholders and develop the State guidelines. The Maryland Department of Health can handle implementation with existing resources. Local boards of education can adopt and implement the required policies with existing budgeted resources, though local school systems may experience operational or space challenges. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 522 directly tasks the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), jointly with the Maryland Department of Health, to develop State guidelines for student participation in telehealth appointments during the school day. The State Board of Education must adopt the guidelines, and MSDE is required to provide technical assistance to local school boards. The fiscal note indicates an expenditure increase of $100,000 in FY 2025 for MSDE to procure contractual support.

HB 522 directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), jointly with the Department of Education, to develop State guidelines for school health services concerning student access to telehealth appointments in public middle and high schools, including consulting with stakeholders on operational, clinical, and privacy matters.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 528 modifies and standardizes restrictions on orphans' court judges practicing law, repealing county-specific exceptions to apply a uniform statewide rule. Under the bill, an orphans' court judge is prohibited from acting as an attorney during their term of office in civil or criminal matters related to the administration of an estate or guardianship of a minor within the court's jurisdiction, or in preparing estate planning documents that may fall under the court's jurisdiction upon an individual's death.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary (Maryland Orphans' Courts and Orphans' Court Judges)
qa_results.stakeholders: Orphans' court judges who are licensed attorneys, their prospective legal clients, and individuals involved in estate planning, estate administration, or minor guardianship matters across Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Department of Legislative Services Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill has no State fiscal effect and does not directly affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative, legal, and operational support to Maryland's judicial branch. The bill alters statutory ethical and practice restrictions governing orphans' court judges across the state.

The Register of Wills serves as the clerk to the Orphans' Court and oversees the administrative probate of estates and records of probate proceedings, which are directly related to the court matters and estate proceedings addressed by the practice restrictions in this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that the Maryland Parole Commission assess a monthly $50 supervision fee against individuals on parole supervised by the Division of Parole and Probation, as well as the authorization to require parole supervisees to pay for ordered drug and alcohol abuse testing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (specifically the Maryland Parole Commission and the Division of Parole and Probation)
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals placed on parole under the supervision of the Division of Parole and Probation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by at least $53,931 in FY 2025 and by at least $71,908 annually thereafter due to the repeal of the supervision fee. State general fund expenditures increase, potentially significantly, starting in FY 2025 to cover drug and alcohol testing vendor contracts previously offset by supervisee fees. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Central Collection Unit decrease due to fewer debt referrals. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends operations of the Division of Parole and Probation and the Maryland Parole Commission—both units of DPSCS—by repealing the monthly $50 parole supervision fee and the requirement for parolees to pay for drug and alcohol abuse testing. This results in an expenditure increase for DPSCS to cover vendor testing contracts and eliminates fee collection duties.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU), a division of DBM, collects unpaid delinquent parole supervision fees and retains a 17% fee for its operating expenses. Repealing the supervision fee decreases debt referrals to CCU, resulting in a direct reduction in special fund revenues and expenditures for the agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Live Near Your School program and an associated homebuyer assistance program administered by the Community Development Administration from September 30, 2024, to September 30, 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Community Development Administration within the Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Current students and recent graduates of public institutions of higher education in Maryland seeking homeownership assistance near their schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances. Proposed mandatory appropriations were removed, and the Department of Housing and Community Development does not currently operate the programs due to a lack of existing funding and institutional partner interest.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Community Development Administration (CDA) is housed within the Department of Housing and Community Development. The bill directly extends the statutory authorization and sunset date of the Live Near Your School Program and related homebuyer assistance programs administered by CDA.

The Live Near Your School program and related homebuyer assistance program specifically target students and recent graduates of Maryland public institutions of higher education, authorizing these institutions to coordinate and provide matching funds.

As an independent public institution of higher education in Maryland, Morgan State University's students and recent graduates are eligible for the extended homebuyer assistance programs, and the university is authorized to provide matching funds under the program framework.

As an independent public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland has students and graduates eligible under the program and possesses statutory authorization to partner and provide matching funds under the extended program.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Housing Expansion and Affordability Act of 2024 requires local jurisdictions to permit manufactured homes and modular dwellings in single-family residential zones under certain conditions, and mandates density bonuses and mixed-use flexibility for qualified affordable housing developments (such as projects on former state or federal military land, near rail transit stations, or owned/controlled by nonprofits). The bill also limits local governments from imposing unreasonable zoning barriers or requiring excessive public hearings on qualified projects, mandates a public health impact assessment for developments in nonresidential zones, and establishes the Historic Property Revitalization Director within the Department of Housing and Community Development.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
qa_results.stakeholders: Low- and moderate-income residents seeking affordable housing, housing developers, nonprofit organizations, manufactured and modular home builders, and local government planning and zoning bodies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $73,700 in FY 2025, reflecting the January 1, 2025 effective date, and range between $130,200 and $148,100 annually in FY 2026 through FY 2029 to fund salary, benefits, and operating expenses for one Historic Property Revitalization Director position within DHCD. State revenues are not directly affected. Local governments may see varied fiscal impacts: administrative costs may increase if additional staff or contractors are needed for review and inspection processes (partially offset by local permit and development fees), and infrastructure expenditures could accelerate or increase if density exceeds existing local infrastructure capacity.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary state implementing agency for the bill; it houses the newly created Historic Property Revitalization Director position, evaluates and approves public health impact assessments for certain qualified affordable housing projects, and must promulgate implementing regulations.
The bill explicitly directs the new Historic Property Revitalization Director to coordinate with the DGS Office of Real Estate during the disposition of state-owned property.

MDP leads state comprehensive land use policy, houses the Maryland Historical Trust (which manages historic property designations and registers referenced in the bill), and plays a key role on the Smart Growth Subcabinet with which the new director must collaborate.

Commerce is explicitly required by the bill to collaborate with the Historic Property Revitalization Director and the Smart Growth Subcabinet to identify state and federal financing mechanisms and programs to facilitate property redevelopment.

The bill establishes transit-oriented affordable housing density requirements within three-quarters of a mile of rail stations (including MARC, Baltimore Metro, Light Rail, and Metrorail stations), directly impacting transit-oriented development around MDOT infrastructure.
This is a key Administration bill focusing on housing expansion and smart growth priorities, involving interagency coordination through the Smart Growth Subcabinet within the executive branch.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the Cameron Carden Act of 2024, requiring each Maryland public institution of higher education to adopt a policy allowing students to withdraw for extenuating circumstances—including illness, injury, hospitalization, and mental health and wellness—and providing a refund of tuition and fees paid by the student for that semester if the circumstances inhibit their ability to acquire an education.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland public institutions of higher education, including the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, Baltimore City Community College, and local community colleges
qa_results.stakeholders: Students attending Maryland public four-year universities and community colleges who experience extenuating circumstances, as well as public colleges and universities across the state
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Higher education revenues for the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, Baltimore City Community College, and local community colleges will decrease, potentially significantly, due to refunding tuition and fees to qualifying withdrawing students; however, the exact impact cannot be reliably estimated. Higher education expenditures are not materially affected, as institutions can implement the required policies with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires all public institutions of higher education, including constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland, to adopt a student withdrawal policy for extenuating circumstances and issue refunds for tuition and fees, resulting in a potentially significant decrease in higher education revenues.

As an independent public four-year institution of higher education, Morgan State University is directly required to establish a withdrawal policy for extenuating circumstances and refund tuition and fees to qualifying students, which will decrease institutional revenues.

As a public honors college and state institution of higher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland must adopt the mandated withdrawal and refund policy, resulting in potential decreases in tuition and fee revenues.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission is the state's coordinating and regulatory agency for higher education policies and institutions, and it provided information and oversight context regarding statewide public higher education policies affected by this act.

As the statewide coordinating body for public colleges and universities, the commission provides policy leadership and coordination over public higher education institutions required to implement the withdrawal and tuition refund policy.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Anne Arundel County to establish the Anne Arundel County Student Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Educators to assist in the repayment of higher education loans for qualified educators employed by Anne Arundel County Public Schools who commit to serve for at least five years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Public School System
qa_results.stakeholders: Educators employed by the Anne Arundel County Public School System (including classroom teachers, education support professionals, education-related service providers, and eligible specialists) and students within the county school system.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Simply authorizing the program does not impact finances; however, if Anne Arundel County elects to establish and fund the program, county expenditures will increase based on amounts appropriated annually in the county budget separately from the school board's operating budget. Local revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines eligible educators in part based on certification standards set by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), though MSDE has no administrative or fiscal role in this county-run program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to establish, maintain, and distribute a decentralized supply of new luggage (such as backpacks, duffels, or suitcases) for children entering, moving between, or exiting foster care placements, while prohibiting the use of trash bags or disposable bags for transporting their personal belongings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Children in foster care, foster parents, and local departments of social services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $120,500 in FY 2025, which includes an estimated $84,480 to purchase new luggage for approximately 2,816 children and $36,000 in one-time costs to update the MD THINK reporting platform. General fund expenditures of at least $84,500 continue annually thereafter. Donations of luggage may reduce costs. Local departments of social services can likely handle implementation with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of Human Services (DHS) to establish and maintain a decentralized supply of new luggage for children in foster care, prohibits the use of disposable or trash bags for transporting their belongings, requires recordkeeping and annual reporting, and results in direct general fund expenditures for luggage purchases and IT updates.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the statute of limitations for prosecuting sexual extortion to 5 years and stalking to 10 years, and allows the State to prosecute revenge porn offenses at any time without a statute of limitations. It also restricts public inspection of visual representations depicting victims in court records for revenge porn cases and permits defendants convicted of revenge porn to seek in banc review.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, State's Attorneys, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of sexual extortion, stalking, and nonconsensual pornography (revenge porn), criminal defendants, prosecutors, law enforcement agencies, and state and local correctional facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues and expenditures may increase minimally beginning in FY 2026. The extension of the statute of limitations may result in a minimal increase in fine collections in the District Court (State) and circuit courts (local), as well as minimal increases in incarceration costs for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and local detention centers. Specific dollar amounts were not quantified.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the statute of limitations for sexual extortion and stalking, and eliminates it for revenge porn, potentially increasing the number of convictions and subsequent incarcerations in state correctional facilities, leading to a minimal increase in incarceration expenditures.

The bill impacts court caseloads and in banc reviews by expanding prosecution timelines, and mandates procedural protections restricting public inspection of sensitive visual representations contained within court records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The extension and elimination of the statute of limitations for these misdemeanor offenses may result in additional indigent criminal defense cases and increased caseloads for the office.

The Attorney General or their designee is specifically enumerated as an authorized party permitted to inspect restricted visual representations in court records for revenge porn prosecutions, and the office represents the State in appellate proceedings resulting from in banc reviews or convictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award within the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program to include public school nurses who have at least two years of experience providing health services in public schools, and requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to publicize the program to public school nurses to aid recruitment and retention.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission (specifically the Office of Student Financial Assistance)
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school nurses, local school systems, local health departments, and Maryland public school students.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $753,000 in FY 2025, reflecting a $750,000 contingent general fund appropriation to fund loan assistance repayment awards for approximately 115 public school nurses and $3,000 in one-time computer software enhancement costs for the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Expanding eligibility does not mandate out-year spending increases, and state revenues are not affected. There is no local fiscal impact, though public schools may benefit from improved nurse recruitment and retention.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC (through the Office of Student Financial Assistance) is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program and the Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award, modifying the MDCAPS application system, and publicizing the program to public school nurses.

MHEC directly administers the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program and receives the $750,000 appropriation to distribute loan repayment assistance awards to eligible public school nurses.
The bill explicitly includes public school nurses employed by local health departments that provide school health services under agreements with county boards of education.
The bill directly addresses staffing and retention of public school nurses across Maryland's public school systems overseen by MSDE.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances to study and make recommendations regarding the scientific benefits, public health risks, therapeutic access, and potential decriminalization of natural psychedelic substances like psilocybin, psilocin, DMT, and mescaline, requiring a report of findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by July 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients seeking psychedelic therapies, healthcare practitioners, researchers, individuals with nonviolent criminal records related to psychedelic substances, and law enforcement.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational expenditures are minimally affected, as the Maryland Cannabis Administration can provide staffing using existing budgeted resources, and any task force travel expense reimbursements are absorbable within existing resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 548 directly designates the Maryland Cannabis Administration to provide staff support for the newly established Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances, and the MCA Director serves as a statutory member.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances as an executive task force to study psychedelic policies, regulations, and access models, and report recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.
The Governor is required to appoint numerous members of the Task Force, designate the chair, and receive the final report of findings and recommendations by July 31, 2025.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Task Force to examine the public health and therapeutic implications of natural psychedelic substances.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Task Force to consider access to treatment and potential disability-related benefits or impacts.

The Secretary of Veterans Affairs (now Veterans & Military Families) or designee is designated as a statutory member of the Task Force to explore potential therapeutic benefits for veterans (e.g., PTSD and trauma treatment).
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing appointments for the numerous stakeholder and expert seats required on the Task Force.
The Governor may appoint a representative of the University System of Maryland to serve on the Task Force to provide academic and scientific research expertise.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires citations and warning notices issued under automated enforcement systems—such as red light cameras, speed monitoring systems, school bus cameras, work zone speed systems, bus lane systems, toll facilities, and vehicle height systems—to be mailed to the recipient's current mailing address on file with the Motor Vehicle Administration, or to their current residential address if a mailing address is unavailable.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered motor vehicle owners receiving automated traffic citations or video toll notices, and state and local law enforcement and transportation agencies administering automated enforcement systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can make the required reprogramming changes using existing resources. State revenues and local government finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that automated enforcement citations and notices be sent using the current mailing address (or residential address if unavailable) on file with the Administration (MVA). The MVA maintains these address records and may require system reprogramming to ensure appropriate address data sharing.

The bill directly amends provisions governing the Maryland Transportation Authority's collection of video tolls, requiring the Authority or its agent to use the MVA mailing address or residential address when issuing notices of toll due and civil citations.

The bill specifically requires the State Police Department (or its contractors), when issuing citations or warning notices for work zone speed control systems, to use the current mailing or residential address on file with the MVA.
MDOT is the parent department over the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the state's transportation network and vehicle laws affected by this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the sales and use tax exemption for materials, parts, and equipment used to repair, maintain, or upgrade qualifying aircraft and avionics systems through June 30, 2030, and repeals the annual reporting requirement by the Comptroller regarding revenue loss and employment of aviation technicians.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Aircraft owners, aviation maintenance and repair businesses, aviation technicians, and vendors of aircraft parts and equipment
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and special fund (Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund) revenues will continue to decrease through FY 2030 due to extending the sales and use tax exemption. Specific dollar estimates of the revenue loss are unavailable. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state's sales and use tax. The bill directly impacts the Comptroller by extending the sales and use tax exemption on certain aircraft parts and equipment through 2030 and repealing the requirement that the Comptroller submit an annual report to the General Assembly regarding the revenue lost and employment changes resulting from the exemption.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes statutory fee caps for tree expert licenses—up to $45 for an examination, $55 for initial licensure, and $100 for license renewal—rather than limiting fees to processing costs. It also mandates that licensees or employers carry and show proof of workers' compensation insurance for supervised employees, authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to suspend or revoke licenses for failure to maintain required insurance, and requires the Department's annual tree expert report to be submitted to the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed tree experts, applicants for tree expert licensure, tree care and arboriculture businesses, and their supervised employees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues deposited into the Forest and Park Reserve Fund are expected to increase minimally starting as early as FY 2025, as the Department of Natural Resources plans to increase licensing fees via regulation within the new statutory caps. While the bill does not mandate additional expenditures, DNR intends to use the increased revenue to partially fund an additional staff position. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Department of Natural Resources' (DNR) licensing of tree experts. It authorizes DNR to adopt regulations, alters statutory caps on examination and licensing fees collected by the department, establishes an annual reporting requirement to the General Assembly, and allows DNR to suspend or revoke licenses for failure to maintain required insurance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the annual fee for a nonresident applicant purchasing a special Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing license from $50 to $100.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonresident recreational anglers and boat owners fishing in the Chesapeake Bay and Maryland coastal waters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund (Fisheries Research and Development Fund) revenues increase by $359,500 in FY 2025 (reflecting the October 1, 2024 effective date) and by $460,900 annually thereafter due to the fee increase from $50 to $100 for nonresidents. State expenditures and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for administering and issuing the special Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing license, and the fee increase will directly generate special fund revenue for DNR's Fisheries Research and Development Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 565 requires the Department of State Police to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly and publish it online by December 31. The report must detail the number of completed investigations into suspected homicide deaths of individuals in the custody of the Division of Correction, as well as the number of those cases referred for prosecution.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals in Division of Correction custody, their families, the Department of State Police, and correctional administration.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not significantly affected because the Department of State Police can implement the bill's annual reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of State Police post an annual report on its website and submit it to the Governor and General Assembly detailing investigations of suspected homicides of incarcerated individuals and related prosecution referrals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The investigations and subsequent annual reporting specifically concern individuals who die while in the custody of the Division of Correction, an agency under the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
The Department of State Police is statutorily required to submit its annual report regarding suspected homicide investigations in correctional custody directly to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Online Data Privacy Act of 2024 establishes comprehensive regulations governing how businesses (controllers and processors) collect, use, and process consumers' personal data. It grants Maryland residents rights regarding their personal data, including the right to access, correct, delete, obtain a copy of, and opt out of targeted advertising, sale of personal data, or certain profiling. It also prohibits the sale of sensitive data, restricts geofencing around mental health and reproductive health facilities, mandates data protection assessments, and makes violations an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice enforceable by the Consumer Protection Division.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers whose personal data is collected and processed, as well as businesses, controllers, processors, and third-party data handlers operating in or targeting consumers in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures will likely increase, at least minimally, beginning in FY 2026 for the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division to enforce the Act; the OAG estimated costs of up to $390,900 in FY 2026 and $539,200 by FY 2030 for four new positions, though the Department of Legislative Services notes actual costs will depend on complaint volume. State revenues and local government finances are not expected to be materially impacted by penalty provisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates violations of the Maryland Online Data Privacy Act as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General. OAG is responsible for investigating violations, reviewing data protection assessments, issuing cure notices, and pursuing enforcement actions.

The bill authorizes civil enforcement actions under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which may be adjudicated in state courts supported administratively by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Credit for All Language Learning (CALL) Act requires public community colleges in Maryland to consider non-remedial English as a Second Language (ESL) or English language learner courses as eligible for world language or humanities elective credit toward an associate degree. The bill also mandates that these credits be transferable to any public institution of higher education in the State without denial, and requires private nonprofit institutions of higher education to review and consider them for transfer credit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission, public community colleges, and public institutions of higher education
qa_results.stakeholders: Community college students taking ESL or English language learner courses, public community colleges, and public and private nonprofit higher education institutions in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Public four-year institutions of higher education and local community colleges can implement the credit evaluation and transfer requirements using existing resources. State and local higher education revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is responsible for establishing and updating the statewide transfer agreement in collaboration with public higher education institutions to require that non-remedial ESL course credits earned at community colleges transfer to public institutions.
Duplicate entry for MHEC; responsible for the statewide transfer agreement and higher education transfer policy under the bill.
USM institutions are public senior higher education institutions directly required by the bill to accept qualifying non-remedial ESL credits transferred from community colleges without denial.
As an independent public four-year university, Morgan State University is mandated under the bill to accept qualifying transfer credits for non-remedial ESL courses from community colleges.

As a public senior higher education institution, St. Mary's College of Maryland is subject to the statewide transfer agreement mandate prohibiting the denial of qualifying ESL course transfer credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Program by delaying the implementation schedule, altering administrative and enforcement procedures, updating wage and covered employee definitions, and authorizing the Maryland Department of Labor to set application and renewal fees for private employer plans. Notably, it delays required program contributions by nine months to July 1, 2025, and benefit payments by six months to July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers, covered employees, self-employed individuals, health and community service providers, and private plan insurers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State FAMLI special fund revenues decrease by up to $915.5 million in FY 2025 and $457.8 million in FY 2026 due to the delay in contribution collections, while special fund expenditures for benefit payments decrease by up to $869.4 million in FY 2026. As an employer, the State saves up to $26.1 million across all funds in FY 2025 and up to $8.9 million in FY 2026. General fund expenditures decrease by $12.4 million in FY 2025 due to delayed provider reimbursements. Beginning in FY 2026, special fund revenues will increase from private plan fees and assessed appeal costs. Local government employer contributions are also delayed until July 1, 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary implementing agency for the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Program. The bill modifies core operational timelines, sets contribution rates, authorizes application and renewal fees for private employer plans, alters claims and appeals administration, and expands the Secretary's grant-making and enforcement authority.

The Maryland Department of Health is statutorily required to reimburse certain licensed community and health service providers for the employer share of FAMLI contributions. The bill's delay of FAMLI implementation results in a direct general fund expenditure decrease of $12.4 million for MDH in fiscal year 2025.

As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and fiscal planning. The bill's delay in employer contributions results in significant expenditure savings for the State as an employer across all fund types in FY 2025 and FY 2026, and impacts decisions regarding whether the State will self-insure.
The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates insurers issuing private paid leave insurance policies that employers may use to satisfy the statutory requirements of the FAMLI Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the membership of the Citizens Committee for the Enhancement of Communities Surrounding Baltimore-Washington International (BWI) Thurgood Marshall Airport from 11 to 12 members. It alters the appointment recommendations so that instead of one member recommended by District 12 delegates, one member is recommended by the District 12A delegates and one member is recommended by the District 12B delegate.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of Transportation / Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and community associations in legislative districts 12A, 12B, 13, and 32 situated within or within two miles of the certified noise zone of BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) staffs the Citizens Committee for the Enhancement of Communities Surrounding BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport, and the Secretary of Transportation is responsible for appointing its members and reviewing its project funding recommendations.

The Maryland Aviation Administration, a modal administration within MDOT, owns and operates BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport and manages matters relating to the certified airport noise zones addressed by this committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory membership composition of a permanent state advisory committee established to evaluate livability and transportation issues in communities surrounding BWI airport.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Victim Compensation Reform Act of 2024 alters the composition and procedures of the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board, broadens eligibility criteria for victims and their dependents, expands reimbursable expenses and eligible crimes, increases maximum award limits for various compensation categories, establishes streamlined emergency award procedures, and authorizes the Governor to include appropriations in the annual State budget to maintain the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund balance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Criminal Injuries Compensation Board within the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of crime, surviving family members, domestic partners, dependents, and victim service organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase significantly starting in FY 2026 to support expanded victim compensation and administrative costs, including $975,585 for 11 new positions and related operating expenses. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund increase correspondingly. Federal fund revenues and expenditures increase beginning in FY 2028 from federal matching grant funding. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Criminal Injuries Compensation Board (CICB) is housed directly within the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy. The bill substantially reforms the board's composition, powers, claim procedures, award limits, and eligibility criteria, resulting in a significant administrative and fiscal impact on the agency.

HB 575 is an Administration bill that alters the appointment of CICB board members (requiring gubernatorial approval), mandates annual reporting to the Governor, and authorizes the Governor to include appropriations in the annual budget bill to support the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund.

The bill allows claimants to file petitions for judicial review of board reconsideration decisions under Title 7 of the Maryland Rules, and court costs collected in criminal/traffic proceedings continue to serve as a primary revenue source for the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund.

The bill specifies that the board may request investigation records and information from the Department of State Police and requires law enforcement units to provide written information to crime victims regarding victim compensation.
Section 11-819 of the Criminal Procedure Article explicitly designates that the Comptroller shall account for the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund.
Section 11-819 of the Criminal Procedure Article explicitly designates that the Treasurer shall separately hold and invest the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund.
The Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund remains expressly subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits under statutory provisions re-enacted in the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes a statutory framework for Assisted Outpatient Treatment (AOT) programs across Maryland. It allows counties to establish their own AOT programs overseen by a local behavioral health authority or core service agency, or partner with other counties, and requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to establish an AOT program in any county that opts not to create one by July 1, 2026. The bill defines criteria and judicial procedures for petitions, treatment plans developed by multidisciplinary care coordination teams, circuit court hearings, respondent rights, legal representation by the Office of the Public Defender, and mandatory annual reporting.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with serious and persistent mental illness, their families and legal guardians, community mental health providers, county behavioral health authorities and core service agencies, circuit courts, and the Office of the Public Defender.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $3.0 million in FY 2025 due to a contingent budget appropriation. In FY 2026, general fund expenditures increase by at least $291,700, including $158,489 for MDH personnel and $133,209 in one-time programming costs for the Judiciary, with subsequent years reflecting personnel inflation. Additional indeterminate state costs will arise for MDH to establish programs in counties that do not establish their own, for the Office of the Public Defender to handle representation and expert witness costs, and for Medicaid. Local government expenditures and revenues will increase from FY 2026 through FY 2030 depending on whether counties operate local programs (estimated at $250,000 to $5.0 million annually per jurisdiction), partially offset by reimbursements for billable services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH (specifically through the Behavioral Health Administration) is a primary implementing agency tasked with establishing assisted outpatient treatment (AOT) programs in counties that choose not to establish their own, setting clinical and operational standards for programs and care coordination teams, and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Criminal Procedure Article to mandate that the Office of the Public Defender provide legal representation to eligible indigent individuals in all assisted outpatient treatment proceedings, resulting in significant staffing and expert witness fiscal impacts.

The circuit courts are responsible for adjudicating petitions, holding hearings, and issuing and modifying AOT court orders under seal. The Administrative Office of the Courts will oversee case administration and requires judicial information system software programming to prevent public disclosure on Maryland Judiciary Case Search.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Study on the Establishment of a Homeless Shelter Licensing Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). The bill requires DHCD to hire one full-time permanent employee to review current habitability and admission standards of homeless shelters in Maryland, recommend basic standards, and develop a plan to implement a shelter licensing program, reporting findings to the General Assembly by July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeless individuals and shelter residents, homeless shelter owners and operators, and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $77,900 in FY 2025 (reflecting a 90-day start-up delay) for DHCD to hire one permanent full-time program officer to conduct the study. Ongoing costs continue in out-years ($92,700 in FY 2026, increasing to $105,500 in FY 2029) because the position is statutory and permanent, despite the bill's July 31, 2025 termination date. State revenues are unaffected, and local government finances are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to conduct a study on establishing a homeless shelter licensing program, hire a new full-time permanent employee, and report findings and recommendations to the Assistant Secretary of its Homeless Solutions Division and the General Assembly.

The Department of Human Services is the primary state agency assisting residents who are in economic need or facing homelessness; the study's review and recommendations regarding shelter habitability and admissions standards directly intersect with DHS's core mission and clients.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Time to Serve Act of 2024 increases the maximum amount of disaster service leave an Executive Branch employee may use in a 12-month period from 15 days to 30 days. It also increases the maximum amount of paid leave the Secretary of Budget and Management may provide for uniformed services training or active duty in the military reserves or organized militia from 15 days to 30 days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland State Executive Branch employees, State employees serving in the military reserves or organized militia, and certified disaster or volunteer emergency service workers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not anticipated to be materially affected because regular employee salaries are already budgeted and temporary staff are generally not hired for coverage. However, agencies with shift coverage needs, such as the Maryland State Police and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, may incur minimal overtime costs absorbable within existing resources. There is no effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the primary implementing agency. The bill specifically authorizes the Secretary of Budget and Management to provide by regulation up to 30 days of paid leave for uniformed services training or active duty, and DBM oversees executive branch personnel policies, leave systems, and employee administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is specifically cited in the fiscal note as an agency likely to experience an operational impact and potential overtime costs to cover shifts when correctional staff take extended uniformed services or disaster service leave.

MSP is highlighted in the fiscal note as likely to incur overtime expenses and staffing coverage needs when law enforcement personnel utilize the expanded uniformed services and disaster leave allowances.

The Adjutant General commands Maryland's military forces, including the organized militia and National Guard. The bill directly benefits state employees serving in these units by doubling allowable paid military leave for training and active service.
State employees who are active or reserve members of the Maryland National Guard are direct beneficiaries of the bill's expansion of uniformed services leave from 15 to 30 days for training and duty.
The legislation is an Administration bill ('Time to Serve Act of 2024') sponsored on behalf of the Governor to expand disaster and military leave entitlements across Executive Branch agencies.
The fiscal note analyzes the impact on retirement service credit awarded to members of the State Retirement and Pension System whose state employment is interrupted by uniformed service.

MDEM coordinates disaster response in Maryland, which relies in part on volunteers and volunteer emergency services organizations whose members are granted increased disaster service leave under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Transparent Government Act of 2024 requires Maryland principal departments and independent executive units to compile and submit to the Governor a catalog of all permits, licenses, and certificates they issue, along with processing timelines, fees, and application details. Agencies must also publicly post processing descriptions and annual updates on their websites. In addition, the Act establishes the Government Efficiency Commission within the Office of the Governor to monitor processing efficiency, review regulations, and provide annual recommendations to improve permitting processes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Governor, Government Efficiency Commission, and all principal departments and independent units of the Executive Branch
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland individuals, professionals, and businesses applying for state-issued permits, licenses, or certificates, as well as state regulatory and licensing agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect state expenditures or revenues. State departments and independent units are expected to compile catalogs, update websites, and participate in the commission using existing budgeted resources. Member reimbursements and commission staffing by the Governor's Office are assumed to be minimal and absorbable. Local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires each principal department and independent unit to submit a catalog of permits, licenses, and certificates to the Governor. It also requires the Governor to designate the chair of the newly created Government Efficiency Commission, appoint business community members, and requires the Office of the Governor to provide staff for the commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily establishes a new temporary or permanent state body, the Government Efficiency Commission, tasked with monitoring permitting and licensing efficiency and issuing annual recommendations.
The Chief Performance Officer, who leads state performance improvement initiatives, is designated as an ex officio member of the newly established Government Efficiency Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Special Secretary of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (or their designee) is designated by the bill as a statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission.

The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a member of the Government Efficiency Commission, and the agency is subject to the catalog and website publishing mandates for state permits, licenses, and certificates.

The Secretary of the Environment is a designated member of the Government Efficiency Commission, and MDE is one of the state's primary permitting agencies directly subject to cataloging and reporting its extensive environmental permits.

The Secretary of Health is designated as a member of the Government Efficiency Commission, and MDH oversees extensive health facility and occupational board licensing subject to the bill's cataloging and tracking mandates.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is designated as a member of the Government Efficiency Commission and must catalog and report department-issued permits and certificates.

The Secretary of Information Technology is designated as a member of the Government Efficiency Commission. DoIT also manages Maryland's centralized OneStop licensing portal and IT systems relevant to the permit tracking requirements.

The Secretary of Labor serves as a statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission, and MD Labor regulates dozens of professional licensing boards and commissions subject to the cataloging and reporting requirements.
The Secretary of Planning (or designee) is designated by the bill as a statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission.

The Secretary of Transportation is named to the Government Efficiency Commission, and MDOT modal administrations issue a substantial volume of state licenses and permits subject to the catalog requirements.
The Director of the Maryland Energy Administration is designated as an ex officio member of the Government Efficiency Commission.

MSDE is subject to the cataloging and publishing mandates for its educator and childcare licensing functions, and specifically noted in the fiscal note an estimated $200,000 cost to comply with the bill's catalog and web posting requirements.

MDA is explicitly highlighted in the fiscal note as a major regulatory department that issues numerous agricultural permits, licenses, and registrations required to be cataloged and tracked under the bill.
DNR is highlighted as an executive department that issues extensive hunting, fishing, boating, and conservation permits and licenses that must be cataloged, analyzed, and posted online.
MSP and the Office of the State Fire Marshal issue multiple regulatory, firearms, and professional security licenses and permits subject to the catalog and website disclosure mandates.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Pava LaPere Legacy of Innovation Act of 2024 establishes the permanent Pava LaPere Innovation Acceleration Grant Program to provide $50,000 grants to student-founded technology start-ups in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson metropolitan area. It also establishes the Baltimore Innovation Initiative Pilot Program within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to support university-affiliated tech start-ups and commercialization through grants, while repealing the $1.0 million annual mandated appropriation for the Business Telework Assistance Grant Program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO)
qa_results.stakeholders: Student and faculty entrepreneurs, technology start-ups in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson metropolitan area, and participating public and private universities and community colleges in the region.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State net general fund expenditures increase by $1.0 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027, reflecting a $1.5 million appropriation for the Baltimore Innovation Initiative Pilot Program and $500,000 for the Pava LaPere Innovation Acceleration Grant Program, offset by a $1.0 million savings from repealing the mandated appropriation for the Business Telework Assistance Grant Program. Beginning in FY 2028, general fund expenditures decrease by $500,000 annually. Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for TEDCO increase by $850,000 annually from FY 2025 to FY 2027 from participating higher education institution contributions. Higher education expenditures increase by $325,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027 for State institutions' contributions. Local community colleges may see increased expenditures of up to $50,000 each annually to participate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the newly created Pava LaPere Innovation Acceleration Grant Program and the Baltimore Innovation Initiative Pilot Program within the Maryland Innovation Initiative.
The bill directly repeals the $1,000,000 annual mandated appropriation for the Business Telework Assistance Grant Program, which is housed within and administered by the Department of Commerce.

Multiple constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland (including Coppin State University, Towson University, University of Baltimore, UMB, and UMBC) are designated as eligible universities under the Baltimore Innovation Initiative Pilot Program, allowing them to participate, pay annual contributions, and submit project proposals.

Morgan State University is specifically designated as an eligible university under the Baltimore Innovation Initiative Pilot Program, allowing it to contribute up to $50,000 annually and submit project proposals for technology startup commercialization.

DBM oversees the state budget execution and fiscal planning, which is directly impacted by the repeal of the telework grant mandate and the establishment of mandated appropriations for the new innovation programs.
The bill was sponsored by request of the Administration and statutorily requires the Governor to include specific appropriations in the annual state budget bill for the new innovation programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Center for Firearm Violence Prevention and Intervention within the Maryland Department of Health to reduce firearm violence, harm, and misuse statewide through a public health approach, requiring comprehensive strategic plans, interagency coordination, stakeholder consultation, and evidence-based violence prevention initiatives.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Communities disproportionately impacted by gun violence, local health departments, healthcare professionals, community and faith-based organizations, academic researchers, and Maryland residents affected by firearm violence
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million in FY 2025 based on a contingent appropriation in the budget bill, plus $171,387 in federal fund expenditures to cover three personnel positions and contractual planning costs totaling $2,171,387. General fund expenditures are estimated to be $8.0 million in FY 2026 and $10.0 million annually thereafter for grants, contractual services, and operating expenses. Local health department revenues and expenditures increase beginning in FY 2026 to the extent they apply for and receive violence prevention grants from the center.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 583 establishes the Center for Firearm Violence Prevention and Intervention directly within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). The Secretary of Health appoints the Executive Director, and MDH is responsible for staffing, directing, and executing the Center's public health plans, research, grant allocations, and violence prevention operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the newly created Center work in consultation with the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy to ensure a whole-of-government multidepartmental approach to reducing firearm violence and facilitate cross-jurisdictional data and information sharing.

The bill explicitly requires the Center to work in consultation with the Maryland State Police to develop a coordinated, multidepartmental public health and law enforcement strategy to reduce firearm violence.

The Center is required to submit both a preliminary state plan and recurring quadrennial strategic plans directly to the Governor, and the bill authorizes the Governor to include appropriations to fund the Center in the annual budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes occupational disease presumptions under workers' compensation law for eligible career and volunteer firefighters, firefighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, and sworn fire marshals who contract thyroid, colon, or ovarian cancer caused by line-of-duty exposure to toxic substances.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Career and volunteer firefighters, firefighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, fire marshals, local governments, and Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures across all funds may increase minimally beginning in FY 2025 due to expanded workers' compensation claims for eligible State personnel. Local government expenditures are expected to increase, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2025 because local entities employ the majority of eligible first responders. Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company expenditures will also likely increase for claim payouts, offset by potential increases in premium revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission administers Maryland's Workers' Compensation Law and adjudicates claims for workplace injuries and occupational diseases, directly presiding over claims filed under these expanded occupational disease presumptions.

Operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, it serves as the third-party administrator handling workers' compensation claims for State of Maryland employees and insures many local governments, expecting an increase in benefit payouts for covered claims.
