MAA operates BWI Marshall Airport and employs the BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department personnel, who are state employees eligible for the expanded occupational disease presumptions under the bill.
The Office of the State Fire Marshal is an agency within the Department of State Police, and its sworn members are explicitly covered by the bill's expanded cancer presumptions.
The Fund reviews and investigates workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing conditions and permanent disability, which may be impacted by newly compensable cancer presumptions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and regulates Maryland's statewide EMS network, including the rescue squad and advanced life support personnel covered by this legislation.
Section 9-503(e) directly coordinates workers' compensation benefits with retirement system benefits administered by the agency to ensure combined benefits do not exceed weekly salary limits.
MDOT is the parent department of the Maryland Aviation Administration, which directly employs covered airport firefighters.
This is an Administration priority bill introduced on behalf of the Governor to expand protections for public safety employees and first responders.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Protecting Election Officials Act of 2024 prohibits individuals from knowingly and willfully threatening to harm election officials or their immediate family members because of the official's role in administering elections. Violations are classified as misdemeanors punishable by up to three years imprisonment, a fine of up to $2,500, or both.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections, local boards of elections, and state law enforcement agencies and prosecutors
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland election officials (including State and local board members, staff, election judges, and youth pages), immediate family members of election officials, and individuals subject to prosecution for threats
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances, though individuals convicted of violations may be subject to fines of up to $2,500.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly protects State Board of Elections administrators, members, staff, and local election board personnel from threats of harm arising from their election administration duties.
The Office of the State Prosecutor is charged with investigating and prosecuting criminal offenses concerning elections and the electoral process in Maryland.
The state court system will handle filings, trials, and sentencing for the newly created criminal misdemeanor charges established by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender is responsible for providing legal defense to indigent defendants charged with the new misdemeanor, which carries penalties of up to three years of imprisonment.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees state correctional institutions and parole/probation supervision for individuals convicted under the bill's criminal misdemeanor penalties.
The legislation was an Administration bill introduced on behalf of the Governor to advance the executive branch's public safety and election protection policy priorities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Class C (Weinberg Center) beer, wine, and liquor license in Frederick County to the Class C (Weinberg Center/New Spires Arts Stages) license, expanding its coverage to include the New Spires Arts Stages. It alters who may sign the license application and permits the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages during events hosted by outside groups renting either facility.
qa_results.responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Weinberg Center for the Arts, New Spires Arts Stages, patrons and outside groups renting the facilities, and the City and County of Frederick.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Frederick County revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $375 annually beginning in FY 2025 because the $325 annual fee for the permanent license replaces roughly $700 collected annually from multiple Class C per diem licenses. Any enforcement activities can be handled with existing county resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters a local alcoholic beverages license in Frederick County. While the license is administered at the local level by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation of the alcohol industry and collection of applicable alcohol sales and excise taxes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a manufacturer's limited beer, wine, and liquor permit in Frederick County, allowing eligible Class 1 distilleries and Class 5 breweries with local on-site consumption permits to host private events where licensed caterers or contracted parties can serve beer, wine, and liquor not manufactured on-site.
qa_results.responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Frederick County Class 1 distilleries, Class 5 breweries, licensed caterers, and private event patrons.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Frederick County local revenues are estimated to increase by approximately $4,500 annually beginning in FY 2025, assuming up to nine eligible license holders obtain the permit at an anticipated fee of $500. Frederick County can handle any enforcement with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees state manufacturer's licenses (such as Class 1 distillery and Class 5 brewery licenses). While this permit is issued at the local county level by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it interacts with state-level manufacturer license categories regulated by the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County to issue a Class M-G municipal golf course beer, wine, and liquor license to an official of the City of Frederick designated by the Mayor, and allows the transfer of the license to another designated city official upon request.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County
qa_results.stakeholders: City of Frederick municipal golf course patrons, the City of Frederick, and designated municipal officials.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and does not materially affect Frederick County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees the collection and remittance of sales and use taxes, which are referenced in the bill regarding agents selling alcoholic beverages under the municipal golf course license.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts applicants for employment as paramedics, emergency medical technicians, or 9-1-1 center dispatcher specialists within the Dorchester County Department of Emergency Services, and correctional officers at the Dorchester County Detention Center, from the general prohibition against employers requiring polygraph examinations as a condition of prospective employment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for employment with the Dorchester County Department of Emergency Services and the Dorchester County Detention Center, as well as Dorchester County emergency management and corrections administration.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. It has no material effect on Dorchester County operations or finances, and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor (specifically the Commissioner of Labor and Industry) administers and enforces state labor laws under Title 3 of the Labor and Employment Article, including handling complaints regarding unlawful polygraph examination requirements. This bill creates a specific exemption under Section 3-702 for certain emergency service and correctional applicants in Dorchester County.

Under Section 3-702(g) of the Labor and Employment Article, the Attorney General is authorized to initiate legal actions on behalf of applicants or employees for injunctive relief or damages upon referral of a violation by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the number of resident circuit court judges in Prince George's County from 24 to 25.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) and the Circuit Court for Prince George's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and litigants in Prince George's County, the Prince George's County Circuit Court, and court personnel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $361,459 in FY 2025 (funding for which was included in the FY 2025 state budget) to support one additional judge, one courtroom clerk, and one law clerk, increasing to $493,400 by FY 2029. Prince George's County local expenditures will also increase starting in FY 2025 to cover county-funded court costs such as an administrative assistant. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an additional circuit court judgeship in Prince George's County along with associated staff (a courtroom clerk and a law clerk), directly impacting the Judiciary's operational budget and personnel administration managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and recommending candidates to fill newly created judicial seats.
The Governor is constitutionally and statutorily responsible for appointing the judge to the newly established circuit court seat.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes publication requirements for legal advertisements and legal notices in Dorchester County, requiring them to be distributed in both print and digital formats. If no qualifying print and digital publication exists, the notice may be placed in any digital publication accessible in the county that regularly provides local news and information.
qa_results.responsible_party: Dorchester County Government
qa_results.stakeholders: Dorchester County residents, Dorchester County government and courts, and local print and digital news publishers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect because it applies solely to Dorchester County. It is not anticipated to materially affect Dorchester County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines the publication requirements for legal advertisements and notices ordered by a court order, judgment, or decree within Dorchester County, touching upon court proceedings and legal notices managed or overseen in the judicial process, although the state fiscal impact is noted as none.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Growing Apprenticeships and the Public Safety Workforce (GAPS) Act renames the Law Enforcement Cadet Apprenticeship Program to the Public Safety Apprenticeship Program and expands its eligibility to include correctional units and other public safety agencies. It authorizes the Maryland Department of Labor to award competitive start-up grants of up to $200,000 and stabilization grants of up to $5,000 per apprentice. The bill also directs the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to develop mental health wellness policies for law enforcement and correctional personnel and creates a temporary workgroup to study law enforcement and correctional workforce recruitment and retention.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor and the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local public safety agencies, correctional units, law enforcement officers, correctional officers, and individuals pursuing apprenticeships or careers in public safety.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill can be implemented using existing budgeted resources, including the existing annual statutory mandated appropriation of $750,000 in general funds for the apprenticeship program. Start-up grants of up to $200,000 and stabilization grants of up to $5,000 may be awarded to eligible State and local public safety agencies. The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission can develop the mental health wellness policies, report requirements, and staff the workgroup within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Administers the newly renamed and expanded Public Safety Apprenticeship Program, adopts implementing regulations, and awards start-up grants (up to $200,000) and stabilization grants (up to $5,000) to eligible public safety agencies; the Secretary of Labor also serves on the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is required to develop mental health wellness policies for law enforcement and correctional facilities, report annually to the Governor and General Assembly, and staff the newly established workgroup. In addition, the Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services serves on the workgroup and state correctional units are impacted by the policies and eligible for apprenticeships.

The Secretary of State Police is designated as a member of the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce. Additionally, as a primary state law enforcement agency, it is subject to the mental health wellness policies developed by MPTSC and eligible for the expanded Public Safety Apprenticeship Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary advisory body, the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce, tasked with studying workforce shortages, recruitment, and retention, and reporting recommendations by January 1, 2025.

The Governor is tasked with designating the Chair of the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce and receives annual reports from MPTSC on mental health wellness policies and the final report from the workgroup.
The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce.
The Secretary of Higher Education (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce.
The Secretary of Higher Education (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits discrimination based on military status in employment and housing. It defines military status to include members of the uniformed services, reserve components of the U.S. Armed Forces, veterans, and their dependents.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights
qa_results.stakeholders: Active-duty service members, reservists, veterans, military dependents, employers, housing providers, landlords, and real estate professionals.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures likely increase, at least minimally, for the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights due to an increased caseload and potential need for additional investigative staff (illustratively estimated at at least $80,000 annually per investigator). State revenues and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR) is the primary enforcement agency responsible for investigating and resolving complaints of discrimination in employment and housing under Title 20 of the State Government Article. Adding military status as a protected class directly expands MCCR's jurisdiction and investigatory caseload, resulting in projected fiscal and operational impacts.

The bill explicitly specifies that its provisions do not limit the civil rights enforcement authority granted to the Attorney General under Title 20, Subtitle 10, Part III of the State Government Article to investigate and prosecute civil rights violations.

As the primary state department dedicated to advocating for and supporting Maryland's service members, veterans, and military families, the bill directly impacts the legal protections and civil rights of the department's core constituency regarding employment and housing.

The Office of Administrative Hearings employs administrative law judges who adjudicate contested administrative hearings resulting from discrimination complaints certified for litigation by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

The State's judicial branch is responsible for adjudicating civil actions alleging unlawful employment or housing discrimination that are brought by complainants, respondents, or MCCR in the circuit courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Community Investment Corporation (MCIC) as an independent instrumentality of the State to apply for federal New Markets Tax Credits (NMTCs) and make qualified equity investments and financial assistance in low-income communities. The bill also expands eligible uses of the Department of Housing and Community Development's Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund to include debt payments and credit enhancements for revitalization projects.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Community Investment Corporation (with support from the Department of Housing and Community Development, the Department of Commerce, and the Office of the Attorney General)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and businesses located in Maryland's low-income communities, community development entities, local governments, and small businesses seeking revitalization investment.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $800,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2029 for initial administrative and personnel costs of the corporation (contingently appropriated in the FY 2025 budget). Corporation nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures are projected to increase substantially (potentially tens of millions of dollars) beginning as early as FY 2026 from federal NMTC allocations and private investments. Local governments benefit from broader flexibility in applying Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact funding without direct negative fiscal impacts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is a primary agency involved in the implementation of the bill. The Secretary of Housing and Community Development serves on the Board of Directors of the newly created Corporation, DHCD may provide staff and administrative support, the state budget provides funding for the Corporation through DHCD's budget, and the bill amends the DHCD-administered Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund to expand eligible uses to debt payments and credit enhancements.

The bill codifies the Corporation under the Economic Development Article, names the Secretary of Commerce to the Corporation's Board of Directors, authorizes Commerce to provide staff support, and requires reporting on outreach and support involving programs like the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority.

The Attorney General is designated as the legal advisor to the Corporation and is statutorily required to assign Assistant Attorneys General and designate one as General Counsel to provide legal guidance and transaction support.

The Comptroller (or designee) serves as an ex officio member on the Corporation's Board of Directors, and the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund.
The Secretary of General Services (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the Corporation.
The Secretary of Planning (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the Corporation.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the moneys of the Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund, which is amended by the bill to expand eligible funding activities.

The Governor appoints public members to the Corporation's Board of Directors with the advice and consent of the Senate, may remove appointed members for cause, and receives annual and quarterly operational and financial reports from the Corporation.

Members of the Board, officers, employees, and committee members of the Corporation are made subject to the Public Ethics Law and are specifically mandated to disclose potential financial or employment conflicts of interest to the State Ethics Commission.

The Corporation is authorized to make investments under an agreement with the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System pursuant to § 21-123.2 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the gubernatorial appointments to the Corporation's Board of Directors.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases penalties and driver's license points assessments for street racing and speed contests, establishes a statewide prohibition on exhibition driving on highways and publicly accessible private property, and expands special event zone prohibitions statewide.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration and State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists, individuals participating in street racing or exhibition driving, law enforcement agencies, District Court, and local detention centers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2025, State general fund revenues will see a minimal increase from higher fines and new violations, with no material impact on Transportation Trust Fund revenues. State general fund expenditures may increase minimally due to incarceration costs for convictions in Baltimore City. Local expenditures may minimally increase for county detention facilities, while local enforcement costs can be absorbed with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters points assessments under § 16-402 of the Transportation Article, requiring the MVA to assess 8 to 12 points against individuals convicted of participating in a race or speed contest or engaging in exhibition driving.
The bill expands SHA's authority statewide to designate areas on State highways as special event zones and reduce speed limits within those zones to protect public safety.

MDOT is the parent agency for both the Motor Vehicle Administration and the State Highway Administration, which are directly responsible for implementing the driver licensing point provisions and highway special event zone designations.
As the primary law enforcement agency patrolling Maryland highways, MSP is responsible for enforcing the prohibitions on street racing, exhibition driving, and violations within special event zones.

Because the bill establishes imprisonment as a penalty for exhibition driving and general racing offenses, cited individuals can no longer prepay citations and must appear in court, impacting District Court caseloads.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS may experience a minor impact on expenditures due to incarcerating individuals convicted under the bill's new incarceration penalties in Baltimore City.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds penalties of up to 60 days or 1 year of imprisonment for offenses that previously were fines-only, thereby entitling indigent defendants charged with these violations to representation by the Public Defender.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands Maryland's Equal Pay for Equal Work law to prohibit employment discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation. Under the bill, employers are prohibited from providing less favorable employment opportunities or paying wages at a rate less than that paid to other employees based on sexual orientation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Commissioner of Labor and Industry)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employees, job applicants, and employers, particularly small businesses with fewer than 15 employees not previously covered by broad employment discrimination laws regarding sexual orientation.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local revenues. Enforcement can be managed using existing resources by the Maryland Department of Labor, and the State and local governments are not financially impacted as employers because they are already prohibited from discriminating based on sexual orientation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Equal Pay for Equal Work law under the Labor and Employment Article, which is administered and enforced by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the Maryland Department of Labor.

Under the State's Equal Pay for Equal Work law, the Commissioner of Labor and Industry may refer unresolved violations to the Attorney General to bring civil enforcement actions for injunctive relief or damages on behalf of employees.

The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is the primary state entity tasked with enforcing anti-discrimination statutes regarding employment, which closely aligns with the policy scope of prohibiting workplace discrimination based on sexual orientation.
State circuit courts hear civil actions filed by employees or the Attorney General alleging violations of the Equal Pay for Equal Work law.

As the central personnel and human resources agency for State government, DBM monitors state employment standards and compensation policies, though existing law already prohibited discrimination based on sexual orientation for state workers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the Maryland Age-Appropriate Design Code Act (Maryland Kids Code), requiring covered online businesses that offer products, services, or features reasonably likely to be accessed by children to conduct data protection impact assessments. The act prohibits certain data collection, sharing, and profiling practices, restricts the use of dark patterns and geolocation tracking, mandates privacy-by-default settings, and establishes civil penalties enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Children under 18 years old in Maryland, parents and legal guardians, and commercial businesses that develop or offer online products, services, or features reasonably likely to be accessed by children.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures will likely increase, at least minimally, beginning in FY 2025 for the Office of the Attorney General (OAG), Consumer Protection Division to handle enforcement; OAG estimated costs up to $355,700 in FY 2025 rising to $469,000 by FY 2029 for three positions, though the Department of Legislative Services notes the exact need is unclear. State general fund revenues may increase from civil penalties ($2,500 per affected child for negligent violations and $7,500 for intentional violations), though revenues may be minimal due to cure provisions. Local finances and operations are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Consumer Protection Division within the Office of the Attorney General as the primary regulatory and enforcement authority for the Maryland Age-Appropriate Design Code Act. The OAG is responsible for requesting and reviewing data protection impact assessments, issuing violation and cure notices, and bringing enforcement actions for civil penalties.

The Judiciary and the Administrative Office of the Courts would hear any civil enforcement actions brought by the Attorney General under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. However, because the bill explicitly prohibits a private right of action, the overall court caseload and fiscal impact on judicial operations are expected to be minimal.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes a distinct regulatory framework and licensing system administered by the Motor Vehicle Administration for recreational vehicle (RV) manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches. It sets comprehensive requirements governing RV dealer agreements, including terms for agreement termination and nonrenewal, ownership succession, warranty and reimbursement procedures, vehicle inspection and rejection upon delivery, prohibited coercive acts, and dispute resolution mechanisms.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Recreational vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, RV dealers, warrantors, and RV consumers in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not anticipated to be materially affected. The Motor Vehicle Administration can manage the regulatory and licensing responsibilities using existing budgeted resources. Transportation Trust Fund revenues are expected to be maintained at current levels, assuming license fees and fine collections remain comparable to existing vehicle manufacturer provisions. Local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary implementing agency responsible for licensing recreational vehicle manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches, setting and collecting annual licensing fees, receiving surety bonds, and enforcing compliance through fines and license suspensions or revocations.

MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, and licensing fees and regulatory oversight under the bill directly relate to MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund and regulatory purview.
Licensees and warrantors are entitled to administrative hearings to contest fines or enforcement actions imposed by MVA under the bill, which are adjudicated by administrative law judges at the OAH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts applicants for the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship from high school GPA and FAFSA submission requirements if they are enrolling in a noncredit vocational certificate program, enrolling in a sequence of noncredit courses leading to licensure or certification, or participating in a registered apprenticeship program (unless enrolling in a noncredit program eligible for a federal Pell Grant). It also allows community colleges to require an application for admission for these applicants.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Community Colleges and the Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Community college students pursuing noncredit vocational certificates, licensure/certification course sequences, or registered apprenticeship programs, as well as Maryland community colleges.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local revenues or expenditures. Expanding scholarship eligibility does not require additional state spending, as total funding remains subject to the annual budget appropriation (mandated at $15.0 million annually under current law). Expanding applicant eligibility without additional funding may result in more applicants being placed on a waiting list or fewer awards to other applicants. Local community colleges and Baltimore City Community College can update application eligibility criteria using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) oversees state postsecondary financial aid programs, allocates Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship funding to community colleges, provides outreach to high schools, and submits annual reports on the program.

MHEC is the central coordinating and regulatory agency for higher education and financial aid in Maryland, responsible for allocating funding formulas for the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship and reporting on its implementation.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees workforce development and the state's registered apprenticeship programs, which are specifically granted exemptions from GPA and FAFSA submission requirements under this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the Library Workers Empowerment Act, establishing a statutory collective bargaining process for full-time and part-time nonmanagement and supervisory employees of Maryland public library systems (excluding Baltimore, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties). The bill outlines procedures for representation elections, certification, good-faith negotiations, grievance arbitration, impasse resolution and mediation, and prohibits strikes, work stoppages, and lockouts.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public library systems and their respective Boards of Trustees, along with county funding bodies
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonmanagement and supervisory employees of Maryland public library systems, public library employers/administrators, certified employee organizations/unions, and local county funding authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase minimally beginning in FY 2029 to cover higher retirement contribution costs if library salaries rise as a result of collective bargaining. State revenues are unaffected. Local expenditures may increase significantly due to costs associated with collective bargaining (such as mediator and arbitration fees), potential employee wage increases, and local retirement costs for non-State eligible staff. Specific dollar amounts were not estimated in the Fiscal Note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency provides leadership, funding, and strategic coordination for Maryland's 24 public library systems, whose employees are directly granted collective bargaining rights and procedures under this bill.

The State pays retirement benefits for eligible public library personnel through the State Retirement and Pension System; potential increases in library employee salaries from collective bargaining will affect retirement calculations and state contribution costs administered by the agency.

As the state body regulating public sector collective bargaining, PERB was consulted on the legislation, although the bill specifically establishes mediation and dispute resolution for library workers via the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the Electronic Transactions Protection Act, which established the Electronic Transaction Education, Advocacy, and Mediation Unit within the Office of the Attorney General.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers, businesses engaging in electronic commerce, and the Office of the Attorney General.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The Electronic Transaction Education, Advocacy, and Mediation Unit was never funded, and its functions are already handled by the Consumer Protection Division within the Office of the Attorney General.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 611 repeals the Electronic Transactions Protection Act, which statutorily established the Electronic Transaction Education, Advocacy, and Mediation Unit within the Office of the Attorney General.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies the statutory rules for recreationally catching clams and oysters in Maryland by removing specific statutory daily bushel limits for clams in favor of Department of Natural Resources (DNR) regulations and creating an annual recreational oyster license for State residents at a fee of $10. It establishes complimentary licenses for blind individuals, former prisoners of war, and 100% disabled or unemployable veterans, discounts for Purple Heart recipients, fee-free registration exemptions for tidal waterfront property owners, and directs a portion of license revenues to replenish public oyster bars.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents engaging in recreational oyster and clam harvesting, tidal waterfront property owners and their families, authorized commercial license sales agents, qualifying disabled veterans and blind residents, and the commercial oyster and seafood industry.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase annually beginning in FY 2025 from the $10 recreational oyster license fee (for illustrative purposes, by roughly $100,000 per 10,000 non-discounted licenses issued, minus a 50-cent fee per license retained by commercial agents). Special fund expenditures will also increase as DNR uses a portion of fee proceeds to plant shell and juvenile oysters on public oyster bars. DNR can administer the licensing program using existing resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) with establishing and administering the new recreational oyster license, developing application forms, collecting license fees, setting discounted fees, registering exempt property owners, adopting implementing regulations, and dedicating a portion of fee revenues to replenish public fishery oyster bars.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces the annual fee for a stadium beer, wine, and liquor license in Harford County from $10,000 to $7,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners, lessees, or concession managers of professional baseball stadiums in Harford County, as well as the Harford County Board of License Commissioners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are unaffected. Harford County local revenues decrease by $3,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to the license fee reduction, based on one active stadium license. County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for the general regulation of the alcohol industry in the state. While this legislation specifically affects a local Harford County stadium beer, wine, and liquor license fee administered by the local Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it amends the state's Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article governing alcohol regulation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits consumer reporting agencies from including in a consumer report any records of criminal proceedings that did not result in a guilty verdict or guilty plea (such as acquittals, exonerations, false accusations, or nolle prosequi entries) or records that have been expunged. It also prohibits consumer reporting agencies from relying on such records to evaluate a consumer's creditworthiness.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation (within the Maryland Department of Labor)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers who have expunged or non-conviction criminal records, consumer reporting agencies, and entities that utilize consumer reports for credit, employment, or insurance determinations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Office of Financial Regulation can enforce the bill using existing resources. State revenues are likely not materially affected, and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of Financial Regulation (OFR), which has investigative and enforcement authority over consumer reporting agencies and compliance with credit reporting laws under the Commercial Law Article.

The Office of the Attorney General enforces state consumer protection laws under the Commercial Law Article, protecting consumers from unlawful practices in credit reporting and determinations of creditworthiness.

The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the state judicial records system, which handles the expungement orders, acquittals, and non-guilty dispositions referenced in the bill's restrictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers the primary administrative responsibility of the Next Generation Scholars of Maryland Program and its fund from the Maryland State Department of Education to the Maryland Higher Education Commission, while requiring the Department to assist with application reviews, publicity, and school system eligibility determinations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland middle and high school students qualifying for Guaranteed Access Grants or free/reduced-price meals, participating local school systems, and nonprofit organizations delivering college-preparatory and mentoring services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, the administration of $5.0 million in annual special fund expenditures transfers from the Maryland State Department of Education to the Maryland Higher Education Commission with no net fund effect. Assuming existing special funds are reserved for program grants, State general fund expenditures will increase by $223,700 in FY 2026 for 1.5 new staff positions and system upgrades, followed by ongoing costs ranging between $157,600 and $171,800 annually. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 624 transfers the primary responsibility for administering the Next Generation Scholars of Maryland Program and its associated special fund from MSDE to MHEC beginning in FY 2026, resulting in administrative responsibilities, grant management, and estimated fiscal impacts for additional staffing and IT upgrades.

HB 624 transfers the primary administration of the Next Generation Scholars of Maryland Program and its special fund to the Commission starting in FY 2026, requiring MHEC to award grants, solicit applications, adopt regulations, and report on program outcomes.

MSDE transfers primary administration of the program to MHEC but retains statutory obligations to assist MHEC with application reviews, partner selection, program publicity, data identification of eligible school systems, and joint reporting.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the allowable training topics for trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) to include retirement administration, operations, and other relevant topics. It also permits the SRPS Board of Trustees to satisfy annual reporting requirements by publishing system reports and material modifications on the State Retirement Agency's website and making individual personal benefit statements available to members and retirees via a secure access participant portal.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System (and the State Retirement Agency)
qa_results.stakeholders: State Retirement and Pension System trustees, active members, and retirees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect state or local government finances, though the State Retirement and Pension System may realize administrative efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) Board of Trustees, expanding trustee training requirements and authorizing the agency to provide personal benefit statements and system reports via the State Retirement Agency website and a secure online participant portal.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the reciprocal licensure requirements for clinical marriage and family therapists in Maryland. It mandates that the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists waive standard education, experience, and examination requirements for an applicant licensed or certified in another state or jurisdiction, provided the applicant has no disciplinary history, has not committed disqualifying acts, and submits current license documentation and application fees. Additionally, the Board cannot require a national exam, though it may test applicants on Maryland-specific law.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists
qa_results.stakeholders: Clinical marriage and family therapists licensed in other states seeking Maryland licensure, as well as patients seeking marriage and family therapy services in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as the changes are procedural in nature and do not directly affect governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies reciprocal licensure requirements administered by the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists, which is a health occupations licensing board operating under the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates the definition of Consumer Price Index used by the State Retirement and Pension System to replace an obsolete reference to the 1967 index with the 1982–1984 base years for calculating cost-of-living adjustments.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is technical in nature and has no material effect on State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly updates statutory definitions governing the calculation of cost-of-living adjustments for retirees within the State Retirement and Pension System, which is managed and administered by the Maryland State Retirement Agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 630 repeals the requirement limiting benefits for transferred service credit to what would have been payable under the previous retirement system if an individual retires within five years of the transfer. The bill also updates statutory references regarding member contribution rates for transfers into the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System and allows certain Department of Legislative Services employees with over five years of prior contractual service to receive up to 10 years of eligibility and service credit in the Employees' Pension System.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the State Retirement and Pension System transferring service credit, members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, and qualifying contractual/permanent employees of the Department of Legislative Services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because the contractual service credit provisions apply to only two individuals, whose required contribution payments further mitigate any cost. Other provisions conform statute to current State Retirement Agency practice. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is directly responsible for administering the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The bill repeals specific benefit limitation formulas on transferred service credit that SRA cannot administer, corrects statutory contribution rate references for LEOPS transfers, and requires the Board of Trustees to process claims and accept contributions for contractual service credit for eligible employees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class GSF (golf simulator facility) alcoholic beverages license in Harford County, authorizing eligible golf simulator facilities with at least five simulator bays to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption subject to specific sales ratio requirements and reporting.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Golf simulator facility owners, patrons of golf simulator facilities, and Harford County local government.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Harford County revenues increase by $1,500 in FY 2025 for each new Class GSF license issued and $1,500 annually thereafter per license renewal. Harford County can manage any additional enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees the collection of state sales and excise taxes on alcoholic beverages and regulates aspects of the alcohol industry. While the Class GSF license is issued and enforced locally by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, sales generated under the license remain subject to state tax administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to allow the Center to send student information to the United States Census Bureau.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland postsecondary students, higher education institutions, educational researchers, and the U.S. Census Bureau.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 634 directly amends the statute governing the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center by authorizing its Governing Board to transmit student information to the United States Census Bureau.
The Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center is administratively housed within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), and MSDE provides student data sets linked by the MLDS Center.

The bill amends Section 24-703.2 of the Education Article, which establishes the joint data-sharing protocol and privacy standards between the MLDS Center and the Comptroller, though the new provision specifically authorizes transfers to the U.S. Census Bureau.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a performing arts nonprofit organization beer, wine, and liquor license in Harford County, authorizing eligible nonprofit organizations that produce stage performances or show films to sell or serve alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption at up to three designated locations during performances and receptions. It also establishes recordkeeping and reporting requirements, penalties, and an annual license fee of $750.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit performing arts organizations in Harford County and their patrons.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Harford County local revenues increase by at least $750 beginning in fiscal year 2025 based on an estimated issuance of one license at the $750 annual fee, with potential additional revenue from penalties ($250 to $2,000 per violation). Harford County can absorb enforcement responsibilities using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill grants specific regulatory and enforcement authority to the Comptroller regarding the new license in Harford County, including the authority to request reporting under oath, inspect and audit records, and immediately suspend a license for up to 30 days for failure to comply with record-keeping requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Allegany County or a municipal corporation in Allegany County to grant a property tax credit against county or municipal property taxes on property owned by Evergreen Heritage Center Foundation, Inc., or Evergreen Heritage Center Holdings, LLC.
qa_results.responsible_party: Allegany County and municipal corporations in Allegany County
qa_results.stakeholders: Evergreen Heritage Center Foundation, Inc., Evergreen Heritage Center Holdings, LLC, and Allegany County taxpayers and local government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Allegany County property tax revenues may decrease by approximately $5,300 annually beginning in fiscal year 2025 if the optional credit is granted on eligible property assessed at $546,300. County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes Allegany County to grant a local property tax credit for property owned by the Evergreen Heritage Center Foundation. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals regarding real property tax credits and exemptions in Maryland counties, giving it potential jurisdiction over any administrative disputes arising from the credit.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 646 consolidates the Maryland income tax subtraction modifications for volunteer police personnel and volunteer fire, rescue, and emergency medical services personnel under a unified 'public safety volunteer' subtraction modification. The bill also increases the subtraction modification for qualifying police auxiliary and reserve volunteers from $5,000 to $7,000 beginning in tax year 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualifying Maryland police auxiliary and reserve volunteers, local police agencies, and Maryland taxpayers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2025, State general fund revenues decrease by an estimated $21,000 annually due to higher subtraction modification claims. Local income tax revenues decrease by an estimated $14,000 annually beginning in FY 2025. The Comptroller's Office can administer the changes using existing budgeted resources, and local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary tax administration agency responsible for processing the personal income tax subtraction modification, issuing tax guidance, and directly receiving annual certification reports containing names and Social Security numbers of qualifying public safety volunteers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that police agencies and the Maryland State Firemen's Association submit annual reports listing qualified individuals to DPSCS, and references program approval by the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, which operates within DPSCS.

The bill explicitly includes the Maryland Defense Force—which operates under the Adjutant General and the Maryland Military Department—as an eligible public safety organization with specific annual service record keeping and reporting obligations to the Comptroller.

As a primary state police agency, MSP is subject to the provisions governing police agencies that utilize auxiliary or reserve volunteers, requiring record keeping and annual reporting to qualifying members, DPSCS, and the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a comprehensive regulatory framework for pet insurance policies sold or issued in Maryland, setting requirements for consumer disclosures, waiting periods, preexisting condition exclusions, claims processes, and the marketing and sale of separate pet wellness programs, while requiring the Maryland Insurance Administration to create informational materials for veterinary practitioners.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Pet owners, pet insurance companies, insurance producers, and veterinary practitioners in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will increase minimally in FY 2025 only due to rate and form filing fees. Enforcement activities can be handled using existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulatory agency tasked with implementing and enforcing the bill's provisions regarding pet insurance policies, disclosures, and wellness programs. The bill also specifically requires MIA to develop informational material on pet insurance policies by June 1, 2025, and results in a minimal increase in special fund revenues from rate and form filing fees.

The bill references definitions under the Agriculture Article governing veterinary practitioners, who are licensed and regulated under the Department of Agriculture, and establishes informational materials intended to be disseminated to and posted by veterinary practices.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 649 expands Maryland's Equal Pay for Equal Work law by requiring employers to proactively disclose the wage range, general description of benefits, and other compensation in public and internal job postings, or prior to discussing compensation if no posting was made available. Employers must set wage ranges in good faith, maintain compliance records for at least three years, and are prohibited from retaliating against employees or applicants who exercise their rights under the law. It also requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to create a compliance form and expands civil penalties for violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Commissioner of Labor and Industry)
qa_results.stakeholders: Job applicants, employees, and public and private employers (including state and local government agencies) in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $98,800 in FY 2025, $78,400 in FY 2026, $70,600 in FY 2027, $73,600 in FY 2028, and $76,800 in FY 2029 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire one investigator and contractual legal support to handle an estimated 120 complaints annually. State and local government agencies face minimal operational effects to adjust disclosure and recordkeeping procedures. Revenues are not materially affected assuming general compliance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Labor and Industry is the primary regulatory and enforcement agency for the bill. The Commissioner of Labor and Industry is responsible for developing compliance disclosure forms, investigating wage transparency complaints, issuing compliance orders, and assessing civil penalties.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal guidance and assistance in interpreting and enforcing the new provisions, including supporting the Department of Labor via legal counsel and potentially pursuing civil enforcement actions on behalf of the Commissioner or affected individuals.

As the central personnel and human resources agency for the State of Maryland, DBM oversees state classification, salary schedules, and hiring guidelines, which must adhere to the bill's wage range disclosure, benefits posting, and multi-year recordkeeping requirements.

The Office of Administrative Hearings is responsible for adjudicating contested administrative cases and hearings resulting from civil penalties or orders assessed by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry under the state's Equal Pay for Equal Work law.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a report to the General Assembly by October 1, 2024, analyzing apprenticeship mentoring ratios for all nontraditional apprenticeable occupations in Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Apprentices and employers participating in nontraditional apprenticeship programs (outside the building trades) and the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Labor can complete the required report with existing resources, and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 650 directly requires the Maryland Department of Labor to conduct an analysis and submit a report to the General Assembly regarding apprenticeship mentoring ratios for all nontraditional apprenticeable occupations in the State.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a beer, wine, and liquor tasting (BWLT) permit in St. Mary's County, authorizing the Board of License Commissioners to issue permits to Class A alcoholic beverages license holders for on-premises consumption of beer, wine, and liquor for tasting purposes with specified quantity limits.
qa_results.responsible_party: St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class A alcoholic beverages licensees in St. Mary's County and their patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. St. Mary's County revenues increase depending on the number of permits issued at fees of $200 (26-day permit), $250 (52-day permit), or $300 (365-day permit). Any additional local enforcement activity can be managed using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland. Although this tasting permit is administered and enforced locally by the St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it pertains to the state's broader alcoholic beverages statutory framework.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a nonprofit performing arts theater beer and wine license in St. Mary's County, permitting eligible nonprofit theaters to sell or serve beer and wine for on-premises consumption from one hour before to one hour after regular performances or fundraisers, for an annual fee of $300.
qa_results.responsible_party: St. Mary’s County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit performing arts theaters in St. Mary's County, theatergoers/patrons, and county licensing officials.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. St. Mary's County revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $350 annually beginning in FY 2025, as theaters shift from purchasing per diem licenses ($650 annually) to a single annual license ($300). The county expects this revenue loss to be offset by administrative savings from processing fewer individual licenses. County expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcoholic beverage industry and oversees alcohol taxation. Although this bill creates a local retail beer and wine license administered by the St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader statutory and regulatory framework governing alcohol sales.

qa_results.bill_summary: Lowers the minimum age requirement from 19 to 18 years old for individuals to serve as child care teachers in registered large family child care homes and licensed child care centers, prohibiting regulations that disqualify individuals solely for being 18 years old.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: 18-year-old child care teacher applicants, large family child care home operators, and child care centers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the bill using existing resources, with no effect on state revenues. Local finances are not affected. Large family child care homes and child care centers may see a positive impact from a larger applicant pool.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Education Article and mandates that the State Board of Education adopt regulations setting the minimum age of child care teachers in large family child care homes and child care centers to 18 years old. The Maryland State Department of Education is the primary implementing agency responsible for regulating and licensing child care facilities in the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Judge Andrew F. Wilkinson Judicial Security Act establishes the Office of Information Privacy within the Administrative Office of the Courts and creates the Judicial Address Confidentiality Program. It allows protected individuals (state and federal judges, magistrates, District Court commissioners, and their co-residing household family members) or the Office of Information Privacy to request the non-publication or removal of personal information from the internet and social media by governmental entities and individuals. The bill establishes civil remedies, sets criminal penalties for knowingly publishing protected personal information under circumstances causing harm or imminent threat, enables the shielding of real property records, and creates the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Administrative Office of the Courts (Office of Information Privacy)
qa_results.stakeholders: Current and retired state and federal judges, magistrates, District Court commissioners, and their co-residing spouses, children, and dependents; state and local government agencies; custodians of public and real property records; and the general public.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially impacted; the Judiciary can establish the Office of Information Privacy, administer the Judicial Address Confidentiality Program, and staff the safety task force using existing budgeted resources. Task force reimbursements and criminal penalty provisions have negligible fiscal effects. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts is the primary implementing agency for the bill; it houses the newly established Office of Information Privacy, administers the Judicial Address Confidentiality Program, and provides staff support for the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities.

The Secretary of General Services (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities, contributing expertise regarding state-owned facility security standards and infrastructure.

The Superintendent of the Maryland State Police (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities to evaluate courthouse safety and security measures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services (or designee) serves as a member of the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities.

The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) serves as a member of the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities to review physical security deficiencies and associated proposals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities.

The bill amends the Real Property Article provisions governing the Address Confidentiality Program administered by the Secretary of State, integrating the new Judicial Address Confidentiality Program into the existing statutory real property shielding framework.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several members to the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities, including representatives of county leadership, sheriffs, chiefs of police, and the Maryland Association of Counties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory advisory body, the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities, charged with studying courthouse safety and reporting findings and legislative recommendations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill lowers the minimum age from 62 to 60 for a household member to be eligible for Maryland's State-funded Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) supplement and increases the minimum total monthly SNAP benefit for these households from $40 to $50.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland households with members who are at least 60 years of age receiving SNAP benefits.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $4.2 million in FY 2025 (which was included as a contingent appropriation in the FY 2025 state budget) and by approximately $3.9 million annually beginning in FY 2026. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services (DHS) directly administers the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and the State supplemental benefit. The bill modifies the eligibility age and benefit level for this program, increasing DHS general fund expenditures by an estimated $4.2 million in FY 2025 and $3.9 million annually thereafter.

The Department of Aging is responsible for advocating for older adults and coordinating services such as senior nutrition programs; lowering the eligibility age to 60 and increasing SNAP supplemental benefits directly impacts the nutritional support provided to older Marylanders.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the annual salary of the Sheriff of Anne Arundel County to equal the salary of a captain at step 20 on the Anne Arundel County Police Department pay scale, effective at the beginning of the next term of office.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County Sheriff and Anne Arundel County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by a minimum of $20,100 in FY 2027 and by at least $34,400 annually thereafter, reflecting the salary increase taking effect at the start of the next term in December 2026. County revenues are unaffected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies how occupational hearing loss and deafness are calculated for workers' compensation benefits by adding a 4,000 hertz frequency threshold to the calculation, requiring employers to compensate for hearing loss at this frequency, and altering the age-related nonoccupational hearing loss deduction formula.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Workers' Compensation Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Covered employees exposed to harmful industrial noise, employers, and workers' compensation insurers such as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State, local government, and small business expenditures increase minimally beginning in FY 2025 due to altered hearing loss calculations and potentially higher claim benefits (estimated by Chesapeake to average an increase of $12,620 per claim, paid over multiple years). State and local revenues are unaffected, while Chesapeake's nonbudgeted revenues increase correspondingly through adjusted premiums.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Workers' Compensation Commission is the primary agency responsible for administering Maryland's Workers' Compensation Law and adjudicating claims. The bill directly alters statutory formulas and decibel frequency criteria used to determine compensable occupational deafness and hearing loss benefits.

The Injured Workers' Insurance Fund (operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company) administers workers' compensation claims for State of Maryland employees and serves as a major workers' compensation insurer in the state. The bill increases claim payouts and expenditures for occupational hearing loss claims.

The Subsequent Injury Fund reviews and investigates workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing conditions and assumes liability for combined disability impacts funded through assessments on permanent disability and settlement awards, which will be affected by changes to hearing loss calculations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the Maryland Right to Try Act to expand access from terminally ill patients to individuals with life-threatening or severely debilitating illnesses, allowing them to receive individualized investigational treatments tailored to their genetic profile. The bill repeals restrictions preventing manufacturers from profiting or charging patients for the costs of these treatments, clarifies facility standards, updates informed consent requirements, and authorizes health insurance carriers and government agencies to cover associated costs without mandating that they do so.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients with life-threatening or severely debilitating illnesses, treating physicians, health care facilities, manufacturers of individualized investigational treatments, and health insurance carriers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Health insurance carriers and government agencies may choose to provide coverage for treatments or related services, but are not required to do so.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily requires the Office of the Attorney General to develop and maintain the official informed consent form that meets the revised disclosure and counseling criteria for individualized investigational treatments.

The bill amends the Health - General Article and directly prohibits the Department and its affiliated health occupations boards from revoking licenses or taking disciplinary/certification actions against health care providers solely for recommending or administering individualized investigational treatments.

The bill references health insurance coverage provisions under Title 15 of the Insurance Article and clarifies provisions regarding whether health insurance carriers regulated by MIA may cover the costs of individualized investigational treatments and related services.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and is affected by the bill's provisions clarifying that government agencies and third-party administrators are authorized, but not required, to cover costs associated with individualized investigational treatments.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes a principle that Maryland public higher education must promote diversity and inclusion by attracting and graduating a diverse student body committed to service. It requires public four-year higher education institutions (excluding the University of Maryland Global Campus) to adopt and annually update a written policy identifying 'communities of interest' from historically underrepresented groups, demographics, or regions. Institutions must execute targeted recruitment and outreach efforts annually and submit an annual progress and admissions data report to the Governor and General Assembly leadership beginning August 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland public senior higher education institutions (including constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland; excluding University of Maryland Global Campus)
qa_results.stakeholders: Prospective students from historically underrepresented communities, demographics, or geographic areas in Maryland, along with public four-year higher education institutions and their admissions staff.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education expenditures increase, potentially materially, for at least some public four-year higher education institutions to hire additional outreach and reporting staff (for example, Towson University estimated an annual cost of $500,000 for three to five full-time staff, programming, and travel). Other institutions may absorb costs using existing resources. Higher education revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to public senior higher education institutions, requiring constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland (excluding UMGC) to adopt and update written policies regarding communities of interest, carry out targeted recruitment and outreach efforts, and submit annual implementation and admissions reports.

As an independent public senior higher education institution, Morgan State University is directly required to establish and update policies identifying communities of interest, conduct annual targeted outreach and recruitment, and submit annual reports to state leadership.

As an independent public senior higher education institution, St. Mary's College of Maryland must adopt policies on communities of interest, execute annual recruitment and outreach initiatives, and provide annual reporting on its efforts and admissions data.

The bill designates the Governor as a mandatory recipient of the annual reports submitted by each public senior higher education institution regarding communities of interest, outreach efforts, and application/admission data.

qa_results.bill_summary: The bill establishes the Radiation Emergency Response Program within the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), designating MDE as the lead State agency and off-site response organization for nuclear incidents. It establishes annual fees on nuclear power plant owners ($300,000 for program operations and $60,000 transferred to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management for preparedness) and creates the dedicated Radiation Emergency Response Fund to support state readiness, equipment procurement, and emergency response operations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of nuclear power plants affecting Maryland (such as Constellation Energy / Calvert Cliffs and Peach Bottom), emergency response personnel, and Maryland residents residing within nuclear emergency planning zones.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures for MDE increase by $600,000 annually beginning in FY 2025, generated by an annual $300,000 fee assessed on each of two nuclear power plants (Calvert Cliffs and Peach Bottom). An additional $60,000 annual fee per facility ($120,000 total) is collected and transferred to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), which replaces existing payments and results in no net fiscal impact on MDEM. No effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the new Radiation Emergency Response Program, serving as the lead State agency for nuclear incidents, collecting fees from nuclear power plant owners, and administering the Radiation Emergency Response Fund.
