MDEM incorporates MDE's technical emergency radiation response plan into the State Emergency Management Program and receives transferred annual fees ($60,000 per nuclear power plant) to support radiological emergency response preparedness activities.
The State Treasurer is statutorily directed to hold and invest the moneys of the newly created Radiation Emergency Response Fund separately, with interest credited directly to the fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the newly established Radiation Emergency Response Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission within the Department of Commerce to foster innovation in commercial aerospace and space exploration. The commission is responsible for identifying research and funding opportunities, developing and updating an annual strategic plan, establishing aerospace and technology zones, promoting educational programs, and partnering with local communities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial aerospace and space exploration companies, aerospace manufacturing businesses, higher education institutions, students, and local communities located within designated aerospace and technology zones.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by $161,400 in FY 2025, reflecting costs for the Department of Commerce to hire one program manager ($79,141 in salary and fringe benefits), one-time startup and operating expenses ($7,256), and a one-time consultant expense to assist with the strategic plan ($75,000). Expenditures are projected at $103,600 in FY 2026, increasing to $117,900 by FY 2029. State revenues are not directly affected, and local government finances and operations are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission within the Department of Commerce and requires the department to provide staff support and administrative oversight, resulting in an ongoing fiscal impact on Commerce's budget.

The presidents (or their designees) of two University System of Maryland member institutions—the University of Maryland, College Park and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County—are designated statutory members of the new commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation establishes a new permanent state body, the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission, to develop strategic plans, identify funding opportunities, and designate aerospace and technology zones.

The Governor is tasked with appointing several members of the commission with the advice and consent of the Senate, possesses removal authority, and receives annual reports and strategic plan updates from the commission.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recruiting qualified candidates for gubernatorial appointment to state bodies, which applies to the appointed industry and academic representatives on the commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of $5.0 million in the annual budget bill to the Maryland Historical Trust for the Historical and Cultural Museum Assistance Program beginning in fiscal year 2025. It also repeals the restriction prohibiting museums that receive operating support from the Maryland State Arts Council from receiving program grants.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Historical Trust
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit museums, local governments, museum visitors, and small business vendors providing museum-related services such as exhibit design, collections conservation, and strategic planning.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by an assumed $5.0 million annually beginning in FY 2026. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Historic Preservation and Historical and Cultural Museum Assistance Grant Fund increase correspondingly by $5.0 million annually starting in FY 2026, which covers two administrative positions ($188,971 in FY 2026) and museum grant distributions ($4,811,029 in FY 2026). Local government revenues and expenditures increase beginning in FY 2026 from receiving and spending grant funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) is a division of the Maryland Department of Planning. MHT administers the Historical and Cultural Museum Assistance Program, manages the grant awards, and will oversee the authorized $5.0 million in annual funding, including hiring additional administrative staff.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include a discretionary appropriation of $5.0 million in the annual state budget bill beginning in FY 2025 for the Historical and Cultural Museum Assistance Program.

As the agency responsible for state budget preparation and fiscal management, DBM oversees the implementation of budget appropriations, including the potential $5.0 million annual general fund allocation.

Under the program's review structure referenced in the bill, the Museum Assistance Review Panel is required to consult with and seek the recommendations of the State Archivist regarding grant applications that involve archival materials.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership qualifications for the Adult Protective Services Review Board (also known as the Adult Public Guardianship Review Board) in Charles County to permit the appointment of a physician's assistant or nurse practitioner specializing in psychiatry to serve in place of a psychiatrist.
qa_results.responsible_party: Charles County Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Charles County Adult Protective Services Review Board, psychiatrists, psychiatric physician assistants, psychiatric nurse practitioners, and vulnerable adults under public guardianship in Charles County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material fiscal impact on State or Charles County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services oversees the State's Adult Protective Services program and the local departments of social services that interact with county adult public guardianship review boards.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Renters' Rights and Stabilization Act of 2024 establishes the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs in the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to publish a Tenants' Bill of Rights and offer tenant assistance. The bill reduces the maximum residential security deposit from two months' rent to one month's rent (with limited exceptions), creates a tenant's exclusive negotiation period and right of first refusal before certain residential rental properties may be sold, extends the eviction execution waiting period from 4 to 7 days, mandates eviction stays during extreme weather, expands eviction data collection requirements, and increases court surcharges on civil filings to fund rental assistance and legal services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants, residential landlords and property owners, the Judiciary, local sheriff offices, and recipients of state rental assistance and civil legal aid programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase by up to $13.3 million in FY 2025 and up to $17.7 million annually thereafter across the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Fund, Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program, and Rental Assistance for Community Schools Families Fund due to increased civil filing surcharges. State general fund expenditures increase by $379,314 in FY 2025, including $344,515 for DHCD to hire three staff to establish the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs and $34,799 for Judiciary IT modifications, with ongoing DHCD costs rising to roughly $466,500 by FY 2029. Local revenues (particularly in Baltimore City) may decrease minimally if higher surcharges deter eviction filings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It establishes the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs within DHCD, requires the department to create and publish the Maryland Tenants' Bill of Rights, directs civil case surcharge revenues into DHCD rental assistance programs, and mandates that DHCD gather, monitor, and publish statewide eviction and tenant purchase data.

AOC and the Judiciary are directly impacted by significant changes to court filing surcharges in District Court and circuit courts, statutory procedures and mandatory stays for warrants of restitution, and requirements to collect, compile, and transmit detailed monthly eviction data to DHCD, requiring computer programming expenditures.

The bill explicitly references the Department of Human Services, providing an exception that permits landlords to collect up to two months' rent as a security deposit if the tenant has qualified for utility assistance through DHS.

The bill establishes mechanisms for the new Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs to refer landlord violations and unfair housing practices to appropriate enforcement agencies, directly implicating the Consumer Protection Division of the OAG, which contributed to the fiscal analysis.

This legislation was introduced as part of the Governor's legislative package to advance key administration housing and anti-poverty priorities, and requires annual reporting on eviction data to the Governor.

The Department of Labor was consulted as an information source for the legislation, as it regulates certain licensed real estate professionals and property management entities affected by residential leasing statutory changes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes rights for buyers in commercial real estate transactions by requiring contracts to include a bold-faced statement informing buyers of their right to select their own title insurance company, settlement company, escrow company, or title lawyer, and clarifying that sellers may offer owner financing. It also prohibits real estate brokers, salespersons, and attorneys acting as brokers from requiring buyers to use specific settlement service providers as a condition of settlement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial real estate buyers and sellers, real estate brokers and salespersons, title insurance companies, settlement and escrow companies, and real estate title attorneys.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland Real Estate Commission finances or operations, nor does it materially affect local government finances or operations. The impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates real estate brokers and salespersons under Title 17 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article, which is overseen and enforced by the Maryland Real Estate Commission housed within the Maryland Department of Labor.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland election law regarding election judges by requiring the State Board of Elections (SBE) to develop and implement a recruitment marketing campaign, and directing SBE to adopt regulations standardizing and minimizing paperwork for election judges while prohibiting local boards and counties from imposing extra documentation requirements. It also entitles county employees who serve as election judges during scheduled work hours to receive paid administrative leave and election judge pay, permits public school students serving as election judges to earn service-learning graduation credits alongside compensation, and narrows the definition of a 'returning election judge' entitled to additional daily pay to those who served in the immediately preceding statewide election.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Election judges, prospective election judges, county employees serving as election judges, public school students serving as election judges, local boards of elections, and county governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures decrease annually beginning in FY 2026 due to fewer election judges qualifying for the State-reimbursed $50 bonus for returning judges (an illustrative decrease of about $190,100 annually). Local government expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2025 for one-time programming to update the statewide voter registration system, followed by an ongoing annual expenditure decrease beginning in FY 2026 (illustratively around $190,100 annually) from lower election judge bonus payouts. Neither State nor local revenues are affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 700 directly impacts the State Board of Elections (SBE) by requiring it to develop and implement a recruitment marketing campaign for election judges, adopt regulations to standardize and minimize required documentation, and reimburse local boards for additional compensation paid to returning election judges.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts minor league baseball players from the Maryland Wage and Hour Law if they are compensated according to the terms of a collective bargaining agreement that expressly provides for employee wages and working conditions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Minor league baseball players and minor league baseball teams or employers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not substantively change State operations or finances, as the Maryland Department of Labor does not recall receiving any Wage and Hour Law complaints from minor league players. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor administers and enforces the Maryland Wage and Hour Law. The bill alters the scope of their regulatory enforcement by exempting certain minor league baseball players who are covered by a collective bargaining agreement.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a licensed real estate broker to designate themselves as the manager of a branch office maintained by that broker.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, real estate branch office managers, associate brokers, real estate salespersons, and real estate brokerage small businesses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the Maryland Real Estate Commission can implement the changes with existing resources. State revenues are not affected. There is no local fiscal impact. Small business real estate brokerages may experience meaningful cost reductions by avoiding the expense of hiring a separate branch office manager.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Maryland Real Estate Commission, which is directly responsible for administering real estate broker branch office certificates, applications, and manager qualifications regulated by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Household Goods Movers Registration Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund within the Maryland Department of Labor to cover the costs of regulating household goods movers. It authorizes the department to calculate costs annually and set fees to cover those costs, while limiting annual fee increases to no more than 12.5%.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Household goods movers and moving businesses operating in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no net effect on State finances, but shifts an estimated $265,600 in annual operational expenditures and fee revenues from the General Fund to the newly created Household Goods Movers Registration Fund. Approximately 870 household goods movers are anticipated to register at an estimated annual fee of $325. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Household Goods Movers Registration Fund within the Maryland Department of Labor. The Department is responsible for administering the fund, calculating annual direct and indirect regulatory costs, and setting registration fees.
The bill requires all fees collected by the Department of Labor under Title 8.5 to be paid to the Comptroller, who must then distribute the fees directly into the newly created special fund.
The bill statutorily requires the Legislative Auditor to audit the accounts and transactions of the newly established Household Goods Movers Registration Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to issue lifetime complimentary angler's, Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing, and hunting licenses to Maryland residents and eligible out-of-state veterans certified as unemployable by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, and exempts them from trout stamp requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: American veterans determined to be unemployable by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues are likely to decrease annually beginning in FY 2025 due to the issuance of lifetime complimentary licenses and trout stamp exemptions; the total decrease is indeterminate, but DNR estimates a reduction of $7,500 to $17,500 for every 500 licenses foregone by Maryland residents. Expenditures and local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Natural Resources with issuing lifetime complimentary angler's, Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing, and hunting licenses to eligible unemployable veterans, and exempting them from trout stamp requirements, resulting in a direct impact on the department's special fund revenues.

The department is responsible for assisting Maryland veterans in accessing state benefits and resources, served as an information source regarding veterans rated as individually unemployable, and helps communicate and connect veterans with available state privileges.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires every deputy clerk and deputy sheriff in Carroll County to take and sign the oath or affirmation of office prescribed by Article I, § 9 of the Maryland Constitution.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County Sheriff's Office and Carroll County Clerk of the Circuit Court
qa_results.stakeholders: Deputy clerks and deputy sheriffs in Carroll County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None. Local Effect: The bill does not materially affect Carroll County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory oath of office taken by deputy clerks of the court in Carroll County, who operate within the Maryland Judicial Branch supported administratively by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Attorney General to seek injunctive relief on behalf of the State to prevent irreparable harm from imminent or ongoing violations of specified basic rights of residents in health care facilities and assisted living programs, prohibits the Attorney General from duplicating corrective action imposed by the Maryland Department of Health for the same violation, and specifies minimum rights to be included in the assisted living resident bill of rights.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents of health care facilities (such as nursing homes) and assisted living programs, as well as operators and administrators of these facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled using existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not affected. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Attorney General to seek injunctive relief in circuit court on behalf of the State to prevent irreparable harm from imminent or ongoing violations of health care and assisted living facility residents' basic rights.

The Department of Health licenses assisted living and health care facilities, establishes the assisted living resident bill of rights updated by this bill, and coordinates enforcement to ensure OAG actions do not duplicate departmental corrective measures.
The state's circuit courts are designated as the venue for hearing petitions for injunctive relief brought by the Attorney General against non-compliant facilities.
The Department of Aging is statutory co-approver of regulations governing assisted living programs and advocates for the rights and quality of care of older adults in these facilities.
The Department of Human Services has statutory authority to approve regulations implemented by the Department of Health regarding assisted living programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Access to Care Act requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE), in consultation with the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, to apply by July 1, 2025, for a federal Section 1332 State Innovation Waiver to establish the Qualified Resident Enrollment Program. Contingent on federal approval, the program allows Maryland residents to purchase qualified health plans through the State's individual exchange regardless of immigration status.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
qa_results.stakeholders: Uninsured Maryland residents ineligible for federal premium tax credits, Medicaid, or Medicare due to immigration status, as well as individual market health insurance carriers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures: MHBE can submit the waiver application and absorb initial start-up costs within existing budgeted resources. Future program expenditures will increase by an indeterminate amount if the waiver is approved and if the General Assembly subsequently authorizes state subsidies. Receipt of federal pass-through funding is not anticipated. Local effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 728 directly tasks the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) with submitting a Section 1332 State Innovation Waiver application amendment to the federal government, establishing and implementing the Qualified Resident Enrollment Program, adopting regulations, and submitting implementation reports to the General Assembly.

The bill requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to develop the waiver application and establish the program in consultation with the Maryland Insurance Commissioner. Additionally, it grants the Commissioner discretionary authority to waive carrier notification and other statutory requirements in calendar year 2025 to facilitate waiver implementation.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill repeals the prohibition in the Baltimore City Charter that prevents city ordinances or actions of municipal officers from conflicting with, impeding, obstructing, hindering, or interfering with the powers of the Baltimore City Police Commissioner. The repeal is contingent upon voter ratification in the 2024 general election of a Baltimore City Charter amendment regarding the appointment, terms, powers, and duties of the Police Commissioner and the Baltimore City Police Department.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore City government officials, the Baltimore City Police Department, the Baltimore City Police Commissioner, and residents of Baltimore City.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and is not anticipated to materially affect Baltimore City finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's enactment is contingent upon the submission and voter ratification of a Baltimore City Charter amendment at the 2024 general election, which the Maryland State Board of Elections supervises and administers in conjunction with the local board of elections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters and increases various annual, supplementary, and renewal licensing fees for alcoholic beverages in Baltimore City, and authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to set certain per diem and tasting license fees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders and applicants in Baltimore City, including bars, restaurants, breweries, package stores, and event venues
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City licensing and fee revenues are estimated to increase by approximately $823,200 beginning in FY 2025 and annually thereafter due to the fee increases. City expenditures are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the requirement that drivers traveling slower than the general speed of traffic drive in the right-hand lane, if practicable as determined by the driver, from rural interstate highways to all roadways in the State. The bill specifies that this requirement serves as State policy and guidance rather than an offense subject to citations, directs the Motor Vehicle Administration to include it in driver education, and authorizes the State Highway Administration to install informative road signs and use dynamic message signs.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland drivers, particularly slow-moving motorists, and driver education students
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by at least $250,000 and up to $750,000 in FY 2025 only for the State Highway Administration to install between 500 and 1,500 informational signs statewide at an estimated cost of $500 per sign. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Highway Administration is directly responsible for implementing the bill's public notification provisions, including the placement and maintenance of 500 to 1,500 highway signs and the use of dynamic message signs, resulting in an estimated fiscal cost of $250,000 to $750,000 in FY 2025.
The Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the modal administrations implementing the bill (SHA and MVA), and the bill directly increases expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund.
The Motor Vehicle Administration is statutorily tasked with incorporating the expanded slow-moving vehicle right-hand lane requirement into Maryland's driver education curriculum.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing traffic rules on highways, MSP must be aware of statewide rules of the road changes, though the bill explicitly prohibits issuing citations for this specific provision.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the minimum amount of general liability insurance required for licensed home improvement contractors and license applicants from $50,000 to $500,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Home Improvement Commission, Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed home improvement contractors, applicants for home improvement contractor licenses, and Maryland homeowners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC) finances or operations, and has no local fiscal impact. The small business impact is minimal because contractor liability insurance policies in practice are already typically written for $500,000 or $1,000,000.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC), housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, licenses and regulates home improvement contractors and enforces mandatory liability insurance requirements for licensees.

As the state's insurance regulator, the Maryland Insurance Administration oversees the market, rates, and policy forms for commercial general liability insurance products required of licensed contractors.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Stadium Authority to conduct a feasibility study on establishing and operating a sports tourism facility at Reisterstown Regional Park in northwest Baltimore County, and to report its findings and recommendations by December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, local businesses, visitors, and sports recreation participants in northwest Baltimore County and Reisterstown Regional Park.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Stadium Authority increase by $300,000 in FY 2025 and $100,000 in FY 2026 ($400,000 total) to complete the feasibility study. Other consulting State agencies and Baltimore County can participate using existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Stadium Authority to conduct a feasibility study on developing, establishing, and operating a sports tourism facility at Reisterstown Regional Park, requiring $400,000 in general fund expenditures across FY 2025 and FY 2026 and submission of a final report by December 31, 2025.
The Maryland Stadium Authority is required by the bill to consult with the Maryland Department of Commerce in conducting the feasibility study.
The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Stadium Authority to consult with the Maryland Transit Administration during the preparation of the feasibility study.
The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration, which is required to be consulted under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the holder of a stadium alcoholic beverages license in Frederick County to sell liquor for on-premises consumption, in addition to beer and wine, and increases the annual license fee from $2,000 to $2,500.
qa_results.responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Frederick County stadium license holders, professional baseball team franchises, and stadium event attendees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Frederick County local revenues increase by $500 annually beginning as early as FY 2024 due to the increase in the stadium license fee from $2,000 to $2,500. Any additional enforcement activities can be handled by Frederick County using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation of the alcohol industry and collects state sales and excise taxes on alcoholic beverages. While this bill specifically alters local licensing provisions administered by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader alcoholic beverages regulatory and tax framework overseen by the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the holder of a promoter's permit in Frederick County to sell beer, wine, and liquor at an event, provided the permit holder does not hold an alcoholic beverages license.
qa_results.responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: For-profit event organizers and promoters in Frederick County, event attendees, and local businesses hosting or supplying events.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect Frederick County finances or operations. The impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article regarding local promoter permits to sell beer, wine, and liquor in Frederick County. While the permit is administered locally by the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County and has no direct state fiscal impact, the Comptroller of Maryland maintains general regulatory and tax oversight over the state's alcoholic beverage industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates the Maryland Corporations and Associations Article by authorizing corporations and real estate investment trusts to adopt emergency bylaws and take specific operational actions during catastrophic events. It protects corporate directors, officers, employees, and agents from liability for good-faith emergency actions, clarifies when shares cease to be outstanding upon redemption or repurchase, and updates definitions relating to principal offices and resident agents.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland corporations, limited liability companies, limited partnerships, real estate investment trusts, and their directors, officers, agents, and stockholders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and it does not directly affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters corporate governance provisions, authorizes emergency bylaws, and limits civil liability for corporate directors, officers, employees, and agents acting in good faith during an emergency, which impacts civil litigation and matters adjudicated within the state court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to offer applicants for investment financing the voluntary option to provide demographic and business location information without penalty, and requires TEDCO to submit an annual report detailing investment activity and de-identified, disaggregated demographic data.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO)
qa_results.stakeholders: Technology-based businesses, entrepreneurs, and business founders applying for TEDCO investment funding.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for TEDCO increase by $50,000 to $75,000 (midpoint of $62,500) in FY 2025 for one-time information technology costs to update application forms. TEDCO staff can absorb operational and reporting requirements with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends TEDCO's governing statute, requiring the corporation to add voluntary demographic disclosure options to its investment applications and compile an annual disaggregated demographic and investment report, resulting in estimated IT expenditures of $50,000 to $75,000 in FY 2025.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of TEDCO's annual report detailing investment applications, funding, awards, and demographic data.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the membership of the State Board of Social Work Examiners by allowing a licensed master social worker approved for independent practice to fill a board position previously reserved solely for a licensed certified social worker. It also eliminates obsolete statutory references to certified social worker licenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland licensed social workers, specifically licensed master social workers approved for independent practice and licensed certified social workers, as well as applicants and members of the State Board of Social Work Examiners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The bill is clarifying in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners is a health occupation licensing board that operates under the regulatory umbrella of the Maryland Department of Health.
The bill maintains the statutory requirement that one member of the State Board of Social Work Examiners must be a licensed social worker employed by the Department of Human Services.
The Governor is statutorily responsible for appointing members to the State Board of Social Work Examiners, subject to Senate advice and consent.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing candidates for vacancies on state boards and commissions, including the State Board of Social Work Examiners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Secretary of State, upon request, to provide a State flag wholly produced in the United States to drape the casket of an eligible decedent—such as state or local employees who died from job-related injuries, current or former Governors, legislators, judges, or constitutional officers—and establishes procedures for claiming the flag after burial.
qa_results.responsible_party: Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: Next of kin, family members, or associates of eligible deceased Maryland public servants, elected officials, judges, and state or local employees killed in the line of duty.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $14,000 in FY 2025 for the Secretary of State to purchase an initial inventory of 100 cotton flags (approximately $140 per flag), with ongoing minimal annual increases for postage and replenishing inventory. Revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Secretary of State with procuring State flags wholly produced in the United States, adopting regulations to manage requests and verification, and furnishing flags to drape the caskets of eligible decedents, resulting in a direct operational and fiscal impact.
The bill authorizes the Governor to designate additional individuals as eligible decedents via executive order to receive a State flag.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a supervised medical graduate who meets specified educational and examination requirements to perform delegated clinical duties under the direct supervision of a licensed physician for up to two years, pursuant to regulations adopted by the Maryland State Board of Physicians. Additionally, it repeals the September 30, 2024 termination date of Chapter 445 of 2019, making permanent the authority of licensed physicians to delegate duties to registered cardiovascular invasive specialists during cardiac catheterization procedures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Physicians
qa_results.stakeholders: Medical school graduates awaiting residency, licensed delegating physicians, registered cardiovascular invasive specialists, hospitals with cardiac catheterization laboratories, small business healthcare providers, and patients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Physicians expenditures are not materially affected, as regulations can be adopted using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local government fiscal impact. Small business healthcare practices may experience a meaningful beneficial impact from the ability to delegate clinical duties to supervised medical graduates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses and oversees the state health occupations licensing boards, including the Maryland State Board of Physicians (MBP). This bill directly requires the Board of Physicians to adopt rules and regulations governing the delegation of duties to supervised medical graduates and permanently authorizes the delegation of duties to registered cardiovascular invasive specialists.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs) practicing in Maryland to provide written notification to patients and post a conspicuous notice in their practice location if they do not maintain professional liability insurance or if their coverage has lapsed. The signed notification must be retained in the patient's records, and the State Board of Nursing is required to develop standard language for the notice.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs) and their patients in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. The Maryland Board of Nursing can develop the required written notification language using existing budgeted resources. There is no direct effect on local government finances or operations, and the impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Board of Nursing, a regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, with developing the required written notification language informing patients about an advanced practice registered nurse's professional liability insurance coverage status.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each local school system to submit a report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by November 1 of the third year of a six-year audit cycle detailing the implementation status of corrective actions for repeat findings and recommendations from its most recent Office of Legislative Audits review. It also requires school systems to publish the report on their website with any cybersecurity findings redacted.
qa_results.responsible_party: Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee
qa_results.stakeholders: Local school systems, county boards of education, school administrators, and Maryland taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. Local school system expenditures may increase minimally to address repeat audit findings, depending on existing capacity and scope; local revenues are not affected. Cybersecurity redactions and website postings can be performed with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly concerns audits conducted by the Office of Legislative Audits (OLA) under the State Government Article, establishing a reporting timeline and requirement for local school systems to report corrective action on repeat findings and recommendations identified in OLA's six-year audit cycle.

The bill amends provisions in the Education Article governing local school system financial audits and reporting, which fall under the broad regulatory and administrative oversight of the Maryland State Department of Education and the State Superintendent.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a school bus stop from being located on any highway in Montgomery County with five or more undivided traffic lanes beginning December 31, 2026, unless a school crossing guard is posted to assist students or a traffic control device maintaining a red signal during boarding and exiting is installed.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Public Schools and Montgomery County Government
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County public school students, parents, bus drivers, crossing guards, and local motorists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Montgomery County expenditures may significantly increase beginning in FY 2026 to hire crossing guards, install traffic control devices, or relocate bus stops. Furthermore, local revenues from school bus monitoring cameras could decrease if bus stops are moved away from multi-lane undivided roadways; specific dollar amounts are unquantified.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 761 amends the Education Article (§ 7-801.1) to regulate the placement of school bus stops on certain multi-lane highways in Montgomery County. As the state agency overseeing public education standards and policies, MSDE monitors student transportation regulations.

The bill regulates school bus stops along highways with five or more undivided lanes, requiring specific traffic control devices or crossing guards. MDOT oversees roadway infrastructure and traffic safety standards across state roads.

SHA is responsible for traffic signal management, highway safety improvements, and engineering on state highways outside of Baltimore City. Undivided five-lane roadways in Montgomery County that may require traffic control devices or modifications involve SHA-maintained roadways and permitting.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Class B beer, wine, and liquor license holders in Montgomery County to sell beer and wine in original sealed containers for off-premises consumption to customers who purchase prepared food, subject to certain operating restrictions and regulations established by the Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County restaurants and hotels holding Class B beer, wine, and liquor licenses, and their patrons.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not anticipated to materially affect Montgomery County operations or finances. Small businesses holding eligible Class B licenses may experience an increase in sales.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees state sales and alcoholic beverage tax collections and regulates aspects of the alcohol industry. Although this legislation specifically pertains to local licensing under the Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates to the retail sale of alcoholic beverages under the Comptroller's broader regulatory and tax purview.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the composition of the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention within the Office of the Attorney General by replacing several specific organizational seats with 15 members representing or advocating on behalf of protected classes under Maryland hate crime laws (appointed with Senate advice and consent) and adding a representative from the Office of the Public Defender. The bill also resets existing terms and establishes a termination date for the Commission of June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of protected classes under Maryland hate crime laws, civil rights and community advocacy organizations, criminal justice and law enforcement agencies, and members of the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention is established within the Office of the Attorney General, chaired by the Attorney General (or designee), and staffed by the office. The Attorney General is also responsible for appointing members of the Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the composition of the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention to specifically add a representative of the Office of the Public Defender as a member.
The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights holds a designated statutory seat on the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention, whose membership and structure are altered by this bill.
The Maryland Center for School Safety holds a designated statutory seat on the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.
The Commission is mandated to report annually to the State Department of Education with policy recommendations addressing hate crimes occurring in schools.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory membership, appointment terms, and operations of an executive branch commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters distributions from the State Lottery Fund by requiring an annual transfer of $27.0 million to the Bus Rapid Transit Fund and $27.0 million to the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund. It expands authorized uses of the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund to include all expenses incurred or approved by the Maryland Stadium Authority related to corridor facilities, and requires the Authority to submit a comprehensive development report on the corridor by December 15, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority, Maryland Department of Transportation, and the Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Public transit users, local governments operating or developing bus rapid transit systems (including Montgomery County), and residents, businesses, and developers in the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $8.8 million in FY 2025 due to an accelerated distribution of lottery revenues to the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund, with nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the fund increasing by an equivalent $8.8 million in FY 2025. It codifies annual $27.0 million transfers to both the Bus Rapid Transit Fund and the Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund. Local governments, including Prince George's County, can handle engagement and reporting with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 764 directly affects the Maryland Stadium Authority (MSA) by altering authorized expenditures and funding distributions for the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund, which MSA administers. It also mandates that MSA complete and submit a development study and report regarding the Blue Line Corridor by December 15, 2024.

The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) administers the Bus Rapid Transit Fund and is responsible for awarding and distributing grants to eligible jurisdictions. HB 764 codifies an annual $27 million distribution from the State Lottery Fund to this program and requires MSA to consult MDOT on the Blue Line Corridor report.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory distribution formulas and mandates governing how proceeds from the State Lottery Fund are allocated across various specialized funds, which directly governs the agency's fund apportionment framework.

The Comptroller is statutorily required to distribute State Lottery Fund proceeds according to the altered formulas in the bill and maintains the accounting for the Prince George’s County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund.

The bill impacts state fiscal planning and budget execution by decreasing General Fund revenues by $8.8 million in FY 2025 due to the acceleration of mandated lottery distributions to the Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund.

The Maryland Stadium Authority is required to consult and meaningfully engage with the Department of Housing and Community Development in preparing the mandated report on development in the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund separately and invest the money in the fund in the same manner as other state funds.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City and county or municipal governing bodies to grant a property tax credit for newly constructed or substantially rehabilitated hotel and residential development projects. To qualify, a hotel must substantially increase the property's assessed value, and a residential development project must consist of at least 20 units with at least 15% designated as affordable for households earning less than 80% of the area median income.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties, municipal corporations, and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Developers and owners of qualifying hotel and residential projects, low-to-moderate-income households seeking affordable housing, and local county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: County and municipal property tax revenues will decrease beginning in FY 2025 to the extent jurisdictions authorize the tax credit. The precise decrease cannot be reliably estimated because it is contingent on local enactment, the number of eligible properties, assessed values, and the credit amounts granted. Local expenditures are not directly affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits individuals from standing in a roadway, median divider, or intersection to solicit money or donations of any kind from vehicle occupants in Calvert County.
qa_results.responsible_party: Calvert County local law enforcement and Maryland law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals and charitable organizations seeking roadside donations, as well as motorists and law enforcement officers in Calvert County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances or operations, nor is it expected to materially affect Calvert County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Transportation Article to prohibit roadside solicitation in roadways, median dividers, and intersections in Calvert County, affecting roadway use and transportation safety regulations under MDOT's purview.

As a modal administration of MDOT responsible for state highways and roadway safety, the State Highway Administration oversees state road rights-of-way and medians affected by this roadside solicitation restriction.
The Maryland State Police enforces state traffic and vehicle laws on Maryland roadways and would have the authority to enforce this prohibition in Calvert County.
Citations issued for violations of this provision in Calvert County would be processed and adjudicated through the Maryland District Court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a line-of-duty special death benefit for members of the Judges' Retirement System (JRS) killed in the course of performance of duty without willful negligence, consisting of accumulated contributions and an allowance of two-thirds of the current salary for the judicial position. It provides retroactive eligibility for surviving spouses of JRS members killed prior to the bill's effective date and allows eligible surviving spouses, children, or dependent parents to participate in the State employee health plan with the maximum retiree subsidy.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Judges' Retirement System and their surviving spouses, children under 26 or disabled, and dependent parents; surviving beneficiaries of state employees killed in the line of duty eligible for retiree health benefits.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities, contribution rates, and health care expenditures are expected to experience no discernible effect, as the bill is assumed to apply in only a very limited number of cases (the State Retirement Agency identified only one individual eligible for the retroactive benefit). There is no effect on revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency manages the State Retirement and Pension System, which includes the Judges' Retirement System. The agency is directly responsible for administering the newly established line-of-duty special death benefit and processing retroactive death benefit claims under the bill.

The Department of Budget and Management administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The bill directly alters eligibility and mandates the maximum retiree state subsidy for surviving spouses and dependents receiving this special death benefit.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Judicial Branch, whose judges comprise the membership of the Judges' Retirement System affected by this line-of-duty death benefit legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Individuals with Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund, administered by the Maryland Department of Disabilities, to provide grants of up to $40,000 per year to eligible nonprofit organizations that offer sailing, boating, kayaking, canoeing, paddleboarding, and surfing opportunities to individuals with disabilities and service-disabled veterans.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities, service-disabled veterans, and qualifying 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations providing adaptive boating and water sports activities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by at least $47,000 in FY 2025 (rising to $60,300 by FY 2029) to capitalize the fund to cover administrative expenses, specifically hiring one part-time grants coordinator; special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly. General fund expenditures and special fund transactions will increase further by an indeterminate amount to capitalize and award grants of up to $40,000 per nonprofit. The bill has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Department of Disabilities administer the newly created Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund, manage grant allocations to eligible nonprofit organizations, and hire administrative personnel.
The statute explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund.
The statute explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer hold the new special, nonlapsing fund separately.
The legislation directly targets service-disabled veterans as key beneficiaries of the boating and outdoor recreation opportunities funded by the program.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of $500,000 to the fund in the annual state budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2026.
DBM oversees the state budget execution and personnel management, which will be involved in accommodating the new staffing and discretionary budget appropriations for the fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), subject to a written agreement, to provide administrative support and services to entities it creates, owns, controls, or is a member of, and to receive compensation for providing those services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) and business entities created, owned, controlled by, or partnered with TEDCO.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly increase expenditures or revenues for TEDCO, as it is clarifying in nature regarding existing authority to recover costs for administrative services. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 776 directly amends the statutory authority of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), specifically authorizing it, subject to a written agreement, to provide administrative services and support to certain entities it creates, owns, controls, or is a member of, and to receive compensation for providing those services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes competitive sealed proposals as the preferred procurement method for State contracts for security services with an expected value greater than $1,000,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: State procurement officers and State procurement units
qa_results.stakeholders: Security service contractors, prospective bidders, and State agencies procuring security services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to have a material effect on State operations or finances, and has no local fiscal impact. Any effect on small business contractors is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS serves as the primary operational support and central procurement authority for the State of Maryland, overseeing state facilities, Capitol Police, and contracts for state building security services that exceed the $1,000,000 threshold.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state procurement contracts and regulations under State Finance and Procurement law, including high-value security contracts and notice requirements.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel on state procurement matters and is statutorily designated within the amended section to approve in writing any corrections or withdrawals of proposals or best and final offers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes certain officers of volunteer fire companies to equip their privately owned vehicles with red or red and white emergency lights, and permits volunteer fire company fire police to equip their privately owned vehicles with red, red and white, or red and green emergency lights or signal devices.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Volunteer fire company officers, volunteer fire company fire police, volunteer fire departments, and the motoring public.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations. It is authorizing in nature and does not directly affect local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is responsible for administering Maryland Vehicle Law and vehicle equipment standards, including lighting designations authorized by the Motor Vehicle Administrator.
The Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the state's transportation policies and statutory framework within the Transportation Article governing vehicle equipment and highway safety.
The Maryland State Police enforces vehicle and traffic safety laws on state roadways, including regulations governing unauthorized or permitted emergency lights on privately owned vehicles.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS coordinates the statewide emergency medical services system, is explicitly referenced in the amended statute regarding emergency vehicle lighting authorizations, and provided input on the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Freedom to Read Act establishes State standards for school library media programs and state-funded public libraries, prohibiting the removal or exclusion of materials based on partisan, ideological, or religious disapproval or the creator's background. It requires local school systems to create uniform procedures for reviewing material objections (requiring materials to remain accessible during review), protects library personnel from retaliation for upholding these standards, and authorizes the State Comptroller to withhold State funds from libraries that fail to adopt compliant policies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency, Maryland State Library Board, and the State Comptroller
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents and guardians, school personnel, school and public librarians and library staff, and public library patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local fiscal impacts are minimal. The Maryland State Library Agency, local school systems, and local libraries can implement the requirements using existing resources. State funding to regional resource centers, cooperative programs, or county library systems may be withheld by the Comptroller if they fail to adopt policies consistent with the State standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the duties of the State Library Board and Maryland State Library Agency (MSLA), requiring them to develop policies aligned with the new State standards for libraries, ensure funded libraries adhere to these standards, and certify compliance or noncompliance for funding withholding.

The bill creates State policy and standards governing school library media programs across all local school systems, mandates objection review policies and timelines, and establishes employment protections against retaliation for school library personnel.

The bill mandates that the Comptroller withhold State funding from regional resource centers, metropolitan cooperative service programs, and county library systems upon certification by the State Library Board that they have failed to meet the State standards for libraries.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill includes correctional facility libraries under the definition of libraries subject to the State standards for library operation, impacting how libraries within state correctional institutions manage collections and services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Dental Examiners to waive certain dental education requirements for foreign-trained applicants seeking a limited license to practice dentistry on adults, in addition to pediatric dentistry, provided they fulfill service requirements in public health clinics or qualified health centers. The bill also establishes a pathway for these practitioners to obtain a general license to practice dentistry in Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Foreign-trained dentists, adult dental patients in underserved populations (including Medicaid, uninsured, and indigent patients), public health dental clinics, and federally or Maryland qualified health centers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled within existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not likely affected. Any impact on local health departments can also be absorbed with existing resources, with local health departments potentially benefiting from an expanded pool of licensees to fill adult dental care vacancies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses and oversees health occupation regulatory boards, including the State Board of Dental Examiners, which is responsible for implementing this bill by granting waivers and issuing limited and general dental licenses.

The bill explicitly references the University of Maryland School of Dentistry (part of the University System of Maryland), expanding qualifying fellowship programs and adjusting statutory provisions involving dental school fellowship completion.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Allegany Regional Recreational Economic Development Authority in Allegany County to support the planning, development, and construction of regional recreation facilities, including indoor and outdoor athletic fields and other recreational tourism amenities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Allegany Regional Recreational Economic Development Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and visitors of Allegany County, local businesses, the municipalities of Cumberland and Frostburg, Frostburg State University, and Allegany College.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct State fiscal impact; expense reimbursements and staffing are anticipated to be handled using existing resources, and State funding is authorized but not mandated. Local expenditures may increase minimally if participating local governments cannot absorb administrative and staffing needs within existing resources. Local and State revenues are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the President of Frostburg State University—a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland—or their designee as a voting member of the newly established Authority, and notes that the Authority may manage university funds associated with planning and design for a regional sports complex.
The newly established Allegany Regional Recreational Economic Development Authority is required to submit an annual report of its activities to the Governor by October 31 each year.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Carroll County to borrow up to $29.8 million through the issuance of general obligation bonds to finance the acquisition, construction, improvement, and renovation of public facilities and infrastructure, including public schools, water and sewer projects, roads, agricultural land preservation, and loans to volunteer fire departments.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Carroll County
qa_results.stakeholders: Carroll County residents, public school students and staff, and local volunteer fire departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Carroll County revenues increase by up to $29.8 million from bond proceeds. County debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $2.1 million annually over a 20-year period, based on a 3.37% interest rate.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters release and conditional release proceedings for individuals committed to the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) after being found not criminally responsible (NCR). It applies circuit court civil discovery rules to administrative release hearings, requires MDH and courts to promptly notify a committed person's counsel of alleged release violations, mandates court hearings upon request regarding applications to modify conditional release under a preponderance of the evidence standard, obligates MDH to disclose certain evaluations and records upon written request, and authorizes courts to shorten, extend (by up to five years), or terminate conditional releases.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals committed to state facilities after being found not criminally responsible (NCR), defense counsel (including the Office of the Public Defender), State's Attorneys, and MDH personnel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by as much as $377,041 in FY 2025 (reflecting the October 1, 2024 effective date) and rise to $500,600 by FY 2029. This covers six new positions at MDH (three paralegals, one administrative officer, and two social workers) to manage circuit court civil discovery requirements and additional release hearings. State revenues are unaffected, and local governments experience no material fiscal impact beyond potential operational efficiencies for State's Attorneys' offices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends procedures for individuals committed to MDH psychiatric facilities following a finding of not criminally responsible. MDH is required to provide comprehensive evaluations and reports upon written request, provide notices of conditional release violations to defense counsel, and manage discovery demands under circuit court civil rules, resulting in an estimated fiscal impact of over $377,000 and six additional positions.

Administrative Law Judges from OAH conduct the administrative release and conditional release revocation hearings for committed individuals. The bill applies circuit court civil discovery rules to these administrative proceedings, requiring OAH to adjust procedures and handle discovery disputes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD attorneys represent the vast majority of individuals committed to MDH facilities facing release, revocation, or conditional release modification proceedings. The bill ensures counsel of record receives mandatory violation notices, access to MDH records upon written request, and discovery rights under civil court rules.

The bill directly impacts court procedures by requiring prompt notice to defense counsel regarding conditional release violations, mandating hearings upon request for changes in conditional release, and codifying the court's authority to shorten, terminate, or extend conditional release terms.

As legal counsel representing MDH and its state healthcare facilities, OAG may be called upon to advise on, respond to, and litigate civil discovery demands, subpoenas, and disputes arising in administrative release proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies local zoning restrictions and distance requirements for licensed cannabis dispensaries and growers, prohibiting political subdivisions from adopting zoning rules for cannabis dispensaries that are more restrictive than those for licensed alcohol retail dealers. It also establishes a process allowing groups of at least 10 nearby residents, commercial tenants, or property owners within 1,000 feet to file a sworn protest with the Maryland Cannabis Administration against a cannabis license renewal.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Cannabis dispensary and cultivation licensees, local governments and zoning authorities, and property owners, residents, and commercial tenants located within 1,000 feet of licensed cannabis establishments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures and revenues for the Maryland Cannabis Administration may increase minimally from FY 2028 through FY 2030 (including an estimated $44,100 in FY 2028 and $78,700 in FY 2029 if a contractual employee is needed) to conduct protest-of-renewal hearings. Any increase in operational costs slightly reduces remaining adult-use cannabis sales and use tax revenues distributed to the General Fund, specified special funds, and counties. Local zoning departments can implement changes with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA) is the primary regulatory agency tasked with implementing the bill. MCA is directly responsible for receiving and reviewing protests against cannabis license renewals, holding hearings on valid protests, issuing determinations, and promulgating implementing regulations.

MCA routinely delegates contested regulatory hearings to the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH). Under the bill, mandatory hearings on contested cannabis license renewals may be delegated to OAH administrative law judges, resulting in an operational impact on the agency's caseload.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Physician Assistant Modernization Act of 2024 transitions physician assistants (PAs) from delegation agreements to collaboration agreements with patient care team physicians, expands the PA scope of practice and prescriptive authority, and updates licensure qualifications and advanced duty approval processes. It also allows federally employed PAs to practice in Maryland during declared disasters and explicitly defines PAs as healthcare providers for medical malpractice claims.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Board of Physicians (within the Maryland Department of Health)
qa_results.stakeholders: Physician assistants, patient care team physicians, healthcare facilities, and patients in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Board of Physicians are not expected to be materially affected, as any revenue loss from ending standard delegation agreement approval fees ($200 per submission) can be offset by setting fees for approving collaboration agreements that include advanced duties. State expenditures are unchanged, as the board can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources and may experience a reduced workload regarding agreement reviews. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Physicians, which is the primary regulatory and licensing body responsible for implementing the bill, including establishing collaboration agreement procedures, regulating PA scope of practice, and reviewing advanced duties.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Office of Controlled Substances Administration to enter and inspect the practice offices of physician assistants who dispense prescription drugs and directly implicates CDS registrations required for PA prescriptive authority.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Courts and Judicial Proceedings § 3-2A-01, the foundational statute governing medical malpractice claims filed with HCADRO, by explicitly adding physician assistants to the statutory definition of 'health care provider.'

The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article to update qualifications for physician assistants acting as certifying providers under the state's cannabis program, replacing the delegation agreement requirement with a collaboration agreement.
The bill amends the Education Article regarding student physical examination requirements, permitting PAs with active collaboration agreements to perform required school physical examinations.

The bill amends Transportation Article § 13-616, updating the definition of a licensed physician assistant authorized to certify disabilities for special registration plates and placards issued by the MVA.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 807 updates the statutory definition of submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) surveys beyond traditional aerial surveys to include alternative surveys approved by the Department of Natural Resources and the EPA's Chesapeake Bay Program. It also mandates that the Department of Natural Resources study and report on the feasibility and implications of using alternative methods other than aerial surveys to delineate SAV protection zones by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial watermen, clammers and dredgers, aquaculture leaseholders and applicants, environmental conservation organizations, and bay researchers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not expected to be affected, as the Department of Natural Resources can complete the required study using existing budgeted resources. If the department chooses to adopt additional or alternative survey methods in the future, general fund expenditures would increase by an indeterminate amount depending on the survey method and scope. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) with approving submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) surveys, delineating and adjusting SAV protection zones, and conducting a comprehensive study and report to the General Assembly on the feasibility of alternative survey methods.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes an annual $1,000 local delivery service permit authorizing holders to deliver alcoholic beverages from licensed retailers to consumers within the same jurisdiction in localities where boards have adopted authorizing regulations, establishing requirements for age verification, delivery operations, and penalties for violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local alcoholic beverages licensing boards and the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcohol retail license holders, third-party delivery services and drivers, adult alcohol consumers (age 21 and older), and local licensing authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues and expenditures are not materially affected.
