As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and the state budget, which will be fiscally impacted by an estimated increase in annual state pension contributions of approximately $4.87 million beginning in FY 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the timeframe under which the State of Maryland can recover grant funding awarded under the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program if a facility is transferred or ceases to operate as a federally qualified health center. Specifically, it reduces the State's recovery window from 30 years to 15 years after project completion if the property was leased by the health center, while maintaining the 30-year recovery period if the property was owned by the health center.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), nonprofit organizations, and local governments (counties and municipalities) that own, lease, or operate FQHC facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational workloads can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. General fund revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount sooner than expected due to the accelerated recovery timeline for certain leased properties. The bill has no direct effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHC) Grant Program, recommends grants to the Board of Public Works, and monitors compliance regarding the use and potential recovery of grant funds.

The Board of Public Works awards grants under the FQHC Grant Program upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Health and approves any potential transferees to avoid triggering state recovery proceedings.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State of Maryland in legal proceedings to recover grant funds and associated costs if an FQHC property is improperly transferred or ceases qualifying operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill authorizes certain State officers and employees who are required to be covered by surety bonds to instead be covered by insurance policies. It repeals the Maryland State Employees Surety Bond Committee and transfers its duties to the State Treasurer, who is tasked with determining the required type, amount, and term of coverage and maintaining records of procured insurance policies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Treasurer
qa_results.stakeholders: State officers and employees required to be bonded or insured, and State agencies employing them.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill likely results in operational efficiencies and potential State expenditure savings, as insurance policies may be less expensive than surety bonds. The State Treasurer's Office can implement the requirements using existing resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the State Treasurer and transfers the duties and powers of the Maryland State Employees Surety Bond Committee directly to the State Treasurer, authorizing the Treasurer to determine the type, term, and amount of coverage for state employee bonds and insurance policies.

The Comptroller was a statutory member of the abolished Surety Bond Committee and is tasked under the bill with maintaining official records of all surety bonds purchased for state officers and employees.
The Attorney General was a member of the repealed Maryland State Employees Surety Bond Committee and previously had specific statutory duties regarding approving the form of bonds.
The bill repeals the requirement under former law that the Board of Public Works provide prior approval for the purchase, cancellation, or termination of surety bonds by the State Treasurer.

The bill tasks the Governor, in consultation with the State Treasurer, with determining coverage for insurance policies covering the State Treasurer, and retains the Governor's role in approving bonds/insurance for correctional leadership and the Comptroller.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally abolishes a statutory executive entity, the Maryland State Employees Surety Bond Committee, and transfers its functions to the State Treasurer.

The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article regarding the use of the Unemployment Insurance Administration Fund for insurance policy premiums and requires the State Treasurer to consult with the Secretary of Labor on coverage.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Correctional Services Article to authorize insurance policies in lieu of surety bonds for the Commissioner and employees of the Division of Correction.
The bill amends the Insurance Article to permit insurance policy coverage in lieu of surety bonds for the Insurance Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner.
The bill updates the State Personnel and Pensions Article regarding surety bond and insurance requirements for fiduciaries of the State Retirement and Pension System.
The bill amends the Education Article (§ 18-1908) governing bonding and insurance coverage requirements for fiduciaries of Maryland 529 trust funds.
The bill amends the Transportation Article (§ 8-204) authorizing employees of the Administration to be covered by an insurance policy in lieu of a surety bond as determined by the State Treasurer.
The bill amends statutory requirements in the State Government Article regarding surety bond or insurance policy coverage for the Legislative Auditor.

The bill updates Agriculture Article sections (§ 8-205 and § 8-303) governing surety bonding and insurance policies for officers and employees of the State Soil Conservation Committee and soil conservation districts.
The bill updates Natural Resources Article provisions governing bonding and insurance requirements for the Treasurer, Deputy Treasurer, and designated officers/employees of the Service.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a licensed clinical professional counselor to sign the certificate of illness or disability required for an employee in the State Personnel Management System to receive paid sick leave when using five or more consecutive workdays for personal or immediate family illness or disability.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: State Personnel Management System employees and licensed clinical professional counselors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill generally codifies existing administrative practice, is procedural in nature, and does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM serves as the central personnel agency for the State of Maryland and administers the State Personnel Management System (SPMS), including the leave policies and certificate of illness requirements amended by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Frederick County School Construction Master Plan Workgroup to evaluate school facility needs, examine solutions to balance fiscal demands with educational construction priorities, and explore cost-saving and cost-sharing opportunities for new projects, maintenance, and renovations, with a report due by December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Frederick County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Frederick County Public Schools students, staff, administrators, and Frederick County taxpayers and local officials.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local fiscal impacts are minimal; the Interagency Commission on School Construction and Frederick County Public Schools can fulfill workgroup duties and staffing requirements using existing resources. Neither state nor local revenues are affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1016 explicitly designates one member of the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) to serve on the Frederick County School Construction Master Plan Workgroup and requires the workgroup to submit its findings and recommendations to the IAC by December 31, 2024.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary statutory body, the Frederick County School Construction Master Plan Workgroup, to study educational facility needs and report recommendations before sunsetting on June 30, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Consolidates the two existing soil conservation districts in Frederick County—the Catoctin Soil Conservation District and the Frederick Soil Conservation District—into a single Frederick County Soil Conservation District with boundaries corresponding to Frederick County.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Landowners, agricultural producers, farmers, and soil conservation district personnel and supervisors in Frederick County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations. While statute maintains a $10.0 million mandated appropriation for statewide soil conservation districts, consolidating the two Frederick County districts into one does not materially change State expenditures for the Maryland Department of Agriculture or Frederick County's local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Agriculture Article to consolidate two soil conservation districts in Frederick County into a single district. The Maryland Department of Agriculture oversees statewide soil conservation programs and provides technical, financial, and staffing assistance to soil conservation districts.

The bill updates statutory language regarding the Governor's mandated annual budget appropriation for the state's soil conservation districts, which DBM administers as the state's principal budgeting agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Washington County to borrow up to $50,000,000 through the issuance and sale of general obligation bonds to finance the acquisition, construction, improvement, or renovation of public facilities, including public schools, public works, water and sewer projects, emergency facilities, and loans to volunteer fire departments.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Washington County
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, public school students and staff, and volunteer fire departments in Washington County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Washington County bond proceeds and revenues increase by up to $50.0 million. County debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $3.4 million annually over a 20-year period based on a 3.37% interest rate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill exempts the authorized Washington County general obligation bonds, refunding bonds, and any interest or income derived from them from all State taxation, which falls under the tax administration and collection purview of the Comptroller of Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: The bill reforms operations of the Washington Suburban Transit Commission (WSTC) and Maryland's representation on the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) Board. It permits the Secretary of Transportation's designee to attend WMATA Board meetings with full voting powers whenever the Secretary is unavailable, allows the WSTC commissioner serving on the WMATA Board to be reappointed, and eliminates the requirement that Montgomery and Prince George's county governing bodies review and approve contracts and agreements entered into by WSTC.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation and the Washington Suburban Transit Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and transit riders in Montgomery and Prince George's counties, the Washington Suburban Transit Commission, county governing bodies, and the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority Board of Directors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT). It authorizes the Secretary of Transportation's designee—who must be an MDOT employee—to attend meetings of the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) Board of Directors with full powers when the Secretary is unavailable.

WMATA is an interstate compact agency operating among Maryland, Virginia, and the District of Columbia. The bill alters governance and representation rules for Maryland's delegates serving on the WMATA Board of Directors.

The Governor appoints commissioners to the Washington Suburban Transit Commission (WSTC), and the bill authorizes the reappointment of a gubernatorial appointee serving as a principal member on the WMATA Board of Directors.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments and reappointments to state and regional boards, including the gubernatorial seats on the Washington Suburban Transit Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission's (WSSC) Connection Pipe Emergency Replacement Loan Program to cover sewer pipes and diagnostic actions, increases the maximum loan amount from $5,000 to $10,000, doubles the total outstanding loan cap to $2,000,000, increases annual WSSC budget funding from $100,000 to $200,000, and extends the program's termination date to June 30, 2034.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential customers of the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission in Montgomery and Prince George's counties needing pipe repairs or diagnostics, and WSSC-licensed plumbers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. WSSC expenditures increase by $100,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2034 to provide additional funding for the loan program. WSSC revenues increase as customers repay loans through separate charges on their water and sewer bills. WSSC cannot provide or have outstanding more than $2,000,000 in total loans at any given time.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill adds members of the U.S. Space Force to various provisions of Maryland law governing the armed forces. It authorizes military spouses and Maryland residents serving in another state's National Guard or military reserves to cancel or suspend certain service contracts upon receiving relocation orders, adds Space Force and out-of-state National Guard dependents to the Purple Star Schools Program, and authorizes the Governor to posthumously award Maryland Defense Force commissions, appointments, or promotions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Military Department and Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the U.S. Space Force, military service members, military spouses, out-of-state National Guard members residing in Maryland, military-connected students and their families, and consumer service providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Any impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Adjutant General oversees the Maryland Military Department and organized militia; the bill amends statutory provisions concerning the Adjutant General's recommendations to the Governor for appointments, commissions, and promotions in the State militia, as well as the Maryland Code of Military Justice.

The bill updates qualifications, military justice definitions, and civil relief provisions impacting National Guard members, and specifically mandates that service providers deliver notices of service member rights posted on the Maryland National Guard's website.

The bill amends the Education Article to expand the definition of 'military-connected student' under the Purple Star Schools Program, which is administered by the Maryland State Department of Education, to include dependents of Space Force members and out-of-state National Guard members.
The bill authorizes the Governor to posthumously award commissions, appointments, or promotions in the organized militia on recommendation of the Adjutant General.

As the primary state executive agency dedicated to supporting active-duty military members, veterans, and military families, DVMF is directly interested in statutory expansions protecting military families, military spouses, and including the U.S. Space Force.

The bill amends the Family Law Article regarding expedited court hearings and child custody and visitation orders during the deployment of parents serving in the armed forces, including the Space Force.

The bill expands consumer contract cancellation protections and civil relief for military members and spouses, which intersects with the enforcement responsibilities of the Consumer Protection Division within the Office of the Attorney General.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup to develop a framework for reliability and reporting standards for EV charging stations, evaluate governmental accountability, and make recommendations regarding regulations for the retail use of electric vehicle supply equipment. The workgroup is required to submit a report of its findings and recommendations by November 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Electric vehicle owners and drivers, electric vehicle service providers, charging equipment operators and installers, electric utilities, and state regulatory agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly affected: the Public Service Commission can staff the workgroup with existing budgeted resources, and any member expense reimbursements are assumed to be minimal and absorbable. The bill has no effect on State revenues and does not materially affect local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup and requires the Public Service Commission to provide staff, have its Chair designate the workgroup chair, designate two public interest and two private sector members, and appoint a representative to serve on the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates a new temporary study and advisory body, the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup, which terminates on June 30, 2026.
The Director of the Maryland Energy Administration is required to designate a representative to serve as a member of the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup.
The Secretary of Transportation is required to designate a representative from the Maryland Department of Transportation to serve on the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup.

The Comptroller is required to designate a representative to serve on the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup, and the workgroup is charged with evaluating reporting and regulatory frameworks that involve the Office of the Comptroller.

The Secretary of Agriculture is required to designate a representative to serve on the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup, relevant to the department's oversight of weights, measures, and retail commercial standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill codifies and updates the Tourist Area and Corridor (TAC) Signage Program administered by the State Highway Administration (SHA) in collaboration with the Department of Commerce. The program establishes a system of supplemental highway guide signs directing motorists to qualifying recreational, historical, cultural, or leisure attractions, while requiring participating attractions to bear sign fabrication, installation, and maintenance expenses and pay review and annual administrative fees.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration (in collaboration with the Department of Commerce)
qa_results.stakeholders: Tourists and motorists, operators of Maryland cultural, historical, leisure, and recreational attractions (including small businesses), and the State Highway Administration.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures for the Department of Commerce increase by $53,049 in FY 2025 and $14,741 in FY 2026 for a temporary contractual administrator. Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) expenditures for the State Highway Administration increase by $86,397 in FY 2025, rising to $117,900 by FY 2029 for personnel and operating costs. TTF revenues from sign review and annual administrative fees are projected to match TTF expenditures each year. Local governments are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Highway Administration with administering the Tourist Area and Corridor Signage Program, evaluating signage plans, determining highway space availability, issuing permits, and collecting review and annual administrative fees.

The bill explicitly mandates the Department of Commerce to collaborate with the State Highway Administration to establish program standards, provide initial approval for attraction applications, and coordinate signage plans with eligible attractions. The fiscal note also identifies direct general fund expenditures for Commerce to hire staff.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, the Department of Transportation's Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) is directly impacted with expenditures for program administration and corresponding fee revenues.

Operating within the Department of Commerce, the Office of Tourism Development is directly involved in promoting Maryland attractions and destinations, which aligns with the program's purpose of directing motorists to tourism attractions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the number of assistant sheriffs required to be appointed by the Baltimore City Sheriff from one to three, authorizes the Sheriff to appoint up to two social workers, and permits the appointment of additional sworn or civilian personnel if funding is provided in the Baltimore City Ordinance of Estimates or another funding source.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Sheriff
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore City Sheriff's Office personnel, including deputy sheriffs, assistant sheriffs, social workers, civilian staff, and residents of Baltimore City.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Local finances for Baltimore City are also not anticipated to be materially affected; Baltimore City reports no fiscal impact because the bill grants staffing flexibility without altering the city budget authorization process, and additional personnel may only be appointed if funding is provided in the Ordinance of Estimates or other sources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Budget and Management is referenced in the statute reenacted by the bill (Section 2-316(i)(10)) regarding conflicts between rules or regulations and collective bargaining agreements. However, the bill does not materially affect State operations or finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services to evaluate existing reentry programs, identify service gaps, assess measures of successful reentry, and develop plans to create a Division of Returning Citizens within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and expand housing, employment, health, legal, and educational post-release services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals preparing for release, formerly incarcerated individuals (returning citizens), their families, county reentry organizations, workforce development programs, and community-based reentry service providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for staffing costs and travel reimbursements for task force members are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources of the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services. State revenues are not affected. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary implementing agency; it is required to staff the Task Force, has two members designated on the Task Force (the Secretary and a representative of the Division of Parole and Probation), and the Task Force is charged with developing a plan to establish a Division of Returning Citizens within DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services to study reentry services and report findings and recommendations to the General Assembly.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) serves as a member of the Task Force, which is charged with developing plans to expand housing services for returning citizens.

The Secretary of Health (or designee) serves as a member of the Task Force, which is tasked with assessing and expanding health, mental health, and substance abuse counseling services for individuals released from incarceration.

The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) serves as a member of the Task Force, which is charged with evaluating support services and legal assistance relating to child support and family reintegration.

The Secretary of Labor (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force, which will evaluate and plan for expanded employment, entrepreneurship training, and workforce development services for returning citizens.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force to examine reentry services, including legal assistance, record expungement, and barriers to reintegration.
The Attorney General (or designee) serves as a member of the newly established Task Force.
The Governor is responsible for appointing twelve distinct stakeholder representatives and members to the Task Force.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing candidates for gubernatorial appointments to the newly created Task Force.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill streamlines the hiring process for State positions by repealing the requirement that appointing authorities submit selection plans and job announcements to the Secretary of Budget and Management at least one week before posting, and allowing appointing authorities to review qualified applicants before a job announcement closes rather than waiting until after the closing date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Appointing authorities in State government and the Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies, appointing authorities, and applicants for skilled service and professional service positions within the State Personnel Management System
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None. The bill is procedural and does not directly affect state finances, although it creates operational efficiencies by reducing delays in the hiring process. Local Effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM serves as the central personnel agency for the State of Maryland and administers the State Personnel Management System (SPMS). The bill directly modifies SPMS hiring procedures by repealing the requirement that appointing authorities send job announcements to the Secretary of Budget and Management one week prior to posting and permitting applicant reviews prior to the closing of job announcements.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits the sale, offer for sale, or distribution of self-administered sexual assault evidence collection kits not issued by the Maryland Department of Health, classifying violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices subject to enforcement and civil penalties. It renders information indicating physical evidence was obtained using such kits inadmissible in criminal or civil proceedings regarding sexually assaultive behavior, invalidates liability waivers or warranty disclaimers on sexual assault evidence collection products, and establishes the Forensic Nurse Examiner Training Grant Program and Fund to support training for nurses conducting forensic examinations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) and the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of sexual assault, forensic nurses and healthcare providers, nonprofit victim service organizations, institutions of higher education, and sellers/distributors of evidence collection kits.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2025, State general fund expenditures increase by at least $50,000 annually to capitalize the Forensic Nurse Examiner Training Grant Program Fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures are assumed to increase correspondingly by $50,000 annually to award grants to eligible entities. Civil penalty revenues deposited into the fund are anticipated to be negligible. General fund interest earnings increase minimally. Local community colleges and higher education institutions may experience a minimal increase in grant revenues and expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is statutorily designated to administer the newly established Forensic Nurse Examiner Training Grant Program and its associated special fund, including developing the application process and eligibility criteria.

The bill provides that only the Attorney General may enforce the prohibition on self-administered sexual assault evidence collection kits under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, and mandates that the Attorney General adopt statewide regulations implementing specific provisions.
The bill explicitly carves out an exception to the prohibition for any self-administered sexual assault evidence collection kits issued directly by the Maryland Department of Health.
The bill mandates that the State Treasurer hold the Forensic Nurse Examiner Training Grant Program Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the newly created Forensic Nurse Examiner Training Grant Program Fund.
The bill establishes new statutory rules governing the inadmissibility of certain physical evidence in civil and criminal proceedings involving sexually assaultive behavior.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal cases where the new statutory restrictions on the admissibility of physical evidence obtained from self-administered kits will directly apply.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the membership and terms of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, requiring both bodies to meet jointly at least three times per year and coordinate on their annual reporting. It also directs the Commission, in coordination with the Council, to make recommendations regarding Maryland's Medicaid behavioral health carve-out and somatic-behavioral health integration, while expressing legislative intent for the Maryland Department of Health to evaluate the federal Innovation in Behavioral Health Model.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Behavioral Health Advisory Council, and Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access
qa_results.stakeholders: Behavioral health care and substance use disorder treatment providers, Medicaid recipients, individuals with behavioral health disorders and their families, and State health agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and local government operations and finances are not anticipated to be affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by MDH and directly affects its operations, requiring MDH leadership to participate in joint Council and Commission meetings, evaluate the CMS Innovation in Behavioral Health Model, and evaluate Medicaid behavioral health carve-outs and service integration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation directly alters the governance, composition, joint meeting mandates, workgroup deadlines, and reporting responsibilities of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access.

The bill explicitly adds the Secretary of Aging (or designee) as a member of the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access to address geriatric behavioral health, while continuing membership on the Council.
The bill designates the Secretary of Labor (or designee) as a statutory member of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates and maintains statutory representation for the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy on both the Council and the Commission.

The Secretary of Disabilities is an ex officio member of both bodies, which are tasked with developing recommendations on services for individuals with developmental disabilities and complex behavioral health needs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender is a statutory member of the Council and Commission, providing input regarding court-ordered, forensic, and justice-involved populations.
The Governor appoints multiple stakeholder members to both bodies (with member terms altered under the bill) and receives their coordinated annual reports and recommendations.
The Executive Director serves on the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, which examines hospital rates, inpatient care, and behavioral health reimbursement strategies.
The Executive Director serves on the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, participating in assessing statewide service delivery and health infrastructure.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner serves on the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, which oversees parity compliance and insurance carrier practices.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange is a statutory member of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director serves on the Behavioral Health Advisory Council to represent accessibility and behavioral health needs for deaf and hard of hearing individuals.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services serves on both the Council and Commission, which examine youth behavioral health and justice-involved youth services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary serves on both bodies to coordinate behavioral health infrastructure and care for the forensic and incarcerated populations.
The Secretary of Human Services serves on both the Council and Commission to coordinate social services, vulnerable youth, and family behavioral health support.
Representatives of the State Superintendent of Schools and the Division of Rehabilitation Services serve on the Council to coordinate school-based behavioral health and youth transitions.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Maternal Health Act of 2024 establishes requirements for health care providers, birthing facilities, and local health departments concerning maternal health care, assessments, and reporting. It requires Medicaid obstetric providers to complete prenatal risk assessment forms, requires hospitals and freestanding birthing centers to submit postpartum referral forms and conduct follow-up calls within 24 to 48 hours after high-risk deliveries, mandates participation in the Severe Maternal Morbidity Surveillance and Review Program, and directs the Maryland Department of Health to create a Maryland Report Card for Birthing Facility Maternity Care.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant and postpartum individuals (particularly Medicaid recipients and high-risk pregnancy patients), obstetric health care providers, hospitals, freestanding birthing centers, and local health departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Local health departments can likely collect required referral information and submit reports within existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with developing prenatal risk assessment forms, establishing an electronic submission process for providers, receiving annual referral reports from local health departments, publishing the annual Birthing Facility Maternity Care Report Card, and overseeing Medicaid reimbursement and maternal morbidity surveillance.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Health to collaborate with the Maryland Health Care Commission to develop the Maryland Report Card for Birthing Facility Maternity Care and collect the necessary data to complete the annual report card for each facility.
The Governor's Office is designated to receive the final report detailing findings and recommendations on severe maternal morbidity surveillance and quality improvement efforts by December 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue up to 10 new Class B-D-7 licenses and up to 2 new Class A-7 licenses in a specified area of the 46th alcoholic beverages district, creates exemptions to the 300-foot distance requirement from schools and places of worship under certain conditions, permits after-hours exemptions for certain restaurants, extends expiration dates for specific licenses for transfer or renewal purposes, and establishes rules for license conversions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage licensees, prospective license applicants, restaurant and bar operators, community associations, places of worship, schools, and residents in Baltimore City's 46th alcoholic beverages district.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City revenues may increase minimally beginning in FY 2025 from application, licensing, renewal, and transfer fees. Issuing a new Class B-D-7 license generates $1,920 in initial fees and $1,370 annually thereafter; a new Class A-7 license generates $2,100 in initial fees and $1,550 annually thereafter. Additional revenue may also be generated from special transfer fees (such as a $15,000 fee for certain license conversions).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Although the bill is implemented locally by the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City with no direct state fiscal impact, the Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation of the alcohol industry and collection of applicable alcoholic beverage and sales taxes.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the qualifications for the Executive Director of the State Board of Nursing by repealing the requirement that the executive director must be a registered nurse with a master's degree in nursing or equivalent professional education and administrative experience.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Candidates for the Executive Director position of the State Board of Nursing and regulated nursing professionals in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The change in executive director qualifications is technical in nature and does not directly affect governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Nursing is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill alters statutory qualification requirements for the board's executive director, directly impacting the department's operational and regulatory framework.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits pharmaceutical manufacturers in the federal 340B Drug Pricing Program from restricting, denying, or discriminating against the acquisition or delivery of 340B drugs to pharmacies authorized by covered entities, with limited federal exceptions. Violations constitute unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices enforceable with civil fines of up to $5,000 per violation and professional licensing penalties, and the bill directs the Maryland Prescription Drug Affordability Board to conduct a study on the 340B Program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Pharmacy, the Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division), and the Maryland Prescription Drug Affordability Board
qa_results.stakeholders: 340B pharmaceutical manufacturers, wholesale drug distributors, third-party logistics providers, contract pharmacies, 340B covered entities (including federally qualified health centers, Ryan White HIV/AIDS grantees, and certain hospitals), and low-income or uninsured patients who utilize 340B drugs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $39,600 in FY 2025 (rising to $47,600 by FY 2029) for the State Board of Pharmacy to hire a part-time contractual investigator. General fund expenditures increase by $7,500 in both FY 2025 and FY 2026 for the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to hire contractual support for the required study. The Office of the Attorney General and Maryland Department of Health can handle implementation with existing resources, and penalty revenues will have a minimal impact. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill grants investigative, enforcement, and licensing disciplinary authority to the State Board of Pharmacy (a unit within MDH) regarding violations of 340B drug distribution rules, resulting in special fund expenditures for board investigators. MDH is also required to consult on the study of the 340B Program.

The bill classifies violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act and authorizes the Consumer Protection Division of the OAG to investigate alleged violations committed by manufacturers and distributors.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Maryland Prescription Drug Affordability Board (PDAB), an independent state board, with conducting a comprehensive study on the scope, implementation, and finances of the 340B Program and reporting its findings to the General Assembly by July 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the annual salary of the Carroll County Sheriff from $140,000 to $191,078.10 beginning in 2026, and further increases the salary to $212,309 beginning in 2027, taking effect at the start of the next term of office pursuant to constitutional requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County Government
qa_results.stakeholders: Carroll County Sheriff and Carroll County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Carroll County expenditures increase by approximately $47,000 in FY 2027 and by $84,100 annually thereafter to cover the salary increases and associated fringe benefits. County revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references the Department of State Police pay plan (specifically the salary scale for a lieutenant colonel) in establishing the benchmark for the Carroll County Sheriff's salary, though the bill has no operational or fiscal impact on the agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the definition of "underlying crime" used to establish a "pattern of organized crime activity" under Maryland's criminal organization laws. The expansion includes offenses such as using a firearm in the commission of a crime, contraband offenses, felony fraud, bribery, false statements, impersonating a police officer, threat of mass violence, child pornography, felony insurance fraud, VIN tampering, and abuse or neglect of a vulnerable adult.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, Maryland State's Attorneys, and the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals accused or convicted of criminal organization offenses, victims of organized crime, law enforcement, state prosecutors, and state correctional facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase minimally due to the expanded application of incarceration penalties by the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; State revenues are unaffected. Local revenues may experience a potential minimal increase from fines imposed in circuit courts, while local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the definition of 'underlying crime' for criminal organization offenses, potentially increasing felony convictions and commitments to State correctional facilities, leading to a minimal increase in agency incarceration expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Expanding predicate offenses for organized crime charges may increase caseloads and litigation effort for public defenders representing indigent defendants in complex criminal organization prosecutions.

Under Criminal Law § 9-804, the Attorney General has concurrent authority to investigate and prosecute criminal organization violations alongside local State's Attorneys upon request, directly relating to the expansion of actionable underlying crimes.
The Judiciary is responsible for adjudicating expanded criminal organization charges and handling sentencing, restitution, and fine assessments.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, MSP investigates criminal organizations and the expanded list of underlying predicate offenses across multiple jurisdictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Allows a Maryland state income tax subtraction modification for death benefits paid under a collective bargaining agreement by a county or municipality to the surviving spouse or other beneficiary of a law enforcement officer or firefighter who died in the course of employment, applying retroactively to tax year 2022 and beyond.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Surviving spouses and beneficiaries of deceased law enforcement officers and firefighters who receive municipal or county collective bargaining death benefits.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues and local income tax revenues decrease, likely minimally, beginning in fiscal year 2024 as eligible taxpayers claim the subtraction modification. Specific dollar estimates cannot be determined because the number of qualifying claimants and benefit amounts are unknown. The Comptroller's Office can administer the changes using existing budgeted resources, and local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state's personal income tax system and is responsible for implementing the subtraction modification on state tax forms and processing claims with existing budgeted resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Entertainment District Security Grant Program and an associated special fund to assist community organizations, nonprofit entities, and local governments with funding security operations during high pedestrian traffic times in designated entertainment districts experiencing higher than average calls for police assistance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services (Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy)
qa_results.stakeholders: Community organizations, nonprofit entities, local governments, law enforcement, visitors, and small businesses located within Maryland entertainment districts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in FY 2025 due to funding in the state budget, and by an estimated $1,000,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 to capitalize the fund under discretionary gubernatorial appropriations. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by $1,000,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 for grant awards and administrative expenses. Local government revenues and expenditures increase beginning in FY 2025 to the extent local jurisdictions receive grant awards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (formerly Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) to establish the application process, criteria, and administer the Maryland Entertainment District Security Grant Program and its associated special fund.
The bill explicitly mandates the State Treasurer to hold the Maryland Entertainment District Security Grant Program Fund separately and invest the moneys of the fund.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the newly created Maryland Entertainment District Security Grant Program Fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an annual appropriation of up to $1,000,000 in the State budget for the fund beginning in fiscal year 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller of Maryland to implement procedures allowing individuals who file their Maryland resident individual income tax return electronically to register as organ donors via a hyperlink to the State's anatomical gift donor registry.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland resident electronic individual income tax filers, organ procurement organizations, and organ transplant recipients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Comptroller's Office can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Comptroller implement procedures to offer electronic income tax return filers the opportunity to register as organ donors via a hyperlink to the state donor registry and transmit required registration information.

Under the Maryland Revised Anatomical Gift Act, the Secretary of Health contracts with the nonprofit entity that operates the anatomical gift donor registry to which tax filers will be directed and registration information will be transmitted.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing to study and make recommendations on specialized case management, program development, advocacy, outreach, and communication access to enhance the quality of life for individuals who are deaf, deafblind, or hard of hearing. The workgroup must report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by June 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
qa_results.stakeholders: Deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals residing in Maryland, as well as community and nonprofit organizations serving these populations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $67,100 in FY 2025 only for the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to support the workgroup with a part-time graduate assistant ($7,123), consultant services ($50,000), and interpreter services ($10,000, which was included as a contingent appropriation in the FY 2025 budget). Revenues are not affected, and there is no material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Director of the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (or designee) as a member of the Workgroup and requires the Office to provide staff support, resulting in an estimated fiscal expenditure of $67,100 in FY 2025.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary advisory body, the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing, tasked with studying and reporting recommendations on services and advocacy for deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals.
The Governor is responsible for appointing 10 community representatives to the Workgroup and will receive the Workgroup's final report and recommendations by June 1, 2025.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for the 10 community representative positions established on the Workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: This emergency legislation modifies and makes permanent reporting requirements for health insurance carriers to demonstrate compliance with the federal Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act. It repeals the sunset of existing reporting requirements, adjusts the comparative analysis of nonquantitative treatment limitations (NQTLs) to focus on Commissioner-selected limitations, establishes that carriers bear the burden of persuasion in demonstrating parity compliance, and enhances the Insurance Commissioner's enforcement tools and penalty authority.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration (Insurance Commissioner)
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers operating in Maryland and individuals enrolled in individual, small group, and large group health benefit plans seeking mental health and substance use disorder benefits.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2025 and biennially thereafter from daily penalties and expense reimbursements levied against noncompliant carriers. MIA special fund contractual expenditures decrease by an indeterminate amount in FY 2024 and FY 2025 due to a substantial reduction in the volume of required NQTL reviews, but expenditures will increase every two years thereafter beginning in FY 2027 due to the repeal of the sunset date. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA), led by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, is the primary regulatory agency responsible for administering and enforcing the bill. MIA must select the nonquantitative treatment limitations (NQTLs) to be audited, develop standardized data reporting templates, review carrier compliance reports, enforce penalties, and handle noncompliance orders.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes requirements for local boards of education to determine by March 15 each year the instructional materials needed for the upcoming school year for blind and visually impaired students with IEPs or 504 plans, and coordinate with the Instructional Resources Center to provide them in specialized formats by the first day of class. If the board is unable to fulfill these requirements, it must develop an agreed remedy plan with the student's family at least 45 days before classes begin. It also requires contracts with textbook publishers to mandate delivery of electronic files in NIMAS format to the National Instructional Materials Access Center and establishes annual reporting requirements for the Instructional Resources Center and the Maryland State Department of Education.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and local county boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: Blind and visually impaired students, their families, local public school systems, and textbook publishers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $86,400 in FY 2025, rising to $117,900 by FY 2029, to support one new education program specialist at MSDE to oversee data collection, compliance, and reporting. State revenues are unaffected. Local school system expenditures may increase significantly if local boards are unable to arrange materials through standard channels and must implement remedy plans developed with students' families.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) by requiring it to support the Instructional Resources Center, execute memorandums of understanding with local boards and NIMAC, publish compliance information online, adopt implementing regulations via the State Board, and report annually on textbook equity. The fiscal note also identifies an expenditure increase for MSDE to hire an education program specialist.

The bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education to submit an annual report of its findings regarding the equity of textbooks and supplemental materials for blind and visually impaired students directly to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) to provide coverage and reimbursement for remote ultrasound procedures and remote fetal nonstress tests under certain conditions, including using FDA-approved and HIPAA-compliant digital technology and meeting standard in-person standards of care.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (Maryland Medical Assistance Program)
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant individuals enrolled in Medicaid and prenatal healthcare providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures (40.8% general funds, 59.2% federal funds) may increase by a minimal amount beginning in fiscal year 2025 to the extent that remote options reduce missed appointments and increase service utilization; federal fund revenues will increase correspondingly. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health directly administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which this bill requires to cover and reimburse remote ultrasound procedures and remote fetal nonstress tests, as well as issue implementation guidance for providers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that automatic license plate reader (LPR) data collected by or for a law enforcement agency is the property of that agency and cannot be sold, accessed without express authorization, or uploaded to unauthorized entities. Expands the definition of historical data to include cloud storage, permits data uploads to the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center, extends criminal penalties for misuse of data to contracted vendors, and requires new procedures concerning data breach certification, reporting, and personally identifiable information safeguards.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police and local law enforcement agencies operating automatic license plate reader systems
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland law enforcement agencies, contracted LPR system vendors and operators, Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC), and motorists whose license plate data is collected.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Department of State Police (along with other law enforcement agencies using automatic license plate reader systems) adopt specified procedures regarding data access, protection of criminal justice information, audits, and data breach reporting. It also governs the upload of captured plate data to the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC), which operates under the Maryland State Police.

The Maryland Department of Transportation and its modal law enforcement divisions (such as the Maryland Transportation Authority Police) utilize license plate readers and were consulted in the fiscal analysis regarding operational impacts and compliance with the bill's data storage, access, and vendor requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires each county board of education to provide $150,000 for the salary and fringe benefits of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future implementation coordinator, funded jointly by the State and county in the same proportion as the foundation education aid formula. It also permanently extends the requirement for counties and local school systems to appoint an implementation coordinator beyond its prior fiscal 2026 expiration.
qa_results.responsible_party: Accountability and Implementation Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Blueprint for Maryland's Future implementation coordinators, county boards of education, local school systems, and county governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by approximately $1.8 million annually, supported by the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund through fiscal 2027 and general funds starting in fiscal 2028. Local school systems receive $1.8 million annually in State aid beginning in fiscal 2025. Because the coordinator mandate is extended indefinitely rather than expiring after fiscal 2026, local school system expenditures increase by $3.6 million annually beginning in fiscal 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts public school system funding and administration by requiring county boards of education to fund Blueprint for Maryland's Future implementation coordinators, funded jointly by the State and counties based on the foundation program formula overseen by MSDE.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB), an independent state entity created to oversee the Blueprint, is directly responsible for administering the required salary grants and monitoring county implementation plans.
The bill creates a mandated State appropriation of approximately $1.8 million annually beginning in FY 2026, impacting DBM's preparation and supervision of the annual executive state budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1083 modifies the requirements for Class 4 limited winery licenses in Maryland by replacing the specific cultivation and ingredient requirements for grapes and fruit with broader Maryland-grown agricultural products (excluding cannabis and THC products). It also permits license holders to purchase finished wine made entirely of Maryland-grown agricultural products fermented by a licensed manufacturer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Class 4 limited winery license holders, Maryland farmers and agricultural producers, and Maryland wine consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State revenues or expenditures, nor will it materially impact local government finances or operations. A meaningful small business impact is anticipated, as the updated standards may affect the ability of some wineries to obtain or renew licenses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Secretary of Agriculture with the authority to grant annual exemptions from the Maryland-grown agricultural product percentage requirements for Class 4 limited winery licenses, and requires the Secretary to adopt regulations governing the exemption process in consultation with industry stakeholders.

The Comptroller regulates aspects of the alcoholic beverage industry in Maryland and is explicitly referenced in the bill regarding reporting and record-keeping requirements for licensed wineries conducting winemaking and packaging activities across facilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the compensation and benefits available to individuals who were erroneously convicted, sentenced, and confined in Maryland. It expands eligibility to include individuals erroneously convicted of conspiracy to commit a felony and those whose convictions were reversed or vacated with no retrial permitted. It also extends the higher education benefit duration from 5 to 8 years, adjusts the start dates for housing and healthcare benefits to begin from the date of the eligibility order, requires the State to give 15 days written notice before introducing evidence to reduce compensation due to concurrent sentences, and repeals obsolete filing deadlines.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works and Office of Administrative Hearings
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals erroneously convicted, sentenced, and confined in Maryland (particularly those convicted of conspiracy to commit a felony) and their estates.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase due to extending compensation eligibility to individuals erroneously convicted of conspiracy to commit a felony; the total impact cannot be reliably quantified, though the Office of the Attorney General identified two individuals who retroactively qualify. Other benefit alterations are not expected to materially affect State finances. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works is the primary paying agency responsible for disbursing monetary compensation and benefits awarded by administrative law judges to erroneously convicted individuals, adopting implementing regulations, and reporting annually to the General Assembly.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates petitions for eligibility for compensation and benefits, determines monetary awards, directs appropriate agencies to provide statutory benefits, and adopts procedural regulations in consultation with the Board of Public Works.

The Office of the Attorney General requested the bill, represents the State as a mandatory party in all erroneous conviction compensation proceedings, must be served with all petitions, and is required to provide 15 days written notice if introducing evidence of concurrent sentences.

The Judiciary and court system are impacted as eligibility determinations rely on court orders vacating or reversing convictions without allowing retrial, and the compensation statute includes reimbursement for court fines, fees, and restitution.
The bill extends the period of enrollment during which eligible individuals may attend public senior higher education institutions with tuition and fees paid from five years to eight years.

As a public senior higher education institution, Morgan State University is subject to the provisions extending tuition and fee payment benefits for eligible exonerated individuals from five years to eight years.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission coordinates state higher education policies and was consulted regarding the extension of tuition and fee benefits at Maryland public higher education institutions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue Class B beer, wine, and liquor licenses to qualifying restaurants located in Ward 4, Precincts 1 and 2, provided they meet specific food receipt percentages, health facility classifications, and enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Downtown Partnership of Baltimore. It prohibits off-premises sales except via a refillable container permit, prohibits license transfers, and bars the issuance of new licenses under these provisions after June 30, 2028, while allowing renewals.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Restaurants located in Baltimore City Ward 4 (Precincts 1 and 2), restaurant patrons, the Downtown Partnership of Baltimore, and the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Baltimore City revenues may increase minimally starting in FY 2025 to the extent licenses are issued under the bill. For each license issued, local revenues increase by $1,920 to $2,400 in FY 2025 (comprising a $600 application fee and an annual license fee of $1,320 or $1,800 depending on seating capacity) and by $1,370 to $1,850 annually thereafter (including a $50 renewal fee).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation of the alcohol industry and collects applicable alcoholic beverage taxes. While this bill specifically authorizes the local Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue Class B licenses with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates generally to alcohol regulation in the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the allowable purposes of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund to include funding the costs of telecommunications cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training for public safety answering point personnel.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management (Maryland 9-1-1 Board)
qa_results.stakeholders: Public safety answering point (PSAP) personnel, 9-1-1 dispatchers, county emergency services, and individuals experiencing out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures and revenues are not affected because CPR training is already an allowable expense under the 9-1-1 Trust Fund, making the bill clarifying in nature. Local finances are not materially affected because any training costs incurred by counties for PSAP personnel are reimbursable by the fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) houses and oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board, which administers the 9-1-1 Trust Fund and oversees funding and standards for public safety answering points (PSAPs).

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS regulates and coordinates the statewide emergency medical services system and statewide emergency communications infrastructure, which interfaces with telecommunications CPR and prehospital cardiac arrest emergency protocols.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Anne Arundel County Human Relations Commission to apply to a circuit court for an order to compel witness attendance, testimony, and the production of documents or evidence if an individual fails to obey a subpoena, with failure to obey the court order punishable as contempt of court.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Human Relations Commission and the Circuit Court
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County residents, subpoenaed witnesses, respondents, and parties involved in discrimination investigations or hearings before the Anne Arundel County Human Relations Commission.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Anne Arundel County Human Relations Commission to apply to circuit courts for orders compelling witness attendance and document production, and allows the courts to punish violations as contempt of court.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill defines and authorizes specific scopes of practice for veterinary assistants and veterinary technicians under varying levels of supervision by a licensed veterinary practitioner. It permits veterinary assistants to perform tasks such as obtaining vitals, nail trims, and administering medications under direct supervision, as well as anesthesia setup and monitoring under immediate supervision. It also allows veterinary technicians to perform expanded procedures, including certain emergency treatments and euthanasia under specified circumstances, while continuing to prohibit them from diagnosing, prescribing, or performing surgery.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Veterinarians, registered veterinary technicians, veterinary assistants, animal emergency hospitals, animal shelters, and pet/animal owners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners Fund are estimated to increase by $2,700 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027 and by $5,400 annually thereafter due to an anticipated increase in veterinary technician registrations and triennial renewal fees. State expenditures are not affected, and there is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners is housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture. The bill directly alters the Agriculture Article regarding the scope of practice and supervision levels of veterinary technicians and veterinary assistants, requires board regulations, and affects special fund revenues for the board.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Clean Water Justice Act of 2024 authorizes individuals and organizations meeting federal standing requirements to bring civil actions against persons or local political subdivisions violating certain state water standards. Specifically, it applies to requirements governing nontidal wetlands lacking a continuous surface connection to surface water, as well as ephemeral and intermittent streams. The bill establishes notice requirements, allows intervention in state enforcement proceedings, and permits courts to award injunctive relief, civil penalties, and litigation costs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents and environmental advocacy groups, businesses and regulated entities operating near protected waters or nontidal wetlands, and local governments and political subdivisions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of the Environment increase by $86,400 in FY 2025 (increasing to $117,900 by FY 2029) to hire an assistant Attorney General to handle 60-day notices and related legal proceedings. Special fund revenues from civil penalties deposited into the Nontidal Wetland Compensation Fund and the Maryland Clean Water Fund may increase. Local governments may experience increased litigation and compliance expenditures if named as defendants in enforcement actions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs enforcement of standards, permits, and regulations under MDE's jurisdiction regarding nontidal wetlands and water pollution control. MDE must receive 60-day notices of alleged violations, review proposed consent decrees and settlement agreements, and may intervene in civil actions. The fiscal note also assigns direct general fund expenditures to MDE for an Assistant Attorney General to handle these duties.

The OAG must be served with mandatory 60-day pre-suit notices and copies of proposed consent judgments and settlement agreements. OAG is responsible for advising MDE, handling State interventions, and prosecuting enforcement actions, with an Assistant Attorney General position funded under the bill's implementation.

The bill creates citizen standing to file civil enforcement actions in State circuit courts, authorizes courts to grant equitable relief and impose civil penalties, and may require training for circuit court judges regarding equitable environmental remedies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Miriam Kelty Aging and Senior Social Connection Hub and Spoke Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Aging, administered in partnership with the Montgomery County Village Consortium for a three-year period. The program is designed to develop best practices for a hub-and-spoke model of village administration, centralize administrative burdens on volunteers, coordinate resources, and combat loneliness among seniors choosing to age in place.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: Seniors aging in place, community volunteers, local volunteer-led village organizations, and the Montgomery County Village Consortium.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $80,000 annually across fiscal years 2026 through 2028 (totaling $240,000) to fulfill a mandated appropriation for the pilot program, which will be transferred to the Montgomery County Village Consortium. State revenues are not affected, and there is no direct impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Miriam Kelty Aging and Senior Social Connection Hub and Spoke Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Aging. The department is charged with administering the program, disbursing mandated funds to the Montgomery County Village Consortium, and receiving annual and final implementation reports.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of $80,000 in the annual state budget bill for fiscal years 2026 through 2028 for the pilot program.

As the state's principal budget agency, the Department of Budget and Management must account for and incorporate the mandated $80,000 annual appropriation in the executive budget for fiscal years 2026 through 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires an individual to be certified as an advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) before practicing advanced practice registered nursing in Maryland, while establishing exceptions for graduate APRN students practicing in accredited programs and individuals authorized under rules and regulations adopted by the Maryland Board of Nursing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs), students in graduate APRN programs, and the Maryland Board of Nursing.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as the changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental revenues or expenditures.
