agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health Occupations Article governing the practice and certification of Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (APRNs), which is regulated by the Maryland Board of Nursing, a regulatory board within the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the City of Frederick to participate in the Maryland Intrastate Emergency Management Assistance Compact, enabling it to coordinate, request, and provide mutual emergency management assistance and resources with other member jurisdictions across Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, local officials, and emergency responders in the City of Frederick and other member jurisdictions participating in the Maryland Intrastate Emergency Management Assistance Compact.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances. Local government finances are not anticipated to be significantly affected, although the City of Frederick and other participating jurisdictions may benefit operationally from mutual aid.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds the City of Frederick to the Maryland Intrastate Emergency Management Assistance Compact (MIEMAC). The Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) coordinates emergency management with party jurisdictions and receives notifications and copies of all assistance requests made under the compact.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Transparency in Education Spending Act requires the State Board of Education to adopt a uniform process for local school boards to report budget information to county governing bodies. It mandates that county boards include information on reserve funds, federal funding, and postemployment/retiree health care benefit obligations in their annual budgets. Additionally, county school boards must publish their proposed and approved budgets and certain periodic reports on their public websites and submit annual financial audit results to county commissioners or county councils.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education and the Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: County boards of education (local school systems), county governing bodies (county councils, commissioners, executives), and Maryland public school communities and taxpayers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as the Maryland State Department of Education can implement the uniform reporting process with existing resources. Local school system administrative expenditures may increase by a potentially minimal amount to meet the additional budget category reporting and website posting requirements. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1115 directly impacts the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and the State Board of Education by requiring the State Board to establish a uniform process for county boards of education to report detailed budget information to county governing bodies. The State Superintendent also receives copies of local budgets and annual financial audit results.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the exemption to the trader's license requirement for licensed restaurants, specifying that only restaurants generating 10% or less of their annual sales from nonfood items are exempt from needing a trader's license when doing business as a trader or exhibitor.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Court
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland restaurant owners, particularly restaurants selling nonfood merchandise exceeding 10% of annual sales, and local licensing authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances or operations, as circuit courts can absorb any additional licensing workload with existing resources. Local government revenues may experience a minimal increase from additional trader's license fees (which are split 92% to counties and 8% to the State general fund), but the overall fiscal impact is negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Trader's licenses and restaurant licenses under Title 17 of the Business Regulation Article are issued through the Clerks of the Circuit Court, which are supported administratively by the Administrative Office of the Courts. The fiscal note confirms that circuit courts handle licensing activity related to this bill.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees business and occupational licensing and regulation under the Business Regulation Article and was consulted as an information source regarding licensing compliance.
The Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division) was consulted as an information source regarding legal and consumer regulation implications of altered trader licensing exemptions.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Tenant Safety Act of 2024 establishes an implied warranty of habitability in residential rental agreements, deeming dwellings warranted as fit for human habitation. It expands tenant remedies for landlords' failure to repair serious and dangerous defects (including dangerous mold), permits multiple tenants to join as plaintiffs in legal actions against a landlord, establishes rebuttable presumptions regarding rent escrow and prospective rent abatement, and authorizes courts to award attorney's fees, litigation expenses, actual damages, rent abatement, and lease termination.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland District Court and Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants, residential landlords, and property management companies across Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It carries a meaningful impact on small business landlords and property management entities due to expanded legal liability, multi-tenant joinder actions, and potential awards of attorney's fees and damages.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies court procedures regarding rent escrow actions, warranty of habitability lawsuits, and failure to pay rent proceedings in the Maryland District Court. It permits tenant joinder, establishes evidentiary presumptions, and authorizes judicial orders for rent abatement, lease termination, and attorney's fees.

The Office of the Attorney General, through its Consumer Protection Division, oversees and enforces consumer protection standards regarding unfair and deceptive trade practices in residential leasing, making these statutory tenant remedies and habitability standards relevant to their consumer protection work.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the eligibility requirements for a performing arts theater alcoholic beverages license in Harford County, allowing the license to be issued to a for-profit organization rather than a nonprofit organization and removing film and movie showings from the theater definition. It permits license holders to sell and serve liquor in addition to beer and wine for on-premises consumption and increases the annual license fee from $500 to $1,500.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: For-profit performing arts theaters in Harford County and their patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Harford County license fee revenues are estimated to increase by $1,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2025, based on the issuance of one license at the new $1,500 annual fee (an increase from $500). Harford County can monitor the license using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees state alcohol taxes. While this legislation specifically affects local licensing administered by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it amends state alcoholic beverage statutes and involves requirements regarding purchases from licensed wholesalers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a person to submit an acquisition request to the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) at least 60 days before the closing date of a nursing home acquisition and notify residents, resident representatives, and staff. Authorizes the MHCC executive director to approve, approve with conditions, deny, or refer the request, and establishes criteria and reporting requirements for purchasers following an acquisition.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Nursing home buyers and operators, nursing home residents, residents' family representatives, and nursing home staff and employees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Maryland Health Care Commission increase by $107,100 in FY 2025, rising to $148,100 by FY 2029, to hire one program manager to review, analyze, and regulate nursing home acquisitions. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHCC is the primary implementing agency responsible for reviewing nursing home acquisition requests, adopting implementing regulations in the State Health Plan, rendering decisions on acquisitions, and collecting and distributing post-acquisition compliance reports.

MHCC is located within MDH, and the Secretary of Health (or designee) must be consulted by MHCC on acquisition requests. Additionally, MDH's Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) licenses nursing homes based on MHCC acquisition approval and receives copies of all final decisions and reports.

The MHCC Executive Director must consult with the Office of the Attorney General to determine if a proposed nursing home acquisition raises public interest concerns, and the OAG receives copies of all final acquisition decisions and annual reports.

The Secretary of Aging and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman must receive copies of all final acquisition decisions and post-acquisition reports from MHCC, and the review process interacts with continuing care retirement communities regulated by the Department.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the credentialing and licensing structure for certified nursing assistants in Maryland by replacing the geriatric nursing assistant credential with new designations: Certified Nursing Assistant-I (CNA-I), authorized to practice in all care settings after passing an approved training program and competency evaluation, and Certified Nursing Assistant-II (CNA-II) for assistants with restricted practice settings. It also updates competency evaluation requirements, establishes exemptions for certain nursing students and short-term assistants operating under federal regulations, and requires the State Board of Nursing to update regulations and notify credential holders.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified nursing assistants (CNAs), geriatric nursing assistants (GNAs), certified medicine aides, nursing students, nursing assistant training programs, nursing homes, hospitals, and long-term care facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $209,900 in FY 2025 to fund one nurse program administrator position and $150,000 for one-time licensing software updates. Ongoing annual expenditures range between $103,600 and $117,900 through FY 2029 for personnel and operating costs. Special fund revenues are not expected to be materially affected, as existing certificate holders are not expected to pay additional fees for redesignation. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Nursing (MBON) and the Office of Health Care Quality. MBON is the primary implementing agency responsible for updating CNA certification standards, creating the CNA-I and CNA-II credentials, establishing training and examination requirements, notifying certificate holders, and updating regulations, resulting in a direct special fund fiscal impact.

Under Section 8-6A-14 of the Health Occupations Article, the Maryland Higher Education Commission collaborates with the Board of Nursing to approve nursing assistant training programs and develop program regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes reimbursement by the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board for sexual assault forensic examinations conducted via peer-to-peer telehealth at no cost to victims, extends civil liability immunity to providers conducting such examinations, and requires the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee to study and report on the feasibility of implementing a statewide TeleSAFE pilot program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Criminal Injuries Compensation Board (within the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy) and the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee (staffed by the Office of the Attorney General)
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of alleged sexual assault and child sexual abuse, forensic nurse examiners, licensed healthcare providers, hospitals, and law enforcement
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2025 to cover additional reimbursement claims and potential administrative costs within the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, though a reliable estimate cannot be made in advance. The mandated study and report can be completed using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Criminal Injuries Compensation Board (CICB) and its Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit (SARU), which reside within GOCPP, are responsible for processing and funding reimbursements for sexual assault forensic examinations, including the peer-to-peer telehealth exams authorized by the bill.

The Office of the Attorney General provides primary staff support to the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee, which is mandated by the bill to study the feasibility of a TeleSAFE pilot program and report recommendations to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee to conduct a feasibility study on a statewide telehealth program (including a TeleSAFE Pilot Program) and submit a report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Talent Innovation Program and the nonlapsing Talent Innovation Fund within the Maryland Department of Labor to increase access to high-quality job training using innovative financing models in high-demand industry sectors, starting with an initial pilot program supporting regional cyber ranges for cybersecurity training.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (jointly administered by the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning and the Governor's Workforce Development Board)
qa_results.stakeholders: Job seekers and trainees, employers in high-growth and emerging industries (such as cybersecurity, healthcare, biotechnology, manufacturing, and artificial intelligence), higher education institutions, registered apprenticeship sponsors, and local workforce development boards.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million annually beginning in FY 2025 to capitalize the Talent Innovation Fund (a $2.0 million appropriation was included in the FY 2025 budget). Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by $2.0 million annually as funds are collected and disbursed. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent local entities receive program grants or provide matching funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Talent Innovation Program and the Talent Innovation Fund within the Maryland Department of Labor, tasking its Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning with joint administration of the program and the Secretary with fund administration.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor's Workforce Development Board jointly administer the Talent Innovation Program alongside the Department of Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly created Talent Innovation Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill requires the Comptroller of Maryland to account for the newly created Talent Innovation Fund and its interest earnings.
The Department of Labor is required to submit an annual report to the Governor detailing program activities and the use of the Talent Innovation Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of an "accredited residential treatment center" under Maryland law to include residential treatment centers accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities (CARF) or the Council on Accreditation (COA), alongside the Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential treatment centers, accreditation organizations (CARF, COA, and the Joint Commission), and children and adolescents receiving residential psychiatric treatment.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can absorb the bill's requirements using existing budgetary resources, with no impact on state revenues. There is no direct fiscal effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) regulates and licenses hospitals and related healthcare facilities, including residential treatment centers. This bill expands the accepted accreditation bodies for residential treatment centers, directly affecting MDH's licensing, survey, and deficiency oversight processes.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill makes permanent the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Pilot Program by repealing its June 30, 2025 sunset date. The program awards grants to local jurisdictions and child care resource centers to establish and sustain family child care providers in underserved areas.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Family child care providers, county governing bodies, child care resource centers, and families in underserved communities with child care shortages
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures of $450,000 are maintained annually starting in FY 2025. This includes effectuating a $450,000 contingent appropriation in FY 2025, a mandated appropriation of $450,000 in FY 2026, and an assumed continuation of $450,000 in discretionary funding annually thereafter (which may be mitigated by federal funds if available). Local government grant revenues and matching expenditure obligations are maintained accordingly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill permanently establishes the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), requiring MSDE to administer the program, award grants, develop guidelines and annual goals, and report annually to the General Assembly.

The bill creates a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $450,000 for the program in the state budget bill for fiscal year 2026 and each fiscal year thereafter.

As the agency responsible for preparing and supervising the executive budget, DBM must implement and account for the mandated annual general fund appropriation of $450,000 beginning in fiscal year 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Emergency Department Wait Time Reduction Commission to evaluate and address factors across the health care system contributing to prolonged emergency department wait times, develop strategic reduction initiatives, coordinate data sharing among health entities, and report annual recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) and Maryland Department of Health (MDH)
qa_results.stakeholders: Emergency department patients, hospital staff and administrators, emergency medical services (EMS) personnel, managed care organizations, and health care providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Health Services Cost Review Commission increase by $100,000 annually in FY 2025, FY 2026, and FY 2027 (totaling $300,000) for contractual services to staff the commission and complete mandatory reports. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no direct impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the HSCRC co-chairs the newly established Commission, the HSCRC is responsible for providing staff and managing data sharing agreements, and the agency incurs a fiscal impact of $100,000 annually in special fund expenditures for contractual staffing support.

The Secretary of Health co-chairs the Maryland Emergency Department Wait Time Reduction Commission, appoints nine stakeholder members, and the Department is subject to data requests to support the Commission's work.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of MIEMSS serves as a designated statutory member of the Commission, and the institute may be requested to provide data related to emergency medical services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state commission—the Maryland Emergency Department Wait Time Reduction Commission—effective for three years to evaluate and recommend strategies to decrease emergency department wait times.
The Executive Director of the MHCC serves as a statutory member of the Commission, and the agency can be requested to share health data.
The Commission is required to submit an annual report of its activities, findings, and policy recommendations to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits the installation, supply, sale, solicitation, or offering for sale of playground surfacing materials that contain more than 90 parts per million of lead or intentionally added PFAS chemicals beginning October 1, 2024. It requires manufacturers of playground surfacing materials to establish and provide certificates of compliance upon request, establishes administrative and civil penalties for violations, and authorizes local governments to adopt more stringent, but not less stringent, standards.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Children and the public who use playgrounds, manufacturers, distributors, and installers of playground surfacing materials, and State agencies and local governments (including public school systems) that construct or maintain playgrounds.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by $118,900 in FY 2025, $97,700 in FY 2026, $68,700 in FY 2027, $70,800 in FY 2028, and $72,900 in FY 2029 for the Maryland Department of the Environment to employ compliance personnel, purchase a vehicle, and contract for laboratory testing services. State and local government expenditures for playground construction and renovation may also increase minimally if compliant surfacing materials are more costly. Penalties and revenues are not expected to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and enforcement agency for the bill, tasked with collecting certificates of compliance from manufacturers, testing surfacing materials, adopting regulations, and enforcing prohibitions on lead and PFAS in playground materials.

DNR manages extensive state park lands and recreational areas and is specifically identified in the fiscal note as a state purchaser and user that constructs or renovates playgrounds subject to the surfacing material restrictions.
MSDE oversees public school systems across Maryland, which frequently install, maintain, and renovate playgrounds and must comply with the new material standards when procuring playground surfacing.

DGS oversees state facility construction, maintenance, and central procurement, and would be required to ensure that playground construction and renovation contracts on state-owned facilities comply with the statutory prohibitions.

The OAG represents state agencies and is specifically tasked under the incorporated enforcement provisions of the Environment Article (§ 9-344) with prosecuting civil or criminal violations arising under the subtitle.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts accounts established under the Maryland 529 Program—including the Prepaid College Trust, College Investment Plan, and Maryland ABLE Program—from the Maryland Uniform Disposition of Abandoned Property Act, while clarifying that sums payable on uncashed checks drawn against these accounts remain subject to the abandoned property provisions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Treasurer's Office
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders and beneficiaries of Maryland 529 Program accounts (including college investment plans, prepaid college trusts, and ABLE accounts) and recipients of checks drawn from those accounts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill codifies an existing interpretation of current law and does not materially affect State operations or finances. It is not anticipated to impact State revenues, and there is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office administers the Maryland 529 Program (including the College Investment Plan, the Prepaid College Trust, and the Maryland ABLE program) and requested this legislation to clarify internal procedures regarding inactive accounts and uncashed distribution checks.
The bill explicitly exempts Maryland 529 Program accounts from the Maryland Uniform Disposition of Abandoned Property Act while clarifying the treatment of checks drawn against those accounts.

The Comptroller serves as the administrator of abandoned and unclaimed property in Maryland under the Maryland Uniform Disposition of Abandoned Property Act and receives abandoned property and uncashed checks remitted to the State's Unclaimed Property Division.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Protecting State Waters From PFAS Pollution Act requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), in collaboration with publicly owned treatment works and significant industrial users, to identify users that intentionally use PFAS chemicals, establish monitoring and testing protocols, and develop PFAS action levels and mitigation plans for industrial pretreatment permits. It also requires covered significant industrial users to monitor and report PFAS levels, implement reduction measures by July 1, 2026, and follow specific storage and disposal rules for captured PFAS.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Significant industrial users with pretreatment permits that intentionally use PFAS, publicly owned treatment works (POTWs), commercial water testing laboratories, and Maryland residents benefiting from cleaner water resources.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, as the Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources, and any penalty revenues from violations are expected to be negligible. Local government finances are also not materially affected, as publicly owned treatment works can collaborate with MDE using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with identifying significant industrial users utilizing PFAS, developing monitoring protocols, action levels, and mitigation plans, approving disposal systems, and updating the state's PFAS Action Plan.

The bill explicitly entitles the Attorney General to request documentation of PFAS storage or reuse from significant industrial users and provides legal enforcement authority for environmental violations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires hospitals to establish and maintain protocols and capacity in their emergency departments to treat patients presenting with opioid-related overdoses or emergency medical conditions with medications for opioid use disorder. It also requires hospitals to possess specified FDA-approved medications, make referrals for voluntary community-based treatment prior to discharge, and coordinate with peer support professionals.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients presenting at hospital emergency departments with opioid-related overdoses, opioid-related emergency medical conditions, or opioid use disorder, as well as hospitals, emergency department staff, and peer support specialists.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact because the bill's requirements primarily apply to private-sector hospital operations and activities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds provisions to the Health - General Article requiring hospitals to establish and maintain clinical protocols and capacity to treat opioid-related overdoses and opioid use disorder. Hospital protocols must align with Department of Health requirements regarding prescribing opioid agonist treatments, and MDH is the principal regulator of hospital standards and public health policies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Grow Your Own Educators Grant Program, administered by the Maryland State Department of Education, to provide competitive grants to partnerships between local school systems, employee unions, and higher education institutions. The program supports noncertified education support professionals and provisional teachers pursuing teaching degrees with tuition, fees, books, and mentorship in exchange for a minimum two-year service obligation in a high-needs school or teacher shortage area.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Noncertified education support professionals, provisional teachers, mentor teachers, local school systems, public and private higher education institutions with teacher preparation programs, and students in high-needs public schools.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $1.5 million in FY 2025, expanding to at least $5.4 million annually by FY 2028 to support grant funding and two administrative staff positions at the Maryland State Department of Education. Public four-year higher education institutions will likely see increased tuition revenues and operational expenditures. Participating local school systems will incur administrative and stipend costs, partially or fully offset by an estimated $1.2 million in grant revenues in FY 2025, increasing in out-years as cohorts phase in.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the Grow Your Own Educators Grant Program, reviewing and approving collaborative plans, distributing grant funds, and collecting and publishing program data.
The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Labor to collaborate with MSDE to provide technical assistance to collaboratives in securing federal, State, or other funding for the program.

USM member institutions with approved teacher preparation programs are eligible to form collaboratives with local school systems and will receive grant-funded tuition, book, and fee payments for enrolled teacher candidates.

As a public university offering an approved teacher preparation program, Morgan State University can enter into program collaboratives and receive grant-funded tuition and fee payments for participating candidate cohorts.

St. Mary's College of Maryland operates an approved teacher preparation program and is eligible to participate as a partner in collaboratives, receiving tuition and fee coverage for candidate participants.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation for the Grow Your Own Educators Grant Program in the annual state budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters reporting requirements for the Attorney General by repealing the requirement to submit an annual report under the Maryland Defense Act, removing the requirement to include an itemized statement of receipts and disbursements in the annual report, requiring the annual report to also be submitted to the General Assembly, and requiring the Attorney General to publish annual reports and opinions on its website rather than in bound volumes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General, Maryland General Assembly, the Governor, and the general public seeking access to Attorney General opinions and reports.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to have a material effect on State operations or finances, though the Office of the Attorney General may experience administrative efficiencies. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory reporting, recordkeeping, and publication requirements for the Office of the Attorney General, repealing the Maryland Defense Act annual reporting mandate, removing the requirement to publish opinions and reports in bound volumes in favor of website publication, and modifying the contents of its annual report.

The bill repeals an annual reporting requirement from the Attorney General to the Governor regarding actions taken under the Maryland Defense Act and maintains the requirement that the Attorney General submit its annual report to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the 9-1-1 Specialist Recruitment and Retention Workgroup to examine recruitment and retention challenges affecting 9-1-1 specialists across Maryland and submit interim and final reports with recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services and Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland 9-1-1 specialists, Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) directors, and local emergency management agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational costs for staffing and expense reimbursements are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources of the Department of Legislative Services and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management, though general fund expenditures may increase if external contractual support is needed. Local governments can provide necessary data within existing resources. No impact on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1162 designates the Secretary of Emergency Management (or designee) as a member of the 9-1-1 Specialist Recruitment and Retention Workgroup and requires the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) to jointly staff the Workgroup and assist in producing its interim and final reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS), or the Executive Director's designee, is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup.
The Secretary of State Police, or the Secretary's designee, is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary advisory body, the 9-1-1 Specialist Recruitment and Retention Workgroup, to examine recruitment and retention issues and report findings and recommendations before abrogating in December 2025.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several members to the Workgroup (including 9-1-1 specialists, PSAP directors, and local association representatives) and will receive both the interim and final reports.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to include an increased General Fund appropriation in the annual budget bill for the Division of Rehabilitation Services within the Maryland State Department of Education to ensure the State meets its required matching fund amount under federal rehabilitation acts.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (Division of Rehabilitation Services)
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities receiving vocational rehabilitation or independent living services, including transitioning students with disabilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by $700,000 in FY 2025, reflecting contingent funds in the FY 2025 State budget. Otherwise, the legislation is discretionary and authorizing in nature, posing no ongoing direct mandate or effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly concerns funding for the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), which is an operational division housed within the Maryland State Department of Education.
The bill explicitly grants statutory authorization to the Governor to include increased general fund appropriations in the annual state budget bill to meet federal matching requirements.
DBM is the principal agency responsible for developing the Governor's annual budget and overseeing agency general fund appropriations and expenditures.
Under the amended section of the Education Article, the State Treasurer serves as the custodian of the federal funds received under the rehabilitation acts and oversees their disbursement.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Whole Watershed Act establishes the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership and the Whole Watershed Fund within the Department of Natural Resources to accelerate the restoration of the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays and their watersheds. The partnership provides technical support and grants for up to five comprehensive watershed restoration projects every five years, drawing support from multiple existing State agricultural and environmental special funds. The act also establishes public notice, review criteria, and five-year post-construction monitoring requirements for stream and floodplain restoration projects administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE)
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments, watershed project sponsors, residential and business property owners near restoration project sites, overburdened and underserved communities, farmers/agricultural landowners, and restoration contractors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures for the Whole Watershed Fund increase from transfers across existing environmental funds, which could exceed $5,000,000 annually. The bill mandates a distribution of up to $100,000 annually from the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays 2010 Trust Fund from FY 2026 through FY 2030 for operations grants ($20,000 per project). DNR general fund expenditures increase by at least $200,000 in FY 2025 (with two positions funded in the FY 2025 budget) and ongoing. Beginning in FY 2026, MDE expenditures increase by an estimated $285,000 to $325,000 annually for three staff to conduct stream restoration application reviews and monitoring. Local governments and State agencies that execute stream restoration projects face potentially significant cost increases and project delays due to enhanced public notice, evaluation, and five-year monitoring mandates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR serves as the primary implementing agency for the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership. The Secretary of Natural Resources administers the newly established Whole Watershed Fund, chairs the State Management Team, awards grants, and develops a public permit tracking dashboard.

MDE serves on the State Management Team, authorizes transfers from the Bay Restoration Fund and Clean Water Commerce Account to the Whole Watershed Fund, and is given extensive regulatory authority and staffing requirements to review, authorize, and conduct five-year monitoring of stream and floodplain restoration projects.

MDA is designated a seat on the State Management Team and the bill alters the purposes of the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund and the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program to authorize funding transfers to the Whole Watershed Fund.
The Secretary of Planning designates a representative to serve on the State Management Team to evaluate, approve, and assist in managing whole watershed restoration projects across the state.
The Chief Resilience Officer (housed within MDEM) or their designee is statutorily designated as a member of the State Management Team administering the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership.

SHA holds an MS4 permit and undertakes stream and floodplain restoration projects to meet permit conditions and TMDL water quality goals; the bill's new application, public notice, and monitoring mandates will increase project compliance and implementation costs.

MDOT undertakes stream restoration projects to meet environmental mitigation and stormwater permit requirements, and the fiscal note notes that the bill's rigorous new stream restoration standards will likely increase project costs and timelines.

MDTA is specifically noted in the fiscal note as an agency that uses stream restoration projects to satisfy environmental and permit requirements, incurring potential cost increases and delays under the new project standards.
The Comptroller is statutorily tasked with accounting for the newly established Whole Watershed Fund.
The State Treasurer is required to hold and invest the monies of the Whole Watershed Fund, with interest earnings specifically credited to the fund under State Finance and Procurement § 6-226.
The bill explicitly references the statewide digital watershed file maintained by DoIT to establish the geographic eligibility boundaries (8-digit watersheds) for project proposals.
The Board of Public Works is referenced regarding approvals for agricultural cost-sharing projects financed with State bond proceeds and agreements under the Waterway Improvement Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Secure Schools Emergency Response Grant Program within the Maryland Center for School Safety to provide competitive grants to local school systems to improve emergency notification systems and enhance communications among school personnel, public safety answering points, and first responders during emergency events.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety
qa_results.stakeholders: Local school systems, public elementary and secondary school staff and students, local law enforcement, first responders, and public safety answering points (PSAPs).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $3.0 million annually beginning in FY 2025 to provide funding for the grants, with no effect on State revenues; the Maryland Center for School Safety can administer the program with existing resources. Local school system revenues and expenditures increase by up to $3.0 million annually beginning in FY 2025 to the extent local school boards apply for and receive grant awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Center for School Safety with administering the newly established Secure Schools Emergency Response Grant Program, managing grant applications from local school boards, and ensuring the program is operating and available by September 1, 2026.

The Maryland Center for School Safety is an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education, and the program directly impacts public elementary and secondary schools across Maryland's 24 local school systems.

The Department of Emergency Management oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and statewide 9-1-1 systems, which directly intersect with the bill's provisions requiring school emergency notification platforms to integrate with Public Safety Answering Points (PSAPs) and 9-1-1 communications.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation for the Secure Schools Emergency Response Grant Program in the annual state budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a regulatory framework for green death care options in Maryland, specifically authorizing and governing the processes of alkaline hydrolysis and natural organic reduction (human composting). The bill creates registration and permitting requirements for reduction facilities and operators, mandates contamination testing and safety standards, establishes rules for handling unclaimed veteran remains, and prohibits the use of resulting soil remains for growing food for humans or livestock or commercial soil resale.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Cemetery Oversight (Maryland Department of Labor) and the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors (Maryland Department of Health)
qa_results.stakeholders: Funeral homes, morticians, crematory operators, cemetery operators, reduction facility operators, consumers seeking alternative death care options, veterans service organizations, and the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Office of Cemetery Oversight and the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors may increase minimally beginning in FY 2025 through permit, registration, and renewal fees (illustratively estimated at $20,000 for OCO over a five-year period). Regulatory and operational duties can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Local health departments may experience an operational impact from monitoring compliance, but local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Cemetery Oversight, housed within the Department of Labor, is one of the primary regulatory bodies tasked with implementing the bill, including establishing registration, permitting, inspection, and regulatory requirements for reduction facilities and operators.

The State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors is housed within the Maryland Department of Health and is jointly responsible with the Office of Cemetery Oversight for regulating reduction facilities, adopting identical regulations, and overseeing health and safety standards for alkaline hydrolysis and natural organic reduction.

The bill establishes specific statutory procedures for handling unclaimed hydrolyzed or soil remains of veterans and eligible dependents, requiring reduction facilities and funeral establishments to notify and transfer qualifying remains to the Department for appropriate disposition.

The Division of Consumer Protection within the Office of the Attorney General is statutorily required to collaborate with the Director of the Office of Cemetery Oversight and the State Board of Morticians to publish a consumer information pamphlet describing consumer rights regarding natural organic reduction.

Facilities performing alkaline hydrolysis and natural organic reduction may require air quality permits to construct and environmental permits regarding wastewater and soil contamination, and the bill incorporates biosolid contamination parameters.

The bill explicitly prohibits the use of soil remains produced by natural organic reduction to grow food for human or livestock consumption and bans incorporating soil remains into commercial compost.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill allows registered nurses at local health departments to provide nonprescription drugs and devices without a prescription, under certain conditions. It requires the Committee on Registered Nurses Personally Preparing and Dispensing Drugs and Devices in Local Health Departments to include all FDA-approved over-the-counter nonprescription contraceptives in its formulary. Additionally, it repeals the prohibition against vending machine sales of nonlatex condoms and instead prohibits the sale of natural membrane condoms via vending machines, while excluding this violation from standard criminal and civil penalties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Committee on Registered Nurses Personally Preparing and Dispensing Drugs and Devices in Local Health Departments
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered nurses, local health departments, patients seeking reproductive healthcare and nonprescription contraceptives, and vending machine operators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, as the Maryland Department of Health committee can update its formulary using existing budgeted resources, and the repeal of criminal penalties will not have a material impact on State courts. Local health department operations and local government finances are likewise not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts MDH by regulating the distribution of nonprescription drugs and devices in local health departments, expanding the authority of registered nurses under MDH policies and training programs, and altering provisions within the Maryland Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act administered by the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Committee on Registered Nurses Personally Preparing and Dispensing Drugs and Devices in Local Health Departments with amending and annually maintaining its formulary to include all FDA-approved over-the-counter nonprescription contraceptive drugs and devices.

The bill repeals a misdemeanor criminal penalty regarding the sale of certain condoms via vending machines and excludes violations of the new natural membrane condom prohibition from standard civil/criminal court penalties, having a minor operational effect on District Court filings.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters video lottery employee licensing disqualifications by allowing individuals with certain nonviolent misdemeanor offenses involving moral turpitude to obtain a license, provided they will not work in gaming operations or security and the casino operator requests the license. Additionally, it defines the 'value' of a table game chip under the State's criminal theft statute as either the face value depicted on the chip or the color-designated value set by the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Video lottery facility operators (casinos), applicants for video lottery employee licenses with nonviolent misdemeanor records, and individuals subject to criminal theft laws regarding table game chips.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material fiscal impact on State or local finances or operations. Alterations to licensing qualifications are not expected to significantly change license application volumes or associated administrative costs and fee revenues, and altering the statutory definition of value for table game chips does not materially affect finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency (and its Commission) directly regulates video lottery facilities, oversees employee licensing requirements, evaluates disqualification criteria, and is tasked under the bill with determining the value of table game chips based on color when no face value is depicted.

qa_results.bill_summary: Known as Elijah's Law, this bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to jointly develop guidelines to reduce the risk of exposure to anaphylactic major food allergens in child care settings and identify at least one free training resource. MSDE must establish a model policy, and registered large family child care homes and licensed child care centers caring for at least one child with a food allergy must adopt, implement, and annually distribute the policy to parents. It also grants civil immunity to child care providers and staff responding in good faith to a child's anaphylactic reaction in accordance with the guidelines or via epinephrine autoinjector, absent gross negligence or willful misconduct.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed child care centers, registered large family child care homes, child care workers, and children with severe food allergies and their parents or guardians.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: MSDE and MDH can develop the guidelines and model policy using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) with jointly developing guidelines with the Maryland Department of Health, creating a model food allergy policy for child care providers, and publishing the guidelines, model policy, and free training resources on its website.

The bill mandates that the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) work jointly with the Maryland State Department of Education to develop guidelines aimed at reducing exposure to anaphylactic major food allergens in child care settings.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes a Class M-F (Municipal Family Fun Center) alcoholic beverages license in the 40th alcoholic beverages district in Baltimore City for use at a municipal bowling alley and skating rink on Pennsylvania Avenue. It also authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class B beer, wine, and liquor license for a restaurant on West 29th Street under specific conditions, and extends the expiration of a Class A license on West Biddle Street until July 1, 2025, for renewal purposes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Operators and patrons of municipal bowling alleys and skating rinks on Pennsylvania Avenue, restaurant owners on West 29th Street, the Class A license holder on West Biddle Street, neighborhood associations (Upton West Community Association and Greater Remington Improvement Association), and Baltimore City.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City revenues increase by at least $3,000 (specifically estimated at $3,300 in FY 2025 and $1,650 annually thereafter) from application, license, and renewal fees for three Class M-F licenses. Revenues may increase further by $1,920 to $2,400 in FY 2025 and $1,370 to $1,850 annually thereafter if a Class B beer, wine, and liquor license is issued. Baltimore City can handle additional enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is tasked with regulating the state's alcohol industry and administering alcohol-related taxes. While the licensing and oversight authorized by this bill are handled locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, the bill amends the state's Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article governing alcohol sales and operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Transportation Institute at the University of Maryland to conduct a comprehensive study to identify methods to improve the Maryland Transit Administration's Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) MobilityLink paratransit service, consult with riders and disability advisory bodies, and report its findings and recommendations by July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Institute at the University of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: MobilityLink paratransit riders, individuals with disabilities, paratransit workers and operators, and the Maryland Transit Administration
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education expenditures for the University of Maryland increase by $448,986 ($449,000) in FY 2025 to conduct the study. General fund expenditures increase by $448,986 in FY 2026 to reimburse UMD, with higher education revenues increasing correspondingly. Local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly investigates and evaluates the Maryland Transit Administration's ADA MobilityLink paratransit service, requiring the administration to provide operational, performance, and workforce data for the study.

The Maryland Transportation Institute at the University of Maryland, College Park (a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland) is mandated to conduct the comprehensive study and submit the final report, incurring estimated study costs of $449,000.

As the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration, MDOT is directly impacted by service and policy recommendations regarding paratransit operations and is designated to receive the final study report.

The study must be conducted in consultation with the Maryland Commission on Disabilities (the advisory body to the Department of Disabilities) to solicit input and comments from riders with disabilities and the public.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates consultation with the State Coordinating Committee for Human Services Transportation and the Maryland Commission on Disabilities during the study.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $150,000 in the fiscal year 2026 budget bill to fund the study and requires the final report to be submitted to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program and Fund within the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) to provide loans of up to $20 million for real estate and infrastructure projects in sustainable communities, priority funding areas, and transit-oriented development areas. The bill also authorizes MEDCO, with local governing body approval, to pledge alternative local revenues under the Tax Increment Financing Act to service debt or support the revolving loan fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Economic Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Infrastructure and real estate developers, local governments, businesses, and residents within sustainable communities, priority funding areas, and transit-oriented development areas.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for MEDCO are estimated to increase by $15.0 million in FY 2025 and $20.0 million annually from FY 2026 through FY 2029 under discretionary funding assumptions. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly as loan funds are received, disbursed, and repaid. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2025 as local alternative revenues are collected, pledged to TIF special accounts, and used for debt service, infrastructure projects, or revolving fund contributions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEDCO is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the new Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program and Fund, promulgating regulations, establishing an advisory loan committee, approving loans, and exercising expanded tax increment financing authority.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other State funds.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller of Maryland to account for the newly established Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Fund.

The program specifically targets projects located in Sustainable Communities designated under the Housing and Community Development Article to promote community development, and DHCD provided information during the bill's fiscal analysis.
The program targets real estate and infrastructure loans in Transit-Oriented Development areas defined in the Transportation Article, and MDOT was consulted regarding the bill's impacts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class BWLT beer, wine, and liquor tasting permit in Allegany County, allowing holders of a beer, wine, and liquor license to host on-premises tastings upon notifying the Board of License Commissioners at least seven days in advance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Allegany County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Beer, wine, and liquor license holders in Allegany County and consumers attending tasting events
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Allegany County local revenues increase by at least $1,200 in FY 2025 and at least $600 annually thereafter, based on an estimated four to six licensees paying an annual fee of $150 and a one-time issuing fee of $150. County expenditures are unaffected as permit monitoring and regulation adoption can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for broad regulation of the alcohol industry in Maryland. While this bill directly concerns local tasting permits administered by the Allegany County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it pertains to the state's alcoholic beverages statutory framework.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission within the Department of Commerce to study, promote, and make recommendations regarding bilateral trade, investment, business and academic exchanges, and policy issues of mutual interest between Maryland and Ireland.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland businesses, academic institutions, members of the Irish-American community, and international trade partners in Ireland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly affected; the Department of Commerce can support the commission and expense reimbursements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1206 establishes the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission within the Department of Commerce, includes the Secretary of Commerce (or designee) as a commission member, and requires the department to staff and support the commission using existing resources.
The bill designates the Secretary of State, or the Secretary of State's designee, as an ex officio member of the newly established Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission.

As the division within the Office of the Secretary of State responsible for managing the State's international engagement and the Maryland Sister States Program (which includes ties with Ireland), this division is directly relevant to supporting bilateral trade and cultural ties with Ireland.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new statutory advisory body, the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission, to study and submit annual recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Governor appoints four members to the commission with the advice and consent of the Senate, holds removal authority over appointed members, and receives annual reports and recommendations from the commission.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for the new commission positions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain reemployed retirees of the Teachers' Pension System from mandatory retirement benefit earnings offsets if jointly employed by a local school employer and the Maryland Association of Boards of Education (MABE) with salary fully funded by MABE, applying retroactively to January 1, 2021, and sunsetting December 31, 2024. The bill also repeals an obsolete exemption from earnings offsets for retirees reemployed by the State whose positions were fully funded by non-State grants.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Retirees of the Teachers' Pension System jointly employed by local school boards and the Maryland Association of Boards of Education, local school boards, and retirees of the Employees' and Teachers' Retirement and Pension Systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because it is expected to apply in a very limited number of circumstances. It has no effect on State revenues and no direct local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the calculation and enforcement of earnings offsets for reemployed retirees, and is specifically responsible for receiving documentation and certifying eligibility under the bill's provisions.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system, where local school system retirees and personnel impacted by the Teachers' Pension System reemployment rules operate, and served as an information source on the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the State Retirement Agency to employ a Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion to reduce barriers to access and promote opportunities for underrepresented groups. It also formally establishes and codifies a governance program within the Investment Division to evaluate and manage material environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors impacting system investments.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: State Retirement Agency staff, State Retirement and Pension System members and participating employers, underrepresented groups, and minority business enterprises
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special and reimbursable fund expenditures increase by $107,100 in FY 2025, reflecting the salary, benefits, and operating expenses for one new Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion position. SRA revenues increase commensurately from administrative fee assessments on State agencies (reimbursable funds of $42,800) and local participating employers (special funds of $64,200). Local participating governmental units face minimal expenditure increases to cover their prorated administrative share. The governance program codifies existing agency operations and has no additional fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1212 directly governs the State Retirement Agency (SRA) by mandating that the Executive Director hire a Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion and establishing statutory guidelines and staffing requirements for a governance program within the agency's Investment Division.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the individual implementing SRA's governance program to support the Board of Trustees with the implementation of the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) policies within the Investment Division, directly aligning with GOSBA's statewide role in overseeing the MBE program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the annual salary of the Baltimore County Sheriff beginning in the next term of office, setting specific salary amounts from calendar years 2026 through 2029 and authorizing the Baltimore County Council to determine the salary in its annual budget for subsequent years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Council
qa_results.stakeholders: The Baltimore County Sheriff and Baltimore County taxpayers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Baltimore County expenditures increase by $48,800 in fiscal 2027 and by at least $90,400 annually thereafter through fiscal 2030 to reflect the salary increases and associated fringe benefits taking effect at the beginning of the next term of office in December 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Known as The Bailey Bullock Act, this bill requires public middle and high schools to update their venue-specific emergency action plans for athletic facilities to include a cardiac emergency response plan. It also requires state-funded nonpublic middle and high schools to establish similar venue-specific emergency action plans and cardiac emergency response plans for their athletic facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education, local county boards of education, and the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
qa_results.stakeholders: Public and state-funded nonpublic middle and high school students, student athletes, athletic coaches and training staff, school nurses, and local emergency medical services personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS) may increase starting in FY 2025 to provide AEDs to participating nonpublic schools, though the exact amount cannot be reliably estimated. Local school systems may incur minimal administrative and training costs that are expected to be absorbed within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE oversees the public school system and administers programs providing state funding to nonpublic schools, both of which are required under this act to implement venue-specific emergency action and cardiac emergency response plans for athletic facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS administers the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator (AED) Program referenced in the bill, and the fiscal note indicates MIEMSS expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2025 to furnish AEDs to compliant nonpublic schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters property insurance requirements for condominium councils of unit owners regarding detached units. It requires condominium councils to maintain property insurance on detached units and common elements if the condominium is not composed entirely of similar detached units, requires annual written notice to owners of detached units regarding their insurance obligations, and clarifies that detached unit owners are only required to carry homeowners insurance on their entire unit if the condominium is composed entirely of detached units (unless the council elects to carry that insurance).
qa_results.responsible_party: Council of Unit Owners
qa_results.stakeholders: Condominium unit owners (specifically owners of detached residential units), condominium councils of unit owners and governing boards, and property insurers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies statutory property and homeowners insurance coverage requirements, deductible responsibilities, and cancellation terms applicable to condominium unit owners and councils of unit owners, which falls under the regulatory oversight of the Maryland Insurance Administration regarding property and casualty insurance products.

The Maryland Secretary of State oversees the registration and regulation of condominiums under the Maryland Condominium Act, making changes to condominium statutory obligations and governing structures relevant to its administrative responsibilities.

The Office of the Attorney General, specifically through its Consumer Protection Division, investigates and enforces consumer protection matters and inquiries concerning condominium councils of unit owners and unit owner disclosures.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for fiscal analysis and supports the state courts, which handle civil litigation arising from condominium property damage, insurance proceeds allocation, and deductible disputes under the Real Property Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts noncommercial telephone solicitations conducted for public opinion research from restrictions against automated dialing systems or prerecorded messages. The bill also establishes a private right of action permitting an aggrieved called party to sue violators to enjoin future violations and recover the greater of actual damages or up to $500 (or up to three times that amount for willful or knowing violations), and prohibits the contractual waiver of telephone solicitation protections except as part of a legal dispute settlement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland telephone subscribers and called parties, telephone solicitors, and organizations conducting public opinion research.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. The impact on small businesses is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Violations of Maryland's telephone solicitation laws constitute unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.
The bill creates a private right of action authorizing aggrieved called parties to bring civil lawsuits in state courts to enjoin violations and recover actual or statutory damages.

The bill references and coordinates with telephone solicitation and automated dialing provisions in the Public Utilities Article, which are within the regulatory purview of the Public Service Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Kratom Consumer Protection Act regulates the preparation, distribution, labeling, advertising, and sale of kratom products in Maryland. It prohibits sales to individuals under 21, restricts advertising directed at minors or making therapeutic claims, bans adulterated or synthetic kratom products, and establishes civil and criminal penalties for violations. Additionally, it directs the Maryland Department of Health, in collaboration with the Maryland Hospital Association, to report on adverse health events associated with opioid-like substances by December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Retailers, manufacturers, distributors, and wholesalers of kratom products; consumers of kratom products; individuals under 21 years of age; and local health departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances and operations. The Maryland Department of Health can adopt regulations and complete the required study using existing budgeted resources, and local health departments can handle enforcement with existing resources. Revenues and expenditures associated with the civil and criminal penalty provisions are not expected to have a material impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) with adopting regulations to implement the Kratom Consumer Protection Act and requires MDH, in collaboration with the Maryland Hospital Association, to submit a report to the General Assembly by December 31, 2025, on adverse health events associated with opioid-like substances such as kratom and tianeptine.

The bill creates new civil penalties, civil liability for damages, and misdemeanor criminal penalties (up to 90 days imprisonment and/or fines up to $5,000) for violations of kratom distribution, labeling, and marketing regulations, which fall under the jurisdiction of the state court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Tianeptine Consumer Protection Act prohibits retailers from distributing, selling, exposing for sale, or advertising for sale any tianeptine product marketed for human consumption. Violations constitute a misdemeanor carrying penalties of up to a $5,000 fine, up to 90 days imprisonment, or both, alongside liability for civil damages sustained by an individual.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Retailers, convenience stores, grocery stores, gas stations, dietary supplement manufacturers, distributors, and consumers of tianeptine products.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially impacted. The Maryland Department of Health can adopt regulations and local health departments can handle enforcement using existing budgeted resources. Criminal penalty and civil liability provisions are not expected to have a material financial impact, though small business retailers face a potential meaningful impact due to sales restrictions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new subtitle to the Health - General Article and specifically mandates that the Maryland Department of Health adopt regulations to carry out and implement the subtitle.

The bill establishes new criminal misdemeanor penalties (fines up to $5,000 and/or imprisonment up to 90 days) and civil liability for retailers violating tianeptine restrictions, which fall under the jurisdiction of the Maryland court system.
The Office of the Attorney General provides statutory legal advice and regulatory guidance to the Department of Health and oversees state consumer protection enforcement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a misdemeanor offense punishable by up to 90 days imprisonment, potentially requiring public defender representation for indigent defendants charged under the statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the statutory restriction prohibiting the Department of Natural Resources from taking action to reduce or alter the boundaries of certain oyster sanctuaries established in 2010 until an updated fishery management plan for oysters was developed.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial oyster harvesters, watermen, and conservation and environmental organizations involved in Chesapeake Bay oyster management.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances; the Fiscal Note projects no impact on State revenues or expenditures and no local effect.
