qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Howard County Board of Education and the Howard County Superintendent of Schools to publish reports on the school system's website and submit them to the Maryland General Assembly when there are differences between proposed and approved school capital budgets or capital improvement programs, detailing the discrepancies and the rationale for each difference within 30 days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Board of Education and Howard County Superintendent of Schools
qa_results.stakeholders: Howard County Public Schools, Howard County Board of Education, Howard County school administrators, parents, students, and county residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: The Howard County Board of Education and Superintendent of Schools can produce and publish the required reports using existing resources. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates the reporting of local public school capital improvement programs (CIP) and capital budgets in Howard County, which directly relate to the school construction CIP processes and submissions reviewed and funded by the Interagency Commission on School Construction.

The bill amends the Education Article regarding the governance and transparency of local school board and superintendent capital budgeting within the public school system overseen by the Maryland State Department of Education.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies requirements for publicly funded prekindergarten programs in Maryland by establishing an early childhood educator career ladder for private providers, adjusting teacher and assistant teacher credentialing and experience requirements, phasing in target proportions of private provider slots, establishing prekindergarten provider hubs and provider support programs, authorizing local school boards to seek capital improvement funding to renovate leased facilities, and extending mandated funding timelines for the Child Care Credential Program and Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible public and private prekindergarten providers, early childhood educators and teaching assistants, local school systems and county boards of education, and preschool-age children (specifically 3- and 4-year-olds) and their families.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.0 million in FY 2025 for MSDE to implement the career ladder and train staff on the CLASS assessment. Special fund expenditures from the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund increase by $5.7 million in FY 2026 due to the mandated appropriation for the Child Care Credential Program. Extending the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant through FY 2029 requires $26.6 million annually in grant funding offset by reductions in the full-day prekindergarten formula, creating indeterminate secondary impacts on State education aid and local wealth-equalized funding formulas. Local school systems gain flexibility to lease space and receive more time to meet private provider ratios.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary implementing agency for the bill. MSDE is tasked with establishing the early childhood educator career ladder for private providers, creating prekindergarten provider hubs, developing model memorandums of understanding, administering provider aid programs, and managing prekindergarten grant and credential programs.

The bill directly impacts the IAC by authorizing local boards of education to apply for funding from the Capital Improvement Program (administered by the IAC) for renovations to public facilities leased for prekindergarten programs, and touches upon IAC funding priorities for prekindergarten classrooms.

The bill establishes and extends statutory mandated funding requirements across several fiscal years for prekindergarten programs and the Maryland Child Care Credential Program, which directly impacts state budget formulation supervised by DBM.

The bill mandates that the Governor include specific appropriations in the state budget for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program, the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund, and the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program across multiple fiscal years.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Howard County Task Force to Study Revenue Options for School Capital Needs to examine school capital needs and deferred maintenance through 2035, identify funding gaps, and explore potential revenue options such as commercial excise taxes or transfer tax reallocations. The task force must report findings by October 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Executive
qa_results.stakeholders: Howard County Public Schools, Howard County students and educators, Howard County taxpayers, and county residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. Howard County local expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount to staff the task force and potentially hire contractual support to conduct the analysis and generate the report within the five-month timeframe. County revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Howard County Task Force to Study Revenue Options for School Capital Needs, a temporary task force established by the General Assembly to study and report on funding gaps and revenue options for local public school capital projects.

The IAC oversees public school construction and capital improvement funding in Maryland, served as an information source for the fiscal note, and administers the state school construction programs that interact with local school capital funding.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Arts Incubator Workgroup to study how arts and cultural institutions can support local artists. The workgroup must submit a preliminary report on findings by January 1, 2025, and a final report with recommendations by October 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Arts Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Local artists, arts educators, arts and cultural entities and venues, local arts councils, arts districts, and Maryland arts supporters.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are minimal and can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources by the Maryland State Arts Council, which is responsible for staffing the workgroup and handling standard travel expense reimbursements for members. There is no material effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC), an agency within the Department of Commerce, is designated to provide administrative and operational staff for the newly created Arts Incubator Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state workgroup (the Arts Incubator Workgroup) tasked with studying support mechanisms for local artists and issuing preliminary and final reports before sunsetting in December 2025.
The Governor is responsible for appointing 12 members to the workgroup, designating the chair, and receiving the workgroup's preliminary and final reports.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and coordinating the appointment of the 12 gubernatorial appointees to the workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes soil conservation districts to recommend and establish a fee system to cover the reasonable costs of reviewing small pond plans, subject to enactment or review by local governing bodies, and establishes procedures for developing and implementing the fees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Soil Conservation Districts and Local Governing Bodies
qa_results.stakeholders: Landowners, agricultural producers, developers, small businesses constructing or repairing small ponds, and local soil conservation districts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund (Wetlands and Waterways Program Fund) revenues may decrease minimally starting in FY 2025 if more reviews shift from MDE ($750 fee) to local districts; State expenditures are not materially affected. Local soil conservation district revenues may increase beginning in FY 2025 depending on the fee structures enacted, which cannot exceed the actual cost of plan reviews and cannot be used to reduce existing county or State funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1465 amends Title 8 of the Agriculture Article concerning the powers of soil conservation districts to establish fee systems for reviewing small pond plans, which directly affects the soil conservation programs and districts overseen and supported by the Maryland Department of Agriculture.

The bill directly amends Section 5-503 of the Environment Article regarding small pond permit exemptions and review fee recommendations, with potential fiscal impacts on MDE's special fund revenues (Wetlands and Waterways Program Fund) due to shifts in small pond plan reviews to local soil conservation districts.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the funding for the Professional and Volunteer Firefighter Innovative Cancer Screening Technologies Program by repealing the annual mandated appropriation of $100,000 and instead authorizing the Governor to include at least $500,000 in the annual state budget for the program beginning in fiscal year 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Professional and volunteer firefighters, local fire departments, and volunteer fire companies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Assuming the full discretionary funding is provided, State general fund expenditures increase by $400,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 (the bill replaces a $100,000 mandate with discretionary funding of at least $500,000). The FY 2025 State budget includes $400,000 total for the program ($100,000 mandated plus $300,000 contingent on legislation). State revenues are unaffected. Local revenues and expenditures increase to the extent that local fire departments apply for and receive grants from the program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Professional and Volunteer Firefighter Innovative Cancer Screening Technologies Program and is responsible for evaluating grant applications, distributing grant funding, and reporting program activities.
The bill replaces a statutory funding mandate with discretionary authority for the Governor to include at least $500,000 in the annual state budget for the program beginning in fiscal year 2025.

The Department of Budget and Management prepares and supervises the state annual budget, which is directly affected by the shift from a mandated $100,000 appropriation to a discretionary authorization of at least $500,000.
The bill specifies that appropriations and expenditures made for the program, including grant funds received, remain subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to appoint audiologist members to the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists from a list of nominees submitted by the Maryland Academy of Audiology instead of the Board itself.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor and the Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed audiologists in Maryland, the Maryland Academy of Audiology, and the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and has no effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists operates within the Maryland Department of Health, and the Secretary of Health is statutory advisor to the Governor regarding these board appointments.

The bill directly modifies the Governor's appointment process for audiologist members of the regulatory board, requiring appointments to be selected from a list submitted by the Maryland Academy of Audiology.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in managing candidate submissions, vetting, and administering appointments for state regulatory boards and commissions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases penalties for uninsured motor vehicles and alters how penalty revenues are distributed. It establishes the Driver Education in Public High Schools Grant Program and the State-Aided Institutions Field Trip Grant Program within the Maryland State Department of Education (along with corresponding special funds) to assist public schools with driver education and transportation to State-aided educational institutions. Additionally, it increases statutory funding distributions to the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) for its Uninsured Division.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and the Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Uninsured motor vehicle owners, Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF), public high school students (particularly those eligible for free and reduced-price meals), local public schools and school systems, and nonprofit organizations offering driver education courses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Total uninsured motorist penalty collections increase by an estimated $3.0 million annually starting in FY 2025, with $900,000 retained by the Transportation Trust Fund. Mandated distributions from penalty collections provide $2.0 million annually to the Driver Education in Public High Schools Fund, $600,000 annually to the State-Aided Institutions Field Trip Fund, and $3.0 million in FY 2025 (increasing with inflation in future years) to MAIF as nonbudgeted revenue. Because new mandated distributions exceed additional penalty collections, General Fund revenues decrease by $3.5 million in FY 2025, rising to a $3.8 million reduction by FY 2029. Special fund expenditures increase by $2.6 million annually for grants and MSDE administrative costs ($85,000 to $120,000 annually). Local school systems benefit from incoming grant revenues and matching operational expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MAIF is a primary subject and beneficiary of the bill, which substantially increases statutory penalty distributions dedicated to the exclusive use of MAIF's Uninsured Division by $3.0 million in FY 2025 and adjusts the base formula for future fiscal years.

MVA is the primary agency responsible for administering and collecting uninsured driving penalties, enforcing registration suspensions, implementing the increased fine structure, and distributing collected penalty revenues.

MSDE is charged with establishing and administering two new grant programs and their associated special funds: the Driver Education in Public High Schools Grant Program and the State-Aided Institutions Field Trip Grant Program.
MDOT is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration; penalty distributions directly affect the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which retains 30% of assessed uninsured driver penalties.

The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold and invest the monies of the two newly created special funds: the Driver Education in Public High Schools Fund and the State-Aided Institutions Field Trip Fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily tasked with accounting for the two newly established special funds created by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill permanently establishes and codifies the Maryland Entertainment Industry Council within the Department of Commerce as the successor to the temporary Maryland Entertainment Council. It expands council membership, broadens its powers (such as entering into contracts and accepting gifts or federal funds), removes the previous June 30, 2025 termination date, and updates reporting requirements to study and support Maryland's film, television, and entertainment industries.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland's film, television, and entertainment industry professionals, production companies, independent creators, organized labor representatives, and workforce development institutions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are unaffected. State expenditures are minimal and can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources by the Department of Commerce and any other agency designated by the Governor to assist with staffing. Travel reimbursements for members are absorbable. General fund expenditures could increase if the council exercises its authority to hire outside consultants, but no specific dollar amount is mandated or estimated. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill codifies the Maryland Entertainment Industry Council directly within the Department of Commerce, designates the Secretary of Commerce (or designee) as a council member, and requires the department to staff the council.

The Governor's appointed Senior Advisor on Film, Television, and Entertainment chairs the council. Additionally, the Governor appoints 19 members and up to three honorary cochairs, receives annual and special reports, and may designate other state agencies to provide staff support.
The Secretary of Labor (or designee) serves as a member of the Maryland Entertainment Industry Council, and the agency may be called upon to support the council or assist with staffing.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is designated as a member of the Maryland Entertainment Industry Council, and the department may potentially be designated to assist with council staffing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and codifies the Maryland Entertainment Industry Council as a permanent statutory advisory council to study and make recommendations on Maryland's film, television, and entertainment industry.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for the 19 appointed members and up to three honorary cochairs established for the council.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1492 alters the requirement that public schools automatically select 'Option 8' to block the release of student scores to military recruiters when administering the Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery (ASVAB). Instead, public schools must notify participating students and their parents or guardians at least two weeks before administering the test of the option to select 'Option 8' to prohibit the release of personal information and test scores. The bill also maintains the authority of local boards of education to select Option 8 system-wide and outlines procedures for later releasing scores.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local school systems and public schools (county boards of education)
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students taking the ASVAB, parents and guardians of participating students, local school systems, and military recruiters.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Local school systems can handle the notification requirements using existing resources, and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1492 amends Section 7-111 of the Education Article governing public school administration of the Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery (ASVAB) and the release of student directory information to military recruiters. Although the direct operational impact falls on local public school systems, the Maryland State Department of Education provides oversight, regulatory framework, and policy guidance for public schools across the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of "practice massage therapy" to include instrument-assisted soft tissue manipulation techniques such as muscle scraping and vibration therapy, subject to regulations established by the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners. It also requires individuals seeking license or registration reinstatement to submit proof of a State and national criminal history records check, and authorizes the Board to require applicants or licensees to submit to an examination by a designated health care provider at the Board's expense if there is reason to believe they may cause harm.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, applicants for massage therapy licensure or reinstatement, and massage therapy clients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact. The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can implement the bill and adopt required regulations using existing budgeted resources, as the volume of required health care provider examinations is expected to be minimal and absorbable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners is a health occupation licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly alters the scope of practice, reinstatement requirements, and examination investigative procedures administered by the Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits an individual from aiding or abetting the unauthorized practice of massage therapy in Maryland. Violators face felony criminal penalties, including fines and imprisonment, must reimburse the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners for prosecution costs, and are subject to civil fines of up to $10,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals and businesses operating or assisting in massage therapy establishments, unlicensed massage practitioners, and licensed massage therapists.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The civil and criminal penalty provisions of the bill do not have a material impact on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill authorizes the Board to assess civil fines up to $10,000, collect reimbursed prosecution costs, and deposit penalties into the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners Fund.

The bill creates a new felony offense for aiding or abetting the unauthorized practice of massage therapy and authorizes court-ordered reimbursement of Board prosecution costs upon conviction, impacting court caseloads and judicial administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation of a new felony criminal offense carrying penalties of up to five years imprisonment may result in additional indigent criminal defendants requiring legal representation by the Office of the Public Defender.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new felony penalty with prison sentences of up to five years for subsequent offenses, which can impact state correctional intake and supervision.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to health occupations licensing boards, including the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners, and represents the State in legal actions and appeals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces the required frequency of performance audits conducted by the Office of Legislative Audits for the Baltimore City Board of Liquor License Commissioners and the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners to at least once every six years, rather than every four and three years, respectively.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Legislative Audits
qa_results.stakeholders: Board of Liquor License Commissioners for Baltimore City, Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County, and the Office of Legislative Audits
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations, although the Office of Legislative Audits may realize administrative efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1501 directly modifies statutory requirements for the Office of Legislative Audits (OLA), reducing the mandatory frequency of its performance audits of the Baltimore City and Prince George's County liquor boards to at least once every six years.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the Maryland State Treasurer, and any person acting on their behalf, from engaging in certain campaign finance activities—such as receiving, soliciting, or depositing campaign contributions and hosting fundraising events—during a regular legislative session of the Maryland General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: The Maryland State Treasurer, individuals acting on behalf of the State Treasurer, and associated campaign finance entities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, and it has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1503 directly applies to the State Treasurer by adding the official and anyone acting on their behalf to the list of state officials prohibited from engaging in specified campaign finance activities during the regular legislative session of the General Assembly.

The State Board of Elections regulates campaign finance activities and entities in Maryland, oversees compliance with the Election Law Article, and has the authority to assess civil penalties for violations of legislative session fundraising prohibitions.

The Office of the State Prosecutor is responsible for investigating and prosecuting offenses relating to the integrity of state officials and violations of state election laws, which encompass campaign finance restrictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the information that the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) must publish on its website prior to holding a public hearing regarding a proposed major service change, including impacts on paratransit, local schools, businesses, and rider demographics. It also requires the MTA to distribute its final impact report on proposed major service changes to each member of the General Assembly whose district would be impacted.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Transit riders including bus and paratransit users, communities and businesses in affected transit service areas, and Maryland General Assembly members representing impacted districts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase, likely minimally, for the Maryland Transit Administration to modify its consultant contract to collect and publish the required additional information. State revenues are not affected, and there is no direct impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MTA is the primary implementing agency responsible for compiling and publishing the expanded route, rider demographic, and paratransit impact data on its website prior to holding public hearings on major service changes, as well as distributing the required reports to affected legislators.

MDOT is the parent agency of the Maryland Transit Administration and collaborates on required transit equity analyses. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures will be impacted to update consultant contracts to gather and report the required information.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Model Workgroup to evaluate and analyze potential regional water and wastewater governance models for the Baltimore metropolitan area, requiring the hiring of independent consultants and submission of a final report by June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore Regional Water Governance Model Workgroup
qa_results.stakeholders: Water and wastewater ratepayers, vulnerable residents, and municipal utility workers in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and surrounding jurisdictions (Anne Arundel, Carroll, Harford, and Howard counties), as well as independent consulting firms.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 in FY 2026 due to a mandated appropriation to hire independent consultants for the workgroup. State revenues are unaffected, and State agencies (MDE and OAG) can provide consultation within existing resources. Baltimore City and Baltimore County will collectively receive $500,000 in grant revenue in FY 2026, with an equal increase in expenditures to contract independent consultants across FY 2026 and FY 2027.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates and establishes the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Model Workgroup, an advisory body tasked with analyzing and developing recommendations on a regional water and wastewater governance model.

The bill statutorily requires the Workgroup to consult with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) while developing its findings and report on regional water and wastewater governance and operations.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Workgroup consult with the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) in analyzing legal issues and developing its report.

The Governor appoints two members to the Workgroup, is mandated to include a $500,000 appropriation in the fiscal year 2026 annual budget bill for independent consultants, and is designated to receive the final report.
The bill mandates a $500,000 general fund appropriation in the fiscal 2026 state budget to hire independent consultants, which directly affects state budget formulation overseen by DBM.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing the appointment of two members to the newly formed Workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill delays the effective date of the majority of the forest preservation and retention provisions enacted under Chapters 541 and 542 of 2023 from July 1, 2024, to July 1, 2026. It enacts specified provisions to take effect on July 1, 2024, including altering the definition and use of qualified conservation for forest mitigation banking, expanding priority retention areas, and exempting solar photovoltaic facilities from afforestation requirements. The bill also directs the Department of Natural Resources to update the model local government ordinance by July 1, 2025, and adopt regulations by July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Land developers, construction companies, solar photovoltaic facility owners, forest mitigation bankers, local governments administering forest conservation programs, and environmental consultants and landscapers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill delays most state and local fiscal impacts associated with Chapters 541 and 542 of 2023 until fiscal 2027 at the earliest. Potential increases in state general fund and local capital expenditures for public construction projects to comply with modified reforestation requirements are postponed. Potential increases in fee-in-lieu revenue to the State Forest Conservation Fund and local forest conservation funds are likewise delayed, while potential decreases in fee-in-lieu revenue due to forest mitigation banking and solar facility exemptions remain effective starting July 1, 2024. DNR can fulfill administrative requirements to update model ordinances and adopt regulations using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Forest Conservation Act. The bill directly mandates DNR to update the model local government ordinance by July 1, 2025, adopt implementing regulations by July 1, 2026, approve local justifications regarding qualified conservation in mitigation banks, and adjust application timelines.

MDE is explicitly referenced in the bill's statutory criteria for forest retention priorities, specifically designating Tier II and Tier III high-quality watersheds, and served as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

The bill addresses exemptions from afforestation requirements for solar photovoltaic facilities and references certificates of public convenience and necessity (CPCN) issued by the Public Service Commission under § 7-207 of the Public Utilities Article regarding grandfathering and applicability timelines.

qa_results.bill_summary: Permanently authorizes the use of the Bay Restoration Fund's Septics Account for costs associated with connecting properties on septic systems to existing municipal wastewater facilities that are under construction or under a funding agreement to achieve enhanced or biological nutrient removal standards, by repealing the June 30, 2024 sunset date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners using on-site sewage disposal systems, local governments, municipal wastewater facility operators, and contractors involved in wastewater connections.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected overall because the bill permanently extends an existing authorized use of the Bay Restoration Fund Septics Account, and the Maryland Department of the Environment can continue administration with existing resources. Local government grant revenues and expenditures may shift depending on whether jurisdictions receive funding to connect properties to municipal wastewater facilities rather than for other authorized septic projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) administers the Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) and its Septics Account. The bill repeals the sunset date, making permanent the authorization for MDE to disburse BRF grants and loans for connecting septic systems to municipal wastewater facilities under construction for enhanced nutrient removal.

The Comptroller of Maryland is statutorily responsible for establishing the separate account within the Bay Restoration Fund and disbursing revenues collected from septic system users in accordance with statutory requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: This emergency legislation temporarily extends the deadline from January 31, 2024, to May 1, 2024, for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to mail real property reassessment notices for taxable year 2025, preventing an irrebuttable presumption that property values did not change.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners of approximately 100,009 residential properties across Maryland, as well as county and municipal governments and the State.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill prevents significant property tax revenue losses for the State and local governments over a three-year cycle. Absent the bill, State property tax revenues would decrease by $3.1 million ($3,072,080) in FY 2025 and $18.4 million ($18,432,477) over three years; county revenues would decrease by $30.1 million ($30,095,457) in FY 2025 and $180.6 million ($180,572,740) over three years; and municipal revenues would decrease by $2.1 million in FY 2025 and $12.6 million over three years.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1516 extends the deadline for SDAT to issue real property reassessment notices, preventing an irrebuttable presumption that property values did not change for over 100,000 accounts. Because these notices include appeal rights and establish assessed values, allowing the revaluations to proceed directly impacts the pipeline of property tax assessment disputes that may be appealed to the local Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body hearing appeals regarding real property assessments following determinations by Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards. By permitting over 100,000 updated property valuations to take effect rather than reverting to prior-year values, the bill indirectly affects potential downstream appeals before the Court.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the eligibility requirements and administration of the Maryland Children’s Health Program (MCHP) by eliminating the MCHP premium plan, thereby repealing the requirement that families with incomes between 201% and 300% of the federal poverty guidelines pay premiums or family contributions for healthcare coverage.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Children under 19 years of age in families with incomes up to 300% of the federal poverty guidelines and their parents or guardians, particularly those previously subject to MCHP premium plan contributions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for MCHP decrease by a minimal amount in FY 2024 and by an estimated $99,965 annually beginning in FY 2025 (comprising a $35,000 general fund decrease and a $65,000 federal fund decrease). This net reduction results from saving $966,132 in administrative and mailing expenses by eliminating the collection infrastructure, which offsets an estimated $866,167 loss in annual premium revenue. Federal fund revenues decrease by approximately $65,000 annually. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health directly administers the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) and requested this departmental bill, which repeals the MCHP premium plan and eliminates family contribution requirements for enrollees between 200% and 300% of the federal poverty guidelines.
The bill amends sections of the Insurance Article to repeal obsolete provisions and references to the sunsetted MCHP private option plan governing insurance carriers.
The bill results in a net reduction in state general and federal fund expenditures for an entitlement program and was reviewed by DBM for state budget impacts.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill facilitates the transfer of ownership, operation, and redevelopment of thoroughbred racing facilities in Maryland from the Maryland Jockey Club to the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority (MTROA). It authorizes the Maryland Stadium Authority to issue up to $400 million in bonds for the planning, design, and construction of racing facilities at Pimlico and a new training facility, alters revenue distributions and mandates from the State Lottery Fund and other gaming accounts, and extends the sunset of MTROA to June 30, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland thoroughbred horse racing industry participants (owners, trainers, jockeys, breeders), the Maryland Jockey Club, the Maryland Stadium Authority, the City of Bowie, Baltimore City, and Prince George's County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State debt authorizations increase by $400.0 million in bonds issued in FY 2025, resulting in estimated annual debt service payments of $24.0 million from FY 2026 through FY 2055 ($720.0 million total). General fund expenditures increase by $10.7 million in FY 2026 due to mandated appropriations of $4.5 million to the Racetrack Facility Renewal Account and $6.2 million to Prince George's County. General fund revenues decrease by $3.6 million annually beginning in FY 2025 due to a $3.0 million annual lottery distribution to Prince George's County and claiming horse sales tax diversions (roughly $600,000 annually), alongside indeterminate decreases from various tax exemptions. Prince George's County revenues increase by $3.0 million annually starting in FY 2025 and by an additional $6.2 million in FY 2026, while Baltimore City experiences an indeterminate decrease in property, transfer, and recordation tax revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Stadium Authority with financing the planning, design, and construction of racing facilities at Pimlico and a new training facility on behalf of the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority, and increases MSA's bond issuance authorization from $375 million to $400 million.

The Department of Labor houses the State Racing Commission, which regulates horse racing in Maryland under Title 11 of the Business Regulation Article. The bill authorizes the Commission to issue racing licenses and award racing days to eligible non-profits, adopt regulations regarding facility renewal funds, and oversee transmittals from the Purse Dedication Account.

The Comptroller is mandated to administer and transfer various funds, including depositing at least $17 million annually from the State Lottery Fund into the Financing Fund, paying supplemental local impact grants, paying out operating loss amounts from the Purse Dedication Account, distributing sales tax from racehorse claiming sales, and implementing sales and use tax exemptions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts the State Lottery Fund through statutory distributions to racing and community funds, expresses legislative intent regarding the operation and frequency of the Racetrax lottery game, and exempts certain horse racing licensees from the application fee for a Class A-2 sports wagering facility license.

The bill requires a joint plan between MTROA and DHCD for investments in workforce housing, affordable housing, and community revitalization around Pimlico. It also reallocates $10 million in prior capital funding from DHCD's Division of Development Finance to a grant for workforce housing administered in consultation with DHCD.

The Board of Public Works must approve the issuance of up to $400 million in MSA bonds for racing facilities, approve agreements for MTROA to manage and oversee day-to-day racing operations, and receive required notices regarding long-term agreement wind-down plans.

The Chair or Executive Director of MEDCO serves on the board of the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority, and MTROA is authorized to coordinate with MEDCO to acquire property or contractual interests for racing facilities.

The bill affects the Pimlico Community Development Authority by maintaining and structuring local impact grant allocations distributed to Baltimore City with PCDA acting as the local development council for community and capital projects surrounding Pimlico Race Course.

The Governor is required to include mandated appropriations in the FY 2026 budget ($4.5 million to RFRA and $6.2 million to Prince George's County), is authorized to make a $10 million budget amendment in FY 2025, and appoints members to the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority.

DBM is responsible for supervising state budget execution and must incorporate the bill's mandated appropriations totaling $10.7 million in general funds for fiscal 2026, as well as process authorized budget amendments for fiscal 2025.

The Treasurer is statutorily responsible for investing and reinvesting funds in the Purse Dedication Account, which is drawn upon under the bill to cover potential MTROA operating losses, and serves on the Board of Public Works reviewing the bond issuances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Capital Works Fund and the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Emergency Repair Fund as special, nonlapsing funds administered by the Maryland Stadium Authority. The funds finance capital improvements, repairs, and emergency repairs at the Camden Yards football sports facility, initially capitalizing both funds through a required transfer of $10 million in existing bond proceeds.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: The Baltimore Ravens, visitors and fans at Camden Yards football sports facility (M&T Bank Stadium), and the Maryland Stadium Authority.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2025, nonbudgeted expenditures for the Maryland Stadium Authority increase by $10.0 million to transfer bond proceeds ($5.0 million each to the Capital Works Fund and the Emergency Repair Fund), resulting in a corresponding $10.0 million increase in special fund revenues. Special fund revenues increase by $2.0 million annually from FY 2026 through FY 2030 ($1.0 million each from MSA and the Ravens) and by $1.0 million annually thereafter through at least FY 2038. Special fund expenditures increase as needed for capital projects and emergency repairs. There is no effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes two new special funds (the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Capital Works Fund and Emergency Repair Fund) to be administered directly by the Maryland Stadium Authority to finance capital improvements, repairs, and emergency repairs at Camden Yards.

The State Treasurer is required to hold the newly established funds separately, invest the money in the funds, and transfer $10 million in Series 2023B bond proceeds currently held by the Treasurer into the two funds.
The bill designates that the Comptroller of Maryland shall account for both of the newly created special funds.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Protecting Opportunities and Regional Trade (PORT) Act provides relief and economic support following the collapse of the Francis Scott Key Bridge and the resulting reduced operations at the Port of Baltimore. The act establishes temporary relief programs administered by the Maryland Department of Labor and the Department of Commerce for impacted workers and businesses; authorizes fund transfers of up to $25 million increments from the State Reserve (Rainy Day) Fund or existing agency balances; creates the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Program and Fund; waives unemployment insurance benefit charges against affected employers; provides personal income tax subtraction modifications for certain bridge collapse benefit payments and scholarships; increases the Maryland Transportation Authority's revenue bond cap by $1 billion; and directs the Attorney General to pursue legal remedies to recover economic damages.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor and Maryland Department of Commerce (along with the Maryland Higher Education Commission, Maryland Transportation Authority, and Office of the Attorney General)
qa_results.stakeholders: Port of Baltimore workers, individuals laid off or injured due to the bridge collapse, port-dependent businesses and trade associations, families and surviving spouses of fallen transportation workers, and Maryland employers paying into the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by at least $75.0 million in FY 2024, reflecting a $60.0 million transfer from the Rainy Day Fund and $15.0 million from existing Department of Commerce special fund balances (with up to $275.0 million authorized across FY 2024 and 2025). Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) debt capacity increases by $1.0 billion (from $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion), increasing potential nonbudgeted bond revenues and future debt service expenditures. General fund expenditures increase beginning in FY 2025 for MHEC to fund Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship awards. Nonbudgeted Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund (UITF) revenues decrease in FY 2025 through FY 2029 due to employer benefit charge waivers. Local tax revenues may be positively affected to the extent assistance preserves business activity; local expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the Department of Labor to establish temporary relief programs for affected port workers and businesses, waive unemployment insurance benefit charges against employers' rating records, exempt eligible individuals from work search requirements, and enforce subrogation/recapture provisions.

The bill directs the Department of Commerce to establish and administer temporary financial relief programs for businesses whose operations or cargo were diverted due to the reduced operations of the Port of Baltimore, including managing program eligibility, subrogation, and fund recapture.

The bill directly increases the Maryland Transportation Authority's statutory revenue bond debt cap by $1.0 billion (from $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion) to facilitate financing related to transportation facilities projects and bridge reconstruction.

The bill establishes the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Program and the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund, requiring the Commission to administer the fund, verify eligible recipients, and allocate scholarship awards across postsecondary institutions.

The bill explicitly requires the Attorney General to pursue all available legal options, including filing lawsuits, to recover economic damages on behalf of the State arising from the Key Bridge collapse and port closure, and report monthly to the General Assembly.

The bill authorizes the Governor to transfer funds in increments up to $25 million from the Rainy Day Fund via budget amendment to fund temporary relief programs and mandates monthly reporting to the Legislative Policy Committee.

The bill administers income tax subtraction modifications for Key Bridge benefit payments and scholarships, accounts for the newly created scholarship special fund, and authorizes the disclosure of certain tax data to Labor and Commerce to prevent program fraud.

MDOT is tasked with identifying and providing contact information for families of fallen transportation workers to the Higher Education Commission, and oversees the overall transportation infrastructure affected by the disaster.
The State Treasurer is required to hold and invest the monies of the new Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund, crediting interest earnings directly to the fund.

As the modal agency operating state-owned marine terminals at the Port of Baltimore, the administration is central to the operational recovery and economic activity addressed by the relief provisions.
DBM oversees the state budget execution and processes the budget amendments and transfers from the Revenue Stabilization Account authorized under the bill.

USM institutions serve as the statutory benchmark for the maximum scholarship award amounts under the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Program, and member institutions will process applications and enroll eligible recipients.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill significantly reforms the regulation of retail electricity and natural gas supply in Maryland by establishing licensing requirements for energy salespersons and energy vendors, capping residential retail rates relative to standard offer service, setting strict terms for contracts and automatic renewals, prohibiting commissions for sales enrollments, restricting green power marketing to verified renewable energy credit thresholds, and increasing regulatory oversight and consumer protection under the Public Service Commission.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential electric and gas utility customers, retail electricity and gas suppliers, energy salespersons, energy vendors, and electric and gas utilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission and the Office of People's Counsel increase by $1.7 million in FY 2025, rising to $2.1 million by FY 2029 for personnel and operational implementation. Special fund revenues increase correspondingly via licensure fees, an initial one-time special assessment of up to $275,000, and annual assessments on public service companies. The bill has no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PSC is the primary regulatory and implementing agency under the bill. It is responsible for licensing energy salespersons and vendors, enforcing consumer protections, setting green power price caps, administering the Education and Protection Fund, establishing a new retail supply division, and conducting a study on co-located load configurations.

OPC represents residential utility consumers in proceedings and is granted specific authority to file complaints, investigate violations, and petition PSC regarding green power pricing. The bill and accompanying budget actions also directly impact OPC's funding and staffing.

The bill requires PSC to consult with the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General before adopting consumer protection regulations, preserves OAG's independent consumer protection enforcement authority, and authorizes OAG to file complaints against noncompliant suppliers and vendors.

The bill expresses General Assembly intent for DBM to create and include two new Position Identification Numbers (PINs) in the PSC's fiscal year 2025 budget to support the newly established retail supply division.
The Comptroller is statutorily required under the bill to account for the newly renamed and expanded Education and Protection Fund.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold and invest the monies of the Education and Protection Fund separately as a nonlapsing fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to include system upgrades that allow for automated expungement and partial expungement of charges in any vendor contracts being negotiated as of the bill's effective date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with criminal records or charges eligible for automated or partial expungement, IT vendors contracting with the State, and criminal justice information system personnel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $26.0 million over five years, assumed to begin in FY 2026, to rebuild and upgrade DPSCS systems (Computerized Criminal History System and CJIS-Central Repository) via vendor contracts. Additional ongoing vendor costs will be incurred beyond five years for operation and maintenance. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) include system upgrades for automated expungement and partial expungement of charges in any vendor contracts being negotiated as of October 1, 2024, resulting in an estimated $26.0 million fiscal impact over five years to rebuild its Criminal Justice Information System and Central Repository systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the District Court to shield court records relating to a failure to pay rent proceeding within 60 days of final resolution if the proceeding did not result in a judgment of possession. It also authorizes the District Court to shield records on motion by a tenant in cases that resulted in a judgment of possession under certain conditions, such as the tenant exercising the right of redemption at least 12 months prior or showing good cause. Additionally, it requires the Maryland Judiciary to create and publish a petition form to facilitate the shielding process.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (District Court of Maryland)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants, residential landlords, and District Court personnel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $23,400 (or $23,426) in FY 2025 only for one-time computer programming costs to automate record shielding timelines, with potential minimal additional expenditure increases due to higher judicial workload from tenant shielding motions. Revenues are not affected. There is no material effect on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the District Court and the Judiciary, requiring the court to shield certain failure to pay rent records automatically or upon motion, and requiring the Judiciary to develop and publish a petition form. The fiscal note identifies $23,400 in FY 2025 programming costs and operational workload increases for the courts.

The Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division) monitors landlord-tenant laws and public record protections affecting consumers, and was consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers the authority to appoint, fill vacancies for, and remove members of the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners from the Mayor of Baltimore City and the President of the City Council to the Governor, subject to Senate advice and consent. The bill also places board members and employees under State public ethics laws and State Ethics Commission oversight rather than city ethics provisions, and temporarily allows executive secretaries to qualify through five years of Baltimore City government service in lieu of the residency requirement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and employees of the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, Baltimore City officials, the State Ethics Commission, and Baltimore City alcoholic beverage businesses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland State operations or finances, nor does it materially affect Baltimore City operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill shifts the authority to appoint, fill vacancies for, and remove members of the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners from the Mayor and City Council President to the Governor.

The bill places the Board of License Commissioners and its employees under the jurisdiction of the State Ethics Commission for conflicts of interest, public ethics compliance, and financial disclosure requirements.

As the unit within the Executive Department responsible for vetting and processing gubernatorial appointments to state and local boards, the Office of Appointments will manage the recruitment and processing of candidates for the Board of License Commissioners.
The bill mandates that if the Governor removes a member of the Board, the statement of charges and findings must be officially filed with the Office of the Secretary of State.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Maryland public high schools to inform students of employment and skills training opportunities—including registered apprenticeships, registered employers, and licensed vocational or skills training schools—in the same manner they provide information regarding postsecondary educational options, with an emphasis on high-demand, high-skilled careers that do not require a college degree.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local county boards of education and public high schools
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public high school students, public high schools, registered apprenticeship sponsors, licensed career and technical schools, and registered Maryland employers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None, as the bill pertains only to local school boards. Local Effect: The bill is not anticipated to have a material effect on local school system operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill places statutory requirements on public high schools and county boards of education, which operate under the oversight and leadership of MSDE, to inform high school students about employment and skills training opportunities.

The bill explicitly references apprenticeship programs registered with MD Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning as well as employers registered with MD Labor as key training pathways to be promoted to high school students.
The bill specifically directs high schools to inform students of career and skills training opportunities offered through schools licensed by the Maryland Higher Education Commission.
The bill specifically directs high schools to inform students of career and skills training opportunities offered through vocational and career schools licensed by the commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners to extend renewal application deadlines for alcoholic beverages licenses. It also allows certain licenses that lapsed between March 5, 2020, and December 31, 2023, to be considered unexpired until July 1, 2025, permitting them to be brought up-to-date upon meeting renewal requirements and paying all past-due fees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license and permit holders in Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Department of Legislative Services, the bill has no effect on state finances and does not materially affect Prince George’s County finances or operations. Small business impacts are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill relates to alcoholic beverages license renewals and deadline extensions in Prince George's County. While implementation rests with the local Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller has broad statutory responsibilities regarding the regulation and tax administration of the alcohol industry in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires hospitals, before discharging a newborn infant, to provide oral and written educational resources to the parent or legal guardian on establishing a safe sleep environment and supply a list of resources for obtaining necessary safe sleep items. It also requires hospitals to implement confirmation and recordkeeping processes by January 1, 2025, and directs the Maryland Department of Health, in consultation with local health departments, to produce and annually update a county-level directory of safe sleep resources.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Newborn infants, new parents and legal guardians, Maryland hospitals, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $19,400 in FY 2025 only for the Maryland Department of Health to hire part-time contractual staff to develop the county resource directory. State revenues are unaffected. Local health departments can handle the annual updates to the resource directory using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 59 requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), in consultation with local health officers, to develop and annually update a list of county resources for birthing parents and legal guardians to obtain safe sleep items for infants, resulting in an estimated fiscal impact of $19,400 in FY 2025 for contractual staff.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of 'legally protected health care' under Maryland law to include all lawful gender-affirming treatment, medications, and supplies. As a result, it extends legal protections against health occupations disciplinary actions, foreign subpoenas, interstate civil or criminal investigations, out-of-state judgment enforcement, extradition demands, and the use of State resources in furtherance of out-of-state proceedings targeting lawful gender-affirming care.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (Health Occupations Boards), the Maryland Judiciary, the Governor's Office, and State and local government agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Transgender and gender-diverse individuals receiving gender-affirming health care, licensed health care practitioners providing gender-affirming care, and health professional licensing boards.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services indicates no material state or local fiscal impact. The changes are procedural in nature and are not anticipated to materially affect governmental finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the health occupations boards housed within MDH by prohibiting them from revoking, suspending, disciplining, or taking adverse licensing actions against health care practitioners for providing or supporting gender-affirming care that is lawful in Maryland.

The bill restricts judicial actions in Maryland courts, prohibiting judges and court clerks from issuing certain subpoenas, ex parte wiretap/investigative orders, witness/document production orders, or filing foreign judgments related to out-of-state investigations or proceedings regarding legally protected health care.

Under the Criminal Procedure Article provisions amended in scope by the bill, the Governor is explicitly prohibited from surrendering a person on demand of another state's executive authority if the extradition request relates to the provision or procurement of legally protected gender-affirming care.

As the State's chief legal representative and legal counsel to executive agencies and the Governor, the OAG advises on the enforcement of interstate shield provisions, constitutional and interstate subpoena conflicts, and extradition demands.

The bill amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article to prohibit State agencies and employees from expending time, money, or State resources in furtherance of certain interstate investigations into legally protected health care, falling within DBM's oversight of State personnel and budget execution.

The Office of the Secretary of State is responsible for processing extraditions on behalf of the Governor, which are restricted under the bill for demands originating from other states concerning legally protected gender-affirming health care.

Under the broader statutory framework governing legally protected health care that is expanded by this bill, medical professional liability insurers regulated by the MIA are prohibited from taking adverse underwriting or rate actions against practitioners for providing legally protected care.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes the Office of the Correctional Ombudsman as an independent unit of Maryland State government to monitor, inspect, and investigate administrative acts and conditions in facilities operated by the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Department of Juvenile Services. It also creates a Correctional Ombudsman Advisory Board, transfers the Juvenile Justice Monitoring Unit from the Office of the Attorney General to the new office, and provides whistleblower protections for employees reporting information to the ombudsman.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Correctional Ombudsman
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals confined in or supervised by State correctional and juvenile facilities, their families, and employees of the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and Department of Juvenile Services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $1,000,000 in FY 2025 from the Performance Incentive Grant Fund to fund the initial operations and 7 new positions for the Office of the Correctional Ombudsman. In subsequent years, general fund expenditures are projected to range between $836,800 in FY 2026 and $914,000 in FY 2029. Additionally, 4 positions and $603,067 in general funds are transferred from the Office of the Attorney General to the Office of the Correctional Ombudsman. DPSCS expenditures may also increase, while local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary subject of oversight by the newly established Office of the Correctional Ombudsman, which is tasked with investigating administrative acts, inspecting DPSCS facilities, reviewing inmate health and mental health services, conducting audits of rehabilitation programs, and coordinating with the Commission on Correctional Standards.

The bill transfers the Juvenile Justice Monitoring Unit (including four positions and over $600,000 in funding) out of the Office of the Attorney General into the newly created independent Office of the Correctional Ombudsman, and involves referrals for legal and disciplinary reviews.

The Juvenile Justice Monitoring Unit transferred under this act monitors DJS facilities, investigates grievances, inspects conditions, and reviews disciplinary actions involving youth under DJS jurisdiction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP oversees the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board and administers the Performance Incentive Grant Fund, which provides $1.0 million in funding for the Ombudsman in FY 2025; its Division of Children and Youth also coordinates with juvenile justice monitoring.

The bill impacts the courts through subpoena enforcement and contempt actions, and directly tasks the Judiciary's Mediation and Conflict Resolution Office with evaluating and reporting on best practices for mediating grievances in the corrections system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the 12-member Correctional Ombudsman Advisory Board to assist and advise the Office and tasks the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board with funding recommendations.

The Governor is responsible for appointing the Correctional Ombudsman with Senate advice and consent, appointing the members of the Correctional Ombudsman Advisory Board, and receiving mandatory annual and coordination reports.

The Secretary of Budget and Management must cooperate with the Ombudsman to set minimum salaries, qualifications, and standards of training and experience for positions within the office, and manage state budget allocations.

The bill directs the monitoring unit to collaborate with MDH regarding the licensing and monitoring of children's residential facilities, while the Ombudsman conducts independent reviews of healthcare and behavioral health services provided to confined individuals.

The monitoring unit is required to collaborate with DHS regarding children's residential facility licensing and participate in multidisciplinary team child protective services investigations concerning allegations of abuse or neglect.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment, vetting, and appointment of the Correctional Ombudsman as well as the members of the Correctional Ombudsman Advisory Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup to Study Funding for the Westernport Wastewater Treatment Facility to examine current and prospective funding sources, evaluate whether increased funding would improve operations, compare regional facilities, and report recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and municipalities served by the Westernport Wastewater Treatment Facility (including Westernport and Luke, Maryland, and Piedmont, West Virginia), Allegany County, and the Upper Potomac River Commission.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expense reimbursements for workgroup members and staffing costs for the Maryland Department of the Environment are assumed to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Secretary of the Environment (or designee) serve as a member of the Workgroup and requires the Department of the Environment to provide staff support for the Workgroup's operations and report.
The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup to evaluate funding sources and operational costs.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup studying wastewater treatment operations and funding.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a temporary study body, the Workgroup to Study Funding for the Westernport Wastewater Treatment Facility, charged with reporting findings and recommendations before sunsetting in 2025.
The Workgroup is required to submit its final findings and recommendations regarding funding and operations of the wastewater facility to the Governor by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Senate Bill 143 permits local school systems and the Maryland School for the Deaf to rehire up to five retirees of the Teachers' Retirement System or Teachers' Pension System into any position within the system—including central office and nonschool-based roles—without a retirement benefit offset. It also retroactively applies this exemption to an eligible retiree reemployed by the Harford County Board of Education's Payroll Department who exceeded earnings limits in 2022 or 2023, requiring any offset benefits to be refunded by December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System (and local school system superintendents / Maryland School for the Deaf)
qa_results.stakeholders: Retirees of the Teachers' Retirement System and Teachers' Pension System reemployed in local school systems or the Maryland School for the Deaf, local school systems, and the Harford County Board of Education.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no discernible effect on State pension liabilities, contribution rates, or revenues because it applies in only a limited number of circumstances. There is no local fiscal effect. Any retirement benefit offsets previously deducted for qualifying retroactive cases must be refunded by the State Retirement and Pension System by December 31, 2024.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the Teachers' Retirement System and Teachers' Pension System, oversees reemployment earnings limitations and benefit offsets, and is specifically required by the bill to process refunds for retirees impacted by the retroactive provisions.

The superintendent of the Maryland School for the Deaf is explicitly granted statutory authority under the bill to rehire up to five retirees into any position within the agency without a retirement benefit offset.

MSDE provides leadership and oversight for Maryland's 24 local school systems, whose superintendents are directly affected by the expanded flexibility to hire retired teachers into central office or nonschool-based roles without offset penalties.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of $1,000,000 in the annual State budget bill for fiscal years 2026 through 2028 to provide operating grants to qualifying nonprofit organizations that offer automotive repair training and reentry services to incarcerated and formerly incarcerated individuals. The bill requires the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to administer the grant program and mandates annual reporting on performance metrics and fund usage.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Prince George's County to grant a local property tax credit of up to $2,500 for eligible Prince George’s County Public School System (PGCPS) employees who relocate to the county and purchase a dwelling.
