qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers statutory duties and administration relating to the Volunteer Company Assistance Fund from the Military Department to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Volunteer fire, rescue, and ambulance companies, the Maryland State Firemen's Association, the Maryland Department of Emergency Management, and the Military Department.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact as it codifies existing practice. The Maryland Department of Emergency Management already administers the Volunteer Company Assistance Fund under an interagency agreement established in 2021.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 255 directly transfers statutory duties and administrative oversight for the Volunteer Company Assistance Fund (VCAF) to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management, codifying current interagency practice.
The Adjutant General heads the Maryland Military Department, from which statutory responsibility and administration of the Volunteer Company Assistance Fund are formally transferred.
The Board of Public Works approves grant and loan requests from the Volunteer Company Assistance Fund and receives the annual report required by statute.
The Legislative Auditor receives the annual report on the Volunteer Company Assistance Fund and has statutory authorization to review fund expenditures.
The Comptroller retains statutory authority under the subtitle to audit the financial affairs of the Maryland State Firemen's Association to ensure compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill continues the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act by extending its termination date by five years from July 1, 2025, to July 1, 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed physical therapists, licensed physical therapist assistants, and Maryland consumers receiving physical therapy services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners are maintained through fiscal year 2030. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners is housed within the Maryland Department of Health. This departmental bill extends the board's termination date under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act to July 1, 2030, maintaining its regulatory operations and special fund revenues and expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the statutory authorization and operation of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners, an ongoing regulatory board of public servants and appointed citizens.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill codifies Executive Order 01.01.2023.07 by increasing the State's target for reducing average energy consumption in State-owned buildings from 10% by 2029 to 20% by 2031 compared to a fiscal 2018 baseline. It directs the Maryland Green Building Council to update the High Performance Green Building Program to align with achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2045, requires the Department of General Services (DGS) to conduct annual energy and emissions audits of at least 2 million square feet of State buildings, and mandates that State agencies implement energy conservation and emissions reduction measures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: State government agencies, occupants of State facilities, and contractors and small businesses in the energy efficiency and building renovation sectors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no direct state or local fiscal impact attributable to the bill, as it codifies an existing executive order. DGS noted a need for 6.5 FTE positions to manage increased performance contracts and oversee decarbonization projects, the costs of which would be covered through reimbursable energy purchasing fees paid by State agencies. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with establishing energy performance standards, conducting annual energy and greenhouse gas emissions audits of at least 2 million square feet of state buildings, maintaining the utility database, and overseeing energy performance contracts.
MEA is explicitly required by statute to cooperate with DGS to assist State agencies in reducing average energy consumption in State buildings by 20% by 2031.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Includes the Maryland Green Building Council, which is statutory mandated by the bill to update the High Performance Green Building Program by October 1, 2024, to align with net-zero greenhouse gas emissions goals.
The bill codifies Governor Moore's Executive Order 01.01.2023.07 and requires DGS to submit annual reports to the Governor regarding state progress and agency compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill continues the State Board of Barbers by extending its statutory sunset date by three years to July 1, 2027, under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. It also requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit an informational report regarding the board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Barbers, barber-stylists, apprentice barbers, barber shop owners, and Maryland consumers of barbering services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures for the board (State Barbers and Cosmetologists Boards' Fund) are maintained through FY 2027 instead of terminating. The Maryland Department of Labor can implement the reporting requirement with existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Barbers is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill extends the Board's termination date to July 1, 2027, and requires the Department of Labor to submit a report regarding the Board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board of Cosmetologists under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act by three years to July 1, 2027, and requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a report regarding the board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor and the State Board of Cosmetologists
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed cosmetologists, senior cosmetologists, hairstylists, blow-drying stylists, nail technicians, estheticians, cosmetology apprentices, salons, cosmetology schools, and consumers in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Cosmetologists are maintained through FY 2027 rather than expiring on July 1, 2024. The Maryland Department of Labor can prepare the required report with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Cosmetologists is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill extends the board's statutory termination date to July 1, 2027, maintaining its licensing and regulatory operations, and directly mandates that the department submit a report regarding the board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters enforcement and after-the-fact application approval procedures under local Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Programs to apply to all Critical Area violations. It repeals a 30-day waiting period required before the Chair of the Critical Area Commission can refer local enforcement failures to the Attorney General, and expands the Attorney General's authority to bring equitable actions for violations of an order, permit, plan, local program, or Critical Area law and regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Critical Area Commission for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays and the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, developers, and individuals undertaking activities in the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area, as well as the 64 local Maryland jurisdictions with lands bordering tidal shorelines.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Although the expansion of enforcement authority may result in additional enforcement actions brought by the Office of the Attorney General, the fiscal and operational impact is expected to be minimal due to the limited number of severe local Critical Area violations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Critical Area Commission for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays operates as an administrative unit within the Department of Natural Resources and requested this departmental legislation to streamline enforcement procedures and referrals.

The bill expands the authority of the Office of the Attorney General to initiate equitable enforcement actions for Critical Area violations and removes the 30-day waiting period required before the Critical Area Commission Chair can refer matters to the Attorney General.
The bill clarifies and expands provisions under which civil and criminal enforcement actions, misdemeanor prosecutions, and suits in equity may be adjudicated in Maryland District and Circuit Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the composition and terms of adult public guardianship review boards by reducing the required membership from 11 to 8, modifying professional qualifications for board positions, requiring local appointing authorities to recruit members, and permitting members to serve consecutive terms upon reappointment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Vulnerable adults under public guardianship, adult public guardianship review board members, local social services departments, and local appointing authorities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances, as adult public guardianship review boards are volunteer entities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a Department of Human Services departmental bill directly affecting Adult Protective Services. Local departments of social services under DHS administer adult public guardianships, which are reviewed by these adult public guardianship review boards, and each board includes a professional representative of a local department.

The bill maintains the requirement that each adult public guardianship review board include a representative of a local commission on aging, which forms part of the local network overseen and coordinated by the Maryland Department of Aging.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland election law by requiring court clerks to report monthly to the State Administrator of Elections only those individuals convicted of a felony who are sentenced to imprisonment with commitment papers. It also mandates that public officials make requested public buildings available at no charge for early voting centers, directs the State Board of Elections to adopt an appeals process for public officials contesting building availability, and allows incumbent members of political party central committees who are candidates for party office to serve as any responsible officer of the committee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland registered voters, court clerks, individuals convicted of felonies, local boards of elections, public officials overseeing public facilities, and political party central committee members.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $170,000 in FY 2025 only for Judiciary programming costs to adjust reporting on felony convictions. State revenues are unaffected. Local government expenditures are expected to decrease annually beginning in FY 2026 in certain counties because local election boards can use free public buildings for early voting centers rather than renting private facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 271 is a departmental bill requested by the State Board of Elections. It alters reporting of felony convictions to the State Administrator of Elections, requires the State Board to adopt regulations establishing an appeals process regarding requests for public buildings as early voting centers, and adjudicates final appeals on the use of such buildings.

The bill directly alters monthly reporting requirements for clerks of the circuit courts and District Court regarding individuals convicted of a felony and sentenced to imprisonment. The fiscal note indicates an increase in general fund expenditures of $170,000 in FY 2025 for Judiciary programming updates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits individuals from operating an unmanned aircraft over a correctional facility to record images without proper authorization, and prohibits using an unmanned aircraft to deliver contraband to a person detained in a place of confinement. Violations are misdemeanors punishable by up to three years imprisonment and/or a maximum fine of $1,000, and correctional facilities are required to post warning signage on their property.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Drone/unmanned aircraft operators, correctional facility staff, and individuals detained or incarcerated in places of confinement.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues and expenditures, as well as potential minimal increases in local revenues and expenditures, resulting from the bill's criminal penalty provisions (fines up to $1,000 and imprisonment terms up to 3 years).

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary sponsor and implementing agency of this departmental bill. The legislation authorizes the Secretary of DPSCS and facility managing officials to permit drone flights over correctional facilities, establishes criminal offenses for unauthorized drone recording and contraband delivery into facilities, and mandates the posting of public warning signage on facility exteriors.
The bill creates two new misdemeanor offenses carrying penalties of up to three years imprisonment and/or fines, resulting in potential judicial impacts on court caseloads and proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD will be responsible for providing legal defense and representation to indigent defendants charged under the newly established misdemeanor offenses.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is responsible for investigating criminal activity, including the unlawful operation of unmanned aircraft and the external delivery of contraband to confinement facilities.

DJS operates juvenile detention and residential facilities that qualify as places of confinement under Maryland criminal law, making the statutory prohibition against delivering contraband via unmanned aircraft applicable to its facilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals an obsolete statutory requirement that prohibited a notary public from signing and issuing a protest of a negotiable instrument unless using a form prescribed by the Comptroller.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland notaries public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on state or local finances or operations, as the form prescribed by the Comptroller was never created or used.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State oversees the appointment, commissioning, and regulation of notaries public in Maryland and requested this departmental bill to repeal the obsolete protest form requirement.
The bill repeals Maryland Code § 18-106 of the State Government Article, which previously required notaries public to use a protest form prescribed by the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes an applicant for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit to attest to gross income under penalties of perjury instead of providing an income tax return, provided the applicant was not required to file and did not file an income tax return.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners and prospective home purchasers applying for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit who are not required to file income tax returns.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not affected. The bill will not significantly impact the operations or finances of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions of the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit statute (§ 9-104), which directs the Comptroller to pay certified property tax credits to eligible homeowners and purchasers. The Comptroller was also consulted as an information source for the fiscal note.

PTAAB hears appeals regarding disputes over property tax credits following decisions by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Altering eligibility substantiation rules to allow gross income attestation indirectly relates to administrative disputes and appeals over credit eligibility.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the statutory termination date for the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers by one year, from July 1, 2026, to July 1, 2027, under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. It also requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit an informational report regarding the board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Individual tax preparers in Maryland and consumers of tax preparation services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers are maintained through fiscal 2027. The Maryland Department of Labor can likely prepare the required report with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Individual Tax Preparers is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor (MDL). The bill extends the statutory termination date for the Board and requires MDL to prepare and submit a report regarding the Board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum percentage of a designated continuing, nonlapsing special fund that the State Department of Assessments and Taxation may use to pay administrative expenses of the Office of the Director from 5% to 15%.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: State Department of Assessments and Taxation, particularly the Office of the Director
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill does not affect overall funding for the Office of the Director, but authorizes the department to allocate additional funding from an existing special fund for administrative expenses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under the amended section of the Corporations and Associations Article (§ 1-203.3), the State Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the special fund whose expenditure cap for administrative expenses is modified by this bill.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated under § 1-203.3 to hold and invest the continuing, nonlapsing fund whose administrative expense allowance is adjusted by this legislation.

DBM oversees the state budget execution and appropriation process, and the bill affects how the State Department of Assessments and Taxation allocates special fund versus general fund appropriations for the Office of the Director through the state budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill changes the annual reporting deadlines for waivers granted under the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program. It extends the deadline for the Office for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program within the Maryland Department of Agriculture to submit its annual waiver report to the Board of Public Works from July 31 to October 31, and moves the deadline for the Board of Public Works to submit waiver records to designated General Assembly committees from October 1 to December 31.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture (Office for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program) and the Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: State procurement agencies and public four-year universities, the Maryland Department of Agriculture, the Board of Public Works, the General Assembly, and certified local farm enterprises and Chesapeake invasive species providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. It is purely procedural in nature, altering reporting deadlines to align with agency food purchasing reporting schedules, and has no effect on governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 290 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Agriculture. It alters the deadline by which the Office for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program, housed within the Department of Agriculture, must submit its annual report on waiver requests and approvals to the Board of Public Works.

The Board of Public Works receives the annual waiver report from the Office for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program, and the bill alters the statutory deadline for the Board to compile and submit the record of waiver requests to legislative committees from October 1 to December 31.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the statutory title of the Assistant Secretary of State to Deputy Secretary of State to conform Maryland statute with current practice.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: The Office of the Maryland Secretary of State and the Deputy Secretary of State.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The bill makes a technical change in title and does not directly affect governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill directly concerns the Office of the Secretary of State by updating the statutory title of the Assistant Secretary of State to Deputy Secretary of State and codifying their delegated statutory powers.

The bill updates the Governor's statutory appointment authority and delegation powers regarding the Deputy Secretary of State for duties relating to special police officer commissions and notary public sanctions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the statutory requirement for the Maryland Department of Planning to prepare and periodically update inventory lists of the State's natural resources and major public works and private facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Department of Planning, other State agencies (such as the Department of Natural Resources, Department of Budget and Management, and Maryland Department of Transportation), and the General Assembly.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances, and has minimal or no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory responsibilities of the Maryland Department of Planning by repealing the requirement that the agency prepare and periodically revise inventory lists of state natural resources and major public works and facilities.

The Department of Natural Resources is noted as an information source and identified as the state entity that naturally maintains and oversees state natural resource inventories following the repeal of MDP's obsolete requirement.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board for Professional Land Surveyors by three years to July 1, 2027, under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act, and requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a report regarding the board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed professional land surveyors, property line surveyors, and Maryland consumers of land surveying services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the board are maintained through FY 2027 rather than terminating. The Maryland Department of Labor can complete the required report using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board for Professional Land Surveyors is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor (MDL). This departmental bill extends the board's statutory termination date to July 1, 2027, maintaining its licensing operations and special fund finances, and directly mandates MDL to submit an informational report regarding the board by July 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill reduces the number of years of professional engineering practice required for an engineer member to qualify for appointment to the State Board for Professional Engineers from 12 years to 10 years.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board for Professional Engineers within the Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Professional engineers in Maryland and prospective candidates for the State Board for Professional Engineers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as modifying the qualifications for board members does not affect governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board for Professional Engineers is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing, and this departmental bill directly alters the statutory qualification requirements for engineer board members appointed to that board.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates to state boards and commissions, and this bill directly alters the eligibility requirements for engineer members of the State Board for Professional Engineers.

The Governor holds the statutory authority to appoint members to state licensing boards, including the State Board for Professional Engineers, for which this bill modifies member qualification criteria.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill authorizes the State Board of Electricians to impose a civil monetary penalty of up to $5,000 per violation instead of, or in addition to, reprimanding a licensee or suspending or revoking a license. Penalties collected are remitted to the General Fund. The bill also requires the Board to submit a report by October 1, 2024, detailing its complaint handling practices, complaint backlog, licensing timelines from 2018 through 2023, and strategies to prevent future backlogs.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Electricians
qa_results.stakeholders: State licensed electricians, license applicants, and consumers of electrical services in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected. Civil monetary penalty revenues deposited into the General Fund are expected to be minimal, and the required report can be completed using existing Board resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Electricians is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. This departmental bill directly expands the regulatory and enforcement authority of the Board by authorizing civil penalties up to $5,000 and requires the Board to submit a detailed report on complaint resolution and licensing processes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the duties of the Coast Smart Council to include establishing eligibility criteria, standards, and procedures for categorical exemptions from Coast Smart requirements for capital projects designed with adaptation and resiliency features. The bill also authorizes the Council to recommend regulations for adoption by the Secretary of Natural Resources.
qa_results.responsible_party: Coast Smart Council and the Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local government agencies managing capital construction projects subject to Coast Smart siting and design criteria
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations, as categorical exemptions are already being utilized under the Coast Smart Program. State and local entities may benefit from an expedited and streamlined project review process.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by DNR and directly expands the duties of the Coast Smart Council, which is housed within DNR. Additionally, it authorizes the Council to recommend regulations for formal adoption by the Secretary of Natural Resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Coast Smart Council is an executive advisory and regulatory council whose statutory duties, criteria development responsibilities, and authority to recommend regulations are directly expanded by this bill.

MDOT works in consultation with the Coast Smart Council to establish siting and design criteria, and MDOT's highway and transit capital projects in coastal areas are directly affected by Coast Smart requirements and categorical exemptions.
DGS manages planning, design, and construction of State-owned capital facilities that must comply with Coast Smart requirements or navigate categorical exemption procedures.

MDEM coordinates disaster resilience and hazard mitigation for coastal flooding and extreme weather events; emergency-use facilities are among the types eligible for Coast Smart categorical exemptions.

IAC oversees public school construction and capital projects, which may be subject to Coast Smart flood and sea level rise standards or eligible for categorical exemptions when state funding thresholds are met.

USM undertakes significant State-funded capital construction and renovation projects, some of which are located in coastal or tidally influenced zones and subject to Coast Smart guidelines and exemption processes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources (DNR), with prior approval from the Maryland Historical Trust and following internal review, to permit archeological research, salvage, excavation, and the stabilization and restoration of historic structures existing as of December 1, 1985, within the Belt Woods Wildland in Prince George's County. It also allows mechanical or motorized equipment to stabilize or remove existing structures and debris, and requires consultation with the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission prior to work on the Seton Belt Barn.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Visitors to Maryland wildlands, historic preservationists, environmental conservationists, prospective restoration contractors, and Prince George's County residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are anticipated to be handled with existing budgeted resources. DNR estimates the total restoration project cost for the two historic barns to be approximately $1.2 million, funded through prior-year appropriations that remain available. Local governments face no direct fiscal impact, as the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission can conduct required consultations using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a departmental bill requested by DNR, SB 300 authorizes the department to approve archeological research, excavation, and the stabilization and restoration of historic structures (specifically the Calvert and Seton Belt barns) within the state-owned Belt Woods Wildland.

The bill explicitly requires the prior approval of the Maryland Historical Trust—which is administered within the Department of Planning—before DNR can authorize any archeological research, excavation, or historic structure stabilization within the wildland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends from June 30, 2024, to June 30, 2027, the authorization allowing aquaculture leaseholders, with prior written approval from the Department of Natural Resources, to place shellfish, bags, nets, and structures on submerged aquatic vegetation, and extends related annual reporting requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Aquaculture leaseholders, shellfish farmers, and commercial aquaculture small businesses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances. However, it provides a meaningful positive economic impact on small businesses by enabling aquaculture leaseholders to continue operations and maximize working lease areas in locations with submerged aquatic vegetation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 301 is a departmental bill for the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). It extends DNR's authority to approve the placement of aquaculture shellfish, bags, nets, and structures on submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) through June 30, 2027, and extends DNR's annual reporting requirements on the impacts and characteristics of these aquaculture activities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of "shellfish" under Maryland aquaculture law to include live bivalves and bivalve shells, broadening the scope of shellfish that cannot be imported or possessed from out-of-state for planting in Maryland waters without approval from the Department of Natural Resources.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Aquaculture leaseholders, shellfish farmers, and commercial entities importing or planting shellfish and bivalves in Maryland waters.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances, has no local fiscal impact, and is estimated to have minimal or no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 303 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) that alters the statutory definition of 'shellfish' under the Natural Resources Article to include live bivalves and bivalve shells. This expands DNR's regulatory authority over the importation and planting of shellfish species to protect State waters against diseases.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date of the Board of Boiler Rules within the Maryland Department of Labor by five years to July 1, 2029. It also expands the board's membership to include a representative with at least 10 years of experience in constructing, installing, and repairing boilers and pressure vessels, and requires the Department of Labor to submit an informational report regarding the board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners, users, manufacturers, installers, repairers, and insurers of boilers and pressure vessels, as well as engineers and consumer members involved with boiler safety standards.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures for the Board of Boiler Rules are maintained through FY 2029. Adding a board member and completing the required report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Boiler Rules is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill extends the board's termination date to July 1, 2029, adjusts the board's composition, and mandates that the Department submit a report regarding the board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the composition and extends the statutory authorization under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act for the Board of Boiler Rules.
The bill adds an additional member to the Board of Boiler Rules who must be appointed by the Governor with the advice of the Secretary of Labor and advice and consent of the Senate.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and managing appointments to state boards and commissions, which includes the newly established seat on the Board of Boiler Rules.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill repeals the requirement that the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP) serve as a clearinghouse and repository for federal and State financial and technical assistance information, as well as the mandate to adopt related regulations. It also requires MDP to annually publish information regarding State financial and technical assistance programs online via the Maryland InfoPortal rather than through a physical catalog.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies, local governments, civic and private organizations, and individuals seeking information on State and federal assistance programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances, as it simply modernizes statutory language to match current digital practices on the Maryland InfoPortal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 310 is a departmental bill directly concerning the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP). It removes the statutory mandate for MDP to act as a clearinghouse and repository for federal and State assistance, removes its requirement to adopt certain regulations for other state units, and updates the requirement that MDP annually publish State assistance program information digitally on the Maryland InfoPortal.

The Governor's Grants Office serves as Maryland's central clearinghouse for federal grant information and resources. The bill repeals a duplicative statutory requirement for the Department of Planning to serve as a repository and clearinghouse for federal assistance, acknowledging the modern role fulfilled by the Governor's Grants Office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to enact a local property tax credit for newly constructed or substantially rehabilitated hotel or residential development projects. To qualify, hotel projects must substantially increase the assessed value of the property, and residential developments must include at least 20 residential units with at least 15% of units affordable to households earning less than 80% of the area median income.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial and residential real estate developers, hotel operators, low- to moderate-income households seeking affordable housing, and county and municipal governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues will decrease beginning in FY 2025 to the extent that county or municipal governments choose to authorize the tax credit. The revenue loss cannot be reliably estimated because it depends on the number of qualifying projects, their assessed values, and the specific terms of credits granted by local jurisdictions. Local expenditures are not directly affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2024 implements various budgetary actions to balance the State budget, adjust mandated appropriations, increase revenues, contain spending, and authorize fund transfers. Key actions include altering higher education funding formulas (John A. Cade formula for community colleges and the Sellinger Program for private institutions), modifying full-day prekindergarten implementation and funding, increasing motor vehicle registration fees and emergency medical services surcharges, establishing a transportation network company (TNC) impact fee, increasing tobacco and electronic smoking device taxes, and redirecting special fund interest earnings and fund balances.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers, vehicle owners, ride-hailing and transit passengers, tobacco and electronic smoking device consumers and vendors, lottery retailers, public community colleges, private higher education institutions, local school boards, prekindergarten students and families, and trauma care facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by $469.4 million in FY 2024 and $284.9 million in FY 2025, while general fund expenditures decrease by $24.5 million in FY 2024 and $129.0 million in FY 2025 (yielding a two-year net general fund improvement of $907.8 million). Special fund revenues decrease by $82.3 million in FY 2024 and increase by $320.3 million in FY 2025, while special fund expenditures increase by $4.5 million in FY 2024 and decrease by $15.8 million in FY 2025. Local impacts include a $12.7 million reduction in direct State aid to local community colleges in FY 2025, alterations to local prekindergarten aid and county funding requirements, and potential increases in local revenue from transportation network company fee distributions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is significantly impacted through major revenue restructuring, including the establishment of the Transportation Network Company (TNC) impact fee and account, increases to vehicle registration fees across multiple vehicle classes, surcharges on electric and plug-in electric vehicles, diversion of sales tax from nonresidential vehicle charging to the Transportation Trust Fund, and staffing support for the TRAIN Commission Advisory Committee.

The Comptroller is responsible for collecting, administering, and distributing substantial new and altered revenue streams, including the new TNC impact fee, increased tobacco taxes, floor tax collections, increased sales and use taxes on electronic smoking devices, vehicle charging electricity sales taxes, and managing transfers involving the Local Income Tax Reserve Account.

MSDE is heavily impacted by formula adjustments and funding shifts under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, alterations to the full-day prekindergarten per pupil funding amounts and Tier II phase-in schedule, a prohibition on increasing Child Care Scholarship Program copayments, and transfers to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund.

MHEC is directly responsible for calculating and administering altered statutory funding formulas for local community colleges (the Senator John A. Cade formula) and private nonprofit institutions of higher education (the Joseph A. Sellinger Program), as well as certifying student full-time equivalent counts.

MDH experiences multiple budgetary transfers and fund modifications, including receiving transfers from health professional licensing boards into the Behavioral Health Administration, expanding allowable uses of the Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program Fund, receiving reimbursements for Medicaid school-based behavioral health services, and transfers from the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund.

The Treasurer is responsible for maintaining the sinking fund for consolidated transportation bonds pledged from TNC fees, handling fund allocations and accounting for various special funds, and managing the redirection of net interest on special funds to the General Fund.

The bill reduces the annual supplemental state contribution to the pension system from $75 million to $50 million beginning in fiscal 2025 and repeals provisions that allowed offsetting employer contributions by certain administrative and operational expenses.

In FY 2027, the average employer cost for an eligible member to claim the maximum five years of service credit ranges from $5,100 to $11,400 depending on the retirement plan, funded 60% general funds, 20% special funds, and 20% federal/other funds. There is no effect on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies eligibility for military service credit within the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), which the Maryland State Retirement Agency administers. The agency is responsible for processing member applications for service credit and calculating retirement allowances.

As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and long-term fiscal planning, including the state budget appropriations needed for employer contributions to the State Retirement and Pension System.

DVMF advocates for and assists military service members, veterans, and their families in securing benefits and resources, which encompasses state-level service credits and recognitions for uniformed service.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires residential service agencies that provide personal assistance services under Medicaid home- and community-based service programs to submit an annual report to the Maryland Department of Labor detailing average, highest, and lowest wage rates for personal care aides starting September 1, 2025. It also requires the Maryland Department of Health to report to the General Assembly within 180 days of the release of the federal Ensuring Access to Medicaid Services final rule on how it will operationalize the rule and review wage reports and reimbursement rates.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor and Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential service agencies, personal care aides, and Medicaid beneficiaries receiving home- and community-based personal assistance services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly affected: the Maryland Department of Labor can receive the wage reports and the Maryland Department of Health can complete the required federal rule report using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local government fiscal impact. Small business residential service agencies face an operational impact to fulfill the reporting mandates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill concerns the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and home- and community-based services administered by MDH. It requires MDH to submit a report to the General Assembly regarding the federal 'Ensuring Access to Medicaid Services' rule, detailing how the department will operationalize the rule, review wage reports of personal care aides, and use the data to review Medicaid reimbursement rates.
The bill mandates that residential service agencies submit annual wage reports for personal care aides directly to the Maryland Department of Labor in a form and manner determined by the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the inclusion of certain provisions in State contracts, such as indemnification without an appropriation, binding arbitration, out-of-state venue selection, unauthorized unilateral terms, and restrictions on recovering replacement contractor costs. Any such prohibited provisions included in a State contract are deemed void ab initio, with the remainder of the contract remaining enforceable under Maryland law.
qa_results.responsible_party: State agencies and procurement units entering into State contracts (including the Department of General Services, Board of Public Works, and the Office of the Attorney General)
qa_results.stakeholders: State contractors, vendors, businesses entering into agreements with the State of Maryland, and State procurement officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is procedural in nature and generally conforms statute to current State procurement and contracting practices. Small business impact is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Attorney General, prohibiting State contracts from designating any other person as legal counsel for the State unless authorized by law. The OAG also serves as the State's chief legal representative responsible for reviewing, drafting, and enforcing State contracts.

As the State's central procurement authority overseeing state contracts for goods, services, facilities, and leases, DGS must ensure all executed State contracts comply with the mandatory prohibitions on terms like indemnification, arbitration, and unilateral amendments.

The Board of Public Works reviews and approves significant State procurement contracts and capital expenditures, and will oversee the implementation and enforcement of these contract requirements across state procurements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSBCA adjudicates disputes and claims arising from State contracts. The bill declares prohibited clauses void ab initio and dictates how disputed contract provisions are construed under Maryland law.

MDOT enters into extensive procurement, construction, and service contracts across its modal administrations and must conform its contracting templates and agreements to the new statutory prohibitions.

The Treasurer manages the State Insurance Trust Fund, protects the State against financial liabilities, and serves on the Board of Public Works, directly aligning with provisions restricting unappropriated indemnification and limits on contractor liability.

The bill mandates that State contracts cannot require binding arbitration or designate dispute venues outside of Maryland courts of proper jurisdiction, directly touching upon judicial branch forum requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Senate Bill 376 permanently extends an annual state budget appropriation of at least $5 million for the University of Maryland School of Medicine to provide specialized clinical care at the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center. It also establishes a phased-in annual General Fund appropriation for the MPowering Joint Steering Council to use exclusively on the University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing, starting at $1.5 million in fiscal year 2026 and rising to $6.0 million annually by fiscal year 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: MPowering Joint Steering Council and University of Maryland School of Medicine
qa_results.stakeholders: University of Maryland School of Medicine faculty, University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing researchers, University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center, and patients receiving clinical care in the region.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by $1.5 million in FY 2026, $3.0 million in FY 2027, $4.5 million in FY 2028, and $6.0 million annually starting in FY 2029 for the University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing. Expenditures could increase by an additional $5.0 million annually beginning in FY 2026 to maintain clinical care funding if discretionary funds would not have otherwise been provided. There is no effect on local finances or revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts institutions within the University System of Maryland (specifically the University of Maryland School of Medicine, University of Maryland, Baltimore, and University of Maryland, College Park) and its MPowering Joint Steering Council by mandating annual General Fund appropriations for clinical care at UM Capital Region Medical Center and the UM Institute for Health Computing.
The bill creates and extends statutory mandated appropriations that DBM must incorporate into the annual State operating budget preparation and financial planning from FY 2026 onward.
The bill places a statutory requirement upon the Governor to include specific mandated appropriations in the annual State budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill renames the Task Force to Study Crime Classification to the Task Force to Study Crime Reclassification and Penalties, expands its membership, alters its duties, and extends its termination date. The task force is charged with reviewing penalties across various State statutory articles and sentencing guidelines, evaluating offense classifications and mens rea standards, and submitting a report with findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals involved in the Maryland criminal justice system, including criminal defendants, crime victims, prosecutors, defense attorneys, law enforcement, and victim advocacy organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General increase by $177,300 in FY 2025 and $155,900 in FY 2026 to fund 1.5 contractual staff positions (one attorney and one part-time paralegal) to support the task force's research and reporting requirements. Member travel reimbursements are assumed to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General is designated to staff the Task Force, the Attorney General (or designee) serves as a member, and the agency incurs a direct fiscal impact of $177,300 in FY 2025 and $155,900 in FY 2026 to hire contractual staff to fulfill the bill's requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (referenced under its prior name, the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) is added as an ex officio member of the Task Force.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Task Force, which is charged with reviewing criminal penalties, reclassifying offenses, and studying mens rea requirements that directly impact indigent criminal defense.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the composition, name, scope of duties, and operational timeline of an existing state task force (the Task Force to Study Crime Reclassification and Penalties).
The Task Force is required to report its findings and recommendations regarding crime reclassification, sentencing, and penalties to the Governor by December 31, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit by allowing recipients of credits for phased projects to claim 100% of the credit in the year the phase certificate is issued rather than spreading it over five years. It also permits the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to award initial tax credit certificates to multiple projects within a two-year period, up to an aggregate cap of $15 million, and establishes provisions for revoking and reallocating initial certificates.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals, nonprofit organizations, and business entities rehabilitating qualifying catalytic revitalization properties (formerly government-owned out-of-service facilities), as well as local communities undergoing redevelopment.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by at least $2,700,000 in FY 2025, $2,600,000 in FY 2026, $1,100,000 in FY 2027, and $100,000 in FY 2028 due to accelerated credit claiming for phased projects. Beyond FY 2028, net revenue impacts are less clear. If credits are claimed against the corporate income tax, the Higher Education Investment Fund, Transportation Trust Fund, and local highway user revenues will also experience revenue decreases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary agency administering the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit. The bill amends the Secretary of Housing and Community Development's authority regarding certificate issuance, revocations, application limits, and phased project regulations.
The statute specifically requires the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to adopt program regulations in consultation with the Department of Commerce.

As the State's tax collector and administrator of state income taxes, the Comptroller processes claims for the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit and is directly affected by alterations to the claiming schedule and resulting revenue reductions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Correctional Training Commission by removing the Federal Bureau of Prisons representative and expanding the Governor-appointed correctional officers or officials from four to five. It requires these five appointees to be from local correctional facilities representing five designated geographic regions of Maryland, and removes the requirement that one appointee be a Department of Juvenile Services employee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Correctional Training Commission within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Local correctional officers and facility officials across Maryland's geographic regions, members of the Correctional Training Commission, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Any expense reimbursements for additional local members can be handled with existing local resources, and local government finances are not otherwise affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Correctional Training Commission is established within DPSCS, and key agency leadership—including the Secretary, a Deputy Secretary, and an additional department representative—serve as statutory members.

The Secretary of Juvenile Services and a designated DJS representative serve on the Commission. The bill directly alters DJS representation by repealing the requirement that at least one of the Governor's appointed correctional officials be a DJS employee.

The Governor is responsible for appointing five correctional officers or officials from local correctional facilities to the Commission, adhering to new geographic representation requirements across five specified regions.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing the appointment process for the five regional local correctional facility seats on the Commission.
The Attorney General of Maryland serves as a statutory ex officio member of the Correctional Training Commission.
MHEC is statutorily responsible for appointing a college or university president with a correctional education curriculum to the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Senate Bill 417 updates election administration requirements in Maryland by mandating annual performance evaluations of the State Administrator by the State Board of Elections, and annual evaluations of local election directors by the State Administrator. It requires local election boards to maintain a warehouse, cover early voting center expenses, and consult with the State Administrator before appointing an election director. Furthermore, it shifts several optional duties of local election directors into mandatory responsibilities, including managing voting equipment security, adhering to cybersecurity requirements, and reporting security incidents within 24 hours.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: State Administrator of Elections, local boards of elections, local election directors, election workers, and Maryland voters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the State Board of Elections, establishing requirements for the Board to annually evaluate the State Administrator of Elections, expanding the State Administrator's oversight of local election directors, and setting statutory duties and cybersecurity requirements for local election boards and directors.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the purpose and eligible use of the Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund to include providing grants and loans to anchor institutions for community development projects in sustainable communities in addition to blighted areas. It also broadens the definition of anchor institution to encompass departments, foundations, and other entities of qualifying higher education institutions and hospitals, and removes the restriction that matching funds must come exclusively from private sources.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Institutions of higher education, hospitals, their respective departments and foundations, and residents and organizations in designated sustainable communities and blighted areas.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Overall finances of the Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund are not affected, as the bill does not alter the existing $10.0 million annual appropriation mandate. However, broadening fund eligibility and removing the private match requirement may shift how funds are distributed among eligible entities. The Department of Housing and Community Development can administer the changes with existing resources, and local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Administers the Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund and evaluates grant and loan applications for community development projects in blighted areas and designated sustainable communities.

Constituent higher education institutions and their associated foundations and departments qualify as anchor institutions eligible for grants and loans, benefiting from the broadened scope and the repeal of the private matching fund restriction.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State and its affiliated entities qualify as eligible anchor institutions under the fund for community development projects.
Hospital institutions are defined as anchor institutions eligible for funding under the program, and MDH was consulted as a stakeholder agency regarding the bill's impacts.
Statutorily tasked with holding and investing the monies of the Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund.
Statutorily responsible for accounting for the Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund.
As an independent state public honors college, it qualifies as an institution of higher education eligible to apply for anchor institution funding.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires county tax collectors, treasurers, or finance directors to provide a certificate upon request listing all taxes, assessments, and charges due against a real property, which protects bona fide purchasers from unlisted charges. It authorizes local governments to charge up to $55 for the certificate and requires collecting agents to endorse deeds upon payment of the listed charges. Additionally, it mandates that clerks of the circuit courts and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation coordinate procedures to facilitate electronic payments and the electronic satisfaction of conditions required to record documents.
qa_results.responsible_party: County treasurers, tax collectors, or directors of finance; Clerks of the Circuit Courts; and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
qa_results.stakeholders: Property buyers and sellers, bona fide purchasers, title and settlement agents, county and municipal tax/finance departments, and circuit court land record offices
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Local government revenues may increase due to an authorized fee of up to $55 per certificate issued, which is expected to offset any minimal administrative costs incurred to implement the certification process.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that clerks of the circuit courts coordinate with State and county officials to facilitate electronic procedures and payments for recording land instruments, operating under standards established by the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC).

qa_results.bill_summary: The Garrett County Alcoholic Beverages Act of 2024 establishes Class B-resort beer licenses, Class B-resort beer and wine licenses, and beer, wine, and liquor (BWL) festival licenses in Garrett County. It allows resort license holders to sell alcoholic beverages at recreational facilities, moves up Sunday alcohol sales from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 a.m. in eligible districts, establishes a Maryland residency requirement for at least one applicant on a license, prohibits bringing alcoholic beverages into adult entertainment venues, and increases the maximum fine for county alcohol law violations from $3,000 to $5,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Garrett County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license holders, resorts, hotels, restaurants, recreational facilities, event organizers, adult entertainment establishments, and alcohol consumers in Garrett County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Garrett County can administer the changes with existing resources. County revenues may increase minimally starting in fiscal year 2025 from up to four new BWL festival licenses and higher maximum violation fines, though revenues could potentially be offset if existing resort license holders switch to less expensive beer or beer and wine resort licenses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry and administering state alcohol laws. While the bill primarily affects local licensing, hours of sale, and enforcement overseen by the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it directly concerns alcohol regulation and references statutory application provisions under the state's alcoholic beverages law.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the uncodified Maryland Vestry Act concerning the Protestant Episcopal Church, Diocese of Washington, and enacts codified provisions governing religious corporations affiliated with the diocese. The bill formally recognizes the corporate existence of specific parishes across Montgomery, Prince George's, Charles, and St. Mary's counties and establishes rules for corporate bylaws and filing certificates of incorporation with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Parishes, vestries, and congregations affiliated with the Protestant Episcopal Church, Diocese of Washington, located primarily in Montgomery, Prince George's, Charles, and St. Mary's counties.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase minimally to the extent parishes file articles of incorporation. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the bill using existing resources. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly estops courts of the State from denying the corporate existence and validity of the specified Episcopal parishes, and the Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted in the fiscal and policy analysis.

The Office of the Attorney General was consulted on the legal and constitutional parameters regarding religious corporation charters and the repeal and reenactment of statutory corporate governance provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill codifies and establishes the Community Health and Safety Works Grant Program and a corresponding special, nonlapsing fund within the Department of Housing and Community Development. The program provides grant funding to nonprofit organizations, local governments, and higher education institutions for facility and community improvements, business district and neighborhood security projects, and community-centered crime and violence intervention and prevention initiatives.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, institutions of higher education, local business districts, and Maryland community residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $10.0 million annually beginning in FY 2025 to capitalize the special fund, reflecting a statutory budget mandate of $10.0 million for FY 2025 through FY 2028. Special fund revenues and grant expenditures increase correspondingly by $10.0 million each year. DHCD can administer the program with existing staff. Local governments and State higher education institutions may see increased revenues and expenditures to the extent they apply for and receive grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary administering agency responsible for establishing and managing the Community Health and Safety Works Grant Program and the associated special, nonlapsing fund, including adopting regulations and awarding grants.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a $10,000,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for the fund for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2028.
DBM oversees the development and execution of the state budget and will be responsible for implementing the statutory mandate requiring $10,000,000 annual appropriations from FY 2025 through FY 2028.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Community Health and Safety Works Grant Program Fund separately, invest its money, and ensure interest earnings are credited to the fund.
The Comptroller is explicitly tasked with accounting for the newly established Community Health and Safety Works Grant Program Fund.

Institutions of higher education within the system are eligible applicants for Business District and Neighborhood Security Project grants in collaboration with local neighborhood associations, which would increase institution revenues and expenditures.

As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is eligible to partner with local neighborhood associations to apply for and receive grants under the Business District and Neighborhood Security Project category.

As a public higher education institution, the college is an eligible applicant in partnership with a local neighborhood association for grants under the Business District and Neighborhood Security Project category.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the per capita State funding calculation formula for the State Library Resource Center (the Central Library of the Enoch Pratt Free Library System) from $1.97 to $2.07 per State resident beginning in fiscal year 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: State Library Resource Center (Central Library of the Enoch Pratt Free Library System), local public library systems across Maryland, and Maryland residents who utilize public library services and resources.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $616,500 in FY 2025, rising to $632,800 by FY 2029 due to projected population growth. State funding for the enhancement was already incorporated into the FY 2025 State budget, and the bill increases a mandated appropriation starting in FY 2026. Revenues are unaffected. Local library systems benefit from expanded State Library Resource Center services, but local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency is responsible for funding and coordination of Maryland's public library systems and the State Library Network, which includes the State Library Resource Center (SLRC) and the Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled (LBPD). The bill directly modifies statutory per-capita state aid formulas that fund SLRC operations.

The bill creates an increased mandated General Fund appropriation for the State Library Resource Center starting in fiscal year 2025, which DBM must incorporate and supervise in the development and execution of the annual state budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires victims of domestic violence programs to be certified by the federally recognized State domestic violence coalition as comprehensive domestic violence programs. It also creates the Victims of Domestic Violence Program Grant Fund, administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (formerly the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services), to provide grants to certified public or private nonprofit domestic violence programs, and authorizes the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $5 million for the fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (formerly Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services)
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of domestic violence and their children, and certified public or private nonprofit domestic violence service providers and shelters.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually beginning in FY 2025, reflecting the receipt and disbursement of grant funding. Assuming the full authorized discretionary appropriation of $5.0 million is provided, general fund expenditures increase by $2.9 million annually beginning in FY 2025 (offset by $2.1 million in existing general funds redirected from the Domestic Violence program to the new fund). The office can administer the fund using existing resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary agency responsible for administering the Victims of Domestic Violence Program, setting program standards and regulations, and administering the newly established Victims of Domestic Violence Program Grant Fund.
The State Treasurer is statutorily mandated to hold the Victims of Domestic Violence Program Grant Fund separately and invest the fund's moneys.
The Comptroller is statutorily directed to account for the newly established special Victims of Domestic Violence Program Grant Fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an annual appropriation of up to $5.0 million to the Victims of Domestic Violence Program Grant Fund in the state budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Study African American Civil War Soldiers in Maryland to research the history of African American Union soldiers from Maryland and formulate recommendations regarding the funding, design, construction, and location of an appropriate memorial dedicated in their honor.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Archives
qa_results.stakeholders: Historians, preservationists, descendants of African American Civil War veterans, and the general public interested in Maryland military history
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $63,800 in FY 2025 for the Maryland State Archives to hire a temporary contractual archivist trainee to staff the commission and draft the required report. Commission member reimbursements are assumed to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources. There is no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives is designated to provide staff support for the Commission to Study African American Civil War Soldiers in Maryland, conduct research on muster rolls and historical records, and has a direct fiscal impact of $63,813 in FY 2025 for contractual staff.

The Department of Planning is statutorily designated to have a representative on the Commission, and it administratively oversees the Governor's Commission on Maryland Military Monuments, which also has a designated seat on the Commission.
The Governor is responsible for appointing several members of the Commission, designating the Commission chair, and receiving the final findings and recommendations report by December 1, 2024.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state study commission—the Commission to Study African American Civil War Soldiers in Maryland—which operates from July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for seats on the newly established commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that provisions in contracts or agreements relating to the use of a recreational facility that purport to limit liability, release from liability, or indemnify/hold harmless the facility for injury caused by the facility's or its employees' negligence or wrongful acts are void and unenforceable as against public policy, with exceptions for certain adult health club service agreements, certain lodging establishments, and government units leasing land or facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Patrons and operators of commercial recreational facilities, athletic facilities, amusement attractions, gymnasiums, and swimming pools, as well as state and local government entities leasing or managing recreational properties.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Revenues are not affected. Depending on judicial interpretation regarding government liability, State special fund expenditures (State Insurance Trust Fund) and general fund expenditures may increase due to increased liability exposure and insurance assessments. Local government expenditures may also increase due to greater liability exposure.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF), which covers tort claims under the Maryland Tort Claims Act (MTCA). Depending on judicial interpretation, any increased tort liability exposure for State-owned facilities could impact SITF expenditures and agency assessments.
