agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Specifically highlighted in the fiscal note as anticipating moderate to significant operational and personnel costs to implement the required data and AI inventories and impact assessments.
Specifically identified in the fiscal note as anticipating moderate to significant costs for specialized staff to comply with data inventories, AI system inventories, and impact assessments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for an existing Maryland income tax subtraction modification of up to $5,000 to include State law enforcement officers who reside in a political subdivision with a crime rate exceeding the State's crime rate.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: State law enforcement officers residing in Maryland political subdivisions with higher-than-average crime rates.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an estimated $203,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to additional subtraction modifications claimed on personal income tax returns. Local income tax revenues decrease by an estimated $132,000 annually beginning in FY 2025. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's chief tax administrator, the Comptroller oversees the personal income tax, updates tax forms and systems to incorporate the expanded subtraction modification, and receives triennial certifications of qualifying political subdivisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, which is mandated by statute to determine and certify to the Comptroller every three years which political subdivisions have crime rates exceeding the statewide rate.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, its sworn officers are direct beneficiaries of this bill, making them newly eligible for the $5,000 income tax subtraction modification if they reside in qualifying jurisdictions.

The bill amends the specific statutory paragraph governing the Maryland Transportation Authority Police to expand the subtraction modification from MDTA police to all other state law enforcement units.
The department operates the Natural Resources Police, whose state law enforcement officers are now eligible to claim the expanded income tax subtraction modification if they meet residency criteria.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum line-of-duty funeral expense benefit from $10,000 to $25,000 for specified public safety officers, repeals the requirement that this benefit be reduced by workers' compensation payments, and indexes the cap to inflation starting in fiscal year 2026. It also increases the line-of-duty death benefit for State employees and Maryland National Guard members from $100,000 to $125,000, extends eligibility to legislative and judicial branch employees, establishes a line-of-duty funeral benefit of up to $25,000 for State employees, indexes these benefits to inflation beginning in fiscal year 2026, and allows retroactive claims for eligible State employee deaths occurring on or after January 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: State employees across executive, legislative, and judicial branches; Maryland National Guard members; public safety officers including law enforcement, correctional officers, firefighters, rescue personnel, State Fire Marshal personnel, and hazardous materials response employees; and their surviving spouses, children, dependent parents, or estates.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $340,000 in FY 2025 ($250,000 for the Department of Budget and Management and $90,000 for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services) and by at least $206,700 annually thereafter, growing with inflation and depending on the number of line-of-duty deaths. State revenues are unaffected. Local government expenditures may experience a minimal impact if local agencies cover the increased funeral benefit for local hazardous material response team personnel.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Budget and Management to determine eligibility for and administer line-of-duty death and funeral benefits under the State Personnel and Pensions Article, including retroactive claims, resulting in a direct operational and fiscal impact of over $250,000 in FY 2025 and ongoing expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill increases the cap on reasonable funeral expenses from $10,000 to $25,000 and indexes it to inflation for public safety personnel killed in the line of duty under the Public Safety Article, which DPSCS administers and pays, increasing their general fund expenditures by at least $90,000 annually.

The statute explicitly includes members of the Maryland National Guard serving on specified state or federal orders as eligible recipients for the enhanced line-of-duty death and newly established funeral expense benefits.

MSP law enforcement officers and aviation personnel are among the primary public safety personnel covered by the enhanced line-of-duty death and funeral expense provisions under Public Safety Article § 1-202.

The bill explicitly expands the definition of a unit of State government under § 10-404 to include the Judicial Branch, extending death and funeral benefits to judicial officers and court personnel (specifically noted in the fiscal note regarding the line-of-duty death of a circuit court judge).
The bill repeals the statutory requirement that reduced public safety funeral expense benefits by the amount of workers' compensation benefits paid under § 9-689 of the Labor and Employment Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the Maryland Safe Haven Program by increasing the timeframe from 10 to 60 days after birth during which an unharmed newborn can be safely surrendered without criminal prosecution or civil liability. It permits newborns to be left at designated facilities—including hospitals, licensed medical offices, police barracks, and insured fire stations—and authorizes these facilities to utilize approved newborn safety devices (baby boxes). The bill also directs the Secretary of Human Services to establish a public information program to promote awareness and report annually on program metrics to the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Parents of newborns, surrendered infants, hospitals, licensed medical providers, law enforcement, fire and emergency medical services personnel, and local departments of social services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 for the Department of Human Services to develop, implement, and maintain the public information campaign. Required annual reporting and literature distribution by State and local entities can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected, though local agencies that voluntarily opt to install a newborn safety device would incur installation costs of approximately $15,000 and ongoing annual maintenance costs between $500 and $5,000.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS is the primary implementing agency under the bill. The Secretary of Human Services is required to adopt implementing regulations, administer the Maryland Safe Haven Program, operate a comprehensive public information campaign (costing $250,000 annually), handle custody and intake via local departments of social services, and submit annual reports to the General Assembly.

State Police barracks are explicitly designated as authorized facilities where individuals may surrender a newborn with civil and criminal immunity, and law enforcement officers are among the personnel to be trained under the program.
The bill mandates the regular distribution of Safe Haven Program informational materials at State and local health department offices.

The bill mandates the regular distribution of Safe Haven Program educational and informational literature across publicly funded educational institutions in Maryland, which fall under MSDE's oversight.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS regulates and coordinates the statewide emergency medical services network; the bill requires newborn safety devices to connect to alert systems requesting immediate EMS dispatch and requires training for EMS providers on Safe Haven protocols.

MDEM oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board, while the bill requires newborn safety devices to interface automatically with the 9-1-1 system to dispatch emergency services and requires training for 9-1-1 operators.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the time period in which the State may recover grant funds under the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program if a facility is sold, transferred, or ceases to operate as a center, establishing a 15-year recovery window for leased properties while maintaining a 30-year recovery window for owned properties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), nonprofit organizations, and county and municipal governments operating or sponsoring health center projects.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount sooner than anticipated due to the shortened recovery period (from 30 years to 15 years) for leased properties. Any operational workload can be handled within existing budgeted resources. There is no direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program, evaluates grant applications, and recommends awards and recovery actions.

The Board of Public Works awards the capital grants under the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Health and approves any transferees of grant-funded properties.
The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in legal proceedings to enforce statutory rights and recover state grant funds, costs, and attorneys' fees.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases various annual, supplementary, and renewal licensing fees for alcoholic beverages in Baltimore City and authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to establish fees for specified per diem and tasting licenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders in Baltimore City, including restaurants, bars, breweries, and event venues.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City licensing and fee revenues are estimated to increase by approximately $823,200 beginning in fiscal year 2025 and annually thereafter due to the fee increases. Baltimore City expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is tasked with regulating the state's alcohol industry. While this legislation specifically alters local alcoholic beverages licensing and renewal fees collected by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates generally to alcohol regulation in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes the Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force to evaluate and recommend models, entities, or strategies for governing the renovation, revitalization, financing, maintenance, and ongoing operations of the Baltimore Convention site and surrounding areas. The task force is required to report its findings and recommendations by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore City hospitality and tourism businesses (hotels, restaurants), convention workers and labor unions, local African American business owners and residents near the Baltimore Convention Center, and visitors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in fiscal year 2025 for the Department of Commerce to hire a consultant with expertise in downtown redevelopment to assist the task force. Travel expense reimbursements for task force members are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Commerce is required to staff the Task Force, the Secretary of Commerce serves as a member, and the agency incurs a fiscal impact of $100,000 in FY 2025 to hire a redevelopment consultant.
The Chair of the Maryland Stadium Authority serves as a member of the Task Force, and MSA has existing statutory financing and operating agreements regarding the Baltimore Convention Center.
The Administrator of the Maryland Transit Administration (or designee) is designated by statute as a member of the Task Force.
The Chair of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (or designee) is designated by statute as a member of the Task Force.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force as an executive advisory body.
The Task Force includes the Chair of the Maryland Tourism Development Board, and the task force's mandate directly relates to the state's tourism and convention development strategy overseen by OTD.
MDOT is the parent agency of the Maryland Transit Administration, whose Administrator is a statutorily appointed member of the Task Force.
The Task Force is required to report its findings and recommendations regarding convention and tourism redevelopment to the Governor by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes researchers affiliated with institutions of higher education conducting academic or policy research to access and review confidential court records related to extreme risk protective order petitions, subject to an agreement with the Maryland Judiciary regarding record storage, custody, and confidentiality.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Academic and policy researchers affiliated with institutions of higher education, petitioners and respondents of extreme risk protective orders, and court personnel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Judiciary with requiring institutions of higher education to enter into agreements governing the storage, handling, and confidentiality of extreme risk protective order court records before researchers can access them, and authorizes the Judiciary to seek injunctions for violations.

Academic and policy researchers affiliated with constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland are authorized to access confidential extreme risk protective order court records, subject to entering into formal compliance agreements with the Maryland Judiciary.

Researchers affiliated with Morgan State University conducting related academic or policy research are granted access to confidential extreme risk protective order records under required data handling and confidentiality agreements.

As a public institution of higher education, researchers affiliated with the college may access confidential court records related to extreme risk protective orders for academic or policy research upon entering into the required agreement.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands statewide the authority of local jurisdictions and transit agencies (including the Maryland Transit Administration and the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority) to use automated bus lane monitoring systems to enforce prohibitions against driving, stopping, standing, or parking an unauthorized motor vehicle in a dedicated bus lane. It establishes a maximum civil penalty of $75 for violations, sets operational, signage, and video/image retention standards for the monitoring systems, and creates the Workgroup on Curb Space Management.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists, public transit riders, local governments, law enforcement and parking enforcement agencies, and transit agencies including MTA and WMATA.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $17,298 in FY 2025 only for District Court reprogramming. State general fund revenues increase minimally from contested citations, and Transportation Trust Fund revenues may increase minimally from $30 vehicle registration flagging fees. Local government revenues may increase significantly from the $75 civil citations, which local jurisdictions can retain to recover monitoring system implementation and administration costs, with any excess dedicated to public safety.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is required to provide staff for the newly created Workgroup on Curb Space Management. Additionally, MDOT's modal administrations (MTA and MVA) are directly involved in implementing the bus lane monitoring systems and registration flagging provisions.

MTA is specifically authorized as an agency that may utilize bus lane monitoring systems on its transit routes and bus stops, and is statutorily designated to have a representative appointed to the Workgroup on Curb Space Management.

The District Court of Maryland adjudicates contested citations, coordinates with enforcement agencies, and must establish uniform citation procedures and forms. The fiscal note indicates an expenditure increase of $17,298 for computer reprogramming.

The MVA is authorized to refuse the registration or reregistration of vehicles for unpaid, uncontested bus lane monitoring citations, resulting in administrative flagging processes and potential TTF fee revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on Curb Space Management to study curb regulations, obstruction enforcement, privacy concerns, and public education campaigns.
The Governor appoints members to the Workgroup on Curb Space Management, designates its chair, and receives the workgroup's final report by July 1, 2025.
As a statewide law enforcement agency authorized to enforce vehicle laws, MSP falls under the bill's expanded definition of enforcement agencies and was consulted on the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes new operating standards and prohibitions for assisted living referrers in Maryland. Among other provisions, referrers must maintain general liability insurance, require criminal history records checks for employees, provide clients with a written service description and any financial agreements, and adhere to strict client data and medical record privacy protections. The bill also prohibits referrers from requesting referral fees from assisted living programs more than two years after making a referral and directs the Office of Health Care Quality to maintain a user-friendly database of licensed assisted living programs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Health Care Quality (Maryland Department of Health)
qa_results.stakeholders: Assisted living referrers, licensed assisted living programs and facilities, and individuals (and their families or representatives) seeking assisted living placement.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not expected to change, as the Office of Health Care Quality can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local government fiscal impact. Small business impacts are expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), a regulatory agency within the Maryland Department of Health, with registering assisted living referrers and maintaining a user-friendly database of licensed assisted living programs.
The statute explicitly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to investigate potential violations by assisted living referrers and seek appropriate legal relief.

The bill regulates referral services for assisted living facilities, which directly impacts the housing, long-term care, and consumer protections for older Marylanders overseen and advocated for by the Department of Aging.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Climate Technology Founder's Fund within the Maryland Clean Energy Center to provide early-stage funding and equity investments for start-up companies working on qualified climate technology projects, prioritizing small, minority-, women-, and veteran-owned clean energy businesses. It also mandates an annual transfer of funds from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to the new fund from fiscal years 2025 through 2028 while repealing prior mandated distributions to certain other accounts.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Clean Energy Center
qa_results.stakeholders: Climate technology start-up businesses, small, minority-, women-, and veteran-owned clean energy companies, the Maryland Energy Innovation Institute, and minority-serving institutions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) increase by $1.2 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028. Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the Climate Technology Founder's Fund (CTFF) increase correspondingly by $1.2 million annually as funds are received and disbursed for investments, grants, and administrative costs, with additional nonbudgeted revenue possible from future investment returns. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Energy Innovation Fund may also increase. The bill repeals prior SEIF distributions to the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account and the EARN program. There is no local government fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MCEC is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, administering, and managing the Climate Technology Founder's Fund and appointing the Fund Oversight Committee.

MEA administers the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is mandated under the bill to transfer $1.2 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028 to the Climate Technology Founder's Fund, while repealing previous SEIF allocations.

The Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account (SMWOBA) resides under Commerce; the bill repeals SEIF distributions to SMWOBA and authorizes the transfer of up to $2.2 million in SEIF-attributed SMWOBA funds to the new fund.
The bill repeals an existing $8.0 million distribution from SEIF dedicated to clean energy workforce development programs under the department's EARN program.

The Maryland Energy Innovation Institute (MEII) at the University of Maryland, College Park is allocated up to $2.0 million from the fund for seed grants, with a requirement that 40% support start-ups from minority-serving institutions.
The Governor is granted discretionary authority to transfer up to $2.2 million from SMWOBA to the new fund before June 30, 2024, and receives an annual report from MCEC on the fund's outcomes.
The bill amends State Finance and Procurement § 6-226 to exempt the Climate Technology Founder's Fund from general fund interest sweeps, allowing it to retain its own interest earnings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires holders of Class B or Class D alcoholic beverages licenses in Carroll County, or a designated supervisory employee, to be certified in an approved alcohol awareness program and present on the premises during hours when alcohol may be sold. The bill also establishes fines and penalties for noncompliance and requires at least one license holder listed on the license to maintain certification.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages license holders, supervisory employees, and businesses operating in Carroll County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not affected. Carroll County can handle any additional enforcement activity using existing resources, and local revenues are not materially affected. Small businesses may incur minimal costs to pay for employee alcohol awareness training.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article regarding alcohol awareness training requirements for certain retail licensees in Carroll County. While implementation and enforcement are handled locally by the Carroll County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller regulates the alcoholic beverages industry at the state level.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters prior authorizations of Maryland State debt across several previous capital budgets (2019 through 2023). It updates grantee names, modifies the allowable scope and purposes of specific capital grants, reallocates grant funds among certain projects, removes matching fund requirements, and extends termination deadlines for encumbering or expending funds.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, community associations receiving state capital grants, and local communities benefiting from the funded infrastructure and recreation projects.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, as the bill only modifies the conditions, timelines, purposes, and recipients of previously authorized State debt without altering overall net debt authorizations. Local fiscal impact is limited to local governments that serve as grant recipients, affecting project timelines, allowable uses, or matching requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends prior capital budget authorizations under DNR's Capital Grants and Loans Administration (Local Parks and Playgrounds Infrastructure), altering eligible uses and local allocations.
The bill explicitly names the Maryland Stadium Authority as the new grantee for multiple prior authorizations related to the Fort to 400 Commission Phase 2 design and archaeological analysis.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves state debt expenditures, capital grant agreements, and the certification of required matching funds modified by this legislation.
DGS administers state capital grant programs and manages the execution of capital grants on behalf of the Board of Public Works.
The bill amends prior authorizations that previously designated the Historic St. Mary's City Fort to 400 Commission as the grantee, transferring that role to the Maryland Stadium Authority.
DBM is responsible for state capital budget development and monitoring authorizations of state debt.

The bill modifies grant requirements involving the Maryland Historical Trust (a unit of MDP), specifically waiving the requirement for the grantee to convey a perpetual easement for the Johnston Square project.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill codifies the Private Hospital Grant Program to make recommendations for State funding for capital projects at private hospitals. It requires the Maryland Hospital Association to establish a review committee—in consultation with the Department of Budget and Management and the Department of Legislative Services—to establish criteria, evaluate funding requests, and recommend projects to the Governor and the Secretary of Budget and Management. Beginning in fiscal year 2026, the Governor is authorized to include an annual appropriation of up to $20.0 million in the capital or operating budget bill for the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Private hospitals in Maryland and the patients and communities they serve.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect in FY 2025. Beginning in FY 2026, if the Governor exercises discretionary authority to appropriate $20.0 million for the program via the capital budget, general obligation (GO) bond expenditures for the program may increase by $12.0 million annually above baseline plans ($8.0 million is already included annually in the Capital Improvement Program). However, total capital budget spending remains unaffected because funds would be redirected from other capital projects. DBM and DLS can provide committee consultation with existing resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is directly assigned statutory duties to consult with the Maryland Hospital Association's review committee on establishing the funding request process, evaluating funding recommendations, and establishing conditions under which funding requests may be rejected. In addition, the Secretary of Budget and Management directly receives the committee's final recommendations.

The bill provides that final funding recommendations are submitted to the Governor and authorizes the Governor to include a discretionary appropriation of up to $20,000,000 in the annual capital or operating budget bill starting in fiscal year 2026.

The bill amends the Health - General Article regarding capital funding for private hospitals, a sector regulated and licensed under MDH's jurisdiction, and MDH contributed fiscal and policy analysis on the measure.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Reproductive Health Care Clinic Security Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health to provide financial assistance to reproductive health care clinics for security improvements and facility hardening. The bill also establishes confidentiality protections for grant applicants and recipients and authorizes discretionary funding for the program in fiscal year 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Reproductive health care clinics, clinic staff, and patients receiving reproductive health care services in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $28,732 in FY 2025 for part-time contractual staffing to establish program procedures and by $500,000 in FY 2026, which represents discretionary grant funding and administrative expenses (capped at 5%). No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Reproductive Health Care Clinic Security Grant Program directly within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and requires the Secretary of Health to administer the program, establish application procedures and award criteria, and maintain confidentiality of applicant/grantee data.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include a discretionary appropriation of $500,000 for the program in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2026.

DBM oversees the state budget development and personnel allocations, which includes the handling of the discretionary $500,000 fiscal 2026 appropriation and contractual staffing associated with implementing the grant program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP was the originally designated administering agency in the bill before it was amended to assign administration to MDH, and GOCPP provided information for the bill's fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill centralizes the oversight of state information technology (IT) within the Department of Information Technology (DoIT), renames the Major Information Technology Development Project Fund to the Information Technology Investment Fund, and raises the minimum cost threshold for major IT development projects from $1 million to $5 million. It creates an 'expedited project' category for modernization efforts, requiring at least 20% of the fund to be set aside for such projects annually, alters the duties and membership of the Modernize Maryland Commission, mandates comprehensive legacy system inventories and modernization plans, and requires the addition of two new staff positions at DoIT starting in fiscal year 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland state government agencies, IT vendors and contractors (including small and minority business enterprises), state government workforce, and Maryland residents utilizing state public services and digital systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by approximately $2.1 million in FY 2025 across general and special funds, reflecting $133,705 in salary and start-up costs for two new positions, $1.0 million for a consultant study on the IT procurement process by the Department of General Services, and $1.0 million (from the Dedicated Purpose Account) for DoIT to assess state legacy systems. Out-year expenditures range from roughly $200,000 to $400,000 annually, accounting for ongoing staff salaries and $200,000 biennial consultant costs beginning in FY 2026 to assist with legacy system reporting. The bill also establishes a mandated appropriation beginning in FY 2026 to fund two DoIT positions. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which establishes centralized IT oversight, renames and expands the Major Information Technology Development Project Fund to the Information Technology Investment Fund, creates a pathway for expedited projects, mandates the development of a State Modernization Plan, provides staffing for the Modernize Maryland Commission, and creates two new positions within the department.

DGS is explicitly required, in consultation with DoIT, to hire a consultant to assess the procurement process for IT modernization projects, resulting in an estimated $1.0 million fiscal impact in FY 2025.
The bill mandates that contracts to modernize IT systems or execute expedited projects must be expedited for approval and placed on the Board of Public Works agenda as soon as practicable.

The Secretary of Budget and Management advises on the approval of major IT projects and expenditures, and receives recommendations from the Secretary of Information Technology to withhold project funds when agencies fail to report properly or encounter significant implementation issues.

The Comptroller accounts for the Information Technology Investment Fund and must be consulted by DoIT regarding specific recommendations to transition State agencies off the Annapolis Data Center mainframes consistent with the Comptroller's 2029 sunset goal.
The State Treasurer's Office is statutorily designated to hold the Information Technology Investment Fund separately and manage the investment and reinvestment of its money.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill renames, restructures membership, and redefines the purpose and reporting duties of the Modernize Maryland Commission to focus on best practices for legacy system modernization.

The Governor is required to include annual budget set-asides and mandated positions for DoIT, receives required strategic plans and modernization reports, and appoints several members of the Modernize Maryland Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Language Assistance Services Pilot Program within the Behavioral Health Administration to provide grants to local behavioral health authorities to reimburse licensed and accredited behavioral health providers for language assistance services (such as interpretation and translation) provided to children with limited English proficiency and their parents or legal guardians.
qa_results.responsible_party: Behavioral Health Administration (Maryland Department of Health)
qa_results.stakeholders: Children with limited English proficiency receiving behavioral health care, parents and legal guardians coordinating behavioral health services for their children, local behavioral health authorities, and licensed and accredited behavioral health providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $201,100 in FY 2025 (reflecting discretionary grant funding of $120,000 and administrative/personnel costs), $190,800 in FY 2026 (including a $120,000 mandated appropriation), and $36,900 in FY 2027 for remaining administrative costs. State revenues are unaffected. Local behavioral health authorities receive increased grant revenues and experience corresponding expenditures to reimburse eligible providers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Language Assistance Services Pilot Program within the Behavioral Health Administration (BHA), an administration within the Maryland Department of Health. MDH/BHA is the primary entity responsible for administering the program, adopting regulations, awarding grants to local behavioral health authorities, and submitting annual implementation reports.

The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific appropriation of $120,000 in the annual state budget bill for fiscal years 2025 and 2026, and requires annual reporting on program implementation to be submitted to the Governor.

As the agency responsible for preparing and executing the state budget, DBM is impacted by the bill's statutory mandated general fund appropriation of $120,000 in FY 2026 and associated administrative expenditure increases.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the procedures and deadlines for gubernatorial nominations and executive appointments requiring Senate confirmation. It requires the Governor to submit nominations within 40 days of the start of the regular legislative session if an office term ends during the upcoming recess, establishes conditions for late submissions and Senate consent, caps an officer's holdover service at four years after their term ends, and permits recess appointments to the State Board of Elections and the Accountability and Implementation Board regardless of term expiration timing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Gubernatorial appointees and nominees requiring Senate confirmation, members of state boards and commissions (such as the State Board of Elections and the Accountability and Implementation Board), the Governor's Office, and the Maryland Senate.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. While the bill clarifies existing constitutional and statutory appointment provisions with no formal state fiscal impact, operational compliance by the Governor's Office may require at least two positions and a new tracking system estimated by the Department of Legislative Services at an initial cost of $270,745 in fiscal year 2025. Local finances and small businesses are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly regulates the Governor's constitutional and statutory appointment powers, establishing strict deadlines for submitting nominations requiring Senate confirmation, limiting terms for acting officials and holdover officers, and creating a notable operational impact and potential staffing/IT need identified in the fiscal note.

Operating within the Executive Department, this office recruits, vets, and manages nominations for Senate-confirmable positions across state government; the fiscal note explicitly details the operational burden and need for additional staff and a new tracking system to comply with the bill's 40-day deadline.

The bill explicitly provides an exception and specific authorization allowing the Governor to appoint members to the State Board of Elections during a Senate recess regardless of whether the member's term ends during that upcoming recess.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes rules directly governing the composition, terms, and quorum/voting validity of public bodies and boards whose members require Senate confirmation, including capping post-term service at four years and invalidating votes cast by prohibited appointees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires alcoholic beverages retailers in Baltimore County to obtain written approval from the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners prior to applying to the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission for an individual storage permit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners and the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages retailers in Baltimore County seeking an individual storage permit
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Baltimore County can implement the requirement using existing resources, with no impact on county revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill relates to regulatory requirements for alcoholic beverage individual storage permits. While the permit application is submitted to the Executive Director of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, the Comptroller oversees alcohol industry regulation and related excise tax enforcement according to its agency purview, though this local procedural change carries no state fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Senate Bill 1014 requires State procurement units to submit an annual procurement forecast for contracts over $100,000 and a reconciliation of the prior year's forecast to the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (GOSBA). It also directs GOSBA to consult with primary procurement units to identify contracting opportunities, expand outreach, and provide technical assistance to small businesses navigating the bidding process.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Small businesses in Maryland seeking State contract opportunities and State procurement units.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $77,900 in FY 2025, which reflects the cost of creating a new compliance officer/administrator position in GOSBA, with out-year expenditures rising to $105,500 by FY 2029. State procurement units can meet the reporting requirements with existing resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is required to consult with primary procurement units to develop an outreach and assistance program for small businesses, receive and reconcile annual procurement forecasts from all state units, publish this data on its website, and receive a new staff position (compliance officer) funded by general funds.

As one of Maryland's designated primary procurement units, DGS must consult directly with GOSBA to identify contracting opportunities, expand small business outreach, develop support programs, and report its annual procurement forecasts and reconciliations.

As a designated primary procurement unit, MDOT is required to collaborate and consult with GOSBA on small business procurement programs and outreach, as well as submit procurement forecasts and reconciliations.

The State Treasurer is designated in statute as a primary procurement unit and must consult with GOSBA to identify opportunities and develop small business procurement programs, along with submitting annual procurement forecasts.

USM is a statutory primary procurement unit required to consult with GOSBA to identify small business opportunities and develop procurement assistance programs, while also submitting annual procurement forecasts and reconciliations.
As an independent primary procurement unit, Morgan State University must consult with GOSBA on small business opportunities and programs and submit annual procurement forecasts and reconciliations.
As an independent primary procurement unit, St. Mary's College of Maryland is required to consult with GOSBA on small business contracting initiatives and submit annual procurement forecasts.

The Maryland Port Administration (via the Maryland Port Commission) is designated as a primary procurement unit subject to consultation requirements with GOSBA regarding small business procurement and reporting forecasts.
The Board of Public Works oversees state procurement authority and the primary procurement units that are required to implement and report under this legislation.
GOSBA is an administrative unit within the Executive Department (Governor's Office), and the bill establishes a new state position (PIN) within this office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Circuit Administrative Judge of the Sixth Circuit to establish a Truancy Reduction Pilot Program in the juvenile court in Frederick County to address chronic school absenteeism through court-ordered interventions and support services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Circuit Administrative Judge of the Sixth Circuit
qa_results.stakeholders: Truant juveniles and students in Frederick County, parents and guardians, Frederick County Public Schools, the Frederick County Juvenile Court, and the Office of the Public Defender.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase by $155,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 to provide standard reimbursable grant funding through the Office of Problem-Solving Courts. Local grant revenues and expenditures for Frederick County increase correspondingly by $155,000 annually. The Office of the Public Defender may experience increased operational workload, and revenues are otherwise unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judicial Branch by authorizing the establishment of a Truancy Reduction Pilot Program in the juvenile court in Frederick County, requiring an estimated $155,000 in annual general fund grant expenditures through the Judiciary's Office of Problem-Solving Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an operational impact on the Office of the Public Defender, as truancy reduction programs generate additional juvenile cases and adult criminal charges against parents requiring indigent legal defense.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes direct delivery permits for licensed Maryland breweries, wineries, and distilleries to deliver their own alcoholic beverages directly to adult consumers in the State, subject to specified delivery limits and age verification rules. The bill also repeals off-premises purchasing limits for consumers visiting Class 1 distilleries and Class 5 breweries, establishes annual reporting requirements for manufacturers, and directs the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission to evaluate a digital age verification system.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland breweries, wineries, distilleries, alcoholic beverage consumers, and retail alcohol manufacturers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by at least $8,400 annually beginning in fiscal year 2025 from initial $200 permit application and annual renewal fees, assuming at least 42 eligible manufacturers obtain permits. The Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission can handle monitoring, enforcement, and the required digital age verification evaluation using existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires holders of direct wine, beer, and liquor delivery permits to file quarterly tax returns with and pay sales and excise taxes directly to the Comptroller of Maryland. It also requires permittees to provide copies of their permits to the Comptroller and authorizes the Comptroller to audit their records for compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Tobacco Retail Modernization Act of 2024 requires retailers to store cigarettes, other tobacco products, and electronic smoking devices behind counters accessible only to employees, and mandates direct face-to-face age verification with government-issued photo ID for buyers under 30 years old. It increases retail license fees for cigarettes, electronic smoking devices, and vape shop vendors to $300 to fund enforcement, repeals sales exceptions for active-duty military members under age 21, mandates at least one annual unannounced inspection of retailers by the Maryland Department of Health or its designees, increases criminal fines and license suspension penalties for sales to minors, and requires a study on retailer density and underage tobacco use.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Tobacco and electronic smoking device retailers, vape shop vendors, adult consumers under age 30, active-duty military personnel under age 21, and local health departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $1.2 million in FY 2025 and $1.6 million annually thereafter due to increased license fees dedicated to enforcement, primarily distributed as grants to local health departments. General fund expenditures increase by $44,800 in FY 2025 for Judiciary IT updates, while general fund revenues increase by $24,000 in FY 2025 and $32,000 annually from higher fines. Local revenues increase via MDH grants for local health departments and increased fee distributions in Montgomery County ($82,688 in FY 2025 and $110,250 annually), offset by inspection operational costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is a primary implementing agency under the bill. It is mandated to conduct annual unannounced inspections of tobacco and electronic smoking device retailers, receives $275 of each $300 license fee collected across most counties (generating roughly $1.2 million to $1.6 million in special funds annually to fund operations and local health department grants), enforces civil citations, and participates in a required study and report.

The District Court adjudicates contested civil citations and criminal violations under the bill. Courts are mandated to order license suspensions or revocations upon certain repeat convictions and transmit final orders to the regulatory commission. The fiscal note indicates a direct expenditure impact of $44,761 in FY 2025 for computer programming updates.

The Comptroller is explicitly required to coordinate with the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, MDH, and MSDE to submit a comprehensive report by October 1, 2025, regarding retailer licensing, geographic density, and the public health and economic impacts of youth tobacco and electronic smoking device use.

MSDE is explicitly tasked with collaborating on a mandated study and report due October 1, 2025, focusing on tobacco and vape retailer density, proximity of retail locations to schools, and the prevalence and impact of tobacco use among minors.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expresses the intent of the General Assembly that the Department of Information Technology evaluate the feasibility of using artificial intelligence to create a statewide virtual 3-1-1 portal for Maryland residents to access nonemergency government information and services, and prioritize the creation of the portal if found to be feasible.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents seeking nonemergency government services and information, as well as state and local government agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Information Technology can perform the required evaluation using existing resources. General fund expenditures may increase if DoIT implements a statewide virtual 3-1-1 portal, but any potential implementation costs cannot be reliably estimated at this time. State revenues are unaffected. There is no direct fiscal impact on local governments, though operations and finances could be affected if a portal is ultimately deployed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly directs the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) to evaluate the feasibility of utilizing artificial intelligence to create a statewide virtual 3-1-1 portal for nonemergency government information and services, and to prioritize the creation of the portal if determined feasible.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill authorizes local school systems in Maryland to use grant funding from the Safe Schools Fund to employ school security employees, expanding the authorized uses of the fund beyond school resource officers and law enforcement coverage.
qa_results.responsible_party: School Safety Subcabinet and Maryland Center for School Safety
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public schools, local school systems, school security employees, and public school students and staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State or local fiscal impact. Expanding the permissible uses of the Safe Schools Fund to include school security employees does not alter total revenues for or expenditures from the fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) provides staff to the School Safety Subcabinet, which administers the Safe Schools Fund. The bill directly impacts the administration of the fund by expanding the authorized uses of these school safety grants to include school security employees.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) houses the Center for School Safety, and the State Superintendent of Schools chairs the School Safety Subcabinet responsible for administering the Safe Schools Fund grants to local school systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Senate Bill 1092 increases the annual motor vehicle registration emergency medical system surcharge from $17.00 to $40.00 and alters its distribution among the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund (MTPSF), the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund (MEMSOF), and the R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center. It expands MTPSF purposes, eligibility, and reimbursement rates, increases maximum fines for certain impaired driving offenses (directing at least 20% of collections to MTPSF), and mandates an annual appropriation of at least $16.5 million for the Senator William H. Amoss Fire, Rescue, and Ambulance Fund beginning in fiscal year 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission, Health Services Cost Review Commission, Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration, and Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered motor vehicle owners in Maryland, trauma centers, trauma physicians and healthcare practitioners, pediatric trauma hospitals, local fire, rescue, and ambulance departments, and individuals convicted of impaired driving offenses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2025, special fund revenues increase by $104,781,905 annually from the $23 vehicle registration surcharge increase, distributed to MEMSOF (up to $45.6 million), Shock Trauma (at least $41.0 million), and MTPSF ($18.2 million). Special fund expenditures increase by $3.41 million in FY 2025 and $4.91 million annually thereafter due to credit card processing costs covered by the Transportation Trust Fund ($2.2 million annually), mandated pediatric grants ($1.2 million annually), and an increased mandated appropriation to the Amoss Fund ($1.5 million annually beginning in FY 2026). General fund and local fine revenues will experience minimal net decreases as at least 20% of impaired driving fine revenues are redirected to MTPSF.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHCC, jointly with the Health Services Cost Review Commission, administers the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund, adopts regulations, establishes reimbursement methodologies and grant application processes, and submits annual reports to the General Assembly.

HSCRC jointly administers the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund with MHCC, participates in developing payment methodologies, accounts for hospital trauma costs in global budgets, and co-authors required annual reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS is a primary beneficiary of the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund, designates state trauma centers, maintains the State trauma registry, and consults on trauma center grant guidelines.
MVA is responsible for collecting the emergency medical services surcharge on motor vehicle registrations, which is increased from $17 to $40 per vehicle per year under the bill.

MDOT oversees the MVA and will incur approximately $2.2 million annually in Transportation Trust Fund expenditures to cover credit card processing fees resulting from the increased registration surcharge.

The Comptroller is statutorily responsible for administering the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund, including accounting for transactions, receiving surcharge balances, and performing year-end reconciliations.
MDEM administers the Senator William H. Amoss Fire, Rescue, and Ambulance Fund, which receives a mandated annual appropriation of at least $16.5 million beginning in fiscal year 2026 under the bill.
MDH receives fund transfers from the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund to cover the State's share of Medicaid undercompensated trauma care expenditures.
Medically oriented aviation functions of the Maryland State Police Aviation Command are funded through MEMSOF, which receives a substantial revenue increase under the altered surcharge distribution.

AOC supports the District and Circuit Courts, which adjudicate driving while impaired offenses with increased fine maximums and must distribute at least 20% of collections to MTPSF; AOC also incurs minor IT programming costs.

The bill requires the Governor to annually allocate at least $9.00 of the surcharge to the R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center and mandate at least $16.5 million for the Amoss Fund in the annual budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2026.
DBM oversees the preparation and execution of the State budget, including the implementation of the mandated $16.5 million annual appropriation to the Amoss Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring to study and make recommendations regarding the costs and availability of both publicly and privately provided pretrial home detention monitoring systems. The workgroup is required to submit an annual report of its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 31 each year until it sunsets.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Pretrial defendants subject to home detention monitoring, private home detention monitoring agencies, local detention centers, county pretrial release programs, and criminal justice system agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are assumed to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources for Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services staffing and workgroup member expense reimbursements. State revenues are unaffected, and local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services (or a designee) serves as a member of the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring, and the department is explicitly tasked with providing staff for the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring as a temporary advisory body tasked with studying pretrial home detention monitoring systems and reporting recommendations to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender of Maryland, or the Public Defender's designee, is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring.
The bill designates a representative of the Judiciary, appointed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland, to serve as a member of the workgroup.
The Governor is responsible for appointing multiple stakeholder members to the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to the newly established workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits an incarcerated individual serving a sentence for first-degree rape from earning diminution credits to reduce their term of confinement in a State or local correctional facility for offenses committed on or after October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals convicted of first-degree rape committed on or after October 1, 2024, victims of crime, and State and local correctional facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State finances in the near term (first five years). In future years, State general fund incarceration expenditures will increase, potentially significantly, as offenders serve longer sentences. For illustrative purposes, State variable incarceration costs increase by approximately $20,160 for each individual serving an additional five years. Local finances and State revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) by prohibiting the awarding of diminution credits to incarcerated individuals serving sentences for first-degree rape committed on or after October 1, 2024. This directly alters sentence calculation administration and increases incarceration terms and associated expenditures for the Division of Correction over time.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Emergency Medical Services Board, in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Health, to develop and implement an initiative under the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator (AED) Program to co-locate up to two doses of naloxone with each AED placed in public buildings by October 1, 2027. It provides civil liability immunity for owners/operators of public buildings and individuals who administer naloxone during an emergency, and authorizes funding for the initiative from the Opioid Restitution Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Emergency Medical Services Board (EMS Board) / Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS), in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals experiencing or at risk of opioid overdoses in public spaces, administrators and owners/operators of public buildings (public transit facilities, public parks/recreation centers, and secondary/higher education facilities), and bystanders administering emergency naloxone.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) increase by at least $74,108 in FY 2025 (rising to $99,900 by FY 2029) to hire one full-time program manager. ORF expenditures will also increase by additional indeterminate amounts to update IT systems and supply naloxone and packaging materials ($70 per AED site initially, plus $45 per replacement kit every three years or as used). State and local operational impacts for inspections are expected to be absorbable within existing resources, and revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Emergency Medical Services Board, which is administered through MIEMSS, with developing, implementing, and adopting regulations for the initiative to co-locate naloxone with automated external defibrillators (AEDs) in public buildings, resulting in direct operational and fiscal impacts.

The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to collaborate with the EMS Board to develop and implement the co-location initiative, jointly adopt regulations, and utilize the Opioid Restitution Fund to finance the program.

The bill applies AED and naloxone co-location requirements to public buildings, explicitly defining them to include public mass transportation accommodations such as stations and terminals supported by public funds.

As the operator of transit stations, terminals, and rail facilities across the state, MTA facilities qualify as public mass transportation accommodations required to comply with the AED and naloxone co-location initiative.
The bill includes public secondary education facilities in its definition of public buildings required to co-locate naloxone with AEDs, impacting public schools under MSDE's oversight.

The bill's definition of public buildings includes improvements of public areas used for gathering or amusement such as public parks and recreation centers, impacting DNR-managed public park facilities.

Facilities primarily used to provide higher education supported by public funds are defined as public buildings under the bill, requiring USM member institutions with AEDs to comply with naloxone co-location mandates.
As a publicly funded higher education institution, Morgan State University's campus facilities fall under the definition of public buildings required to co-locate naloxone with AEDs.
As an independent public higher education institution, Saint Mary's College's facilities are classified as public buildings subject to the AED and naloxone co-location requirements.
As a state-operated public school facility providing secondary education, MSD's campuses are subject to the co-location requirements for public buildings.
The bill references protocols established by the Maryland State Police Medical Director regarding civil liability immunity for individuals administering medications in response to a drug overdose.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program by altering the definition of an eligible institution to include community colleges in Maryland, allowing students and currently employed police officers and probation agents attending community colleges to receive tuition assistance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Community college students intending to become police officers or probation agents, current police officers and probation agents seeking degrees, and Maryland community colleges.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State spending does not increase because the expansion can be absorbed within the existing $5.0 million annual general fund appropriation for the program. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can make necessary administrative updates using existing resources. State revenues and local community college revenues and expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC (through its Office of Student Financial Assistance) administers the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program and must update program regulations, eligibility guidelines, and award administration to include community colleges as eligible institutions.

MHEC administers the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program and is directly responsible for incorporating Maryland community colleges into the list of eligible institutions for award recipients.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs the state's probation agents within the Division of Parole and Probation. Expanding scholarship eligibility to community colleges affects continuing education and recruitment pathways for probation personnel.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP employs police officers who may benefit from tuition assistance at community colleges under the expanded scholarship eligibility.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the required contents of written notices provided to patients regarding hospital outpatient facility fees and modifies related definitions to include certain out-of-state hospital facilities. It also requires the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) to study hospital outpatient facility fees, convene a workgroup to examine expanding facility fee notice requirements, and submit preliminary and final reports with recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024, and December 1, 2025, respectively.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC)
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients receiving outpatient medical services, Maryland and out-of-state hospitals operating outpatient facilities in Maryland, physicians and nonphysician clinicians, health insurers and payers, and employers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Health Services Cost Review Commission increase by $75,000 in FY 2025 and $75,000 in FY 2026 (a total of $150,000) for contractual services needed to conduct the required study and prepare reports. The Maryland Department of Health, Maryland Insurance Administration, and the Health Education and Advocacy Unit can participate using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HSCRC is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. It is mandated to conduct a comprehensive study on hospital outpatient facility fees, convene a stakeholder workgroup, receive annual lists of rate-regulated outpatient services, investigate complaints, and submit multiple reports to legislative committees.

The bill was requested by the Office of the Attorney General. Its Health Education and Advocacy Unit (HEAU) is designated on required patient disclosure notices as the mediation and assistance contact for facility fee complaints, receives annual lists of hospital-based rate-regulated outpatient services, and is required to participate in the study consultation and the workgroup.

HSCRC is an independent commission housed within MDH. MDH is directly required by the bill to be consulted on the facility fee study and to participate in the workgroup advising on expanding notice requirements.

MIA receives annual lists of rate-regulated hospital outpatient services from HSCRC and is named as a required consulting entity for HSCRC's study and recommendations on outpatient facility fees and billing mechanisms.

qa_results.bill_summary: An annual corrective bill that corrects various technical errors, omissions, and obsolete cross-references in the Annotated Code of Maryland, clarifies statutory language, and reorganizes sections without making substantive changes to existing law.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services and the publishers of the Annotated Code of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: The Maryland judiciary, legal practitioners, state and local government agencies, and the general public accessing the Annotated Code of Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is technical in nature and has no state or local fiscal impact, nor does it affect small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes technical corrections to the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding terminology for justices of the Supreme Court of Maryland and judges of the Appellate Court, judicial salaries, and competency hearing terminology.
The bill includes technical corrections touching the Comptroller's accounting of the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund and cost certifications under the Natural Resources Article.
The bill corrects cross-references and formatting errors in the Education Article relating to county superintendent search committees, school funding calculations, and school construction aid.
The bill updates obsolete cross-references in the Labor and Employment Article regarding state minimum wage rates and civil actions by the Uninsured Employers' Fund.

The bill clarifies terminology and statutory phrasing related to the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays 2010 Trust Fund, the Youghiogheny Scenic and Wild River Local Advisory Board, and recreational licensing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill corrects terminology and cross-references regarding the Patuxent Institution Board of Review parole hearings, inmate identification card issuance, and Criminal Justice Information System data reviews.
The bill updates statutory references reflecting the administrative merger creating the Water and Science Administration and corrects cross-references regarding used tire recycling studies.
The bill updates statutory cross-references in the Transportation and Criminal Procedure Articles regarding ignition interlock systems and vehicle registration fee exemptions for disabled veterans.
The bill corrects an obsolete cross-reference in the Insurance Article regarding motor vehicle liability insurance coverage requirements for registered family child care providers.
The bill corrects a structural tabulation error in Public Safety § 5-310 regarding the Secretary's revocation of handgun permits and review of active permit holders.

The bill corrects terminology regarding the State Treasurer's delegation of fiduciary duties under higher education investment plans and statutory duties regarding the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund.
The bill updates statutory references concerning identification card standards for individuals released from correctional facilities and fee exemptions for disabled veterans.
The bill amends an obsolete statutory title reference in State Government § 2-1220 regarding OLA performance audits of local alcoholic beverage and cannabis licensing boards.
The bill corrects cross-references and word usage in the Public Utilities Article regarding generating station exemptions and offshore wind renewable energy credit (OREC) pricing schedules.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires commercial fish dealers and packers, commercial fishers, and individuals holding recreational fishing licenses to submit any required fishery reports in accordance with regulations adopted by the Department of Natural Resources, rather than specifically on paper forms prescribed by the department.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial fish packers and dealers, licensed commercial fishers, and licensed recreational anglers fishing in Maryland nontidal and tidal waters.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not directly affected. The Department of Natural Resources can make existing electronic reporting options available at no additional cost, and there are no immediate plans for costly expansions such as new mobile application development.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies reporting requirements under the Natural Resources Article, authorizing and directing the Department of Natural Resources to adopt regulations governing reporting by licensed commercial fishers, packers, dealers, and recreational anglers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the University System of Maryland to issue up to $30 million in academic facilities bonds to finance and refinance capital improvement and facility renewal projects, including $5 million for campuswide infrastructure at the University of Maryland, College Park and $25 million for systemwide renewal projects.
qa_results.responsible_party: University System of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: University System of Maryland constituent institutions, students, faculty, and staff.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Revenues and capital expenditures from bond proceeds increase by $30.0 million in FY 2025. Higher education expenditures increase by approximately $2.5 million annually beginning in FY 2026 for 20 years to pay debt service on the revenue bonds. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 1120 directly authorizes the University System of Maryland (USM) to issue, sell, and deliver $30.0 million in academic facilities revenue bonds to finance campus infrastructure improvements at UMCP and systemwide facility renewal projects, resulting in an estimated $30.0 million in revenues/expenditures in FY 2025 and ongoing debt service obligations of approximately $2.5 million annually.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill permanently establishes and increases an annual distribution of $500,000 from the State's Unclaimed Property Fund to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund starting in fiscal year 2025. It also increases the annual mandated State budget appropriation for the CASH Campaign of Maryland from $500,000 to $800,000 beginning in fiscal year 2026, requiring at least $150,000 of that appropriation to fund grants for mobile or on-demand tax clinics serving seniors, rural areas, or under-resourced communities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland residents, senior citizens, rural and under-resourced populations, new American populations, the CASH Campaign of Maryland, the University of Maryland School of Law, the University of Baltimore School of Law, and the Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2025, State general fund revenues decrease by $500,000 annually due to the diversion of unclaimed property funds to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund (TCLIM); TCLIM special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $500,000 annually, with $333,300 going to higher education law clinics. Beginning in FY 2026, State general fund expenditures increase by $300,000 annually to raise the CASH Campaign mandated appropriation to $800,000. There is no local fiscal impact.
