agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller administers and accounts for the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund and is responsible for distributing $500,000 annually from unclaimed property funds to this special fund.

Two of the three designated grant recipients from the fund are the University of Maryland School of Law and the University of Baltimore School of Law (both USM institutions), which will each receive one-third of the grant funds (a combined $333,300 annually).
The bill specifies that the State Treasurer must hold the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other State funds.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of $800,000 in the annual State budget bill for the CASH Campaign of Maryland starting in fiscal year 2026.

DBM oversees the state budget execution and fiscal planning, which includes implementing the bill's statutory mandated appropriation for the CASH Campaign and managing the fiscal impact on general fund revenues and expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship by repealing the service terminal dates prescribed by the U.S. Secretary of Defense, allowing uniformed service members who served in Afghanistan on or after October 24, 2001, or in Iraq on or after March 19, 2003, and their eligible dependents, to qualify for the scholarship.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland resident veterans, active-duty service members, reserve and National Guard members who served in Afghanistan or Iraq, and their spouses, children, and stepchildren.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not require additional State spending, as scholarships are funded through the annual State budget appropriation ($750,000 budgeted in FY 2025) and any additional eligible applicants can be placed on a waiting list if funds are exhausted. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can implement the changes using existing resources. There is no effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC and its Office of Student Financial Assistance directly administer the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship, making the necessary administrative and eligibility determinations under the bill.
As the state coordinating board administering state financial aid and scholarship programs, the commission is responsible for implementing the expanded eligibility criteria for this scholarship.
DVMF advocates for Maryland veterans and military families to connect them with educational benefits; the expansion of this scholarship directly impacts the community and services they support.
Members of the Maryland National Guard activated for service in the Afghanistan or Iraq conflicts, as well as their dependents, are explicit beneficiaries eligible for this scholarship.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class B-CAEVC (College Athletic Event Venue Concessionaire) beer, wine, and liquor license in Prince George's County. The bill authorizes the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to contracted concessionaires providing food and beverage services at athletic event venues on the University of Maryland, College Park and Bowie State University campuses, sets an annual fee of $3,500 per venue, and establishes hours and permitted areas of consumption.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Concessionaires operating at college athletic venues on the University of Maryland, College Park and Bowie State University campuses, attendees at campus athletic events, and Prince George's County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations for the University of Maryland, College Park and Bowie State University are not materially affected. Prince George's County local license fee revenues increase by approximately $10,500 annually beginning in fiscal year 2025 due to the estimated issuance of three licenses at $3,500 each. The county can manage any additional enforcement activity using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a specific alcoholic beverages license for concessionaires operating at college athletic event venues located specifically on the campuses of the University of Maryland, College Park and Bowie State University, both of which are member institutions of the University System of Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Urges the presidential administration of Joseph R. Biden to publish the federal Equal Rights Amendment (ERA) as the Twenty-eighth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution without delay, urges Congress to pass an affirming joint resolution, and calls upon other states to adopt similar resolutions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Marylanders and individuals across the United States seeking constitutional protections against sex-based discrimination
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The joint resolution does not directly affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The resolution explicitly references the Maryland Attorney General's legal action in filing an amicus brief supporting the certification and publication of the Equal Rights Amendment as the 28th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution.

The resolution directly concerns the constitutional protection of equal rights and prohibition of sex discrimination, which directly aligns with the Commission's core mission to enforce anti-discrimination laws and protect civil rights in Maryland.
